 on the day of Shabbos itself —
 when Ze'ir Anpin also ascends —
 therefore they read in the Torah
 seven readers [shivah keru'im] —
 corresponding to the seven traits —
 which are the aspects of the seventy facets of Torah.
 And afterward at Minchah
 they read three —
 corresponding to the aspects of Chab"d
 — as explained in the kavannos —
 and this corresponds to the aspects
 of the ancient years —
 which are the aspects of:
 "v'rav chesed
 [and abundant in lovingkindness]."
 And therefore one says then [Psalms 69:14]:
 "va'ani tefilasi lecha Hashem —
 et ratzon
 [and I — my prayer is to You, Hashem —
 a time of favor]"
 — the aspect of:
 "v'Atika Kadisha gali retzoneh
 [and the Holy Ancient One reveals His will]"
 — which is at Minchah of Shabbos.

 And this:
 "Elokim b'rav chasdecha aneini
 [O G-d — in Your abundant lovingkindness — answer me],"
 and so on —
 [Psalms 69:14]
 the aspect of the aforementioned abundant lovingkindness.

 And then afterward
 Ze'ir Anpin ascends to the actual Dik'na
 [beard] —
 and likewise at this third meal [seudata shelishis]
 Atika is the One Who eats —
 and likewise Ze'ir Anpin
 eats from the mouth of Atika —
 as explained in the kavannos.
 For then the aspects of the actual rectifications of Atik
 at their supernal root are drawn.
 And because one who engages
 in awakening human beings from their sleep
 must guard himself
 from students who are not worthy —
 so that the evil from them
 should not attach to him —
 [for this is the aspect of what on Erev Shabbos
 the flame of fire [shalhava d'asha] descends
 to burn the heads of the completely impure husks
 (which are in the aspects of impure animals — as is well-known)
 so that they should not attach themselves
 to the holiness as well, and so on.]
 And for this —
 his teaching must be to learn
 and to teach —
 to guard and to do —
 that is, through his teaching with his students
 it should be as if he made his fellow —
 and as if he made them into words of Torah.
 (And this our Sages of blessed memory derived
 from what is written:
 "u'shemartem es divray habris hazos —
 va'asitem osam
 [and you shall guard the words of this covenant —
 and do them],"
 [Deuteronomy 29:8]
 and so on —
 and as explained elsewhere.)
 And then G-d, blessed be He, guards him —
 so that his words should not be inscribed
 in the memory-power of the unworthy student —
 but rather they shall be forgotten by him —
 and so on —
 as explained within.

 And this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught:
 "nashim chayavos b'Kiddush hayom —
 v'chol haggid —
 amar kra: zachor v'shamor —
 kol she'ishnu b'shmirah — ishnu b'zechirah
 [women are obligated in Kiddush hayom —
 and so on —
 as the verse states: remember and guard —
 all who are included in guarding —
 are included in remembering]."
 For we have already alluded above
 that the Kiddush of the day
 is the aspect of the awakening from sleep
 through the aspect of the stories of the ancient years —
 which are the aspects of Chab"d.
 And therefore one makes Kiddush over wine —
 the aspect of [Song of Songs 7:10]:
 "v'cheichech k'yayin tov —
 v'chol haggid —
 dovev sifsey yeshenim
 [and your palate is like good wine —
 and so on —
 that moves the lips of those who sleep]"
 — and as elaborated on this at greater length
 in Likutay Halachos.
 And therefore — even the women —
 who are the aspects of those who have fallen
 from all the seventy facets of Torah
 (for women are exempt from Torah study —
 as our Sages of blessed memory taught)
 — nonetheless they are not in the category of the
 unworthy students, heaven forfend —
 and one needs to awaken them
 through the aspect of the ancient years —
 which is the aspect of the Kiddush of the day — as mentioned above.
 And this:
 "amar kra: zachor v'shamor —
 kol she'ishnu b'shmirah —
 [the verse states: remember and guard —
 all who are included in guarding]"
 — that is, one who truly wishes
 to receive the teaching —
 to guard and to do —
 is then included in remembering —
 and then the words of the teacher
 are inscribed in his memory-power.
 And it follows clearly
 that one who is not in the state of guarding —
 which is the aspect of the truly unworthy student —
 then is not in the state of remembering —
 for then the words are not inscribed
 in his memory-power —
 as mentioned above.
 And therefore one need not be concerned
 about engaging also with simple people
 (who are in the aspects of women)
 and awakening them
 through the lofty aforementioned stories of high station.
 For one who is truly in the aspect
 of the unworthy students, heaven forfend —
 then certainly the words will be forgotten from him —
 in the aspect of:
 "ana alma b'charuva ashkachteh
 [I found the world as a carob tree — desolate]"
 — as brought within.

 And this is likewise the aspect of:
 "v'shamru Bnay Yisrael es haShabbas —
 la'asos es haShabbas
 [and the children of Israel shall guard the Shabbos —
 to make the Shabbos]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 that it is as if one literally made the Shabbos itself, and so on —
 which is likewise in the aspect of:
 "u'shemartem va'asitem osam
 [and you shall guard and do them]"
 — as mentioned above.
 And therefore also —
 the teacher who engages
 in drawing the illumination of Shabbos
 to his students
 (for the sake of which they are obligated
 to receive the face of the teacher on Shabbos —
 as explained in the kavannos)
 — and awakens them through this from their sleep —
 is likewise in the aforementioned aspect:
 to guard and to do —
 so that it should be as if he made the Shabbos —
 and as if he made his students —
 and one who is an unworthy student —
 who does not allow the teacher to make him —
 and to transform him from evil to good —
 then the illumination of Shabbos also withdraws from him —
 and everything is forgotten by him.
 And this:
 "beini u'vein Bnay Yisrael
 [between Me and the children of Israel],"
 and so on —
 and as explained in Zohar Yisro, folio 88:
 "d'inun seudasi d'meheimanusah —
 d'zara kadisha d'Yisrael —
 d'meheimanusah ila'ah da — d'lehon —
 v'lo d'amim aku'm —
 v'chol haggid —
 u'vigin kach amar: beini u'vein Bnay Yisrael
 [for these are My meals of faith —
 of the holy seed of Israel —
 this supernal faith is theirs —
 and not of the nations —
 and so on —
 and for this reason he stated: between Me and the children of Israel],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And this:
 "la'asos es haShabbas l'dorosaym
 [to make the Shabbos throughout their generations]"
 — for through this the aspect of birth
 and the visiting of the barren
 is accomplished —
 which is the aspect of the physical union —
 as explained within.
 And therefore the essential time
 for the holiness of the union is on Shabbos —
 and this is alluded to likewise
 in the matter of:
 "v'shamru Bnay Yisrael es haShabbas"
 — as is well-known —
 and as also explained in the kavannos —
 for likewise at its supernal root —
 the union and the yichud [unification] of Shabbos
 is for the sake of the drawing forth
 of the birth of new souls —
 as explained in the kavannos.
 For through the aspect of the awakening from sleep —
 drawn through the holiness of Shabbos —
 through this the aspect of:
 "l'hatir peh ilemim
 [to open the mouths of the mute]"
 — is accomplished — as explained within.

 And this is the aspect of:
 "v'daber davar
 [and speaking words]"
 — stated regarding Shabbos —
 for then speech opens in great perfection —
 as also understood in the holy Zohar,
 Bereishis, folio 32 —
 and as mentioned above many times.
 And through this the aspect of:
 "l'hatir peh akros
 [to open the mouths of the barren]"
 — the aspect of birth — is also drawn —
 as explained within.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "ki choh amar Hashem la'sarisim —
 asher yishmeru es Shabsosai —
 v'nasati lahem —
 v'chol haggid —
 yad v'shem tov mibbanim u'mibbanos
 [for so says Hashem to the sarisim —
 who guard My Shabbosim —
 and I shall give them —
 and so on —
 a hand and a good name
 better than sons and daughters]"
 — for through the guarding of Shabbos
 the visiting of the barren and birth
 are drawn upon all of Israel —
 and it is counted as if he fathered them.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "hame'orer yeshenim —
 v'hamekitz nirdamim —
 v'hamashi'ach ilemim —
 u'matir asurim —
 [He Who awakens those who sleep —
 and rouses those who slumber —
 and makes the mute to speak —
 and releases those who are bound —]"
 which is the aspect of the visiting of the barren —
 and likewise:
 "v'hasomech noflim —
 v'hazokeif kefufim
 [and Who supports the fallen —
 and straightens the bent]"
 — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded
 [Midrash Rabbah, Vayetzei, section 71].
 And this is the aspect of:
 "to'amehah chayyim zachu
 [those who taste it have merited life]"
 — stated regarding Shabbos —
 for on Shabbos one merits the opening of speech —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "eileh l'chayyay olam —
 bechinah l'nefesh chayyah —
 l'ruach memalela
 [these [go] to eternal life —
 the aspect of: to a living soul —
 to a speaking spirit]"
 — as explained within.

 And this [Tractate Mo'ed Katan 28a]:
 "chayyay banay u'mezonay —
 b'mazala talya
 [life, children, and livelihood —
 depend on the constellation/fortune]"
 — and this means
 the supernal constellation [mazal elyon]
 in the holy beard —
 as is well-known.
 And this constellation shines
 and flows even more
 through the holiness of the holy Shabbos —
 for then one ascends
 to the aforementioned beard —
 and from there one draws
 the aspect of eternal life [chayyay olam] —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "l'hatir peh ilemim
 [to open the mouths of the mute]"
 — and from there flows likewise
 the aspect of the visiting of the barren
 and the birth of children —
 and therefore it is stated of Chanah [I Samuel 1:10]:
 "v'tispallel Chanah al Hashem —
 al Hashem davka
 [and Chanah prayed to/upon Hashem —
 to/upon Hashem — specifically]"
 — as explained in Zohar Acharei, folio 79.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "az tis'anag al Hashem
 [then you will delight in Hashem]"
 — stated concerning the holy Shabbos.
 And through this fear is revealed —
 and one merits length of days —
 which is likewise included
 in the aforementioned eternal life —
 and through this comes wealth —
 the aspect of the aforementioned mezonay [livelihood].

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha
 [if you return from Shabbos your foot]"
 — that is, that through the holiness of Shabbos
 there shall also awaken and return
 even people of the lowest levels —
 who are the aspects of legs.
 And also — regel [foot/leg] is the aspect of speech —
 as explained elsewhere.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "l'hatir peh ilemim
 [to open the mouths of the mute]."
 And also — the birth of children
 is the aspects of legs —
 in the aspect of:
 "bera kara d'avuha
 [a son is the leg of his father]."
 And this is the aspect of:
 "l'hatir peh akros
 [to open the mouths of the barren]."
 And also — the revelation of fear is the aspect of regel —
 as explained in
 Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 4.
 And also — wealth is the aspect of regel —
 as mentioned above.
 And also — in its plain meaning —
 one should not go beyond the Shabbos boundary —
 and the Shabbos boundary is two thousand cubits.

 Aleph is the language of teaching —
 as in:
 "va'aalfecha chochmah
 [and I shall teach you wisdom]."
 [Job 33:33]
 And the teaching
 with which the teacher engages with his students
 to awaken them from their sleep —
 which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos —
 has within it two aspects:
 for there is the aspect of the teaching
 of the seventy years —
 the seventy facets of Torah —
 and there is the teaching
 of the aspect of the ancient years.

 And this is the aspect of the two thousand cubits
 of the Shabbos boundary.
 For anyone who is not in the aspect
 of a truly unworthy student —
 and has not gone out completely
 from the boundary of holiness —
 the Shabbos boundary —
 can receive the sacred awakening
 through the holiness of Shabbos —
 through the aspects of the two teachings mentioned above
 that illuminate in the holiness of the holy Shabbos —
 as mentioned above.
 And this:
 "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi
 [from pursuing your affairs on My holy day]"
 — he should withhold himself
 from pursuing his weekday affairs —
 which have within them the grip of foolishness —
 in the aspect of:
 "lo yachphotz chesil b'sevunah
 [a fool does not desire understanding]."
 But on Shabbos —
 then the fifty gates of Binah open —
 of which it is stated:
 "bikaish Koheles limtzo divrey chefetz
 [Koheles sought to find words of desire/delight]"
 — as our Sages of blessed memory taught —
 and they are the aspects of the aforementioned contemplation.
 And also — wealth is the aspect of chefetz [desire] —
 as it is written [Proverbs 3:15]:
 "v'chol chafatzecha lo yishvu vah
 [and all your desires cannot compare to her]"
 (only that one's desire should not be in the wealth itself —
 but only in order to arrive through it
 at the aforementioned contemplation).
 And also — life and length of days is the aspect of:
 "Melech chafetz b'chayyim
 [the King Who desires life]."
 [Psalms 21:5]
 And also — fear is the aspect of chefetz —
 as it is written [Nehemiah 1:11]:
 "hachafetzim l'yir'ah es shimcha
 [those who desire to fear Your Name]."
 And also — the teaching with human beings
 to bring them back in repentance
 and to awaken them from their sleep —
 which is the aspect of Chesed —
 as explained within —
 is the aspect of chefetz —
 as it is written [Hosea 6:6]:
 "ki chesed chafatzti
 [for I desire lovingkindness]."
 And also — the awakening and the opening of speech —
 which is the aspect of eileh l'chayyay olam
 [these go to eternal life] —
 is the aspect of chefetz —
 as it is written:
 "hachafetz achphotz —
 v'chol haggid —
 ki im b'shuvo —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'chayah
 [do I truly desire —
 and so on —
 except in his repentance —
 and so on —
 that he should live]"
 [Ezekiel 18:23] —
 which is likewise the aspect of:
 "Melech chafetz b'chayyim
 [the King Who desires life]"
 — as mentioned above.
 And also — the birth —
 drawn through the aspect of the physical union, and so on —
 as explained within —
 is the aspect of chefetz —
 as mentioned above many times —
 and as explained in the holy Zohar:
 "u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti
 [and choose that which I desire],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 [Isaiah 56:4]
 It follows that all the aforementioned aspects
 are the aspects of the affairs of Heaven —
 the aspects of the holy rectifications
 drawn through the holiness of Shabbos —
 as mentioned above.
 And the awakening from sleep through Torah
 is the aspect of chefetz —
 as it is written [Isaiah 53:10]:
 "v'chefetz Hashem b'yado yitzlach
 [and the desire of Hashem shall prosper in his hand]"
 — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded.
 And the awakening through story-telling is the aspect of:
 "gedolim ma'asay Hashem —
 derusim l'chol chaftzeihem
 [great are the works of Hashem —
 sought out by all who desire them]"
 [Psalms 111:2] —
 and it is written [Psalms 115:3]:
 "kol asher chafetz Hashem asah
 [everything Hashem desired — He did],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And this:
 "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg
 [and you shall call the Shabbos a delight]"
 — the aspect of the Shabbos meals —
 which are precious and very holy —
 in the aspect of lechem hapanim
 [the bread of the Presence] —
 for on Shabbos
 the aspect of the holy face is returned to the person —
 as mentioned above.
 And this:
 "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad
 [the holy one of Hashem, honored]"
 — the aspects of the garments of honor of Shabbos —
 for the face is clothed —
 in the aspect of [Psalms 17:15]:
 "ani b'tzedek echezeh panecha
 [I in righteousness shall behold Your face]"
 — the aspect of:
 "tzedek lavashti
 [I clothed myself in righteousness]"
 [Job 29:14] —
 and as explained within.

 And this:
 "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha
 [and honor it — from pursuing your own ways]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 "she'lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah
 [one should not take large strides]"
 — which is the aspect of anger —
 as mentioned above many times —
 which is the aspect of mochin d'katnus —
 the aspect of sleep —
 in the aspect of [Genesis 4:6]:
 "lamah charah lecha — v'lamah naflu fanecha
 [why are you angry — and why has your face fallen?]"
 — and as also explained in Siman 57.
 And this is the aspect of [Habakkuk 3:2]:
 "b'kerev shanim chayyayhu
 [in the midst of the years — give it life]"
 — which is the aspect of the awakening from sleep —
 and it concluded afterward:
 "b'rogez rachem tizkor
 [in anger — remember to have mercy]."
 [Habakkuk 3:2]
 And this:
 "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar
 [from pursuing your affairs — and speaking words]"
 — so as not to blemish through this
 the aspect of the holy speech
 that opens on Shabbos —
 as mentioned above.
 And this is the aspect of [Micah 7:5]:
 "shmor pis'chei picha
 [guard the doors of your mouth]"
 — and as explained within.
 And this:
 "az tis'anag al Hashem
 [then you will delight in Hashem]"
 — "da Atika Kadisha
 [this is the Holy Ancient One]"
 — for one merits the aspects of the rectifications of Atik.
 "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz —
 da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin
 [and I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth —
 this is the Holy Apple Orchard]"
 — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus
 through the three aspects —
 which are Neh"y, Chag"t, Chab"d —
 which is the aspect of the perfect fear
 in its three aspects mentioned above.
 And our Sages in the Gemara expounded on this:
 that one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms —
 that is, one is saved
 from the grip of the Sitra Achra
 during the weekdays —
 which are the aspects of sleep
 and mochin d'katnus —
 for this is the aspect of the Sitra Achra
 that rests upon a person during the time of sleep —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 And at its root in the supernal holiness
 it is the aspect of [Genesis 15:12]:
 "v'tardema nafla al Avram
 [and a deep sleep fell upon Avram]"
 (and this was a deep sleep of prophecy —
 as our Sages of blessed memory expounded):
 "v'hineh eimah chashecha gedolah nofeleth alav
 [and behold — a terror — a great darkness fell upon him]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 this refers to the subjugation of kingdoms —
 for from there is the root of their grip
 and their sustenance —
 from the aspect of tardema [deep sleep] and sleep —
 the aspect of the back — the aspect of mochin d'katnus.
 (And this is the aspect of:
 shanayim mikra v'echad Targum
 [twice the text and once the Targum]:
 the twice reading of the text
 is the aspects of the holy face —
 and the Targum is the aspect of the backs —
 and תרגו"ם [Targum] in gematria
 equals תרדמ"ה [tardema] —
 as all of this is brought in the writings of the holy Ari z"l.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "b'kerev shanim chayyayhu
 [in the midst of the years — give it life]"
 — which is the aspect of the awakening from sleep —
 which is the aspect of the face.
 And therefore our Sages expounded:
 do not read b'kerev shanim [in the midst of the years]
 but rather b'karov shanim —
 the aspect of shanayim mikra —
 and as explained above within in Siman 19
 in the teaching Tefillah l'Chavakuk.
 And echad Targum is the aspect of deep sleep and sleep.)

 For when one merits
 the aspect of the awakening from sleep —
 then even the sleep is encompassed
 in the supernal holiness.
 (For this is the aspect of the holiness of the Shabbos sleep —
 for specifically through sleep and the awakening from sleep —
 through this the building of Malchus is constructed —
 which is the aspect of fear —
 as mentioned above —
 in the aspect of [Genesis 28:16]:
 "vayikatz Yaakov mishenas'to —
 davka —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayira vayomar: mah nora
 [and Yaakov awoke from his sleep —
 specifically —
 and so on —
 and he was afraid and said: how awesome],"
 and so on.)
 In the aspect of [Genesis 2:21]:
 "vayapel Hashem Elokim tardema al ha'adam —
 vayishan —
 vayikach
 [and Hashem G-d caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man —
 and he slept —
 and He took],"
 and so on —
 and as explained in the writings of the holy Ari z"l
 in the kavannos of Rosh Hashanah
 and in other places —
 and as also understood within in this teaching —
 that specifically through the fact that
 there was the aspect of the absence of speech
 during the time of sleep —
 therefore now — after the awakening from sleep —
 speech goes forth with great power —
 and so on —
 and through this the visiting of the barren is accomplished —
 and through this fear is revealed —
 and so on.
 And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught:
 "hamashlem parashiyosav im hatzibur —
 shanayim mikra v'echad Targum —
 ma'arichin lo yamav v'shanosav
 [one who completes his Torah portions with the community —
 twice the text and once the Targum —
 their days and years are lengthened]"
 — for through fear comes length of days.
 And therefore one must be careful
 to complete the parasha at the very least
 before the Shabbos meal —
 as brought in Tosafos there.
 For this pertains to the rectifications
 of the Shabbos meal —
 which is the aspect of lechem hapanim —
 as mentioned above.
 In particular the morning meal of Shabbos day —
 which is the meal of the Holy Ancient One
 [seudata d'Atika Kadisha] —
 the aspect of the rectifications of Atik
 drawn through all the above.
 And therefore it was said to Avraham
 at that time of the deep sleep:
 "yado teda
 [know surely],"
 and so on [Genesis 15:13] —
 and:
 "v'gam es hagoy asher ya'avodu dan anochi —
 u'ferash Rashi: l'rabos arba malchiyos —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'acharay chen yetze'u b'rechush gadol
 [and also the nation that they shall serve —
 I shall judge —
 and Rashi explained: to include the four kingdoms —
 and so on —
 and afterward they shall go out with great wealth]"
 — for specifically through the aspect of sleep
 and the awakening from sleep —
 which in general are the aspects of the exiles and the redemption —
 and through this fear is revealed —
 the aspect of:
 "u'vemora'im gedolim
 [and with great awe]"
 — and likewise:
 "vayiru ha'am
 [and the people feared],"
 and so on. [וכו']

 And there flows the sacred wealth —
 through which one merits
 the contemplation of the Torah.
 And perhaps this is the aspect of the admonition
 to ask from Egypt vessels of silver and of gold —
 and the matter of all the wealth
 they brought out from there —
 and this was also a preparation
 for the aspect of the receiving of the Torah —
 as per the above.
 (And see Zohar Mikeitz, folio 196.)

 And this:
 "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha —
 da Ze'ir Anpin
 [and I will feed you with the heritage of Yaakov your father —
 this is Ze'ir Anpin]"
 — as explained in Adra Nassa, folio 138:
 "man fo'alaych —
 Ze'ir Anpin —
 b'kerev shanim — inun shanim kadmoniyos — chayyayhu.
 L'man chayyayhu — l'Ze'ir Anpin —
 d'chol nehiru dilei —
 mei'inun panim isakimu
 [who is Your work? —
 Ze'ir Anpin —
 in the midst of the years —
 those are the ancient years — give it life.
 For whom give it life? —
 for Ze'ir Anpin —
 for all its radiance
 is established from those faces],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 For this is the aspect of what is explained in this teaching —
 that there is the aspect of the seventy faces of Torah
 (and they are the aspect of Ze'ir Anpin —
 which encompasses the seven traits — as is well-known)
 — and there are the ancient years —
 from which all seventy faces receive their vitality —
 and they are the aspects of Atik —
 the aspect of Zaken [Elder] —
 the aspect of hadras panim [the splendor of countenance], and so on.
 And therefore Ze'ir Anpin
 is the aspect of the heritage of Yaakov —
 which is the aspect of all seventy faces of Torah —
 the aspect of:
 "Torah tzivvah lanu Moshe —
 morasha kehillas Yaakov
 [the Torah that Moshe commanded us —
 the heritage of the congregation of Yaakov]."
 [Deuteronomy 33:4]
 And this is the aspect of:
 "mevakshay fanecha Yaakov selah
 [those who seek Your face — Yaakov — selah]."
 [Psalms 24:6]
 And it is the aspect of an inheritance without limits —
 for it ascends and receives
 from the aspect of the ancient years —
 which are the aspects of above the boundaries and the traits —
 and receives from there vitality —
 and draws it down to all the levels —
 until even those who have fallen, heaven forfend,
 from all seventy faces of Torah —
 it draws to them vitality
 from the aspect of the ancient years mentioned above.
 For this is the aspect of what is explained
 in the introduction to the Zohar, folio 7:
 "v'chol man d'itkashar b'inun shanim kadmoniyos —
 chayyay itkashru bei —
 she'zeh bechinah mah she'amru rz\"l —
 Yaakov avinu lo mes —
 b'kerev shanim todi'a l'ha'i darga d'leis bei chayyay klal
 [and all who bind themselves to those ancient years —
 life is bound to them —
 which is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught:
 Yaakov our Patriarch did not die —
 'in the midst of the years' — make known to that level
 in which there is no life at all]"
 — that is, as mentioned above.
 And therefore our Sages expounded:
 "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha —
 she'zocheh l'nachalah b'li metzarim
 [and I will feed you with the heritage of Yaakov your father —
 that one merits an inheritance without limits]."
 And this is the aspect of:
 "u'vnay haneychar hanilavim al Hashem —
 v'chol haggid —
 kol shomer Shabbas mechalelo —
 v'chol haggid
 [and the children of the stranger
 who attach themselves to Hashem —
 and so on —
 every Shabbos guardian who does not desecrate it —
 and so on]"
 — for even they can draw close
 through the holiness of the guarding of Shabbos.
 And this too is the aspect of the three meals of Shabbos —
 which are the aspects of
 "Eden — Nahar — Gan"
 — the aspect of:
 "v'nahar yotzei mei'Eden l'hashkos es haGan
 [and a river goes out from Eden to water the garden]"
 [Genesis 2:10] —
 that is, as mentioned above.

 And this:
 "ki pi Hashem diber
 [for the mouth of Hashem has spoken]"
 — for through the holiness of Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the awakening from sleep —
 coming through all the aforementioned rectifications —
 through this the holy speech opens in its perfection —
 as mentioned above.
 And also — for all the aforementioned rectifications
 are encompassed in the holiness of the speech
 of the awakening from sleep —
 which comes through the fact
 that the holy face is shown to one —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "panim b'fanim diber Hashem imachem
 [face to face Hashem spoke with you]"
 [Deuteronomy 5:4] —
 and through this speech opens —
 in the aspect of:
 "petach picha l'ilem
 [open your mouth for the mute]"
 [Proverbs 31:8] —
 as mentioned above —
 and through this the visiting of the barren is drawn —
 for this is the aspect of [Genesis 21:1]:
 "v'Hashem pakad es Sarah ka'asher amar —
 vaya'as Hashem l'Sarah ka'asher diber
 [and Hashem remembered Sarah as He had said —
 and Hashem did to Sarah as He had spoken]."
 And through this fear is revealed —
 for this is the aspect of [Exodus 9:20]:
 "hayarei es dvar Hashem
 [one who feared the word of Hashem]"
 — and as also understood above within in Siman 15.
 And through this comes length of days —
 in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 32:47]:
 "u'vadavar hazeh ta'arichuimim
 [and through this matter — your days shall be lengthened]."
 And through this comes wealth —
 for this is the aspect of [Genesis 24:1]:
 "v'Hashem beirach es Avraham b'chol
 [and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything]."

 And this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 15:6]:
 "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem
 [and He shall bless you as He spoke to you]"
 — the aspect of:
 "birchas Hashem hi sa'ashir
 [the blessing of Hashem — it enriches]"
 — and through this one comes
 to the contemplation of the Torah.

 And this is the aspect of [Proverbs 2:6]:
 "mipiv da'as u'sevunah
 [from His mouth — knowledge and understanding]."
 It follows that all the aforementioned aspects
 are encompassed in the aspect of:
 "ki pi Hashem diber
 [for the mouth of Hashem has spoken]"
 — as mentioned above.

segments.he: וזה ושמרתם את השבת כי קדש הוא לכם ודרשו רז"ל (יומא פ"ה:) היא מסורה בידכם ואין אתם מסורים בידה היינו כי היראה הבאה מלמעלה ממילא היא מושלת על האדם והוא מסור בידה כי מגיע אליו מתי שתרצה.
segments.en: Shabbos is the aspect of peace [shalom] — the aspect of Shabbas Shalom — and therefore it is the source of blessing — for the Holy One, blessed be He, found no vessel to hold blessing for Israel except peace. And peace connects two opposites — that is, lovingkindnesses and severities — which is the aspect of Yosef — as explained within. And therefore Shabbos is likewise the aspect of Yosef — as explained in the holy Zohar. And it is stated regarding Yosef that he guarded the Shabbos — as it is written [Genesis 43:16]: "v'tavo'ach teva'ach v'hachen [slaughter and prepare]" — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 66:23]: "v'yanuchu vo kol Yisrael mekadshey Shimcha [and all Israel who sanctify Your Name shall rest through it]." And this is likewise the aspect of [Isaiah 66:23]: "v'al menuchasam yekadshu es Shimcha" — that one must accept upon oneself then self-sacrifice for the sanctification of the Name — as brought — for the sanctification of the Name is likewise from the aspect of lovingkindnesses and severities — as explained within. And therefore Shabbos is among the things Israel sacrificed their souls for — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And behold — the essential matter of all the influences and blessings is so that each person of Israel can speak holy words — that is, that the speech should be connected to the thought and the wisdom — which is the aspect of Kodesh. And this is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the world of thought — and also the aspect of the perfection of speech — as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar.

segments.he: והעיקר הוא שהאדם בעצמו יעורר וימשיך עליו היראה שהוא בחינת קדושת שבת בבחינת צדיק מושל יראת אלקים כנ"ל שזה בחינת היא מסורה בידכם ולא אתם מסורים בידה כנ"ל. וזה גם כן ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת לעשות את השבת וכו' לעשות דייקא לעצמו היראה כנ"ל וזה בחינת אלמלי שמרו ישראל שתי שבתות היינו השתי מיני יראות דייקא. כי גם יראה הראשונה צריכה שמירה כנ"ל. וזה בחינת את שבתותי תשמרו שתי שבתות כנ"ל ועל כן עיקר שלימות התפלה והשפעת השפע רב לישראל והתגלות מלכותו יתברך והכנעת הקליפות תחת הקדושה הכל נמשך בשלימות על ידי קדושת שבת כנ"ל כמה פעמים. וזה אז תתענג על ה' ודרשו רז"ל שנותנין לו כל משאלות לבו היינו שזוכה לשלימות התפלה ויוכל לעורר השפע בעולם על ידי תפלתו והרכבתיך על במותי ארץ ודרשו רז"ל שניצול משיעבוד מלכיות שנאמר ואתה על במותימו תדרוך היינו שנכנעין הקליפות תחת רגלי הקדושה והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב אביך הוא בחינת היראה בחינת ביראתך בזכות יעקב כי פי ה' דבר כי שבת הוא בחינת התגלות הדיבור דקדושה כנ"ל ומשם נתגלה יראה בבחינת ומדברך פחד לבי וכתיב הירא דבר ה'. וגם על ידי היראה נשלם הדיבור שיהיה יכול להמשיך שפע בבחינת כל מי שיש בו יראת שמים דבריו נשמעין כמבואר בפנים. וזה כי פי ה' דבר. כי על ידי היראה דבריו הם בבחינת דבר ה' וממשיכין שפע בבחינת ויברך אתכם כאשר דבר לכם:
segments.en:
Opening of the paths of Torah / fifty gates of Binah / wealth / rectifications of Atik / length of days: Essential opening of pathways of Torah and great contemplation = on Shabbos (Zohar Yisro 85: "oraissa mis'atara bei b'itrin kadishin"; Zohar Chadash Chukas: fifty gates of Binah opened on Shabbos). Torah given on Shabbos (Sages). Shabbos = Binah. "Birchas Hashem hi sa'ashir — zeh Shabbas" = this contemplation requires great wealth. Wealth comes through rectifications of Atik = arichas yamim = lengthening of days = in each subsequent moment more holiness is added. Holiness of Shabbos grows continuously: day greater than night ("kavod yom adif"); within the day: Shacharis → Musaf → Minchah. Preparation: Wednesday = illumination of nefesh; Thursday = ruach; Friday = neshamah; on Shabbos itself = all in full. After Shabbos: the withdrawal of nefesh/ruach/neshamah is for receiving it at a higher level the next Shabbos = "es Shabsosai tishmoru"; "almilai shamru shtay Shabbasos." Shabbos = foretaste of World to Come = entirely long day = arichas yamim. Arichas yamim comes through yirah.
 Fear of Shabbos / grace / beauty / Noach / Moshe / Yosef / Yaakov / Rachel / Malchus / Psalms 45 / subduing of false grace / rains fall on Shabbos nights / elongation of breath / kindling Shabbos lamp: "Yira Shabbas" = fear of Shabbos (many previous simanim). Through Shabbos fear: protected from poverty caused by "sheker hachen v'hevel hayofi" (Proverbs 31:30). True grace of holiness = Shabbos: "v'Noach matza chen" = Noach = Shabbas = "niyacha d'ila'in v'tata'in" (Tikunim); Shabbos = Moshe = "ki matzas chen b'einai." "Eshes chen titmoch kavod" (Proverbs 11:16) = "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha." "Seichel tov yiten chen" (Proverbs 13:15) = essential perfection of intellect is on Shabbos. "Divray fi chacham chen" (Ecclesiastes 10:12) = perfection of holy speech on Shabbos. Essential sacred beauty = Shabbos = union of Yaakov and Rachel; "shufra d'Yaakov"; Rachel = "yefas to'ar v'yefas mar'eh." Shabbos = Yosef (Zohar Chadash) = "vayehi Yosef yefeh to'ar / vayimtza Yosef chen"; Yaakov: "ki channani Elokim." Shabbos = Malchus = "Melech b'yofyo tichzenah einecha" (Isaiah 33:17). Psalms 45:3: "yafyafita mibnay adam — hutzak chen bisfasosecha — al ken berachecha Elokim l'olam" = "vayevarech Elokim es yom hashevi'i / al ken beirach." All false aspects subdued = "afilu am ha'aretz yira lishker b'Shabbas"; vanity of beauty subdued through holy havalim on Shabbos (kavannos of Havu laHashem). Essential time for sacred union (Sages). Shabbos = elongation of breath (Rashi on "vayinafash") = extra soul. Essential time for rain (Rashi on Leviticus 26:4: "b'leiley Shabbasos"). "V'nishmas Shadai tvinam" = Shadai = Shabbos. Elongation of breath → contemplation. "Ner Hashem nishmas adam." Kindling of Shabbos lamp = obligatory = chova = gematria = Aleph-Heh-Yod-Heh = Binah = contemplation.
 Three aspects of fear / Chochmah-Binah-Da'as / Zohar Kedoshim / fear of teacher / spending Shabbos with the Tzadik / Zohar Yisro 92 / fear of father and mother / three portions of wealth / Neh"y-Chag"t-Chab"d / Kiddush on wine and length of days: Three lines of fear: mora shamayim + mora rabbecha + mora av va'eim; each encompasses three aspects. Fear of Shabbos encompasses all. Root of fear = Da'as = in the heart (Siman 15, HaGanuz teaching). Shabbos = Da'as + heart. Therefore fear in its perfection on Shabbos = fear with Da'as (LM Tinyana 17). Fear of Heaven = encompassed in all three mochin: Chochmah, Binah, Da'as. Fear of the teacher completed on Shabbos = "es Shabsosai tishmoru u'mikdashi tira'u"; Zohar Kedoshim 81: "u'mikdashi… al tikri u'mikdashi ela u'mikudoshai" = refers to elders and sages of the generation (Tractate Shabbos 55). The true teacher himself = aspect of Shabbos holiness. Most propitious to spend Shabbos with the Tzadik of the generation. Essential to assemble congregations on Shabbos (Vayakhel Moshe; Sages). Ultimate purpose of teaching = fear of Heaven = Isaiah 33:6: "yir'as Hashem hi otzaro." Essential perfection of fear on Shabbos → fear drawn upon all portions of teaching = "oraissa tilitai" (Torah/Prophets/Writings) = this itself = holiness of Shabbos (Zohar Yisro 92). Fear of father and mother completed on Shabbos = Zohar Kedoshim: "ish imo v'aviv tira'u v'es Shabsosai tishmoru — mokish — kula chad — man d'dachil mei'hai natir l'hai." Shabbos union alluded to in this context = sacred union depends on fear. Three portions of wealth: 1/3 pirkmata'ya (commerce) + 1/3 b'yado (hand) + 1/3 b'karka (land). Malchus even in standing against Neh"y = called Chakla Tupichin Kadishin = alludes to Neh"y/Chag"t/Chab"d. Malchus = yirah = mora malchus; against Neh"y = fear of father and mother = upon portions of wealth = aspects of legs = "v'es hayekum asher b'ragleihem" (Numbers 16:30). Then encompasses Neh"y/Chag"t/Chab"d = three portions of wealth: through fear: commerce with faith (Neh"y = legs; commerce = regel) = 1/3 commerce; through fear: much charity from wealth (Chag"t = hands) = 1/3 hand; through fear: understands wealth is waste = needed only for contemplation (Chab"d = mochin) = 1/3 land. All together = Neh"y = fear of father and mother = "bera kara d'avuha." Fear of teacher = Chag"t = "ki samach Moshe es yadav alav." Fear of teacher himself = fear of Heaven = Chab"d. Fear is then complete → merits length of days. Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 18: "kol hamevareych al haYayin b'leiley Shabbasos ma'arichin lo yamav v'shanosav b'olam hazeh v'yosifu lo shenos chayyim b'olam haba." Kavannos: at Kiddush over wine on Shabbos night → Malchus receives Chab"d of Ze'ir Anpin = perfect ascent of fear until in Chab"d → length of days → contemplation = World to Come = Binah. "(And if I have erred, heaven forfend — may He Who is merciful forgive.)"
 Shabbos = awakening from sleep / shofar blasts on Erev Shabbos / six orders of Mishnah = sleep / eating of Shabbos = lechem hapanim / extra soul = mochin / "vav avdah nefesh" — two explanations: Shabbos = awakening from sleep = "u'shemartem es haShabbas ki kodesh hu" = all that is more holy is farther from sleep (Sefer haMidos). Shofar blasts on Erev Shabbos = awakening from sleep; commerce during weekdays = sleep (Siman 35, Ashray Zaraka). Even simple study of Torah (six orders of Mishnah = six weekdays) = sleep relative to clinging to G-d; essential clinging = on Shabbos. Even weekday Torah study and prayer = mochin d'katnus compared to Shabbos. Therefore: essential time for perfect ascent of Torah and prayer of the entire week on Shabbos. Weekday eating = grip of Sitra Achra → also falls into sleep; eating of Shabbos = entirely holy (Siman 57) = lechem hapanim = secret of the twelve loaves on Shabbos. Shabbos eating alludes to very high mochin (kavannos) = or hapanim = "chochmas adam ta'ir panav" = "berchu b'or panav shel adam / berchu b'mat'amim" = eating Shabbos delicacies themselves = illumination of the light of the face. Shabbos = rectification of the heart (Tikunim) = returns to seek the face (= mochin lost in the weekdays). Extra soul = aspect of the mochin = "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam." "U'veyom hashevi'i shavas vayinafash" + "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh" = impossible to awaken a person from sleep unless he first awakens himself somewhat (is'arus d'l'tata); G-d established: the moment Shabbos arrives → each Jew awakened somewhat → reminds himself of the loss of his soul → cries out "vav avdah nefesh" → through this partial awakening → merits awakening each time more → until the face returns = "pnay Shabbas nekabelah." Second interpretation: "keivan she'shavas" = when Shabbos departs → "vav avdah nefesh" = sometimes G-d sends a holy illumination → immediately withdraws → person awakens to pursue it → this is counted as is'arus d'l'tata → merits complete awakening from above. Applied to Shabbos: extra soul given on Shabbos → after Shabbos departs, person sighs "vav avdah nefesh" → merits higher extra soul the next Shabbos → this too = "almilai shamru shtay Shabbasos."
 Story-telling / the Face / seventy facets of Torah / ancient years / Shabbos night Vayechulu (three times) / Shabbos day seven readers / Minchah three readers / third meal / unworthy students / Kiddush and women / "v'shamru" = "v'asitem" / birth / "la'asos es haShabbas": Awakening from sleep: clothe the face = sometimes in story-telling and ordinary conversation; sometimes in words of Torah; sometimes through one's own face; sometimes through a higher face. Those who have fallen from all seventy faces of Torah → can only be awakened through the stories of the ancient years (sipuray ma'asiyos shel shanim kadmoniyos) from which all seventy faces (= seventy years) receive their vitality = Atik = Zaken = hadras panim = "v'rav chesed." Zohar Bereishis folio 7b + Ramaz; Zohar Beshalach folio 45b + Ramaz. On Shabbos night: ascent only to Malchus (kavannos) = Malchus nested in Asiyah; must draw its rectification through story-telling (= Vayechulu = narration of events only). First recitation of Vayechulu → draws mochin from Neh"y of Ze'ir Anpin (= its place of standing). Second recitation → draws from Chag"t. Chag"t Neh"ym = seventy facets of Torah. First: drawn from its own face (Neh"y of Z"A = essential building = Siman 85 cross-reference); second: drawn from higher face (Chag"t); third: Vayechulu in Kiddush → draws from Chab"d of Ze'ir Anpin = stories of ancient years (Chab"d = yemay kedem = ancient years) = therefore days and years lengthened (= rectifications of Atik = arichas yamim). [Parenthetical on kavannos: three times "Havu laHashem" at entry of Shabbos = 13 (gematria of Havu) = 13 rectifications of beard of Arich Anpin of Asiyah/Yetzirah/Beriyah = elevate Chab"d of Asiyah into Malchus of Yetzirah etc. = 13 rectifications of the beard = rectifications of Atik; in every world: seven traits (= seventy years = seventy facets) + Chab"d (= ancient years) + rectifications of the beard + Atik as such; illumination of Shabbos from Atik at very high level; through ascents of Shabbos → ascend from level to level until reach actual Atik = "v'Atika Kadisha gali retzoneh"; at Minchah of Shabbos: Ze'ir Anpin ascends to actual Dik'na (kavannos); Psalm 92: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fo'olecha b'ma'aseh yadecha aranen" = story-tellings = "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem me'od amku machshevosecha" = stories clothe the depth of thought = Chab"d/Kach"b = ancient years; Psalms 93:1: "Hashem Malach geo'us lavash" = garments of the faces of Torah or the ancient years; "Hashem l'orech yamim" (Psalms 93:5) = through all this: arichas yamim drawn.] Shabbos day: Ze'ir Anpin also ascends → seven readers (= seven traits = seventy facets); at Minchah: three readers (= Chab"d = kavannos) = ancient years = "v'rav chesed" → "va'ani tefilasi lecha Hashem et ratzon" = "v'Atika Kadisha gali retzoneh" at Minchah. "Elokim b'rav chasdecha aneini" = "rav chesed." Afterward: Ze'ir Anpin ascends to actual Dik'na; third meal: Atika is the One Who eats; Ze'ir Anpin eats from the mouth of Atika (kavannos) = actual rectifications of Atik drawn. One who awakens people from sleep must guard from unworthy students → evil should not attach. Remedy: teaching must be "lilmod v'lalamed lishmore v'la'asos" = as if one made his fellow into Torah (Sages from Deuteronomy 29:8). Then G-d guards that words should not be inscribed in memory of the unworthy student. "Nashim chayavos b'Kiddush hayom / zachor v'shamor / kol she'ishnu b'shmirah ishnu b'zechirah": Kiddush = awakening from sleep through stories of ancient years = Chab"d; Kiddush over wine = "v'cheichech k'yayin tov / dovev sifsey yeshenim" (Song of Songs 7:10; Likutay Halachos). Even women (fallen from all seventy facets, exempt from Torah study) = not in category of unworthy students, heaven forfend → must awaken them through ancient years = Kiddush. "Zachor v'shamor / kol she'ishnu b'shmirah" = those who truly want to receive the teaching to guard and do = included in remembering = teacher's words inscribed in their memory. Unworthy student = not in guarding = not in remembering = words forgotten. Therefore: no need to be concerned about engaging with simple people (= aspects of women) with these high-level stories. Truly unworthy student → words will certainly be forgotten = "ana alma b'charuva ashkachteh." "V'shamru Bnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" = as if one literally made the Shabbos (Sages) = "u'shemartem va'asitem osam." Teacher who draws illumination of Shabbos to students (for which students are obligated to receive the face of the teacher on Shabbos — kavannos) = also in this aspect: guard and do = as if he made the Shabbos and as if he made his students. Unworthy student who does not allow the teacher to make him → illumination of Shabbos withdraws from him. Zohar Yisro 88: "d'inun seudasi d'meheimanusah d'zara kadisha d'Yisrael d'meheimanusah ila'ah da d'lehon v'lo d'amim aku'm." "La'asos es haShabbas l'dorosaym" = birth and visiting of the barren = physical union; essential time for sacred union = Shabbos; allusion in "v'shamru Bnay Yisrael es haShabbas"; supernal root of Shabbos union = for drawing new souls (kavannos). Through awakening from sleep → "l'hatir peh ilemim."
 "V'daber davar" / speech / birth / Mo'ed Katan 28 / chayyay banay u'mezonay b'mazala talya / Chanah / "az tis'anag al Hashem" / Isaiah 58 synthesis / two thousand cubits = two teachings / fifty gates of Binah / all rectifications encompassed in "ki pi Hashem diber": "V'daber davar" = speech opens in great perfection on Shabbos (Zohar Bereishis 32). Through this → "l'hatir peh akros" = birth. "Ki koh amar Hashem la'sarisim asher yishmeru es Shabsosai / yad v'shem tov mibbanim u'mibbanos" = through Shabbos: visiting of the barren and birth in all Israel = counted as if he fathered them. "Hame'orer yeshenim — v'hamekitz nirdamim — v'hamashi'ach ilemim — u'matir asurim — v'hasomech noflim — v'hazokeif kefufim" (Midrash Rabbah, Vayetzei 71) = visiting of the barren. "To'amehah chayyim zachu" = speech opens on Shabbos = "eileh l'chayyay olam / l'nefesh chayyah l'ruach memalela." Mo'ed Katan 28a: "chayyay banay u'mezonay b'mazala talya" = supernal mazal in the holy Dik'na; this mazal shines most through Shabbos holiness = ascend to Dik'na = draw chayyay olam = "l'hatir peh ilemim" → visiting of barren → birth of children. "V'tispallel Chanah al Hashem — al Hashem davka" (Zohar Acharei 79). "Az tis'anag al Hashem" = stated concerning Shabbos. Through this: fear revealed → length of days → wealth. Isaiah 58: "raglecha" = lowest level people awaken through Shabbos holiness; regel = speech = "l'hatir peh ilemim"; birth of children = legs = "bera kara d'avuha" = "l'hatir peh akros"; revelation of fear = regel (LM Tinyana 4); wealth = regel. Literally: don't go beyond Shabbos boundary = two thousand cubits. Aleph = teaching; two aspects of teaching: (1) seventy years / seventy faces of Torah; (2) ancient years. Two thousand cubits of Shabbos boundary = these two teachings. Anyone who has not completely gone out from the boundary of holiness can receive sacred awakening through either of these two teachings on Shabbos. "Me'asos chafatzecha" = guard from weekday affairs = grip of foolishness = "lo yachphotz chesil b'sevunah"; on Shabbos = fifty gates of Binah opened = "bikaish Koheles limtzo divrey chefetz" (Sages) = contemplation. Wealth = chefetz = "v'chol chafatzecha lo yishvu vah" (only for the sake of contemplation, not for the wealth itself). Life and arichas yamim = "Melech chafetz b'chayyim" (Psalms 21:5). Fear = chefetz = "hachafetzim l'yir'ah es shimcha" (Nehemiah 1:11). Teaching people and awakening them = Chesed = chefetz = "ki chesed chafatzti" (Hosea 6:6). Awakening and opening of speech = "eileh l'chayyay olam" = chefetz = "hachafetz achphotz / ki im b'shuvo / v'chayah" = "Melech chafetz b'chayyim." Birth through sacred union = chefetz = "u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti" (Isaiah 56:4). Awakening through Torah = chefetz = "v'chefetz Hashem b'yado yitzlach" (Isaiah 53:10; Sages). Awakening through story-telling = "gedolim ma'asay Hashem derusim l'chol chaftzeihem" (Psalms 111:2) + "kol asher chafetz Hashem asah" (Psalms 115:3). "Call it delight" = Shabbos meals = lechem hapanim = holy face returned to person on Shabbos. "Honored" = garments of honor = face clothed = "ani b'tzedek echezeh panecha / tzedek lavashti." "Honor it / no large strides" = anger = mochin d'katnus = sleep = "lamah charah lecha v'lamah naflu fanecha"; "b'kerev shanim chayyayhu" = awakening from sleep → "b'rogez rachem tizkor" (Habakkuk 3:2). "Your affairs / speaking words" = blemish holy speech = "shmor pis'chei picha" (Micah 7:5). "Then delight" = Atika Kadisha = rectifications of Atik. "Heights of earth" = Chakla Tupichin = ascent of Malchus in three aspects = Neh"y/Chag"t/Chab"d = perfect fear in three aspects; saved from subjugation = Sitra Achra during weekdays = sleep = mochin d'katnus = "Sitra Achra that rests on a person during sleep" (Zohar); root: "v'tardema nafla al Avram" (Genesis 15:12) = "eimah chashecha gedolah" = Sages: subjugation of kingdoms = root of their grip = sleep/tardema = backs = mochin d'katnus. Parenthetical on shanayim mikra v'echad Targum: text = holy face; Targum = backs; "Targum" gematria = "tardema" (Ari z"l); "b'kerev shanim chayyayhu" = awakening from sleep = face; Sages: do not read "b'kerev shanim" but "b'karov shanim" = shanayim mikra (Siman 19, Tefillah l'Chavakuk cross-reference); Targum = sleep. When merit awakening from sleep → sleep itself encompassed in supernal holiness (= holiness of Shabbos sleep; sleep + awakening = building Malchus = fear: "vayikatz Yaakov mishenas'to davka… vayira vayomar mah nora"; "vayapel Hashem Elokim tardema al ha'adam" = Ari z"l kavannos of Rosh Hashanah; absence of speech during sleep → afterward speech goes forth with great power → visiting of barren → fear revealed); "hamashlem parashiyosav im hatzibur shanayim mikra v'echad Targum ma'arichin lo yamav v'shanosav" = through fear → length of days; must complete parasha before Shabbos meal (Tosafos); pertains to Shabbos meal = lechem hapanim; in particular: morning meal of Shabbos = seudata d'Atika Kadisha = rectifications of Atik drawn. "Yado teda" said to Avraham at the time of tardema; "v'gam es hagoy asher ya'avodu dan anochi / Rashi: arba malchiyos / v'acharay chen yetze'u b'rechush gadol" = through sleep and awakening (= exiles and redemption) → fear revealed = "u'vemora'im gedolim / vayiru ha'am"; sacred wealth flows → contemplation of Torah. Perhaps: admonition to take Egyptian silver and gold = preparation for Torah (Zohar Mikeitz 196). "Heritage of Yaakov" = Ze'ir Anpin; Adra Nassa 138: "man fo'alaych Ze'ir Anpin — b'kerev shanim — inun shanim kadmoniyos — chayyayhu / l'Ze'ir Anpin — d'chol nehiru dilei mei'inun panim isakimu." Seventy faces of Torah = Ze'ir Anpin (seven traits); ancient years = Atik = Zaken = hadras panim; Ze'ir Anpin = heritage of Yaakov = "Torah tzivvah lanu Moshe morasha kehillas Yaakov"; "mevakshay fanecha Yaakov selah." Nachalah b'li metzarim = ascends and receives from ancient years (above boundaries and traits) → draws vitality to all levels → even those who fell from all seventy faces. Zohar introduction folio 7: "v'chol man d'itkashar b'inun shanim kadmoniyos chayyay itkashru bei / Yaakov avinu lo mes / b'kerev shanim todi'a l'ha'i darga d'leis bei chayyay klal." Sages: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov = nachalah b'li metzarim." Isaiah 56: even sons of the stranger can draw close through Shabbos. Three meals = Eden/Nahar/Gan = "v'nahar yotzei mei'Eden l'hashkos es haGan." "Ki pi Hashem diber" = through Shabbos = awakening from sleep = all rectifications → holy speech opens; all rectifications encompassed in the holiness of the speech of awakening from sleep = through showing the holy face = "panim b'fanim diber Hashem imachem" → speech opens = "petach picha l'ilem" → visiting of barren = "v'Hashem pakad es Sarah ka'asher amar" (Genesis 21:1); fear revealed = "hayarei es dvar Hashem" (Siman 15 cross-reference); length of days = "u'vadavar hazeh ta'arichuimim" (Deuteronomy 32:47); wealth = "v'Hashem beirach es Avraham b'chol" (Genesis 24:1); blessing = "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem / birchas Hashem hi sa'ashir" → contemplation of Torah → "mipiv da'as u'sevunah" (Proverbs 2:6). All the aforementioned aspects are encompassed in "ki pi Hashem diber."
 

 Siman 61 (Chadi Rabbi Shimon) continues in the next installment.

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman

Yikara DiShabsa — Siman 61: Chadi Rabbi Shimon

 Yikara DiShabsa · יקרא דשבתא
 Siman 61 — Chadi Rabbi Shimon

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 61 — סימן סא
 Chadi Rabbi Shimon — "Rabbi Shimon rejoiced…"
 [Likutay Moharan I, Siman 61]

 Translator's note: This siman contains four embedded teachings: Siman 61 proper (translated here), followed by Simanim 62, 63, and 64, which will be translated in the following installments. The source text of Siman 61 begins with a cross-reference to Siman 57, where the connection between Shabbos and faith in the Sages was first established. The entire siman is a deeply unified teaching centered on emunas chachamim, the rectification of judgment, the Oral Torah, and the sanctity of holy books — all rooted in and flowing from the holiness of Shabbos.

 It has been explained above in this treatise
 in Siman 57
 that on Shabbos there is drawn
 the aspect of the rectification of
 faith in the Sages [emunah chachamim] —
 and therefore through this
 our judgment [mishpat] goes forth to light —
 and one merits the rectification of judgment —
 for this is the aspect of [Ezekiel 20:19–20]:
 "v'es mishpatai shamru va'asu osam —
 v'es Shabsosai kidashu
 [and My judgments they guarded and did —
 and My Shabbosim they sanctified]"
 — for Shabbos is likewise the aspect of judgment —
 the central column [amuda d'emtza'isa] —
 that adjudicates between right and left.
 For this is the aspect of what is brought
 in Tikkun 19, folio 40 side 2:
 "terin dra'in — Gedullah u'Gevurah —
 T' — Tiferes
 [two arms — Greatness and Might —
 Tav — Tiferes],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And this is likewise the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught:
 "revi'i — chamishi — shishi —
 kodem haShabbas.
 Rishon — sheni — shelishi —
 hem b'ser Shabbasa
 [the fourth — the fifth — the sixth —
 are before Shabbos.
 The first — the second — the third —
 are after Shabbos]"
 — and as also understood in
 Megillas Amukos, Ofan 249.
 And therefore Shabbosim were given
 only for words of Torah —
 for then is the essential perfection of the learning —
 to derive from it true judgments
 and upright practices —
 each one according to his level.
 For the essential judgment [mishpat]
 comes through the mind [moach].
 And the mind is according to the nourishment —
 as explained within.

segments.he:
סימן קג-עזי וזמרת 
שבת הוא בחינת תשובה כנ"ל כמה פעמים ועיקר התשובה תולה בתורה כמבואר בפנים. והכל מודים כי בשבת ניתנה תורה ואז עיקר הזמן של חידושי תורה כנ"ל כמה פעמים. ועל ידי זה נתקבצין האותיות והניצוצות שנתפזר על ידו. וזה בחינת עליית הניצוצות בשלימות שעולין על ידי קדושת שבת כידוע.
segments.en:
And therefore on Shabbos —
 when then is the essential perfection of the mental faculties —
 as mentioned above many times —
 and likewise then the eating and the nourishment
 is entirely holy —
 as explained within in Siman 57 mentioned above —
 and then is also drawn
 the aspect of the rectification of faith in the Sages
 in its perfection —
 through all of which one merits
 the rectification of judgment.
 And therefore the one being ordained [hanismach] —
 who must receive ordination [semichah] from the true teacher —
 in order to receive through this
 the spirit of wisdom —
 so that through this he should be able
 to judge and guide Israel
 through true judgments and upright practices —
 therefore it is most propitious
 to receive ordination from him
 on the holy Shabbos.
 For this is the aspect of what Yehoshua
 received ordination from Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him,
 on the holy Shabbos —
 as it is written in Parashas Ha'azinu:
 "vayavo Moshe vayedaber —
 v'chol haggid —
 hu v'Hoshea ven Nun
 [and Moshe came and spoke —
 and so on —
 he and Hoshea the son of Nun]"
 — and Rashi explained:
 "Shabbas shel diyuzgey hayah —
 he'emid lo Moshe turgeiman l'Yehoshua
 she'yihyeh doresh b'chayyav
 [it was a Shabbos of public address —
 Moshe established for him an interpreter for Yehoshua
 who would expound in his lifetime],"
 and so on —
 for this is the aspect of the ordination —
 as Rashi explained in Parashas Pinchas.
 And also — through the holiness of Shabbos —
 the strength of our handwriting [kesav yadeinu] is fortified —
 for the hand that writes
 is the aspect of Tiferes —
 as explained in the Tikunim.
 And likewise the pen and the quill
 are also the aspect of Tiferes —
 and the parchment and the paper
 are the aspect of Malchus.
 (And see in the Pardes, in the entries of the appellations.)
 And the root of the letters
 is in Chochmah —
 as explained within.
 And this itself is the aspect of the holy Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of Malchus —
 and is drawn at its root
 from the aspect of Kodesh
 which is the aspect of Chochmah —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "u'shemartem es haShabbas —
 ki kodesh hi
 [and you shall guard the Shabbos —
 for it is holy]"
 [Exodus 31:14] —
 and as explained in the writings.
 And this is likewise the aspect of
 Shabbas ila'ah and Shabbas d'yoma
 and Shabbas d'leila
 explained in the holy Zohar.
 And this itself is likewise the aspect of faith in the Sages —
 through the fact that
 the illumination of the holiness of wisdom
 is drawn upon the faith —
 which is the aspect of Malchus —
 and as explained elsewhere.
 And perhaps this is the aspect of what the Sages of blessed memory
 counted among the things created
 on Erev Shabbos at twilight [bein hashmashos]:
 the writing [kesav] and the inscription [michtav]
 and the tablets [luchos] —
 and as Rashi explained [Tractate Pesachim 54]:
 the kesav is the form of the letters —
 and the michtav is the pen and the stylus, and so on —
 that is, the three aforementioned aspects.
 (And although the tablets are the aspects of Netzach and Hod —
 nonetheless there is a way to reconcile this —
 and as understood in the Pardes
 and in the writings of the holy Ari z"l.)
 And this is the aspect of:
 "u'shney luchos avanim horid b'yado —
 v'chasuv bahem shmiyas Shabbas
 [and two stone tablets he brought down in his hand —
 and written on them the guarding of Shabbos],"
 and so on. [וכו']

 And also — through the holiness of Shabbos
 is drawn the holiness of the Land of Israel.
 For the holiness of the Land of Israel
 is drawn from the holy Shabbos —
 and the extra soul of Shabbos
 is called the Land of Israel —
 the holy soil [admas kodesh] —
 as explained in Tikkun Heh
 of the final Tikunim —
 and as mentioned above many times.
 And therefore through the guarding of the holy Shabbos —
 and each person establishes rest [shevisah] in his place —
 through this the holiness of the Land of Israel
 is drawn upon that place —
 and then one cannot be expelled
 or driven from one's place —
 and Israel are saved from the decree of exile.
 And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]:
 "shvu ish tachtav —
 v'al yetzei ish mimekomo
 [let each person remain in his place —
 let no person go out from his place]"
 — that they should not need to be driven out
 and expelled from their places, heaven forfend —
 as mentioned above.

 And this is the aspect of [Ezekiel 20:23–24]:
 "v'lizros osam ba'aratzos ya'an —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'es Shabsosai chilelu
 [and to scatter them among the lands — because —
 and so on —
 and My Shabbosim they desecrated]."
 And because the holiness of the Land of Israel
 is drawn from the holiness of Shabbos —
 when one blemishes, heaven forfend, in the holiness of Shabbos —
 through this the nations conquer the Land of Israel
 and expel Israel from there.
 For this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught:
 "lo charevah Yerushalayim ela al she'chilellu vah es haShabbas —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'al she'bizzu vah Talmidey Chachamim
 [Jerusalem was destroyed only because they desecrated
 the Shabbos in it —
 and so on —
 and because they disgraced scholars in it]"
 — that is, they blemished faith in the Sages
 (which is also completed through the holiness of Shabbos —
 as mentioned above)
 — and through this
 the strength of our handwriting was also weakened —
 and they gave force to their writing.
 And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught —
 and it is also brought in Shulchan Aruch,
 Orach Chayyim, Siman 306:
 "konin battim me'aku'm b'Shabbas
 b'Eretz Yisrael —
 v'choteim u'ma'aleh b'arkaosaihem
 [one may acquire houses from a non-Jew on Shabbos
 in the Land of Israel —
 and one signs and registers in their courts],"
 and so on —
 and this was permitted on account of
 the settlement of the Land of Israel [yishuv Eretz Yisrael].
 For through the act
 of removing the holiness of the Land of Israel
 from the hand of the non-Jew
 and returning it to the hand of Israel —
 and specifically through the power
 of their writings and their legal documents —
 through this specifically
 one returns the power of our handwriting
 that had fallen among them
 through the blemish of judgment —
 which flows from the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 which is the aspect of a blemish
 in the holiness of the holy Shabbos —
 and then is drawn the aspect of:
 "la'asos bahem mishpat kasuv
 [to execute upon them the written judgment]"
 — and as explained within.

 And also — through the holiness of Shabbos —
 Israel merits the secret of intercalation [sod ha'ibur] —
 of which it is stated [Deuteronomy 4:6]:
 "ki hi chochmasechem u'vinasechem l'einay ha'amim
 [for it is your wisdom and your understanding
 in the eyes of the peoples]"
 — who display the wisdom
 only before their eyes —
 so that they should know
 that this secret is with us —
 without making known to them
 the essential secret of the wisdom —
 and so on —
 as explained within.
 For our Sages of blessed memory taught
 [Tractate Beitzah 16a]:
 "kol hamitzvos nitnu l'Yisrael b'farheisya —
 v'Shabbas nitnah lahem b'tzin'ah —
 shene'emar beini u'vein Bnay Yisrael —
 v'chol haggid —
 i hachi — lo liy'anash aku'm aleha.
 Shabbas ode'inhu — matan scharah lo ode'inhu —
 ibba'is eima —
 v'chol haggid —
 neshamah yetaira — lo ode'inhu
 [all the commandments were given to Israel openly —
 and Shabbos was given to them in privacy —
 as it is stated: between Me and the children of Israel —
 and so on —
 if so — why should the nations not be punished for it?
 Shabbos We informed them of —
 its reward We did not inform them of —
 if you wish to say —
 and so on —
 the extra soul — We did not inform them of it]."
 And also it is known that the holiness of Shabbos
 flows from Chochmah and Binah —
 for this is the aspect of ki kodesh hu —
 and as explained in the writings.
 It follows that the holiness of Shabbos
 is in the aspect of:
 "ki hi chochmasechem u'vinasechem l'einay ha'amim"
 — "l'einay ha'amim
 [in the eyes of the peoples]"
 — specifically — as mentioned above.
 For although they know something
 of the holiness of Shabbos —
 but the essential holiness of Shabbos
 was given in privacy and in secret —
 only to Israel alone —
 and was not made known to the nations — as mentioned above.

 For the essential movements of the celestial spheres
 are also drawn from the holiness of Shabbos —
 as mentioned above in this treatise in Siman 31.
 In particular — as explained here:
 since the spheres are governed
 by intellects [sichliim]
 which are the angels, and so on —
 and all these intellects receive
 from the overall Governor —
 which is the soul [neshamah]
 that flows intellect into them —
 in the aspect of [Job 32:8]:
 "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam
 [and the breath of Shadai gives them understanding]."
 And all of them are governed through it.
 And therefore the great souls
 are expert in the secret of intercalation
 and the movements of the celestial spheres —
 for who knows the management better
 than the manager?
 And it is known that Shabbos is the source
 of all souls —
 in the aspect of:
 "Shabbas vayinafash
 [He rested and was refreshed]"
 — as explained in the holy Zohar
 and in Sefer haBahir.
 And Shabbos is the aspect of Shadai —
 as is well-known — and as mentioned above many times.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "v'nishmas Shadai — davka —
 tvinam
 [and the breath of Shadai — specifically —
 gives them understanding]"
 — for the soul receives
 from the aspect of Shadai — the aspect of Shabbos —
 and flows wisdom and understanding
 to the intellects —
 which are the angels
 that govern the celestial spheres.
 (And see something like this in
 Bris Menuchah, Derech Vav,
 in the secret of [Psalms 80:14]:
 "and the boar from the forest ravages it,"
 and so on.)
 And the essential illumination of the soul
 in its ultimate perfection
 is on the holy Shabbos —
 for this is the aspect of the extra soul
 which each person merits according to his level.
 And through this Israel merit
 the secret of intercalation [sod ha'ibur]
 and the sanctification of the new month [kiddush hachodesh]
 and the calculation of the seasons and the constellations [cheshbon tekufos u'mazalos]
 in their perfection.
 And therefore it is juxtaposed:
 "u'veyom haShabbas
 [and on the day of Shabbos]"
 [Numbers 28:9] —
 next to the matter of:
 "u'vera'ashay chodsheichem
 [and at the beginnings of your months]"
 [Numbers 28:11] —
 and likewise in several places
 Shabbos is juxtaposed to the new month —
 and as also explained from this in the holy Zohar.
 For the essential fixing of the month
 and the intercalation of the year
 is drawn through the holiness of Shabbos.
 And the essential fixing
 of all the festivals and appointed times
 depends also on the aforementioned
 secret of intercalation.
 And therefore Shabbos is the beginning
 of the holy convocations [techilah l'mikra'ay kodesh].
 And the spheres are called shamayim [heavens] —
 as explained within.

 And this is the aspect of:
 "haShomayim mesaprim
 [the heavens declare],"
 and so on —
 [Psalms 19:2]
 recited on Shabbos —
 and as explained in the holy Zohar —
 and brought above in Siman 56.

 That the heavens —
 at their supernal root —
 receive a new illumination
 and a supernal radiance [nitzutzu ila'ah]
 on the holy Shabbos —
 as mentioned above.
 And because these souls
 must have pure and holy bodies —
 that should be formed
 from the aspect of:
 "avira d'Eretz Yisrael machkim
 [the air of the Land of Israel makes one wise]"
 — and therefore the essential time
 for the holiness of the sacred union
 is on Shabbos.
 And through this
 one draws holy souls to one's children —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 For the generative drop [tipah zar'iyis]
 is then pure and holy —
 in the aspect of the Land of Israel —
 through the holiness of the holy Shabbos.
 And then the body
 that is formed from this drop
 can receive a great and bright soul —
 and through this one merits to know
 from the secret of intercalation —
 as explained within.

 And also — through the holiness of Shabbos
 one merits complete counsel —
 for [Proverbs 20:5]:
 "mayim amukkim etzah b'lev ish —
 v'ish tevunos yidlenah
 [counsel in the heart of a person is like deep water —
 and a person of understanding draws it out]."
 And Shabbos is the aspect of the heart —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And it is also the aspect of the world of souls —
 and then each person merits the extra soul —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam"
 — and through this
 one's counsel is rectified —
 in the aspect of:
 "v'ish tevunos yidlenah
 [and a person of understanding draws it out]."
 And through the blemish of faith in the Sages
 and the blemish of the desecration of Shabbos —
 heaven forfend —
 through this the counsel is blemished.
 For the filth of the waste products
 rises to the heart —
 in the aspect of [Ezekiel 14:3]:
 "he'elu giluleichem al libam
 [they raised their idols upon their hearts]"
 — as explained within —
 and this is what is written [Ezekiel 20:16]:
 "v'es Shabsosai chilelu —
 ki acharay giluleichem libam holech
 [and My Shabbosim they desecrated —
 for after their idols their heart goes]."
 And because dispute [machloket]
 is the aspect of May Merivah
 [the Waters of Contention] —
 and it is the aspect of pure waters
 that purify from this filth and from the waste products —
 therefore it is stated [Nehemiah 13:17]:
 "va'arivah es choray Yehudah —
 va'omar lahem: mah hadavar hara hazeh asher atem osim —
 u'mechallelim es yom haShabbas
 [and I contended with the nobles of Judah —
 and said to them: what is this evil thing
 that you are doing —
 and desecrating the day of Shabbos],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And perhaps this was also the cause
 of the decrees that the nations decreed many times
 to desecrate the Shabbos, heaven forfend —
 and this was the aspect of a dispute with Israel
 over the matter of the guarding of Shabbos —
 and Israel sacrificed themselves for this —
 and guarded the Shabbos specifically
 with extraordinary self-sacrifice [mesiyas nefesh] —
 as our Sages of blessed memory taught.
 And this was the aspect of
 the counterbalancing repentance [teshuvah hamishkal]
 for the blemish of desecration of Shabbos.
 And therefore it is explained in the kavannos
 that even now one must intend —
 in the words:
 "v'al menuchasam yekadshu es Shimcha
 [and through their rest they shall sanctify Your Name]"
 — to accept upon oneself at that moment
 self-sacrifice.

 And this is the aspect of:
 "yakiru vanecha v'yeid'u —
 ki mei'itcha hi menuchasam
 [your children shall recognize and know —
 that from You is their rest],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 For just as through the dispute
 one must awaken to repentance
 for the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 and through this
 the holy books composed by the Sages —
 which are the aspect of the Oral Torah —
 become increasingly precious in one's eyes —
 so too: all that the Sitra Achra stands, heaven forfend,
 against the holiness of Shabbos —
 whether in general
 through the decrees of the nations, heaven forfend,
 as mentioned above —
 or in particular —
 when a circumstance arises, heaven forfend,
 that could lead one to desecration of Shabbos
 (and not on account of danger to life, heaven forfend)
 — then one must awaken
 and stand against them
 in the aspect of self-sacrifice —
 and pay them no heed —
 but on the contrary:
 to awaken through this
 to truly return [lashub b'emes]
 for having blemished, heaven forfend,
 the holiness of Shabbos at any time —
 and through this
 the holiness of Shabbos becomes
 even more precious in one's eyes —
 and one merits to taste and to know
 and to feel from the inner dimension
 of the holiness of Shabbos even more —
 in the aspect of:
 "yakiru vanecha v'yeid'u —
 ki mei'itcha hi menuchasam"
 — and it is explained in the kavannos:
 "mei'atcha — kaf
 [from You — the letter Kaf]"
 — which is the aspect of Keser —
 that is their rest.
 And this: "v'al menuchasam yekadshu es Shimcha"
 — as mentioned above.

 And behold — it was explained above in Siman 57
 in the name of the holy Zohar
 that Shabbos is the aspect of the Oral Torah.
 And therefore through the fact
 that the holiness of Shabbos
 becomes increasingly precious in one's eyes each time —
 through which the aspect of faith in the Sages
 is also completed —
 as mentioned above —
 through this the aspect of the Oral Torah
 is completed even more —
 and holy books of the aspect of the Oral Torah
 are multiplied — without end.

segments.he: וגם על ידי קדושת שבת נשלם הדעת שזה בחינת לדעת כי אני ה' מקדשכם ועל ידי זה מתעורר רחמנות שזה בחינת יכולה היא שתרחם האמור בשבת קדש (וכמובא לקמן בפנים סימן קי"ט) וכן ורחמיו מרובים וכו' ועל ידי זה זוכין להמשיך גם כן בחינת רחמים גדולים על ידי תפלת השם יתברך בעצמו כביכול ואז זוכין לישועה שלימה כמבואר בפנים. וזה שאמרו רז"ל אלמלי שמרו ישראל שתי שבתות מיד נגאלין שנאמר אשר ישמרו את שבתותי וסמיך ליה והביאותים אל הר קדשי ושימחתים בבית תפלתי היינו כנ"ל. כי שבת הוא בחינת רחמים בחינת יכולה היא שתרחם כנ"ל.
segments.en:
And there are Tzadikim
 who did not blemish, heaven forfend, in faith in the Sages —
 and also did not blemish, heaven forfend,
 in the holiness of Shabbos —
 and yet even upon them
 comes the aspect of the aforementioned dispute.
 And this is in the aspect of [Isaiah 53:12]:
 "v'hu chet rabim nassa
 [and he bore the sin of the many],"
 and so on —
 as explained within.
 And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:27]:
 "vayehi vayom hashevi'i —
 yatze'u min ha'am lilkot —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayomer Hashem el Moshe:
 ad anah me'anem lishmor mitzvosai v'Sorosai
 [and it was on the seventh day —
 some of the people went out to gather —
 and so on —
 and Hashem said to Moshe:
 until when do you refuse to guard My commandments and My Torahs]"
 — and He included even Moshe among them —
 as our Sages of blessed memory taught:
 "badi hutza laki krava
 [with the thorn — the cabbage was struck]"
 — as mentioned above.
 And this is why the verse specified:
 "v'Sorosai
 [and My Torahs]"
 — in the manner that our Sages of blessed memory expounded
 [Tractate Yoma 28b]:
 "kiyem Avraham avinu afilu eiruv tavshilin —
 shene'emar:
 v'shomar mishmarti —
 v'chol haggid —
 Sorosai.
 Achas Torah she'b'chtav —
 v'achas Torah she'b'al peh
 [our Patriarch Avraham observed even the law of eruv tavshilin —
 as it is stated:
 and he guarded My charge —
 and so on —
 My Torahs.
 One — the Written Torah —
 and one — the Oral Torah]."
 That is — for the holiness of Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the perfection
 of the Oral Torah — as mentioned above —
 through this also the Written Torah is completed.
 And therefore our Sages expounded
 [Midrash Rabbah, Beshalach, section 25]
 on this very verse itself —
 in Torah, Prophets, and Writings —
 that Shabbos is equivalent
 to the entire Torah and all the commandments —
 and as brought in the words of the Sages
 in many places —
 and especially in the holy Zohar.

 And sometimes the aspect of the aforementioned dispute
 comes even upon one who did not blemish at all
 in the holiness of Shabbos —
 and likewise in faith in the Sages.
 But only that the holiness of his Shabbos observance
 was not sufficiently precious in his own eyes.
 And although it seems to him on the contrary —
 that this is because he believes very much
 in the greatness of the holiness of Shabbos —
 and he knows that there are Tzadikim
 and people of attainment
 who merit to feel the holiness of Shabbos
 at an exceedingly great and elevated level —
 therefore it seems to him
 that he is very far from the inner dimension
 of the holiness of Shabbos —
 and it is not sufficiently precious in his eyes.
 But in truth this itself is counted as a blemish
 in the holiness of Shabbos.
 For on the contrary —
 the holiness of Shabbos is so exalted
 that it encompasses
 from the very top of all levels
 to the very bottom of all levels —
 and anyone who is careful
 in the holiness of Shabbos observance properly —
 in the most straightforward simplicity —
 and fulfills the delight and honor of Shabbos —
 even if he has no attainment whatsoever —
 certainly happy is he and happy is his portion —
 and he must rejoice greatly and delight in it greatly —
 and as elaborated on this at great length
 in the holy Zohar.

 And therefore one is obligated
 to produce Torah novellae [chidushay Torah] on Shabbos —
 as explained in the holy Zohar —
 for then the Oral Torah is completed —
 from which is the source of all Torah novellae —
 for in the Written Torah
 it is forbidden to add to it even one letter —
 and the essential addition of Torah novellae
 that are added and renewed at every time —
 in the aspect of [Proverbs 5:19]:
 "dadeha yarvucha b'chol eis
 [her breasts shall satisfy you at every time]"
 — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded —
 all of this is within the category
 of the Oral Torah.
 And this is likewise within the category
 of the proliferation of holy books
 that are multiplied through the holiness of Shabbos —
 that is, through the Torah novellae
 that are renewed each and every Shabbos
 by each person according to his level —
 and one must believe in them
 and they must be precious in one's eyes —
 even if one produces some novellum —
 however small it may be.
 And this too is within the framework of faith in the Sages —
 provided that one's intention is for the sake of Heaven —
 and that the novellum should be built
 on a true foundation —
 from the holy foundations
 that our holy teachers of blessed memory
 established for us in their holy books —
 which are the essential Oral Torah —
 and as elaborated on this elsewhere.
 But nonetheless —
 even one who is not capable of this
 and cannot produce Torah novellae at all —
 nonetheless let his heart not fall —
 and let him too receive the holiness of Shabbos
 with great joy —
 and let him believe that his holiness of Shabbos too
 is high and precious —
 and makes a great impression
 in all the worlds.
 And perhaps through his holiness of Shabbos
 his fellow merits to produce Torah novellae
 and to compose holy books.
 It follows that he too has a share in them —
 in particular one who merits
 to support Torah scholars
 and to be of those who sustain the Torah in truth.
 And he himself should also study
 some new thing in the Torah on Shabbos —
 whatever he is capable of —
 or at the very least:
 let him awaken on every Shabbos
 with a new awakening and new desire
 for the holy Torah —
 and this too is the aspect of Torah novellae —
 as explained below within in Siman 159.
 And this is what [Isaiah 56:2] states:
 "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos —
 u'ven adam yachazik bah
 [happy is the person who does this —
 and the son of man who holds fast to it]."
 And our Sages expounded:
 the Holy One, blessed be He,
 will in the future make a shade and a canopy
 for those who fulfill commandments
 (that is, those of charity and those who sustain the Torah)
 alongside those who labor in Torah, and so on.
 And it is written:
 "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos —
 u'ven adam yachazik bah —
 v'chasuv etz chayyim hi lamachazikim bah
 [happy is the person who does this —
 and the son of man who holds fast to it —
 and it is written:
 it is a tree of life for those who hold fast to it]."
 And also our Sages expounded
 [Tractate Shabbos 118b]:
 "kol hashomer Shabbas kehilcheso —
 afilu oved avodah zarah k'dor Enosh —
 mochalin lo —
 shene'emar: ashrey enosh —
 v'chol haggid —
 shomer Shabbas mechalelo
 [all who guard the Shabbos according to its law —
 even if he worshipped idolatry like the generation of Enosh —
 he is forgiven —
 as it is stated: happy is the person —
 and so on —
 a Shabbos guardian who does not desecrate it]."
 And likewise our Sages expounded
 [Midrash Rabbah, Beshalach, section 25]:
 "im shomer adam es haShabbas —
 k'ilu shomar kol hamitzvos —
 shene'emar: shomer Shabbas mechalelo —
 v'shomer yado me'asos kol ra
 [if a person guards the Shabbos —
 it is as if he guarded all the commandments —
 as it is stated: a Shabbos guardian who does not desecrate it —
 and he who guards his hand from doing any evil]."

 And from all the above it is understood
 how the verse comes to strengthen the person —
 to be very careful to believe
 in the great excellence
 of the preciousness of the holiness
 of guarding the holy Shabbos —
 even if the person himself is as he is.
 For even if he is not a Torah scholar —
 and Shabbosim were given only for words of Torah —
 nonetheless — if he holds fast
 to the Torah scholars —
 he has a share too in their Torah —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "u'ven adam yachazik bah"
 — as mentioned above.
 And even if he actually sinned, heaven forfend —
 and even if he worshipped idolatry
 like the generation of Enosh —
 let him believe that if he repents —
 certainly through the holiness of Shabbos
 everything will be forgiven him —
 as mentioned above.

 And likewise let him believe
 that the guarding of Shabbos
 is equivalent to all the commandments —
 as mentioned above.
 And this:
 "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos —
 v'chol haggid —
 shomer Shabbas."

 For the prophet came to make known
 to the Shabbos observer
 that he should know
 that happy is he and happy is his portion in this —
 so that the holiness of Shabbos
 should have great importance in the eyes of the person —
 for this is the essential matter —
 as understood within —
 and also regarding faith in the Sages —
 as mentioned above.
 And this:
 "v'al yomar ben haneychar —
 v'chol haggid —
 havdel yavdileni Hashem mei'al amo
 [and let not the son of the stranger say —
 and so on —
 Hashem will surely separate me from His people]"
 — as our Sages of blessed memory taught
 [in the aforementioned Midrash Rabbah, Beshalach]:
