 "ki Hashem natan lachem haShabbas —
 lachem nitna v'lo l'aku'm —
 ki aku'm she'shavas chayav misah
 [for Hashem has given you the Shabbos —
 it was given to you and not to the nations —
 for a non-Jew who rests is liable to death]."
 And the evil inclination wishes
 to weaken a person's confidence —
 so that the holiness of his Shabbos observance
 should not be precious in his eyes —
 on account of his lowliness
 and his low level —
 and it finds a different pretext for each person
 according to his aspect —
 in order to weaken his confidence in this matter.
 And therefore the prophet came
 to nullify this matter —
 and made known that although Shabbos was given
 only to Israel — as mentioned above —

 nonetheless —
 even the son of the stranger
 who has drawn close to the holiness of Israel —
 his Shabbos observance too
 is precious in G-d's eyes, blessed be He —
 and as a reward for this:
 "v'hevi'osim el har kodshi
 [and I shall bring them to My holy mountain]"
 — and he too shall have a share
 in the drawing close of the redemption
 that will come through the merit
 of the guarding of the holy Shabbos —
 and as our Sages expounded.
 And likewise:
 "v'al yomar hasaris:
 hen ani etz yavesh
 [and let not the saris say:
 behold — I am a dry tree]"
 — for on the holy Shabbos
 the aspect of the birth of new souls is drawn —
 as explained in the writings.
 And therefore through the union of Shabbos
 one draws holy souls to one's children —
 and one merits holy children —
 Torah scholars and Tzadikim —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 For this is likewise the aspect
 of the proliferation of holy books —
 and as explained elsewhere.
 And therefore the saris
 has a weakness of confidence [chalishes hada'as]
 in the holy Shabbos —
 since he is a dry tree
 and cannot produce fruit.
 And for our purposes here —
 as explained in the holy Zohar —
 one must be fruitful and multiply —
 to produce fruit in words of Torah —
 that is: to produce novellae in them at every time —
 and if not — one is in the aspect of a dry tree.
 And it is even more propitious
 to produce novellae in Torah on the holy Shabbos —
 and therefore one who is not capable of this —
 and cannot be fruitful and multiply in Torah —
 even on Shabbos —
 has a great weakness of confidence —
 and says:
 "hen ani etz yavesh
 [behold — I am a dry tree]"
 — since even on Shabbos
 he does not merit to produce novellae in Torah.

 And the prophet strengthens him:
 "ki choh amar Hashem la'sarisim —
 asher yishmeru es Shabsosai —
 u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti
 [for so says Hashem to the sarisim —
 who guard My Shabbosim —
 and choose that which I desire]"
 — that is, that they should have at the very least
 a new and strong desire [cheshek chadash v'chazak]
 for the holy Torah —
 which is the essential desire of G-d, blessed be He —
 as our Sages expounded:
 "chaftzecha v'chafti lo yishvu vah
 [your desires and My desire are not comparable to it]."
 And it is the aspect of:
 "v'chefetz Hashem b'yado yitzlach
 [and the desire of Hashem shall prosper in his hand]"
 — as our Sages expounded.
 And this:
 "u'machzikim b'vrisi
 [and they hold fast to My covenant]"
 — that is, they should be those who sustain the Torah
 and hold fast to it at the very least.
 "v'nasati lahem b'veisi u'v'chomasai —
 yad v'shem tov mibbanim u'mibbanos
 [and I shall give them in My house and within My walls —
 a hand and a good name —
 better than sons and daughters]."
 That is — for the sarisim who are truly unable to father children —
 nonetheless through Shabbos observance
 they have a share in the drawing forth of new souls
 and in the birth of holy children
 of the other Israelites.
 And likewise — the simple people
 who are unable to produce novellae in Torah on Shabbos —
 nonetheless through their Shabbos observance
 they have a share in the Torah novellae
 of the Torah scholars —
 especially when they merit to support them —
 as mentioned above.
 And this:
 "shem olam etein lo
 [an everlasting name I shall give him],"
 and so on —
 and our Sages expounded
 [Tractate Sanhedrin 93b]:
 "zeh sefer Daniel she'nikra al shemo
 [this is the book of Daniel — that was named after him]"
 — that is, one merits that holy books multiply in the Torah
 even through him —
 as mentioned above.

 It follows that it is clearly explained:
 through the guarding of the holy Shabbos —
 holy books are made —
 which are the aspect of the Oral Torah.
 And also above —
 holy books are made
 from the Shabbos observance of every individual Israelite —
 for Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah.

 And our Sages of blessed memory taught —
 brought in the Maharil
 and in the holy Shelah:
 that every Motza'ay Shabbos [outgoing Shabbos]
 the prophet Eliyahu of blessed memory sits
 and writes the merits of Israel
 who observed the Shabbos.
 It follows that holy books are made
 from the holy Shabbos observance of Israel.
 And also — the Shabbos observers
 are called yirey Hashem [fearers of G-d] —
 as our Sages expounded
 on the verse [Malachi 3:20]:
 "v'zarechah lachem yiray shemi —
 shemesh tzedakah
 [and the sun of righteousness shall rise for you —
 who fear My Name]."
 And through the fact
 that each individual Israelite guards the Shabbos
 and receives its holiness
 according to his aspect —
 and they are encompassed in a single unity —
 and they radiate upon each other —
 as explained above in Siman 34 —
 this is the aspect of [Malachi 3:16]:
 "az nidveru yiray Hashem ish el re'ehu —
 vayakshuv Hashem vayishma —
 vayikatev sefer zikaron lefanav —
 l'yiray Hashem —
 v'l'choshvay shemo
 [then those who fear Hashem spoke —
 each one to his fellow —
 and Hashem listened and heard —
 and a book of remembrance was written before Him —
 for those who fear Hashem —
 and for those who esteem His Name]."
 And also in its plain meaning —
 this likewise alludes to the matter mentioned above —
 for:
 "az nidveru
 [then they spoke]"
 — its interpretation there —
 when they see the success of the wicked
 and the lowliness of the upright ones of the generation —
 which is likewise the aspect of dispute —
 the aspect of the divided heart [chelak libam].
 For the evil inclination incites the person
 to contemplate against His attributes, blessed be He,
 heaven forfend —
 then specifically the fearers of Hashem
 awaken to speak about this —
 not to attach themselves to the deeds of the wicked,
 heaven forfend —
 and not to entertain thoughts against His attributes, blessed be He.
 For this is the aspect of the awakening of repentance —
 to return for the blemish of faith
 that was caused by the dispute —
 and G-d, blessed be He,
 writes their words as a remembrance in the book —
 and a book is made from this above.
 And this is what concluded there afterward —
 with the reward of the Tzadikim
 who guard the Shabbos properly —
 as it is written there:
 "v'zarechah lachem yiray shemi,"
 and so on —
 and as our Sages expounded.
 And this:
 "vayikatev sefer zikaron —
 l'yiray Hashem —
 v'l'choshvay shemo."

 And "v'l'choshvay
 [and for those who esteem]"
 — specifically.
 That is — through the repentance —
 all the holy books become increasingly precious —
 as explained within.
 And this: "v'l'choshvay shemo
 [and for those who esteem His Name]"
 — "shem Hashem da sefer
 [the Name of Hashem — this is the book]"
 — as explained in the holy Zohar —
 and as brought in his words of blessed memory
 in Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 32.
 And in this is also implied the precise language of the Sages —
 who said:
 "afilu aved avodah zarah k'dor Enosh — mochalin lo
 [even if he worshipped idolatry like the generation of Enosh — he is forgiven]."
 For in the generation of Enosh
 they greatly blemished the Name of Hashem —
 as it is written [Genesis 4:26]:
 "az huchal likro b'shem Hashem
 [then it was begun — to call in the Name of Hashem]"
 — [meaning: to desecrate the Name] —
 and the essential cause was
 through the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 for then too there were Tzadikim of the generation —
 Adam and Shet [Seth], and so on —
 but they did not listen to their words
 and appointed leaders of the generation
 who were not worthy —
 until through this
 they came to actual idolatry —
 the aspect of:
 "he'elu giluleichem al libam
 [they raised their idols upon their hearts]"
 — as explained within.
 And then they greatly blemished
 the Name of Hashem —
 and therefore also the rectification was juxtaposed —
 as it is written immediately afterward [Genesis 5:1]:
 "zeh sefer toldos adam
 [this is the book of the generations of Adam]"
 — and on this it was expounded
 in Zohar Bereishis, folio 37:
 "shem Hashem da sefer
 [the Name of Hashem — this is the book],"
 and so on —
 for the Tzadikim of the generation
 were awakened specifically through this
 to rectify the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 through which holy books are multiplied —
 as mentioned above.

segments.he: וכשזוכין לשמור שתי שבתות היינו בחינת שבת תחתון ושבת עליון היינו שזוכין שהרחמים פשוטים מעוררין את הרחמים גדולים שזה בחינת תפלת ה' אז באה ישועה שלימה וזוכין לגאולת עולם. וזה בחינת ושימחתים בבית תפילתי שזה בחינת תפלת ה' כמו שדרשו רז"ל וכמובא גם בפנים.
segments.en:
And it is explained in the holy Zohar:
 "Shabbas shma d'Kudsha Berich Hu
 [Shabbos is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He]."
 And therefore — through the guarding of Shabbos —
 the holy books are also multiplied —
 for they are likewise the Name of Hashem —
 and therefore even one who worshipped idolatry
 like the generation of Enosh — is forgiven.
 And therefore the prophet also opened with this:
 "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos,"
 and so on —
 from which our Sages expounded:
 even if he worshipped idolatry
 like the generation of Enosh — he is forgiven.
 And he concluded:
 "shem olam etein lo,"
 and so on —
 and our Sages expounded:
 "zeh sefer Daniel she'nikra al shemo"
 — as mentioned above.
 And therefore he opened in the plural:
 "v'nasati lahem b'veisi u'v'chomasai,"
 and so on —
 and concluded in the singular:
 "shem olam etein lo,"
 and so on.
 (And as our teachers of blessed memory also noted this precisely
 in Sanhedrin mentioned above —
 and likewise in Zohar Yisro, folio 89.)
 For certainly the composers of the books themselves —
 that the book should be named after them literally —
 are in every generation
 only a few individuals.
 But in truth — in every single book
 there is a great share also for other people of Israel —
 as all the above [shows] —
 and as also understood in his words of blessed memory
 within in Siman 13 and in Siman 20
 and in Siman 192 and in other places.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "v'nasati lahem b'veisi u'v'chomasai —
 yad v'shem tov,"
 and so on —
 "bayis
 [house]"
 — this is the aspect of wisdom —
 as it is written [Proverbs 24:3]:
 "b'chochmah yibaneh bayis
 [through wisdom a house is built]"
 — and as explained above within in Siman 59 —
 and from there is the source of judgment —
 the aspect of [I Kings 3:28]:
 "ki chochmas Elokim b'kirbo la'asos mishpat
 [for the wisdom of G-d was in him to execute judgment]"
 — and as explained within.
 "Chomah
 [wall]"
 — this is the aspect of Malchus —
 the aspect of faith —
 as it is written [Song of Songs 8:10]:
 "ani chomah
 [I am a wall]"
 — that is, through the fact
 that they guard My Shabbosim —
 in the aspect of the two Shabbosim —
 that is: wisdom and faith —
 which is the aspect of faith in the Sages —
 through which judgment is rectified.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "es Shabsosai —
 da igula v'ribua d'lagu
 [My Shabbosim —
 this is the igul and ribua from within]"
 — that is, faith — the aspect of Malchus —
 which is the aspect of igul —
 as it is written [Psalms 89:3]:
 "v'emunascha savivosecha
 [and Your faithfulness around You]"
 — and as explained elsewhere —
 and ribua is the aspect of judgment
 (whose source is from the aspect of
 the rectification of the mental faculties and wisdom mentioned above)
 — and as also explained in Siman 59 mentioned above.
 And through this one merits
 the aspect of yad [hand] and shem [name].
 "Yad
 [hand]"
 — this is the aspect of the hands of ordination —
 which are the aspect of the drawing forth of wisdom —
 the aspect of:
 "maleh ru'ach chochmah —
 ki samach Moshe es yadav alav
 [filled with the spirit of wisdom —
 for Moshe laid his hands upon him]"
 [Deuteronomy 34:9] —
 and as explained within.
 And this is likewise the foundation
 of the entire Oral Torah —
 that was transmitted from generation to generation
 to the ordained Sages —
 for this is the foundation
 of the entire chain of tradition [shalsheles hakabbalah]
 of the Oral Torah —
 in the aspect of:
 "Moshe kibel Torah miSinai —
 u'masarah l'Yehoshua
 [Moshe received the Torah from Sinai —
 and transmitted it to Yehoshua],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And "shem
 [name]"
 — this is the aspect of the hands of writing [yedey haketivah] —
 as our Sages of blessed memory expounded
 [Tractate Megillah 10b]:
 "shem — zeh haktav
 [name — this is the writing],"
 and so on —
 that is, what strengthens our handwriting through this —
 as mentioned above.
 And this also alludes to the proliferation
 of holy books
 that are multiplied in every generation
 through faith in the Sages —
 through which the hands of ordination
 and the hands of writing are rectified —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "ketov zos zikaron b'sefer
 [write this as a memorial in the book]"
 [Exodus 17:14] —
 and our Sages expounded:
 this refers to the reading of the Megillah —
 for specifically through the fact
 that the husk of Haman-Amalek
 then stirred so greatly against them —
 through this Israel awakened in repentance —
 and yet another holy book was added to the Torah —
 which is the Scroll of Esther —
 and as elaborated on this in Likutay Halachos.
 And:
 "shem Hashem da sefer
 [the Name of Hashem — this is the book]."
 And therefore our Sages expounded
 [Tractate Megillah 10b]:
 "v'hayah laHashem l'shem —
 zeh mikra Megillah
 [and it shall be to Hashem as a Name —
 this is the reading of the Megillah]"
 — as mentioned above.
 And through the proliferation
 of the books of the holy Torah
 through the guarding of the holy Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the perfection of the Oral Torah —
 as mentioned above —
 the entire Torah is completed —
 and as explained within.

 And therefore then is the essential time
 for the reading of the Torah in its perfection.
 And therefore they read then:
 "shanayim mikra v'echad Targum
 [twice the text and once the Targum]."
 For the Targum is likewise within the category
 of the Oral Torah —
 as our Sages of blessed memory expounded.
 For the essential perfection of the Torah
 is through the Oral Torah.

 And this is the aspect of:
 "shanayim mikra
 [twice the text]"
 — the aspect of [Job 11:6]:
 "vayaged lecha ta'alumos chochmah —
 ki keflaim l'tushiyah
 [and He would tell you the secrets of wisdom —
 for they are double in their essence]"
 — that is, to indicate
 that the words of Torah are not literally as they appear alone —
 but there are many hidden things within them
 that were not written —
 only transmitted to the Sages orally.
 For:
 "oraissa meChochmah ila'ah nafkat
 [the Torah went forth from the supernal Wisdom]"
 — and it cannot receive from the supernal Wisdom
 except when it has completion —
 and the completion of the Torah
 is through the Oral Torah.
 And this is the aspect of shanayim mikra —
 to indicate:
 "ki keflaim l'tushiyah
 [for they are double in their essence]."
 And echad Targum
 is the aspect of the Oral Torah —
 as mentioned above —
 through which the Torah is completed
 and receives from the supernal Wisdom —
 in the aspect of:
 "vayaged lecha ta'alumos chochmah
 [and He would tell you the secrets of wisdom],"
 and so on — as mentioned above.
 And this is what it concluded:
 "v'da ki yasheh lecha Elo'ah mei'avonecha —
 v'Targumo:
 aram anshi lach Elaha mei'avayech
 [and know that G-d has exacted from you less than your sin —
 and its Targum:
 for G-d has forgotten your sins for you]"
 [Job 11:6] —
 that is, for through this the judgments are sweetened —
 as explained within.
 And through this
 the Holy One, blessed be He, as it were,
 makes Himself as if He has forgotten
 all one's sins —
 and bestows good upon one.
 And this is why it expanded afterward
 in praise of the Torah:
 "gahey shamayim mah tifal —
 v'chol haggid —
 aruchah me'aretz midah —
 u'rechavah miny yam
 [higher than the heavens — what can you do —
 and so on —
 it is longer than the earth in measure —
 and broader than the sea]"
 [Job 11:8–9] —
 for all of this is stated
 regarding the depth and the wonders
 that are in the Torah —
 encompassing everything —
 only in the Oral Torah —
 through which the Torah is completed —
 as mentioned above.

 And therefore on Shabbos
 all judgments are suppressed
 and do not stir at all —
 for through the holiness of Shabbos —
 faith in the Sages is rectified —
 and the Oral Torah is completed —
 which is the perfection of the entire Torah —
 and Shabbos itself is equivalent to the entire Torah.
 And see Zohar Yisro, folio 92 —
 where it is explained that the three levels
 that are in the holiness of Shabbos —
 "ilin inun klala v'raza d'chol oraissa —
 Torah — Nevi'im — u'Kesuvim
 [these are the general principle
 and the secret of the entire Torah —
 Torah — Prophets — and Writings]."
 And therefore in Torah, Prophets, and Writings
 we find that Shabbos is equivalent
 to the entire Torah and all the commandments.
 And then the Torah receives
 from the supernal Wisdom —
 which is the root of the Torah —
 for:
 "oraissa meChochmah ila'ah nafkat"
 — and it itself is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos —
 the aspect of ki kodesh hi
 [for it is holy] —
 as explained in the kavannos.
 And therefore everyone agrees
 that the Torah was given on Shabbos —
 and then the Torah is in the aspect
 of the stone tablets —
 as explained within.

 And this is the aspect of:
 "u'shney luchos avanim horid b'yado —
 v'chasuv bahem shmiyas Shabbas
 [and two stone tablets he brought down in his hand —
 and written on them the guarding of Shabbos]."
 And then the Torah receives
 from the supernal Wisdom —
 in the aspect of the Even Shtyah
 [Foundation Stone] —
 and flows to all the wisdoms
 and to all the particular intellects —
 (for this is the aspect of the extra soul
 that each person of Israel merits at that time —
 for the soul is the intellect —
 as it is written:
 "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam"
 — as mentioned above —
 and as also explained elsewhere.)
 And through this all the contractions [tzimtzumim]
 and all the judgments are sweetened.
 And this is the aspect of:
 ה'ן ת'וי ש'די י'ענני —
 the initial letters of which spell שתי"ה
 [Shtyah — the Foundation Stone] —
 as explained within —
 for Shadai is the aspect of Shabbos —
 as mentioned above many times.

 And this is the aspect of [Exodus 20:8]:
 "zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho
 [remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas
 [remember it from the first day for Shabbos]."
 For all the occupations and labors
 performed during the weekdays —
 all of them are the aspects of contractions [tzimtzumim]
 and clarifications [birurim] —
 through which one clarifies
 and elevates the holy sparks —
 as is well-known.

 And the essential clarification and sweetening
 of each and every contraction
 comes through some aspect
 of the particular intellect
 associated with it —
 as explained within —
 for:
 "kulhu b'machshavah itberiru
 [all of them are clarified through thought]"
 — and this is the aspect of [Psalms 104:24]:
 "kulam b'chochmah asisa
 [all of them You made with wisdom]."
 For even the vitality of holiness
 of all the acts of the six days of deed —
 all comes through wisdom —
 and in each and every day
 a different aspect of wisdom and intellect shines —
 and as also understood in the story
 of the seven beggars.
 But all of them must receive power
 from the overall intellect —
 the supernal Wisdom —
 the aspect of Shabbos.
 And therefore one must remember the Shabbos
 from the first day —
 so that each particular intellect
 should have the power
 to sweeten the contractions associated with it.
 But on Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the overall intellect —
 the supernal Wisdom —
 then all the contractions and judgments
 are sweetened in their generality and in their particularity —
 and then our judgment goes forth to light —
 and as our Sages taught:
 even one who worshipped idolatry, and so on —
 he is forgiven.

 And this is the aspect of the festival of Rosh Hashanah
 that falls on Shabbos —
 and it is brought in the name of the early authorities
 of blessed memory —
 who expounded on this:
 "ba'asher tov yoser — keshe'chal Rosh Hashanah b'Shabbas
 [more than good — when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos]"
 — because it is better as explained there.
 And according to our subject matter here —
 this too is understood —
 for Rosh Hashanah is the day of judgment [yoma d'dina]
 for the entire year —
 and so on —
 for which reason one must travel to the Tzadikim
 for Rosh Hashanah —
 as explained within.
 And this too is the aspect of the shofar blowing
 of Rosh Hashanah —
 as is well-known.
 And therefore when it falls on Shabbos —
 which is itself the aspect of the World of Thought —
 where there is the root of the sweetening —
 the aspect of:
 "kulhu b'machshavah itberiru"
 — and as all the above [shows] —
 certainly then all the judgments
 are sweetened even more.
 (And in this one can also explain
 the matter of the blowing in the Temple
 but not in the provinces —
 and the matter of shofar blowing:
 wisdom — and it is not a labor —
 and the Rabbis decreed lest one carry it
 four cubits in the public domain —
 and so on —
 and the entire matter there —
 but this is not the place for it.)
 And therefore it is a great thing
 to travel to the Tzadikim
 for the holy Shabbos —
 and in the holy Zohar
 and in the writings of the holy Ari z"l
 the great obligation is explained:
 to receive the face of one's teacher
 on the holy Shabbos —
 for through him
 one receives the holiness of Shabbos even more —
 as mentioned above.
 For the Tzadik himself is also the aspect
 of the overall intellect — the supernal Wisdom —
 as explained within.
 And therefore one can receive through him
 the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos even more —
 especially when many people
 gather to him on the holy Shabbos —
 and all their souls are encompassed
 in the soul of the Tzadik —
 the encompassing sage —
 for then certainly they receive
 an even greater illumination —
 and through this all the judgments
 are sweetened even more — as mentioned above.
 And this [Exodus 35:1]:
 "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Bnay Yisrael
 [and Moshe gathered the entire congregation
 of the children of Israel],"
 and so on —
 and then they were commanded
 regarding the work of the Mishkan —
 which is also called Mikdash —
 the aspect of Wisdom — the aspect of Kodesh —
 for all the work of the Mishkan
 was done with wisdom —
 as it is written [Exodus 36:1]:
 "v'chol ish chacham lev —
 asher natan Hashem chochmah u'sevunah beimah —
 lada'as la'asos es kol melaches avodas haKodesh
 [and every wise-hearted person —
 in whom Hashem placed wisdom and understanding —
 to know how to do all the work of the service of the holy],"
 and so on —
 and similarly many times.
 And this [Exodus 35:2]:
 "sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah —
 u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh —
 Shabbas Shabason laHashem
 [six days shall labor be done —
 and on the seventh day it shall be holy for you —
 a complete Shabbos for Hashem],"
 and so on —
 for even the work of the Mishkan
 does not override Shabbos.
 For Shabbos is the aspect of the supernal Wisdom —
 and so on —
 and therefore they were commanded on this
 through Moshe —
 and specifically through the assembly [b'hakhel] —
 as mentioned above.
 And therefore our Sages expounded from this:
 that it is a mitzvah
 to assemble congregations on every Shabbos
 and expound in words of Torah.
 And this is the aspect of the joy of Shabbos —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 For every intellect and every soul
 is the aspect of a lamp [ner] —
 and when they are all encompassed together
 there is made a great light —
 the aspect of [Proverbs 13:9]:
 "or tzadikim yismach
 [the light of the righteous brings joy]"
 — as explained within.
 And therefore when the holy Shabbos arrives —
 which is the aspect of the world of souls —
 the encompassing soul —
 and the encompassing intellect
 of all creation —
 and all the souls of Israel
 come and are encompassed in it —
 in the aspect of:
 "u'veyom hashevi'i shavas vayinafash
 [and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed]"
 — as is well-known —
 through this joy is drawn —
 the aspect of:
 "or tzadikim yismach."
 And therefore one must be very careful on Shabbos
 from all kinds of dispute —
 and there should be only love and peace —
 the aspect of Shabbas Shalom [Shabbos of peace] —
 for through love and peace —
 which is the aspect of the encompassing
 of all souls together
 in the holiness of Shabbos —
 through this one merits to receive even more
 the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos
 with all the holy rectifications encompassed within it —
 as mentioned above.

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha
 [if you return from Shabbos your foot]."
 "Regel
 [foot]"
 is the aspect of faith —
 and also the aspect of Torah scholars —
 which is the aspect of faith in the Sages —
 as mentioned above in Siman 57.
 And also regel is the aspect of counsel —
 as brought in Siman 22 —
 for through this one merits complete counsel.
 And also regel is the aspect of the upright practices —
 that one derives from all one's learning —
 in the aspect of [Psalms 119:105]:
 "ner l'ragli devarscha
 [a lamp for my feet is Your word],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And also regel is the aspect
 of not needing to be wanderers and exiles
 and driven from one's place —
 through the fact that the air of the settlements of Israel
 is sanctified with the holiness of the Land of Israel —
 for this is the aspect of [Joshua 1:3]:
 "kol hamakom asher tidroch kaf ragleichem bo
 [every place upon which the sole of your feet shall tread],"
 and so on —
 see Rashi there —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "al yetzei ish mimekomo
 [let no person go out from his place],"
 and so on — as mentioned above.
 And also the worthy leaders
 ordained through ordination —
 and likewise the holy writings
 written through the hands of writing —
 which is the aspect of the proliferation
 of holy books —
 are likewise the aspects of legs —
 as it is written [Genesis 49:10]:
 "lo yasur shevet miYehudah —
 u'mechokek mibein raglav
 [the scepter shall not depart from Judah —
 nor the lawgiver from between his feet]."

 And mechokek —
 its meaning is from the language
 of lordship and leadership [sharrah u'manhigus].
 And also its meaning is from the language
 of a scribe and one who inscribes on a book [sofer u'mechokek al hasefer].
 And also — the secret of intercalation
 is the aspect of regel —
 for through it
 is the essential fixing of the festivals [regalim]
 and appointed times — as is well-known.
 And it alludes also to the Shabbos union —
 through which are born
 holy souls
 who are expert in the secret of intercalation —
 as mentioned above.
 And it alludes also to the sweetening
 of the contractions and the judgments —
 which are the aspects of legs —
 the aspect of the heel [ekev] —
 as explained in Siman 41.

segments.he: וזה בחינת ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת היינו שבת סתם בחינת רחמים פשוטים. וזה לעשות את השבת היינו לעורר בזה שבת העליון שהוא בחינת רחמים גדולים וזה שאמרו רז"ל (שבת י"ב) הנכנס לבקר את החולה אומר שבת הוא מלזעוק ורפואה קרובה לבא.
segments.en:
And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi
 [from pursuing your affairs on My holy day]"
 — he should refrain from pursuing his weekday affairs —
 that have within them the grip
 of the waste products and the fetid smoke —
 which is the aspect of:
 "he'elu giluleichem al libam
 [they raised their idols upon their hearts]"
 — which is the aspect of the desire
 of the Sitra Achra —
 as it is written [Isaiah 66:3]:
 "u'vshikutzaihem nafsham chafetzah
 [and in their abominations their soul delights]."
 But one should engage in the affairs of Heaven —
 which are the aspect of the rectification of judgment —
 which is the aspect of chefetz [desire] —
 as it is written [Ecclesiastes 8:6]:
 "ki l'chol chefetz yesh es u'mishpat
 [for every desire there is a time and judgment]."
 And as it is written [Jeremiah 9:23]:
 "oseh chesed u'mishpat —
 v'chol haggid —
 ki v'eileh chafatzti
 [who does lovingkindness and justice —
 and so on —
 for in these I delight]."
 And likewise — the Land of Israel
 is called eretz chefetz [a desired land].
 And likewise — repentance is called chefetz —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And likewise — the proliferation of the books
 of the holy Torah
 is in the aspect of [Isaiah 42:21]:
 "Hashem chafetz l'ma'an tzidko —
 yagdil Torah v'ya'adir
 [Hashem desired — for the sake of His righteousness —
 to make the Torah great and glorious]."
 And likewise — the sweetening of the judgments
 that comes about through this
 is in the aspect of [Micah 7:18]:
 "ki chafetz chesed hu
 [for He desires lovingkindness]."

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg
 [and you shall call the Shabbos a delight]"
 — this is the aspect of the meals of Shabbos —
 which are entirely holy.
 And through this
 also the mind and the heart
 are pure and clean —
 which is the essential sacred delight —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad
 [the holy one of Hashem, honored]"
 — the aspect of the perfect faith in the Sages —
 that is completed through the holiness of Shabbos —
 through which one is careful
 in their honor —
 the opposite of the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 which is contempt of Torah scholars.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad —
 da Rashbi
 [the holy one of Hashem, honored —
 this is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai]"
 — as explained in the holy Zohar.

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha
 [and honor it — from pursuing your own ways]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 "she'lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah
 [one should not take large strides]."
 For Shabbos is the World of Thought —
 through which all anger and judgments
 are sweetened — as mentioned above —
 and large strides confuse the thought —
 as mentioned above many times —
 and therefore it is the aspect of anger —
 as it is written:
 "al tirgazu badarech
 [do not quarrel on the way]"
 — as our Sages expounded.

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar
 [from pursuing your affairs — and speaking words]"
 — one should not speak any weekday speech —
 so as not to blemish through this
 the holiness of the holy Shabbos —
 and not be in the aspect of:
 "holech rachil megalleh sod —
 d'les ru'chei ru'cha d'kiyuma
 [one who goes as a slanderer reveals a secret —
 who has no spirit —
 the spirit of enduring]"
 and so on —
 as explained within.
 For the speech of Shabbos is holy —
 since then the light of the supernal Wisdom
 shines upon the letters of speech —
 from which is their root —
 and when one speaks weekday speech —
 this is the aspect of a blemish of the ordination —
 of appointing an unworthy leader —
 through which the light of wisdom
 is withdrawn from the hands —
 which is the aspect of the nullification
 of our handwriting —
 as explained within.

 And this [Isaiah 58:14]:
 "az tis'anag al Hashem —
 da Atika Kadisha
 [then you will delight in Hashem —
 this is the Holy Ancient One]"
 — that is, the great sweetening
 of the general totality of all contractions and judgments —
 that is drawn from the aspect of Atik —
 through which our judgment goes forth to light —
 and all sins are forgiven —
 for this is the aspect of [Daniel 7:9–10]:
 "chazey havit —
 ad di churs'avon remiv —
 v'Atik Yomin yesiv —
 (eyin Adra Nassa daf kuf lamed)
 [I looked —
 until thrones were set up —
 and the Ancient of Days sat —
 (see Adra Nassa, folio 130)]
 levushei k'selag chuvar —
 v'se'ar reishei k'amar neka —
 eyin Rashi sham —
 kurs'aya —
 v'chol haggid —
 dina yesiv v'sifrin pesichin —
 eyin Adra Nassa daf kuf kaf tes
 [His garment was white as snow —
 and the hair of His head was like pure wool —
 see Rashi there —
 His throne —
 and so on —
 judgment sat and books were opened —
 see Adra Nassa, folio 129]"
 — for through the time of favor [es ratzon]
 drawn from Atik Yomin
 on Shabbos at Minchah —
 through this all the judgments
 are sweetened and stilled before Him.
 For this is what is written:
 "dina yesiv —
 klomar: yesiv b'asrei —
 v'dina lo is'aved
 [judgment sat —
 meaning: it settled in its place —
 and judgment was not executed],"
 and so on.
 And this is what concluded:
 "v'sifrin pesichin
 [and books were opened]"
 — this is made through the proliferation of books —
 that are opened through the completion of faith in the Sages —
 through which the holy Torah is completed
 and receives from the overall supernal Wisdom —
 until through this
 is drawn the aspect of this great sweetening
 that comes from the aspect of Atik.
 And this:
 "v'sifrin pesichin
 [and books were opened]"
 — "pesichin
 [opened]" — specifically.
 For the holy books existed also beforehand —
 but on account of the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 they did not open them at all
 to look into them —
 and through this the contractions and judgments intensified —
 until they were unable to sweeten them.
 For this is the aspect of [Job 12:14]:
 "yisgore al ish v'lo yipasach
 [He locks against a person — and it shall not be opened]."
 But through the rectification of faith in the Sages —
 through which all the holy books are opened —
 and one studies them with desire and great importance —
 through this all the judgments are sweetened —
 through the illumination of the time of favor
 from the Holy Ancient One —
 in the aspect of:
 "dina yesiv v'sifrin pesichin"
 — as mentioned above.

 "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz —
 da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin
 [and I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth —
 this is the Holy Apple Orchard]"
 — which alludes to the ascent of Malchus
 until it receives also the illumination of Chab"d —
 that is: the faith — the aspect of Malchus —
 is completed until it receives
 the illumination of wisdom —
 through which the aspect of faith in the Sages
 is rectified — as mentioned above.
 And also — the rectification of counsel
 is the aspect of Malchus —
 as explained within.
 For through the blemish of faith in the Sages —
 one is punished with waste products —
 and then judgment and counsel are blemished —
 through the fact that
 the foolishness and stupidity coming
 from the aforementioned waste products
 grasps them —
 in the aspect of [Job 12:17]:
 "molech yo'atzim sholal —
 v'shoftim yeholel
 [He leads counselors away stripped —
 and judges He makes fools]"
 — and Rashi explained:
 "sholal v'yeholel —
 shneihem lashon shtus
 [stripped and made a fool —
 both of them are the language of foolishness]."
 But through faith in the Sages —
 then judgment and counsel
 are the aspects of the mental faculties and wisdom —
 and this too is the aspect of the building of Malchus —
 as is well-known.
 And this is what our Sages taught:
 that one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms —
 that is, from the grip of the foolishness
 of the Malchus d'Sitra Achra —
 the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 4:13]:
 "Melech zaken u'chesil
 [an old and foolish king]."

 And this is the aspect of:
 "la'asor maleichem b'zikkim —
 v'chol haggid —
 la'asos bahem mishpat kasuv
 [to bind their kings in chains —
 and so on —
 to execute upon them the written judgment]"
 — as explained within.

 "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha —
 da Ze'ir Anpin
 [and I will feed you with the heritage of Yaakov your father —
 this is Ze'ir Anpin]"
 — that is, the aspect of judgment —
 the central column.
 And also — the Torah
 is the aspect of the central column —
 and it is the aspect of:
 "morasha kehillas Yaakov
 [the heritage of the congregation of Yaakov]."
 [Deuteronomy 33:4]

 And this is the aspect of an inheritance without limits —
 for:
 "oraissa meChochmah ila'ah nafkat
 [the Torah went forth from the supernal Wisdom]"
 — and therefore when it has completion
 through faith in the Sages —
 that is rectified through the holiness of Shabbos —
 through this it ascends to the supernal Wisdom —
 the Holy of Holies —
 and draws from there sweetening
 for all the contractions and judgments.
 And then all the constraints [metzarim]
 drawn from the contractions mentioned above
 are nullified.

 And this [Isaiah 58:14]:
 "ki pi Hashem diber
 [for the mouth of Hashem has spoken]"
 — for on Shabbos
 the aspect of the Oral Torah is completed —
 which is the aspect of:
 "Malchus peh
 [Malchus — the mouth]."
 And the Oral Torah is called thus —
 for its foundation is faith in the Sages —
 to believe in them —
 that all their words are literally the words of Hashem —
 as it were — in the aspect of:
 "ki pi Hashem diber."
 And as our Sages of blessed memory expounded
 [Tractate Megillah 19b]:
 "mah dekasuv: v'aleihem —
 k'chol hadvarim asher diber Hashem imachem bahar —
 melamd she'her'ah haKadosh Baruch Hu l'Moshe —
 dikdukay Torah —
 v'dikdukay Soferim —
 u'mah sheha'Soferim atidin l'chadesh —
 u'may nihu — mikra Megillah
 [what is written: and upon them —
 according to all the words that Hashem spoke with you on the mountain —
 this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moshe —
 the fine points of the Torah —
 and the fine points of the Scribes —
 and what the Scribes are destined to produce as novellae —
 and what is this? — the reading of the Megillah]"
 — that is, the aspect of the holy books
 that multiply and are renewed in every generation
 through true Tzadikim and Sages —
 all of them are within the category of:
 "hadvarim asher diber Hashem
 [the words that Hashem spoke]."
 And through this specifically
 the holy Torah is completed —
 until it is in the aspect of the stone tablets —
 as explained within.
 And this is:
 "v'aleihem — v'aleihem davka
 [and upon them — upon them specifically]"
 — that is, upon the stone tablets —
 as was stated there before this.

segments.he: היינו כי בחול צריכין לזעוק בכדי לעורר הרחמים פשוטים על כל פנים ובשבת אין צריכין לזה כי על ידי קדושת שבת בעצמה נתעורר רחמים ועל כן רפואה קרובה לבא. ור"מ אומר יכולה הוא שתרחם. היינו שהוא מבאר ביותר ענין התעוררות הרחמים על ידי קדושת שבת. ר' יהודה אומר המקום ירחם עליך ועל חולי ישראל ר' יוסי אומר המקום ירחם עליך בתוך חולי ישראל (פירוש רש"י שתהא תפלתו נשמעת בזכותן של רבין) שבנא איש ירושלים וכו' אומר שבת הוא מלזעוק ורפואה קרובה לבא היינו כנ"ל ורחמיו מרובים ושבתו בשלום היינו כי אפילו אם אינה יכולה הרפואה לבא על ידי בחינת רחמים פשוטים. יש אצלו יתברך בחינת רחמים גדולים שנתעוררין גם כן על ידי קדושת שבת כנ"ל שזה בחינת ורחמיו מרובים ועל ידי זה בוודאי תבא הרפואה:
segments.en: Shabbos is the aspect of the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — as mentioned above many times. And it is the aspect of the holiness of speech — in the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — and as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar. And therefore one must be very careful not to speak idle speech [sicha betelah] on Shabbos. But nonetheless — it is explained in Teshuvos haDeshen, Siman 61 — where he was asked about the practice of those who are meticulous — who nonetheless did not accustom themselves to be so careful in this — and gather on Shabbos — and so on — and discuss news about kings and ministers — and so on — see there what he answered: because they take delight in this — and therefore it is permitted — and so on — but those who do not take delight — it is forbidden. And this is also brought in the annotation of the Rema [SA OC 307:1] — and there it is elaborated even further — that one who does not take delight — it is forbidden to say these things so that his fellow should take delight in them. And see in the Moshvetzos Zahav — which resolved what appears at first glance problematic — for idle speech is forbidden even on a weekday — so how is it different? — but on a weekday — it is permitted for one's fellow to take delight from it — and on Shabbos — even this is forbidden. And see in the Tur"z there, paragraph 1 — it is understood that if the speaker himself also has delight from the fact that his fellow takes pleasure in his stories — it is also permitted. And all of this is understood for our matters — according to what is explained within — see there. For the essential delight of Shabbos is the mental faculties — the source of delight — in the aspect of: "ein l'ma'alah mei'oneg" — as mentioned above many times. And therefore sometimes — even on Shabbos — it is permitted to tell some secular conversation — in order to open one's mind and revive oneself — and to return to the level of one's mental faculties — which is the aspect of: one takes delight in the conversation — that is, one thereby comes to the level of the mental faculties — which are the aspect of delight. However — if he himself does not take delight from this — but only tells it so that his fellow should take delight — that is, so that his fellow should come to the level of his mental faculties — on a weekday this too is permitted. But on Shabbos — one should reconsider this — as mentioned above — unless he himself also takes delight from this — from the fact that his fellow takes pleasure in his stories — that is, such as when he tells to a Torah scholar — and through the Torah scholar taking delight in his stories — and returning to the level of his mental faculties — through this — the Torah scholar afterward also elevates the storyteller and connects him to the sacred knowledge — where there is the source of delight — as mentioned above. Which is the aspect of: the storyteller takes delight from the fact that his fellow takes pleasure in his stories — as mentioned above. But in truth — the Torah scholar himself also takes very great delight from this — from the fact that he connects even the common people to the sacred knowledge — which is the essential delight of Shabbos — as mentioned above. For "zachay man d'achid b'yada d'chayyava [praiseworthy is one who holds the hand of a sinner]," and so on. And therefore it is also permitted. However — all of this was said regarding the Torah scholar — who knows how to do every matter in its proper time and its proper moment and its proper measure. And in truth — the conversation of a Torah scholar is itself Torah — and so on — and as explained elsewhere and as also explained within in this teaching. But simple people — who are not fixed in Torah study during the weekday — it is explained in Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 290 — that they should not prolong themselves greatly on Shabbos also in the delight of eating and drinking — but should engage more in Torah. And the Torah scholars may prolong somewhat more in the delight of eating and drinking — and so on. And this is likewise from this aspect mentioned above. For although the delight of eating and drinking is an outer service for Torah scholars — compared to their Torah and prayer — and as explained elsewhere — and it is the aspect of the secular conversation of Torah scholars — nonetheless it is also very holy — and sometimes through this specifically one connects the common people to the sacred knowledge — which is the aspect of the excellence of one who merits to sit at the Shabbos meal at the table of a true Torah scholar and Tzadik — and as elaborated elsewhere. And as mentioned from this also above in Siman 69.

segments.he: וזה אז תתענג על ה' דא עתיקא קדישא היינו שזוכין להמשיך בחינת הרחמים גדולים שהם בחינת עתיק כמבואר בפנים. ועל כן דרשו רז"ל מזה שנותנין לו כל משאלות לבו כי בבחינת רחמים האלו בוודאי יכולין למלאות לו כל משאלות לבו וכמבואר בליקוטי הלכות הלכות תחומין. והרכבתיך על במותי ארץ דא חקל תפוחין קדישין היינו עליית המלכות עד המוחין ורז"ל דרשו מזה שניצל משיעבוד מלכיות היינו שנתקבצין הניצוצין והאותיות שבבחינת מלכות שנתפזרו בגלות למקום שנתפזרו. ועכשיו מתקבצין ועולין על ידי קדושת שבת עד שזוכין על ידי זה לדעת שלם שזה בחינת שעולה עד המוחין. והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב אביך דא ז"א היינו בחינת התורה הקדושה כידוע. וכן הרחמים פשוטים שהן בחינת הרחמים דז"א שעל ידם נמשכין גם בחינת הרחמים גדולים על ידי שהרחמים פשוטים מתפללים ומעוררים אותם שזה בחינת תפלת השם יתברך כנ"ל. וזה שסיים כי פי ה' דבר. היינו שזוכין על ידי זה לעורר תפלת השם יתברך בעצמו שהשם יתברך בעצמו כביכול יתפלל וידבר לעורר בחינת הרחמים גדולים שהם בחינת רחמים דעתיק כנ"ל:
segments.en:
Opening / Shabbos = emunas chachamim / rectification of mishpat / Tikkun 19 / days of the week / ordination / handwriting: Cross-reference to Siman 57 (emunas chachamim is drawn through Shabbos → judgment goes forth to light). Shabbos = amuda d'emtza'isa = adjudicates right and left. Tikkun 19, folio 40b: "terin dra'in — Gedullah u'Gevurah — T' — Tiferes." Wednesday/Thursday/Friday = before Shabbos; Sunday/Monday/Tuesday = after Shabbos (Megillas Amukos, Ofan 249). Shabbosim given only for Torah = to derive true judgments and upright practices = judgment through the mind = mind through nourishment. Shabbos: mochin in perfection; eating entirely holy (Siman 57); emunas chachamim drawn → rectification of mishpat. The nismach (one being ordained) receives semichah from the true teacher on Shabbos = Yehoshua's ordination from Moshe on Shabbos (Rashi on Ha'azinu: "Shabbas shel diyuzgey hayah / he'emid lo Moshe turgeiman l'Yehoshua"; Rashi on Pinchas). Shabbos strengthens our handwriting: writing hand = Tiferes (Tikunim); pen and quill = Tiferes; parchment/paper = Malchus (Pardes, entries of appellations); root of letters = Chochmah. Shabbos = Malchus drawn from Kodesh = Chochmah = "u'shemartem es haShabbas ki kodesh hi" (Exodus 31:14; writings). Shabbas ila'ah / Shabbas d'yoma / Shabbas d'leila (Zohar). Shabbos = emunas chachamim = illumination of Chochmah drawn upon the faith (Malchus). Created at twilight of Erev Shabbos: kesav (form of letters) + michtav (pen and stylus) + luchos (Tractate Pesachim 54; Rashi) = three aspects. "U'shney luchos avanim horid b'yado v'chasuv bahem shmiyas Shabbas."
 Shabbos and kedushah of Eretz Yisrael / exile / buying property on Shabbos / SA OC 306 / sod ha'ibur / calendar / celestial spheres / Zohar haBahir / sacred union: Shabbos → holiness of Eretz Yisrael (Tikkun Heh). Extra soul = called Eretz Yisrael = admas kodesh. Each person establishes shevisah in his place → kedushah of Eretz Yisrael drawn → cannot be expelled → saved from gzeiras gerush. "Shvu ish tachtav / al yetzei ish mimekomo" (Exodus 16:29). Blemish of Shabbos → nations conquer Eretz Yisrael; "lo charevah Yerushalayim ela al she'chilellu vah es haShabbas v'al she'bizzu vah Talmidey Chachamim" = pagan emunas chachamim + weakening our handwriting → giving force to their writing. SA OC 306: buying property from non-Jew on Shabbos in Eretz Yisrael is permitted for yishuv Eretz Yisrael = restoring power of our handwriting. Sod ha'ibur: "ki hi chochmasechem u'vinasechem l'einay ha'amim" (Deuteronomy 4:6). Beitzah 16a: Shabbos given in privacy = "beini u'vein Bnay Yisrael" = reward not made known = extra soul not made known. Shabbos flows from Chochmah and Binah = "ki kodesh hu." Celestial spheres (Siman 31 cross-reference): spheres governed by angels; all intellects receive from the encompassing soul; "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam" (Job 32:8). Shabbos = source of all souls (Zohar; Sefer haBahir) = Shadai = "v'nishmas Shadai davka tvinam." Bris Menuchah, Derech Vav, cross-reference. Great souls are expert in sod ha'ibur. "U'veyom haShabbas" juxtaposed to "u'vera'ashay chodsheichem" (Numbers 28:9, 11); Zohar: kiddush hachodesh and ibur hashana drawn from Shabbos holiness; all regalim and moadim depend on sod ha'ibur; Shabbos = techilah l'mikra'ay kodesh. Spheres = shamayim; "haShomayim mesaprim" recited on Shabbos (Siman 56 cross-reference; Zohar). Souls need pure bodies formed from "avira d'Eretz Yisrael machkim" → essential time for sacred union = Shabbos → draw holy souls to children (Zohar); tipah zar'iyis then = kedushah of Eretz Yisrael → body can receive great soul → merits sod ha'ibur. Shabbos → complete counsel: "mayim amukkim etzah b'lev ish v'ish tevunos yidlenah" (Proverbs 20:5); Shabbos = heart; extra soul → "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam" → counsel rectified. Blemish of emunas chachamim → "he'elu giluleichem al libam" (Ezekiel 14:3) → counsel blemished. Ezekiel 20:16: "v'es Shabsosai chilelu ki acharay giluleichem libam holech." Machloket = May Merivah = pure waters = purify from filth. Nehemiah 13:17: "va'arivah es choray Yehudah / mah hadavar hara hazeh / u'mechallelim es yom haShabbas." Nations' decrees to desecrate Shabbos = machloket on Israel re: Shabbos = Israel sacrificed themselves = mesiyas nefesh → teshuvah hamishkal. Kavannos: even now intend "v'al menuchasam yekadshu es Shimcha" = mesiyas nefesh. "Yakiru vanecha v'yeid'u ki mei'itcha hi menuchasam" (kavannos: "mei'atcha — kaf = Keser"). Through machloket awakening and opposition → holy books become even more precious in one's eyes → Shabbos holiness becomes more precious → emunas chachamim more complete → Oral Torah multiplied endlessly.
 Tzadikim who bear collective sin / "badi hutza laki krava" / shanayim Torah u'vo = both Written and Oral / shabbos equivalent to entire Torah / obligatory Torah novellae / Siman 159 / Isaiah 56:2 / Shabbos 118b / Midrash Rabbah Beshalach 25: Tzadikim who did not blemish emunas chachamim or Shabbos nevertheless bear the dispute = "v'hu chet rabim nassa" (Isaiah 53:12). Exodus 16:27: "vayehi vayom hashevi'i yatze'u / ad anah me'anem lishmor mitzvosai v'Sorosai" = G-d included even Moshe = "badi hutza laki krava." "V'Sorosai" = Yoma 28b: "kiyem Avraham afilu eiruv tavshilin / Sorosai — achas Torah she'b'chtav v'achas Torah she'b'al peh." Shabbos = perfection of Oral Torah → Written Torah also completed. Midrash Rabbah Beshalach 25: in Torah, Prophets, and Writings — Shabbos equivalent to entire Torah. Dispute also comes on one whose Shabbos is not sufficiently precious in his own eyes — even if he thinks this reflects deep awareness of Shabbos greatness — this itself is a blemish. Shabbos encompasses from the very top to the very bottom; anyone who guards it properly in plain simplicity is happy and must rejoice greatly (Zohar). Obligatory to produce Torah novellae on Shabbos (Zohar): Oral Torah = source of all novellae; Written Torah cannot be added to; all additions and renewals = "dadeha yarvucha b'chol eis" (Proverbs 5:19; Sages) = Oral Torah. Must believe Torah novellae precious even if small — within emunas chachamim framework — as long as built on true foundations. Even those who cannot produce novellae: don't despair; receive Shabbos with joy; believe their Shabbos is high and precious. Perhaps through their Shabbos their fellow produces novellae → they have a share; especially those who support Torah scholars. Study something new / or at least new awakening and desire on every Shabbos = also chidushay Torah (Siman 159 cross-reference). Isaiah 56:2: "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos u'ven adam yachazik bah" + "etz chayyim hi lamachazikim bah." Shabbos 118b: "kol hashomer Shabbas kehilcheso afilu aved avodah zarah k'dor Enosh mochalin lo" = "ashrey enosh / shomer Shabbas mechalelo." Midrash Rabbah Beshalach 25: "im shomer adam es haShabbas k'ilu shomar kol hamitzvos / shomer yado me'asos kol ra." Isaiah 56: "ben haneychar" + "saris": Beitzah / Midrash Rabbah Beshalach: Shabbos given to Israel only; non-Jew who rests is liable to death; evil inclination weakens confidence. The saris: on Shabbos birth of new souls is drawn (writings); Shabbos union → holy children (Zohar). Zohar: must produce fruit in Torah novellae — else is dry tree. Siman 185 of SA OC cross-referenced implicitly. "Ki koh amar Hashem la'sarisim asher yishmeru / u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti" = new and strong desire for Torah = "v'chefetz Hashem b'yado yitzlach"; "u'machzikim b'vrisi" = sustain the Torah. "Yad v'shem tov mibbanim u'mibbanos" = sarisim: share in drawing souls; simple people: share in novellae of Torah scholars (especially if they support them). Sanhedrin 93b: "shem olam etein lo — zeh sefer Daniel she'nikra al shemo."
 Eliyahu writes merits of Shabbos observers at Motzaei Shabbos / Maharil / Shelah haKadosh / Shabbos observers called yirey Hashem / "az nidveru" / Malachi 3:16 / shem Hashem da sefer / LM Tinyana 32 / generation of Enosh / Zohar Bereishis 37 / Shabbas shma d'Kudsha Berich Hu / Sanhedrin / Zohar Yisro 89: Maharil and Shelah haKadosh: at every Motzaei Shabbos Eliyahu haNaviv sits and writes merits of Israel who observed Shabbos → holy books made from Shabbos observance. Shabbos observers = yirey Hashem = Malachi 3:20: "v'zarechah lachem yiray shemi shemesh tzedakah." Each Jew guards Shabbos and receives its kedushah → encompassed in unity → radiate upon each other (Siman 34 cross-reference). Malachi 3:16: "az nidveru yiray Hashem ish el re'ehu / vayakshuv Hashem vayishma / vayikatev sefer zikaron lefanav / l'yiray Hashem / v'l'choshvay shemo." Plain meaning: when seeing success of wicked and lowliness of upright → machloket aspect → the yiray Hashem awaken to speak → not attach to wicked → not entertain doubts about G-d's ways → awakening of teshuvah for blemish of emunah caused by machloket → G-d writes their words → book made above. "Vayikatev sefer zikaron l'yiray Hashem v'l'choshvay shemo." "V'l'choshvay davka" = through teshuvah all holy books become more precious. "Shem Hashem da sefer" (Zohar; LM Tinyana 32). Precise language of Sages re: "k'dor Enosh": generation of Enosh blemished the Name of Hashem ("az huchal likro b'shem Hashem" Genesis 4:26) = essentially through blemish of emunas chachamim = Adam, Shet, etc. existed but were not listened to; unworthy leaders appointed → idolatry = "he'elu giluleichem al libam." Genesis 5:1: "zeh sefer toldos adam" immediately afterward = Zohar Bereishis 37: "shem Hashem da sefer" = Tzadikim awakened to repair emunas chachamim → holy books multiplied. "Shabbas shma d'Kudsha Berich Hu" (Zohar) → guarding Shabbos → holy books multiplied = Name of Hashem → even worshipper like dor Enosh forgiven. Isaiah 56: "ashrey enosh / shem olam etein lo" → Sanhedrin 93b: "zeh sefer Daniel." Opened in plural "v'nasati lahem" / concluded in singular "shem olam etein lo" (Sanhedrin; Zohar Yisro 89). Composers of books in every generation = only few individuals, yet every book has a share for other Israelites (Simanim 13, 20, 192). "Bayis" = Chochmah = "b'chochmah yibaneh bayis" (Proverbs 24:3; Siman 59 cross-reference) = source of mishpat = I Kings 3:28. "Chomah" = Malchus = emunah = "ani chomah" (Song of Songs 8:10) = two Shabbosim = Chochmah and emunah = emunas chachamim = rectification of mishpat. "Es Shabsosai = da igula v'ribua d'lagu" = emunah = Malchus = igul = "v'emunascha savivosecha" (Psalms 89:3); ribua = mishpat (from rectification of mochin and Chochmah; Siman 59). "Yad" = yedey hasemichah = drawing forth of Chochmah = "maleh ru'ach chochmah ki samach Moshe" (Deuteronomy 34:9) = foundation of Oral Torah chain = "Moshe kibel Torah miSinai u'masarah l'Yehoshua." "Shem" = yedey haketivah = Megillah 10b: "shem — zeh haktav" = strengthens our handwriting; also alludes to proliferation of holy books. "Ketov zos zikaron b'sefer" (Exodus 17:14) → Sages: mikra Megillah → specifically through husk of Haman-Amalek stirring → Israel awakened in teshuvah → Megillas Esther added (Likutay Halachos). "Shem Hashem da sefer." Megillah 10b: "v'hayah laHashem l'shem — zeh mikra Megillah."
 Shanayim mikra v'echad Targum / oraissa meChochmah ila'ah nafkat / ki keflaim l'tushiyah / Job 11 / Zohar Yisro 92 / Even Shtyah / Ven Tav Shin Yod Anenni / zachor es yom haShabbas / birurim / seven beggars cross-reference / Rosh Hashanah on Shabbos / shofar in Temple vs. provinces / traveling to the Tzadik / Vayakhel Moshe / or tzadikim yismach / love and peace / Isaiah 58 complete synthesis: Shanayim mikra v'echad Targum: Targum = Oral Torah (Sages); essential perfection of Torah = through Oral Torah. "Shanayim mikra" = "vayaged lecha ta'alumos chochmah ki keflaim l'tushiyah" (Job 11:6) = hidden things not written = transmitted orally; "oraissa meChochmah ila'ah nafkat" = can only receive from Chochmah ila'ah with completion = Oral Torah provides completion. "Echad Targum" = Oral Torah → Torah receives from Chochmah ila'ah → "vayaged lecha ta'alumos chochmah." Job 11:6 continued: "v'da ki yasheh lecha Elo'ah mei'avonecha / Targum: aram anshi lach Elaha mei'avayech" = judgments sweetened = G-d "forgets" sins; Job 11:8–9: "gahey shamayim / aruchah me'aretz / u'rechavah miny yam" = depth and wonders of Torah = all in Oral Torah = Torah completed. Shabbos: all dinnim are suppressed; Zohar Yisro 92: "ilin inun klala v'raza d'chol oraissa — Torah — Nevi'im — u'Kesuvim." Torah found in Torah/Prophets/Writings equivalent to entire Torah (many places; Zohar). Torah receives from Chochmah ila'ah → itself = Shabbos = "ki kodesh hi" (kavannos); everyone agrees Torah given on Shabbos; Torah = luchos (Siman 59). "U'shney luchos avanim horid b'yado v'chasuv bahem shmiyas Shabbas." Torah receives from Chochmah ila'ah = Even Shtyah → flows to all wisdoms and all particular intellects = extra soul = intellect = "v'nishmas Shadai tvinam." All tzimtzumim and dinnim sweetened. "Ven Tav Shin Yod Anenni" = roshei teivos = SHTYAH (Even Shtyah); Shadai = Shabbos. "Zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho / zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas": all weekday labors = tzimtzumim and birurim = elevate holy sparks. Essential clarification of each tzimtzum = through some particular intellect = "kulhu b'machshavah itberiru" = "kulam b'chochmah asisa" (Psalms 104:24). Each weekday: different aspect of Chochmah and intellect shines = as understood in the story of the seven beggars (cross-reference). All must receive power from the overall intellect = Chochmah ila'ah = Shabbos → "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" = power for each particular intellect to sweeten its contractions. On Shabbos: overall intellect = Chochmah ila'ah → all tzimtzumim sweetened in generality and particularity → judgment goes forth → "afilu aved avodah zarah mochalin lo." Rosh Hashanah falling on Shabbos: brought in name of early authorities ("ba'asher tov yoser keshe'chal Rosh Hashanah b'Shabbas" = better); yoma d'dina of the entire year = reason one travels to Tzadikim for Rosh Hashanah; shofar of Rosh Hashanah; when falls on Shabbos = World of Thought itself = root of sweetening = "kulhu b'machshavah itberiru" → all judgments sweetened even more. Parenthetical: shofar in Temple but not in provinces; "shofar chochmah v'einah melachah / rabbanan gziru shema ya'avireinu arba amos bireshus harabbim" = not the place for this. Traveling to the Tzadik on Shabbos (Zohar; Ari z"l kavannos: great obligation to receive face of teacher on Shabbos → receives Shabbos holiness more); Tzadik = aspect of overall intellect = Chochmah ila'ah; many souls encompassed in the soul of the Tzadik → greater illumination → all judgments sweetened more. "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Bnay Yisrael" → commanded on Mishkan = Mikdash = Chochmah = Kodesh; all work of Mishkan = wisdom = Exodus 36:1: "v'chol ish chacham lev asher natan Hashem chochmah / la'asos es kol melaches avodas haKodesh." "Sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah / u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh" = Mishkan does not override Shabbos. Mitzvah to assemble congregations on Shabbos and expound. Joy of Shabbos (Zohar): each intellect and soul = ner; together = great light = "or tzadikim yismach" (Proverbs 13:9). All souls of Israel come and are encompassed in Shabbos = "u'veyom hashevi'i shavas vayinafash" → joy = "or tzadikim yismach." Must be careful on Shabbos from all dispute → only love and peace = Shabbas Shalom → encompassing of all souls → receive even greater illumination of Shabbos holiness. Isaiah 58 fully mapped through S61 themes: "raglecha" = emunah + emunas chachamim (Siman 57) + counsel (Siman 22) + upright practices ("ner l'ragli devarscha") + not being exiled ("kol hamakom asher tidroch kaf ragleichem" Joshua 1:3 Rashi; "al yetzei ish mimekomo") + worthy ordained leaders and holy books = "lo yasur shevet miYehudah u'mechokek mibein raglav" (Genesis 49:10); mechokek = (1) lordship/leadership; (2) scribe who inscribes; sod ha'ibur = regel = fixing of regalim; Shabbos union → holy souls expert in ibur; sweetening of tzimtzumim = regel = ekev (Siman 41). "Me'asos chafatzecha" = refrain from weekday affairs = grip of waste and fetid smoke = "he'elu giluleichem al libam" = chefetz d'Sitra Achra = "u'vshikutzaihem nafsham chafetzah" (Isaiah 66:3); engage in chaftzei shamayim = tikkun mishpat = chefetz = Ecclesiastes 8:6 + Jeremiah 9:23 "ki v'eileh chafatzti"; Eretz Yisrael = eretz chefetz; teshuvah = chefetz; proliferation of books = "Hashem chafetz l'ma'an tzidko yagdil Torah v'ya'adir" (Isaiah 42:21); sweetening of dinnim = "ki chafetz chesed hu" (Micah 7:18). "Oneg" = Shabbos meals = all holy → mind and heart pure = essential sacred delight. "Mechubbad" = perfect emunas chachamim = careful in honor of sages = opposite of contempt of Torah scholars = "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad da Rashbi" (Zohar). "V'chibadto" = no large strides (Sages) = Shabbos = World of Thought → sweetens anger and judgments; large strides confuse thought; "al tirgazu badarech" (Sages). "Mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" = no weekday speech = blemish Shabbos holiness = not in aspect of "holech rachil megalleh sod d'les ru'chei ru'cha d'kiyuma"; speech of Shabbos = holy = light of Chochmah ila'ah shines on letters of speech; weekday speech = blemish of ordination = appointing unworthy leader = withdrawal of Chochmah from hands = nullification of our handwriting. "Az tis'anag al Hashem da Atika Kadisha" = great sweetening of all tzimtzumim and dinnim from Atik → judgment goes forth to light → sins forgiven; Daniel 7:9–10 + Adra Nassa 130 + Adra Nassa 129: "churs'avon remiv / Atik Yomin yesiv / levushei k'selag chuvar / se'ar reishei k'amar neka (Rashi) / kurs'aya / dina yesiv v'sifrin pesichin" = "dina yesiv — yesiv b'asrei — v'dina lo is'aved"; "v'sifrin pesichin — pesichin davka" = holy books opened through emunas chachamim → Torah completed → receives from Chochmah ila'ah → sweetening from Atik; "yisgore al ish v'lo yipasach" (Job 12:14) = blemish of emunas chachamim = books not opened → dinnim intensify. "Hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus to receive Chab"d illumination = emunah completed through receiving Chochmah = emunas chachamim rectified; tikkun ha'etzah = Malchus; blemish emunas chachamim → punishment with waste products → mishpat and counsel blemished → "molech yo'atzim sholal v'shoftim yeholel" (Job 12:17; Rashi: both = language of foolishness); emunas chachamim → mishpat and counsel = mochin and Chochmah = building of Malchus; saved from subjugation = Malchus d'Sitra Achra = "Melech zaken u'chesil" (Ecclesiastes 4:13). "La'asor maleichem b'zikkim / la'asos bahem mishpat kasuv." "Heritage of Yaakov" = Ze'ir Anpin = mishpat = amuda d'emtza'isa = "morasha kehillas Yaakov." Nachalah b'li metzarim = "oraissa meChochmah ila'ah nafkat" + emunas chachamim rectified through Shabbos → Torah ascends to Chochmah ila'ah = Holy of Holies → draws sweetening for all tzimtzumim → all metzarim nullified. "Ki pi Hashem diber" = on Shabbos: Oral Torah completed = Malchus peh; Oral Torah founded on emunas chachamim = "ki pi Hashem diber." Megillah 19b: "v'aleihem k'chol hadvarim asher diber Hashem bahar / melamd she'her'ah haKBH l'Moshe dikdukay Torah v'dikdukay Soferim u'mah sheha'Soferim atidin l'chadesh / u'may nihu — mikra Megillah" = holy books renewed in every generation = all within "hadvarim asher diber Hashem" → Torah completed → aspect of luchos → "v'aleihem v'aleihem davka" upon the stone tablets.

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman

Yikara DiShabsa — Simanim 62, 63, 64

 Yikara DiShabsa · יקרא דשבתא
 Simanim 62 · 63 · 64

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 62 — סימן סב
 Shabbos is the aspect of faith — intellect — peace — sacred union — fish — Isaiah 58
 [Likutay Moharan I, Siman 62]

 Shabbos is the aspect of faith [emunah] —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And also — Shabbos is the aspect of the mental faculties
 and intellect —
 for then all the gates of the sacred intellect
 open — as mentioned above many times.
 And then the evil inclination
 is subjugated to the good inclination —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 And then one merits to know
 from the knowledge of His divinity, blessed be He,
 with a whole heart —
 in the aspect of [Ezekiel 20:20]:
 "v'es Shabsosai kadshu —
 v'hayah l'os beini u'veinichem —
 lada'as ki ani Hashem Elokeichem
 [and My Shabbosim sanctify —
 and it shall be a sign between Me and you —
 to know that I am Hashem your G-d]."
 And therefore then it is easier for every person
 to concentrate in his prayer [lekavven b'tefilaso]
 and to pray with great blazing —
 and as understood within.
 And also — because the six weekdays
 correspond to the six orders of the Mishnah —
 which are full of sacred disputes [machloket d'kedushah] —
 the dispute of the Tannaim —
 this one forbids and that one permits — and so on —
 and when this descends below —
 the evil inclination draws sustenance from it
 for the dispute in the heart —
 which is the aspect of the concealment
 of the knowledge of His divinity, blessed be He —
 in the aspect of [Hosea 10:2]:
 "chalak libam
 [their heart is divided]."
 And Shabbos is the aspect of peace —
 as explained in the holy Zohar —
 and then the sacred dispute
 is rectified at its root —
 and through this the aspect of the dispute
 of the evil inclination in one's heart is nullified —
 and then one can serve G-d with all one's heart.
 And the gates of the intellect open for him —
 so that he knows how to answer the heretic [apikores] —
 for this is the aspect of:
 שׁ'לוֹ"ם —
 initial letters of:
 "v'da mah she'tashiv la'apikores
 [and know what you shall answer the heretic]"
 — as explained within.
 But there are questions
 for which there is no answer —
 and there one must rely only on faith —
 and this too one merits on Shabbos —
 for then faith is completed in great perfection —
 as mentioned above many times.

 And this is the aspect of [Psalms 92]:
 Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas:
 "tov lehodos laHashem
 [good it is to give thanks to Hashem],"
 and so on —
 which is the aspect of:
 "odecha b'yosher levav
 [I shall thank You with an upright heart],"
 and so on [Psalms 119:7] —
 for since on Shabbos one merits
 that the dispute in the heart is nullified —
 and one merits uprightness of heart [yosher lev] —
 therefore then it is good to give thanks to Hashem —
 and to pray with intention and blazing.
 And this:
 "lehagid baboker chasdecha
 [to declare in the morning Your lovingkindness]"
 — for the mental faculties
 are the aspects of the lovingkindnesses [chasadim] —
 as is well-known —
 and as also explained in Siman 56.
 That is — those questions
 that can be settled with the sacred intellect and mental faculties —
 then on Shabbos
 it is certainly easier to settle them —
 since the gates of the intellect open then.

 "V'emunascha baleilos
 [and Your faithfulness by night]"
 — that is, those questions
 that are the aspects of night and darkness —
 and it is impossible to find an answer to them —
 but one must rely on faith alone.
 Then likewise on Shabbos
 the faith is completed even more — as mentioned above.
 And therefore the eating of Shabbos is precious and very holy.
 For the essential rectification of eating
 and the clarification of foods in its perfection
 is through faith —
 and the perfection of faith
 is through the holiness of Shabbos —
 as mentioned above —
 and then the yichud [union]
 is in the aspect of face to face [panim b'fanim] —
 as explained in the writings of the holy Ari z"l.

 And the essential perfection
 and adornment of faith
 is to draw close specifically those who are distant —
 in the aspect of [Zephaniah 3:9]:
 "likro chulam b'shem Hashem
 [to call them all in the Name of Hashem],"
 and so on.
 And therefore regarding the guarding of Shabbos
 it is also stated:
 "v'gercha asher bish'arecha
 [and your stranger who is within your gates]"
 [Exodus 20:10] —
 and likewise:
 "u'vnay haneychar hanilavim al Hashem —
 v'chol haggid —
 kol shomer Shabbas —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'hevi'osim el har kodshi."
 And drawing the distant close
 is through the clarification of the letters of speech — and so on —
 as explained within.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "v'daber davar
 [and speaking words]"
 — stated regarding Shabbos —
 for then is the essential perfection of speech —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And because to elevate the sparks of speech
 fasting is required —
 and therefore it is explained in Shulchan Aruch,
 Orach Chayyim, Siman 249:
 that it is the practice of people of deed [anshay ma'aseh]
 to fast on Erev Shabbos —
 in particular when eating during the day
 would leave one without appetite to eat at night.
 But on Shabbos itself
 fasting is forbidden —
 for then the eating is very precious —
 in the aspect of the yichud of face to face.

 And therefore there is a mitzvah to eat fish on Shabbos —
 for our Sages of blessed memory taught
 [Midrash Rabbah, Bereishis, section 20]:
 that only three creatures
 interact face to face —
 and they are: the human — the serpent — the fish —
 and so on.
 And therefore one eats fish —
 to indicate that the eating of Shabbos
 is the aspect of the yichud of face to face.
 And this is the aspect of the twelve loaves of Shabbos —
 corresponding to the aspect of the lechem hapanim
 [the bread of the Presence] —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And therefore in the merit of the delight of Shabbos —
 he decrees a decree
 and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills it —
 as our Sages of blessed memory taught
 [Midrash Rabbah, Beshalach, section 25] —
 for at the time of the yichud
 made through this holy eating —
 then the Shechinah, as it were,
 entreats and pleads before G-d, blessed be He —
 to annul the compulsion of nature
 through the prayer of the Tzadik —
 so that they should know
 from the revealed to the hidden —
 that there is a G-d Who exists —
 Who does the will of the Tzadik —
 and as explained within.
 And therefore the Shabbos guardian —
 even if he worshipped idolatry, and so on —
 is forgiven —
 for through the peace of Shabbos
 all heresy and idolatry is nullified —
 and therefore he is forgiven —
 and as explained within —
 regarding the matter of:
 "chavur atzavim Efrayim — hanach lo
 [Efrayim is joined to idols — let him be]."
 [Hosea 4:17]

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha
 [if you return from Shabbos your foot]."
 "Regel
 [foot]" is the aspect of faith.
 And also — livelihood and eating
 is the aspect of legs —
 as brought in Siman 31.

 And also regel is the aspect of
 the drawing close of the distant —
 who are at the lower levels —
 the aspects of legs.
 And also regel is the aspect of speech —
 as explained in Siman 38.
 And this:
 "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi
 [from pursuing your affairs on My holy day]"
 — he should refrain
 from pursuing his weekday affairs —
 which distract the person
 and cover over the light of the sacred faith
 that renews itself each morning —
 in the aspect of:
 "nafkat b'tzafra —
 u'misakya b'yemama
 [it goes forth in the morning —
 and is covered in the daylight]"
 — as explained within.

 And also there are people
 who err even more, heaven forfend —
 and make the causes and their pursuing of affairs
 the essential thing —
 as if they were the means, heaven forfend,
 to draw the flow.
 But on Shabbos —
 all the acts and pursuits of the weekday are nullified —
 and then the light of faith shines in its perfection —
 and then one engages only in the affairs of Heaven —
 for then is drawn the aspect of peace —
 in the aspect of:
 "chafetz shalom avdo
 [His servant Whom He desires — peace]."
 [Isaiah 42:19]
 And likewise the gates of the intellect open —
 which are the aspects of divrey chefetz
 [words of desire/delight].
 And also — the mental faculties of faith
 are the aspects of truth —
 and as explained elsewhere —
 and it is written [Psalms 51:8]:
 "hen emes chafatzta
 [behold — truth is what You desire]."
 And also — the drawing close of the distant
 is the aspect of Torah shel Chesed
 [Torah of lovingkindness] —
 as explained in Siman 14.

 And it is written [Micah 7:18]:
 "ki chafetz chesed hu
 [for He desires lovingkindness]."
 And it is written [Ezekiel 18:23]:
 "hachafetz achphotz —
 v'chol haggid —
 ki im b'shuvo
 [do I truly desire —
 and so on —
 except in his repentance],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And also — the complete yichud of face to face
 is the aspect of [Isaiah 56:4]:
 "u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti
 [and choose that which I desire]"
 — as explained in the holy Zohar.

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg
 [and you shall call the Shabbos a delight]"
 — that is, the Shabbos meals —
 which are very holy —
 in the aspect of the aforementioned yichud of face to face.
 And also — the peace of Shabbos
 is the aspect of delight [oneg] —
 as it is written [Psalms 37:11]:
 "v'his'angu al rov shalom
 [and they shall delight in abundant peace]."
 And this likewise:
 "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad
 [the holy one of Hashem, honored]"
 — the aspect of the nullification of dispute —
 as it is written [Proverbs 20:3]:
 "kavod l'ish sheves meyriv
 [it is honor for a person to cease from strife]."

 And also — the mental faculties and the Da'as of Shabbos
 are the aspects of delight and honor —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And also — faith is the aspect of delight and honor —
 as it is written [Psalms 37:3]:
 "shkon eretz u're'eh emunah —
 v'his'anag al Hashem
 [dwell in the land and tend faithfulness —
 and delight in Hashem],"
 and so on —
 and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded
 this verse in its truth
 regarding the delight of Shabbos.
 And according to our subject matter here —
 this is very fitting —
 that is, for through faith
 the eating is rectified —
 in the aspect of:
 "u're'eh emunah
 [and tend faithfulness]"
 — as explained within.
 And the essential rectification of faith in its perfection
 is through the holiness of Shabbos.
 And therefore the eating of Shabbos is very precious —
 for this is the aspect of
 the commandment of the delight of Shabbos —
 which is a very great matter —
 and through this one merits
 that all the desires of one's heart are fulfilled —
 and he decrees a decree and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills it.

 And this is what it concluded:
 "v'his'anag al Hashem —
 v'yiten lecha mishalos libecha
 [and delight in Hashem —
 and He will give you the desires of your heart]"
 — and as explained in the aforementioned Midrash.
 And also — faith is the aspect of Malchus —
 the aspect of honor —
 the aspect of:
 "v'chevodo hi emunasi
 [and His honor — it is my faith]"
 — as mentioned above many times.
 And this:
 "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha
 [and honor it — from pursuing your own ways]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 "she'lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah
 [one should not take large strides]"
 — that is, so as not to confuse the thought
 from contemplating —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And then the pathways of the intellect
 would be blocked —
 and one would not know how to answer
 even those questions
 that one is permitted to examine.
 And also it wished to say
 one should not take large strides —
 that is, for even though
 the pathways of the intellect open then —
 and one knows how to answer —
 nonetheless one must be deliberate in the matter —
 and not enter into questions
 that it is forbidden to examine.
 But in them one should rely on faith alone.
 And this:
 "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar
 [from pursuing your affairs — and speaking words]"
 — one should not speak any weekday speech —
 so as not to blemish through this
 the holiness of the sacred Shabbos speech mentioned above.
 "Az tis'anag al Hashem —
 da Atika Kadisha
 [then you will delight in Hashem —
 this is the Holy Ancient One]"
 — that is, one merits through this
 such exalted mental faculties —
 that are the aspects of Atika —
 which are the aspects of the mental faculties
 that will be revealed in the future —
 as explained in the teaching
 Atika Tamir v'Satim, Siman 21.
 "V'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz —
 da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin
 [and I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth —
 this is the Holy Apple Orchard]"
 — that is, Malchus receives illumination
 from all the aspects — and also from Chab"d —
 that is, faith — the aspect of Malchus —
 is completed through the fact
 that the pathways of the intellect open —
 as mentioned above.
 And our Sages expounded:
 one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms —
 which comes only through heresy and blemish of faith —
 as explained in Siman 7.

 "V'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha —
 da Ze'ir Anpin
 [and I will feed you with the heritage of Yaakov your father —
 this is Ze'ir Anpin]"
 — that is, the aspect of the holy Torah —
 the aspect of the study of the legal decisors [limmud poskin] —
 which is the aspect of peace —
 through which all kinds of dispute are nullified —
 and the pathways of the intellect open for him.
 And our Sages expounded:
 one merits an inheritance without limits —
 that is, for the holy Torah
 draws illumination from the most exalted mental faculties
 down to the very end of all levels —
 which are the aspects of faith — the aspect of Malchus —
 and through this
 the pathways of the intellect open for him —
 to settle all the questions
 that can be settled.
 And as for those questions
 that it is forbidden to examine —
 he relies on his strong and complete faith —
 which is the aspect of inheritance without limits.

 For all the aspects of the questions and the constraints
 are nullified.
 And also one merits to clarify
 the sparks of the letters of speech in their perfection —
 until through this it is fulfilled [Zephaniah 3:9]:
 "ki az ehpoch el kol ha'amim —
 safah verurah —
 likro chulam b'shem Hashem
 [for then I shall turn to all the peoples —
 a pure tongue —
 to call them all in the Name of Hashem]"
 — which is the aspect of inheritance without limits.

 And this [Isaiah 58:14]:
 "ki pi Hashem diber
 [for the mouth of Hashem has spoken]."
 For on Shabbos
 is drawn the aspect of the perfection of sacred speech —
 which is the aspect of the opening of the pathways of the intellect —
 the aspect of [Proverbs 2:6]:
 "mipiv da'as u'sevunah
 [from His mouth — knowledge and understanding]."
 And also — speech is the aspect of Malchus peh [Malchus — the mouth] —
 the aspect of faith —
 the aspect of [Psalms 89:2]:
 "odiyah emunascha b'fi
 [I shall make known Your faithfulness with my mouth]."
 And also — speech is the aspect of peace —
 as explained in Siman 239.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "adabra na shalom
 [I shall now speak of peace]."
 [Psalms 85:9]
 And also — the essential drawing close of the distant
 is through speech —
 in the aspect of the aforementioned pure tongue.
 And also — the holy eating
 is drawn from the aspect of speech —
 in the aspect of [Ezekiel 41:22]:
 "vayedaber elai: zeh hashulchan asher lifney Hashem
 [and he spoke to me: this is the table that is before Hashem]"
 — that is, the eating —
 which is the aspect of the yichud of face to face —
 and therefore our Sages expounded on this:
 "shulchan mechaper
 [the table atones],"
 and so on.
 For then faith — which is the aspect of the Shechinah —
 advocates on behalf of the distant —
 to forgive them and draw them close —
 as explained within.
