"LiKdosh Hashem mechubbad" = honor = garments = garments = makifin = "sovev kol almin" = merits to attain secret of chalal hapanui = aspect of garments (within). "V'chibadto / lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah" = anger = "al tirgazu badarech" = don't give sustenance to questions from chalal hapanui = contraction and judgment = "b'sechilah alah b'machshavah livros olam b'midas hadin" = as it were anger and dispute; but in truth everything = only for revelation of His mercy. "Mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" = revelation of divinity within creation = letters and speech = but take great care not to cause breaking of vessels through excess of speech = "v'chol hamarbeh devarim." "Az tis'anag al Hashem" = delight in clinging to Ein Sof = "sovev kol almin" = "al Hashem" (well-known); Zohar: "da Atika" = attainment of World to Come = "oraissa d'Atika"; Tzadikim will then attain secret of contraction of chalal hapanui; Sages: "nositin lo kol mishalos libo" = opposite of heaviness of heart re chalal hapanui. "Hirkavticha" = subdue husks = Malchus d'Sitra Achra from sheviyas hakelim; saved from subjugation of kingdoms. "Heritage of Yaakov" = creation of worlds within chalal hapanui = for revelation of His mercy = Yaakov = midas harachamim; Sages: "olami olami mi vera'acha Yaakov vera'acha"; Zohar: "da Ze'ir Anpin" = all traits = the worlds; Ze'ir Anpin itself called a world (Zohar). "Ki pi Hashem diber" = in the worlds there are letters and utterances = creation through speech = "b'dvar Hashem shamayim na'asu" (Psalms 33:6); within speech there is wisdom = "ki Hashem yiten chochmah mipiv da'as u'sevunah" (Proverbs 2:6).

 Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman

 Siman 65 — Vayomar Boaz

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 65 — סימן סה
 Vayomar Boaz — "And Boaz said…" — Shabbos is the supernal field
 [Likutay Moharan I, Siman 65]

 Shabbos is the aspect of the supernal field [sadeh ha'elyonah] —
 for there all the souls of Israel grow —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "Shabbas vayinafash
 [He rested and was refreshed]"
 [Exodus 31:17] —
 for Shabbos is the world of souls.
 For it is the root of all the souls of Israel —
 and from there all the souls flower —
 as explained in the holy Zohar
 and in Sefer haBahir —
 and as mentioned above many times.
 And this is likewise the secret of
 Chakla Tupichin Kadishin
 [the Holy Apple Orchard] —
 stated regarding Shabbos —
 and as explained in the writings of the holy Ari z"l
 in the secret of what
 one goes out to the field
 to receive the Shabbos.
 And also — Shabbos is the aspect of
 the master of the field [ba'al hasadeh] —
 who strives with all the rectifications of the field —
 and to rectify the souls
 and bring them in, and so on —
 as explained within.
 For the holiness of Shabbos encompasses many aspects —
 as understood in the holy Zohar and in the writings.
 And this [Exodus 35:1]:
 "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Bnay Yisrael
 [and Moshe gathered the entire congregation
 of the children of Israel]."

 Moshe is the "ba'alah d'Matroniyta
 [husband of the Matron]"
 — who is the aspect of the aforementioned field —
 as is well-known.
 And then they were commanded
 regarding the work of the Mishkan —
 which alludes to the building
 of the full stature of the Shechinah, as it were
 (as is well-known —
 and as also brought above within in Siman 2)
 — which is itself the aspect of the aforementioned sacred field —
 as is well-known.
 And they were also commanded regarding Shabbos —
 for through the entire holiness of Shabbos —
 all the souls of the congregation of the children of Israel
 are assembled and brought in
 to the holiness of the aforementioned field —
 even those souls that were driven out to the outside,
 heaven forfend —
 for this is the aspect of what our Sages taught:
 even if one worshipped idolatry, and so on —
 he is forgiven — and so on.
 And this itself is likewise the aspect of
 the extra soul
 that each individual of Israel merits to receive on Shabbos.

 And this is what is explained in Zohar Chadash:
 that the rectification of the souls of the wicked,
 heaven forfend —
 all comes through the holiness of Shabbos.

 And this is what is explained
 in the writings of the holy Ari z"l:
 that on every Erev Shabbos —
 Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him,
 descends with other great Tzadikim —
 to elevate the souls of the living and the dead
 that fell into the depths of the husks —
 as mentioned above —
 that he engages in the rectifications —
 to raise them from their fallen state —
 and to bring them inside the sacred field —
 as mentioned above.
 And because the aforementioned master of the field
 endures great suffering [yisurin] —
 and things that are very harsh and bitter —
 and with his great strength and righteousness
 he passes through all of them —
 and performs the work of the field as required —
 and as explained within —
 therefore our Sages taught:
 "Shabbas b'Marah nitztavu
 [Shabbos was commanded at Marah]"
 — the aspect of the bitterness [mirirus]
 and the suffering
 that the aforementioned master of the field endures —
 which is the aspect of Shabbos.
 And therefore the Tanna began the labors
 [the thirty-nine categories of labor] with:
 av melachos — and so on —
 "hacharesh v'hazore'a v'hakotzer
 [the one who plows and the one who sows
 and the one who reaps],"
 and so on —
 which are the labors of the field in the material sense —
 during the weekday pursuits —
 and they were also in the work of the Mishkan —
 which is the aspect of the aforementioned sacred field —
 but on Shabbos all of them are forbidden.
 For then all the rectifications of the field
 are drawn in wondrous perfection
 through the holiness of Shabbos.
 And when the souls —
 which are the growths of the aforementioned field —
 are rectified —
 then it is very good and beautiful to pray —
 for then the prayer is in its rectification —
 as explained within.

 And this [Psalms 92:2]:
 Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas:
 "tov lehodos laHashem —
 v'lezamre lishimcha elyon
 [good it is to give thanks to Hashem —
 and to sing praises to Your Name — Most High]"
 — for then the prayer is in its rectification.

 And when the souls produce fruit —
 doing the will of the Omnipresent —
 then the eyes of the master of the field illuminate —
 and so on.
 And this is the aspect of Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of:
 "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein
 [three colors of the eye and the pupil]"
 — as brought in the Tikunim.

 And when the eyes of the master of the field illuminate —
 then he is able to look at each person —
 to bring him to the ultimate purpose [tachlis] —
 and so on —
 and then the speech is as it should be — in its perfection.
 That is — the speech is in one aspect —
 that in each and every word of the prayer —
 all the words of the prayer should be encompassed —
 and when one stands at the end of the prayer —
 one should still be standing in the first word of the prayer —
 and not be separated from it either —
 for this is the aspect of the ultimate purpose —
 which is the aspect of entirely good —
 entirely one —
 the aspect of [Zechariah 14:9]:
 "bayom hahu yihyeh Hashem echad —
 u'shemo echad
 [on that day Hashem will be One —
 and His Name will be One],"
 and so on —
 as explained within.

 And this is the aspect of Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the ultimate purpose —
 for it is the ultimate purpose of the work of heaven and earth —
 and it is a foretaste of the World to Come —
 which is the ultimate purpose —
 and then:
 "yihyeh Hashem echad u'shemo echad."
 For this is the aspect of what is explained
 in the teaching of the holy Zohar —
 recited at the entry of Shabbos:
 "k'govana d'inun mis'yachadin l'eila b'echad —
 v'chol haggid —
 ad d'is'abed b'raza d'echad —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'ha ukimna: raza d'Hashem echad u'shemo echad.
 Raza d'Shabbas — ihi Shabbas —
 d'is'achat b'raza d'echad —
 v'chol haggid —
 tzalutha d'ma'alay Shabbata —
 d'ha is'achat kurs'aya yekira kadisha —
 b'raza d'echad
 [in the manner that they unite above in the One —
 and so on —
 until it is made in the secret of the One —
 and so on —
 and thus we have established: the secret of Hashem is One and His Name is One.
 The secret of Shabbos — it is Shabbos —
 that is united in the secret of the One —
 and so on —
 the prayer of Erev Shabbos —
 for then the precious holy throne is united —
 in the secret of the One],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And this is what our Sages expounded [Psalms 139:16]:
 "yamim yotzaru — v'lo echad bahem
 [days were formed — and none among them]"
 — "lo [none]"
 is read as "lo echad bahem
 [to Him — one among them]":
 "zeh Shabbas
 [this is Shabbos]."
 For Shabbos is the aspect of entirely one —
 and therefore all six weekdays are also encompassed in it —
 as it is written:
 "ki sheshes yamim —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayanuach b'yom hashevi'i
 [for in six days —
 and so on —
 and He rested on the seventh day]"
 [Exodus 31:17] —
 and as explained in the holy Zohar.
 And likewise in the holy Zohar it is stated:
 "ein tov ela Shabbas
 [there is no good but Shabbos],"
 and so on —
 for Shabbos is the aspect of entirely good —
 entirely one —
 which is the aspect of the ultimate purpose — as mentioned above.
 And therefore all judgments and suffering are nullified on it —
 as it is written [Isaiah 14:3]:
 "b'yom hanicach Hashem lecha mei'atzevecha —
 u'mira'gzecha
 [on the day Hashem gives you rest from your pain —
 and from your anger],"
 and so on —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 And one does not ask for one's needs on it —
 so as not to be reminded of one's pain —
 as our Sages taught.
 For when one merits to look toward the ultimate purpose —
 then all kinds of pain and suffering are nullified —
 for the ultimate purpose is the aspect of entirely good —
 and as explained within.
 For the essential pain that a person has from suffering
 comes only because it takes away his Da'as
 — until he is unable to look toward the ultimate purpose —
 which is entirely good —
 and as explained within.
 But on Shabbos —
 when the illumination of Da'as and mental faculties
 is drawn upon each person of Israel —
 as mentioned above many times —
 and therefore all kinds of pain and suffering are nullified on it —
 through the fact that one merits to look
 toward the ultimate purpose —
 which is itself the aspect of Shabbos — as mentioned above.

 And this itself is likewise the aspect of
 the extra soul that one merits on Shabbos.

 For the ultimate purpose
 is the aspect of Shabbos — the world of souls —
 as explained in Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 39 —
 in the teaching Leku Chazu — and so on.
 And therefore Shabbos is called
 from the language of nullification [bitul] —
 as mentioned above many times.
 For then one merits
 to truly nullify oneself toward the ultimate purpose.
 And this is what our Sages taught:
 "keivan she'shavas —
 (ferush Rashi: she'yatza haShabbas) —
 vav — avdah nefesh
 [since it rested —
 (Rashi explains: when Shabbos went out) —
 vav [woe] — the soul was lost]."

 For when one returns and comes back
 from the nullification to the vessels of the mental faculties —
 then the suffering intensifies even more
 than it was before the nullification —
 as explained within.
 And therefore when Shabbos goes out —
 one feels even more
 the pain and the suffering —
 which are the aspects of the afflictions of the soul [nig'ey hanefesh] —
 and therefore one cries out:
 "vav — avdah nefesh
 [woe — the soul was lost]."
 And from this itself —
 one can know and understand
 that one merited on Shabbos
 the extra soul —
 through the aspect of the nullification
 and looking toward the ultimate purpose —
 from which it follows that after Shabbos —
 the suffering and the judgments
 want to intensify even more, heaven forfend —
 for this is the aspect of:
 "vav — avdah nefesh."

 But through the joy [simchah]
 that one merits through the nullification
 toward the ultimate purpose —
 which is the aspect of the great joy of Shabbos —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 And joy is the vessel [keli] for Torah novellae —
 and therefore everyone agrees
 that on Shabbos the Torah was given —
 and then one reads the Torah
 through all the weekly portions in their perfection.
 And also — it is a great mitzvah
 to produce Torah novellae on Shabbos —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 And through the Torah novellae
 one merits through the impression [rishimo]
 of the nullification —
 through this the suffering is cooled afterward.
 And this is the aspect of what
 on Shabbos at Minchah
 they immediately begin to read in the Torah
 the portion of the coming Shabbos.
 And this [Exodus 15:22–23]:
 "vayeilchu sheloshet yamim bamidbar —
 v'lo matze'u mayim —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayavo'u Marasah
 [and they went three days in the desert —
 and found no water —
 and so on —
 and they came to Marah],"
 and so on —
 and our Sages expounded
 [Tractate Bava Kama 82a]:
 that they went three days without Torah —
 and the prophets arose and instituted for them
 that they should read from the Torah
 on Shabbos at Minchah
 and on Monday and Thursday — and so on.
 And therefore this was juxtaposed
 to the passage:
 "vayavo'u Maratah —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayorehu Hashem etz
 [and they came to Marah —
 and so on —
 and Hashem showed him a tree],"
 and so on [Exodus 15:23, 25] —
 and there they were commanded regarding Shabbos —
 as mentioned above.

 And therefore — for the most part —
 the revelation of Torah novellae
 of the great Tzadikim
 is on Shabbos at Minchah —
 at the third meal —
 and as also understood in
 Midrash Mishlei, section 31 —
 from the sons of Rabbi Meir.
 For precisely because
 the holiness of Shabbos begins to depart —
 which is the aspect of returning and coming back
 from the nullification toward the ultimate purpose
 to the vessels of the mental faculties —
 and then — from the impression of the nullification —
 Torah novellae are made — as mentioned above —
 and through this the suffering is cooled —
 and the thirst of the soul is quenched.
 And therefore one says
 on Erev Shabbos at Minchah
 in the psalm [Psalms 107:33–37]:
 "Hodu —
 yasem neharos l'midbar —
 u'motzaey mayim l'tzimmaon —
 eretz peri l'melacha —
 v'chol haggid
 [Give thanks —
 He turns rivers into desert —
 and springs of water into thirst —
 a fruitful land into salt —
 and so on],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 For the soul is the daughter of the intellect —
 as explained within.
 And therefore on Shabbos —
 when the intellect is in its perfection —
 the soul is in its perfection
 and produces fruit.
 And this is the aspect of [Psalms 1:3]:
 "asher piryo yiten b'ito
 [who gives its fruit in its season]"
 — which our Sages expounded regarding the Shabbos union.
 And when the holiness of Shabbos departs —
 which is the perfection of the sacred intellect and mental faculties —
 then the soul is in the aspect of thirst —
 the aspect of:
 "eretz peri l'melacha
 [a fruitful land into salt]"
 — as understood within.
 And this is the aspect of:
 "vav — avdah nefesh"
 — which is the feeling of the suffering
 during the six weekdays.
 But afterward —
 through the fact that one returns
 and comes back to the holiness of the second Shabbos —
 through this:
 "yasem midbar l'agam mayim —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayizre'u sadosמות —
 v'chol haggid —
 vaya'asu peri tevu'ah
 [He turns the desert into a pool of water —
 and so on —
 and they sow fields —
 and so on —
 and they make fruit of the grain]"
 — the aspect of the rectifications of the aforementioned field —
 and the souls produce fruit — as mentioned above.
 And likewise the beginning of the psalm
 is also on this matter:
 "ta'u b'midbar —
 v'chol haggid —
 re'evim gam tzeme'im —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayitz'aku —
 v'chol haggid —
 yodu laHashem chasdo —
 v'chol haggid —
 ki hisbia nefesh shokekah
 [they wandered in the desert —
 and so on —
 hungry and also thirsty —
 and so on —
 and they cried out —
 and so on —
 they shall give thanks to Hashem for His lovingkindness —
 and so on —
 for He satisfied the yearning soul],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And this is likewise the aspect of [Isaiah 55:1, 2]:
 "hoy kol tzame —
 lechu la'mayim —
 v'chol haggid —
 shim'u shamo'a elai va'ichlu tov —
 v'sisanag b'deshen nafshechem
 [ho — all who thirst —
 come to the waters —
 and so on —
 hearken — hearken to Me and eat what is good —
 and let your soul delight in abundance]."
 And this is likewise the aspect of the delight of Shabbos.

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha
 [if you return from Shabbos your foot]"
 — that is, not to go beyond the Shabbos boundary.
 For through the holiness of Shabbos —
 all the souls of Israel are rectified —
 and return and come back
 and are encompassed within the aforementioned sacred field —
 and then each person —
 according to his aspect —
 establishes rest [shevisah] in his place —
 and it is forbidden for him
 to go beyond the Shabbos boundary —
 in the aspect of:
 "al yetzei ish mimekomo
 [let no person go out from his place],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 [Exodus 16:29]
 For one who goes beyond the Shabbos boundary —
 through this his soul and spirit
 are driven out and exit
 from the holiness of the aforementioned sacred field.
 And then it is very difficult for it
 to return there —
 and as also understood within.
 And also —
 "raglecha
 [your foot]"
 is the aspect of prayer —
 and the aspect of speech —
 and as explained elsewhere —
 and all of this is rectified
 through the holiness of Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 as mentioned above.

 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi
 [from pursuing your affairs on My holy day]"
 — not to pursue one's affairs on Shabbos.
 For in order to nullify oneself toward this ultimate purpose —
 and to look upon it in its full perfection —
 one must close one's eyes
 from the sight of this world
 "michizvo d'hai alma
 [the vision of this world]"
 (which are the aspects of the weekday pursuits
 of the six days of deed — entirely).
 And this [Exodus 16:29]:
 "re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas
 [see — for Hashem has given you the Shabbos]"
 — "re'u
 [see]" — specifically.
 For through the holiness of Shabbos —
 one's eyes illuminate with great holiness —
 and one merits to look toward the ultimate purpose —
 which is itself the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos.
 And this is why He gives them
 on the sixth day bread for two days —
 so that they should not need
 to perform any act on Shabbos —
 and not even to think
 any thought whatsoever for the sake of livelihood
 and the needs of this world —
 as during the weekdays —
 when they had to wait expectantly
 for the falling of the manna
 and would go out to gather.
 But on Shabbos —
 one must close one's eyes
 completely from all aspects of:
 "chizvo d'hai alma
 [the sight of this world]."
 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg
 [and you shall call the Shabbos a delight]"
 — for when one merits
 to close one's eyes completely from the sight of this world —
 and to look only toward the ultimate purpose —
 through this one is saved
 from all the afflictions of the soul —
 in the aspect of [Ruth 2:8–9]:
 "halo tziviitי es hane'arim —
 l'vilti nega'ech
 [have I not commanded the young men —
 not to touch you?]"
 — as explained within.
 And then one merits
 the delight of holiness —
 which is the opposite of the affliction [nega] —
 in the aspect of:
 "ein l'ma'alah mei'oneg —
 v'ein l'matah minegah
 [there is nothing higher than delight —
 and nothing lower than affliction]"
 — as is well-known.
 And this is the aspect of the excellence
 of the holiness of the Shabbos delight —
 for then even the physical pleasures [ta'anugey haguf]
 are of great holiness —
 since one merits to look only toward the ultimate purpose.
 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad
 [the holy one of Hashem, honored]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 "ein kavod ela Torah
 [there is no honor but Torah]"
 — that is, the aspect of the renewal of the Torah —
 one merits through the impression of the nullification
 toward the ultimate purpose.
 And also — because the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 this is the essential perfection of the intellect —
 and the rectification of the soul —
 as understood within.
 And the perfection of the intellect —
 there is the essential delight and honor —
 as mentioned above many times.
 And likewise — the rectification of the soul
 is the aspect of honor —
 as explained elsewhere.
 And it is the aspect of delight —
 the aspect of [Isaiah 55:2]:
 "v'sisanag b'deshen nafshechem
 [and let your soul delight in abundance]"
 — as mentioned above.
 And this is the aspect of the holiness
 of the delight and honor of Shabbos.
 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha
 [and honor it — from pursuing your own ways]"
 — and our Sages expounded:
 one should not take large strides —
 for large strides confuse the thought
 from contemplating —
 and then it is difficult for him
 to nullify himself toward the ultimate purpose
 with a pure and proper thought in its perfection.
 And this [Isaiah 58:13]:
 "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar
 [from pursuing your affairs — and speaking words]"
 — one should not speak any words
 about the matters of his affairs —
 so as not to blemish through this
 the holiness of Shabbos —
 which is the aspect of the nullification
 toward the ultimate purpose in its perfection.
 And our Sages expounded from this:
 one should not ask for one's needs on Shabbos —
 for through the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 all deficiencies and suffering are nullified —
 for there — everything is entirely good —
 entirely one — as mentioned above.
 And this is the aspect of:
 one is given all the desires of his heart —
 as our Sages taught
 regarding one who delights the Shabbos —
 in the aspect of:
 "v'his'anag al Hashem —
 (zeh ikkar bechinah haTachlis) —
 v'yiten lecha mishalos libecha
 [and delight in Hashem —
 (this is the essential aspect of the ultimate purpose) —
 and He will give you the desires of your heart]."
 [Psalms 37:4]

 And this [Isaiah 58:14]:
 "az tis'anag al Hashem
 [then you will delight in Hashem]"
 — that is, one merits
 the aspect of true clinging [devekus amitiy]
 and nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 at the ultimate perfection and at the highest
 and most wondrous level —
 for even within the aspect of nullification
 toward the ultimate purpose —
 there are many many aspects and very many levels.
 And this is what the holy Zohar expounded:
 "da Atika
 [this is Atika]"
 — which is the aspect of:
 "al Hashem
 [upon Hashem]"
 — as is well-known —
 which is the aspect of the nullification and clinging
 that is supreme — wondrous — and awesome — as is well-known.

 "V'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz —
 da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin
 [and I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth —
 this is the Holy Apple Orchard]"
 — the aspect of the rectification
 of the aforementioned supernal field in its perfection.
 And in the writings of the holy Ari z"l
 it is explained that this alludes to
 the ascent of Malchus
 — which is the aspect of the aforementioned field —
 to the aspects of the mental faculties —
 that is: the perfection of the rectification
 and the growth of the soul
 — which is the aspect of Malchus — as is well-known —
 through the intellect —
 as explained within.
 For the soul is the daughter of the intellect.
 And this is likewise the aspect of:
 שׁב"ת —
 שׁ'ין ב'ת':
 שׁ'ין
 is the aspect of the mental faculties and intellect —
 as is well-known — and as explained elsewhere.
 And ב'ת'
 is the aspect of the soul — as mentioned above.
 And our Sages expounded on this:
 one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms —
 which are from the aspect of [Genesis 25:27]:
 "Esav ish sadeh
 [Esav the man of the field]"
 — the aspect of the field of the Sitra Achra.
 For the soul
 that goes out and is driven from the sacred field —
 is immediately trapped, heaven forfend,
 in the net of the Sitra Achra —
 which is the aspect of the subjugation of kingdoms.
 And through the holiness of Shabbos
 one is saved from them.
 And this:
 "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha —
 da Ze'ir Anpin
 [and I will feed you with the heritage of Yaakov your father —
 this is Ze'ir Anpin]"
 — which is the aspect of the holy Torah — as is well-known.

 And this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 33:4]:
 "Torah tzivvah lanu Moshe —
 morasha kehillas Yaakov
 [the Torah that Moshe commanded us —
 the heritage of the congregation of Yaakov]"
 — that is, one merits
 the renewal of the Torah —
 drawn from the aspect of the impression of the nullification —
 as mentioned above.
 And our Sages expounded on this:
 one merits an inheritance without limits —
 that is, all kinds of suffering —
 which are the aspects of constraints [mitzarim] for the person —
 are nullified.
 For the essential rectification of suffering in its perfection
 is through the renewal of the Torah mentioned above —
 as explained within.
 And also —
 an inheritance without limits
 is the aspect of entirely one — mentioned above —
 through which the speech and the prayer are completed —
 to be in the aspect of simple unity —
 that even when one is at the last word
 of the final word of the prayer —
 one is still encompassed and connected
 with the aspect of the beginning of the first word of the prayer —
 which is the aspect of completely above the boundary and constraint —
 the aspect of an inheritance without limits.
 And this [Isaiah 58:14]:
 "ki pi Hashem diber
 [for the mouth of Hashem has spoken]."
 For one merits
 that the words of one's prayer
 are literally the aspects of the words of Hashem —
 the aspect of [Isaiah 59:21]:
 "v'asim devarai b'ficha
 [and I shall place My words in your mouth]."
 And the words of Hashem are
 in the aspect of simple unity mentioned above —
 the aspect of [Psalms 62:12]:
 "achas diber Elokim
 [one thing G-d has spoken],"
 and so on —
 and as our Sages expounded.
 And this is what is brought elsewhere —
 and it is also connected to this teaching:
 that אח"ד
 [echad — one] —
 initial letters of:
 ד'ברי א'לקים ח'יים
 [divray Elokim chayyim — the words of the living G-d].
 For the words of the living G-d
 are in the aspect of simple unity — mentioned above.
 And therefore — even though this one forbids
 and that one permits —
 these and those are the words of the living G-d —
 for there — two opposites are encompassed
 in a single subject — and so on —
 and as explained elsewhere.

 And this is likewise the aspect of:
 ע'דן נ'הר ג'ן
 — initial letters: ענ"ג
 [oneg — delight] —
 as explained in the holy Zohar.
 "Eden"
 is the aspect of the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 as explained within.
 "Nahar
 [river]"
 is the aspect of the drawing forth of the Torah —
 which is the aspect of water —
 through which the thirst of the soul is quenched —
 and it is rectified.
 And the soul is the aspect of
 "Gan
 [garden]"
 — as explained within.
 And also — Eden is the aspect of the ultimate purpose —
 the aspect of:
 "ayin lo ra'asah
 [no eye has seen]."
 [Isaiah 64:3]
 Gan is the aspect of the aforementioned supernal field.
 The river going out from Eden to water the Gan
 is the aspect of the master of the field —
 who engages in the rectifications of the field —
 and this is the aspect of Yaakov and Yosef —
 the aspects of Tiferes and Yesod.
 For Tiferes is the aspect of:
 "ba'alah d'Matroniyta
 [the husband of the Matron]"
 — as is well-known.

 And therefore all the souls of Israel
 are called by the name of Yaakov and Yosef —
 for from them is the root of their growth.
 And therefore the essential subjugation of Esav —
 the man of the field of the Sitra Achra —
 is only through them —
 as our Sages taught:
 "eileh toledos Yaakov — Yosef
 [these are the generations of Yaakov — Yosef],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 [Genesis 37:2]
 And this is what is stated regarding Yaakov —
 when he came close to Charan —
 where he engaged in clarifying and gathering
 from the house of Lavan —
 the souls of Israel —
 who are the trees and the grasses
 that grew in the aforementioned garden and field —
 it is stated there [Genesis 29:2]:
 "vayar v'hineh be'er basadeh
 [and he saw — and behold — a well in the field],"
 and so on —
 that is, he saw the illumination of the river
 going out from Eden — mentioned above —
 which is the aspect of the well —
 and the flowing stream that waters the field.
 And likewise afterward —
 when G-d, blessed be He, said to him
 to return to the Land of Israel —
 it is stated [Genesis 31:4]:
 "vayikra l'Rachel u'l'Leah hasadeh
 [and he called Rachel and Leah to the field],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 And likewise afterward —
 when he came to the Land of Israel —
 it is stated [Genesis 33:18]:
 "vayavo Yaakov shaleim —
 ir Shechem asher b'eretz Kena'an —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayichan es pnay ha'ir
 [and Yaakov came whole —
 to the city of Shechem that is in the Land of Canaan —
 and so on —
 and he encamped before the city]"
 — and from this our Sages expounded:
 that he established boundaries [techum]
 and guarded the Shabbos —
 through which is the essential rectification of the field mentioned above.
 And therefore it is stated immediately:
 "vayiken es chelkas hasadeh
 [and he acquired a portion of the field],"
 and so on. [וכו']
 [Genesis 33:19]
 (And there is more to explain in this — but this is not the place for it.)
 And afterward —
 Shechem was given to Yosef —
 of whom it is also stated
 that he guarded the Shabbos —
 as our Sages taught.

 And therefore Yosef recounted in his dream [Genesis 37:7]:
 "v'hineh anachnu me'almim alumim b'soch hasadeh —
 v'Targumo: mesar'in asrin b'go chakla
 [and behold — we are binding sheaves in the midst of the field —
 and the Targum: binding bundles in the midst of the field]"
 — for all the tribes were great Tzadikim —
 and all of them engaged in the rectifications
 of the aforementioned field —
 through which the prayer is rectified —
 which is like the parable
 of the person who walks in the field
 and gathers beautiful lilies and flowers — and so on —
 and makes one bundle —
 and then gathers again
 and makes another bundle — and so on —
 and as explained within.
 And therefore in truth
 there are twelve versions of prayer —
 corresponding to the twelve tribes.
 And also — because the essential perfection of prayer
 is to encompass it in complete unity — as mentioned above —
 which is the aspect of making bundles and binding-knots.
 For one binds and bundles all the prayer
 into a single bundle.
 And behold — all the tribes who were the sons of Yaakov
 had a share in these rectifications.
 (But):
 "v'hineh kamah alumasi —
 v'gam nitzavah —
 v'hineh tesuvenah alumoseichem —
 v'hishtachavina le'alumasi
 [and behold — my sheaf arose —
 and also stood upright —
 and behold — your sheaves surrounded —
 and bowed down to my sheaf]"
 [Genesis 37:7] —
 that is — for the essential completion
 of the perfect rectifications of the field —
 the rectification of prayer —
 is through him —
 for he is:
 "gannana d'ginata
 [the gardener of the garden]"
 — as is well-known.
 And therefore afterward —
 when the tribes became jealous of him and sold him —
 it is stated [Genesis 37:14–15]:
 "vayishla'cheyhu mei'emek Chevron —
 vayavo Shichmah —
 vayimtza'eyhu ish —
 v'hineh so'eh basadeh
 [and he sent him from the valley of Chevron —
 and he came to Shechem —
 and a man found him —
 and behold — he was wandering in the field]"
 — and it is stated afterward —
 "vayevk osav aviv
 [and his father wept over him]"
 — the aspect of:
 "sadeh bochim
 [the weeping field]"
 — as explained within.
 And likewise afterward —
 when the tribes came to Egypt to Yosef —
 it is stated there many times of weeping —
 as it is written:
 "vayasov mei'aleihem vayevk
 [and he turned away from them and wept]"
 [Genesis 42:24] —
 and likewise:
 "vayevakesh livkos
 [and he sought to weep]"
 [Genesis 43:30] —
 and likewise:
 "vayiten es kolo bivchi
 [and he raised his voice in weeping]"
 [Genesis 45:2] —
 and likewise many others.
 And likewise afterward —
 when the tribes came before Yosef
 after the passing of Yaakov —
 to exculpate themselves before him —
 it is stated [Genesis 50:17]:
 "vayevk Yosef b'dabram eilav
 [and Yosef wept as they spoke to him]."
 And through the selling of Yosef —
 it came about that our Patriarchs descended to Egypt —
 for this is the aspect of the blemish
 of the aforementioned field —
 that all the souls that grow in it
 were, as it were, expelled and driven from there —
 and descended to Egypt —
 which is the counterpart of the aforementioned Gan —
 as it is written [Genesis 13:10]:
 "k'gan Hashem k'eretz Mitzrayim
 [like the garden of Hashem — like the land of Egypt]."
 And therefore it is also stated regarding Moshe [Exodus 2:6]:
 "v'hineh na'ar bocheh
 [and behold — a child was weeping],"
 and so on. [וכו']

 And therefore the essential rectification
 of the sin of the selling of Yosef
 is through the guarding of Shabbos —
 as explained in Zohar Chadash.
 For all the rectifications of the field
 by the aforementioned master of the field —
 all are encompassed in the holiness of Shabbos —
 as mentioned above.
 And because the rectifications of the aforementioned field
 in their perfection
 are a very great and arduous labor —
 until sometimes great Tzadikim —
 who are the aspects of the masters of the field —
 must depart for the sake of this —
 as understood within.
 And this is the aspect of the departure
 of Yosef — Moshe — David —
 on Shabbos at Minchah.
 And they themselves are likewise
 the aspects of Eden, Nahar, Gan — as mentioned above.
 And they are the aspects of
 the perfect rectifications of the field —
 which is the aspect of the perfection of prayer —
 that it should be in the aspect of unity.
 And therefore one says then —
 at the Minchah prayer:
 "Atah echad
 [You are One],"
 and so on —
 for then Ze'ir Anpin and Malchus
 ascend in very great ascents —
 as is well-known —
 and then there shines with wondrous illumination
 the aspect of the light of the ultimate purpose —
 which is the aspect of:
 "bayom hahu yihyeh Hashem echad
 [on that day Hashem will be One],"
 and so on —
 as explained within.
 And this is likewise the aspect of Musaf of Shabbos —
 which corresponds to Yosef —
 as is well-known —
 as mentioned above.
 And this is what our Sages taught:
 all who pray on Erev Shabbos and say Vayechulu —
 it is as if one became a partner with the Holy One,
 blessed be He,
 in the act of creation — and so on.
 For in the passage of Vayechulu —
 it is explained that Shabbos is the aspect of
 the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 the aspect of:
 "vayechulu hashamayim v'ha'aretz —
 v'chol haggid —
 vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i
 [and the heavens and the earth were completed —
 and so on —
 and G-d completed on the seventh day],"
 and so on —
 "vayechal
 [completed]" — literally —
 in its plain meaning —
 the aspect of the ultimate purpose —
 for then everything will be nullified
 to be encompassed in His unity, blessed be He, literally.
 For through the holiness of Shabbos —
 one merits to cling to G-d, blessed be He —
 and to nullify oneself toward the ultimate purpose —
 until one goes out then —
 as a person — as it were —
 completely from the category of creation —
 and then one is above the traits —
 above even the vessels of the mental faculties —
 and truly encompassed in His unity, blessed be He —
 and as also understood within.
 And through this —
 the essential perfection of the prayer of the holy Shabbos.
 And therefore one recites the passage of Vayechulu
 in the first prayer of Shabbos.
 And therefore it is as if one became a partner with the Holy One,
 blessed be He, in the act of creation.
 For the entire act of creation
 was only for this ultimate purpose —
 and as explained in Siman 52
 in the teaching Haniyor b'Laylah
 — and as also explained elsewhere.
 And therefore Shabbos is called
 the ultimate purpose of the work of heaven and earth.
 And therefore they stated there:
 that the angels place their hands upon his head
 and say:
 "v'sar avonecha v'chata'ascha techupar
 [and your iniquity is removed —
 and your sin is atoned]"
 [Isaiah 6:7] —
 for there is no suffering without sin.
 And through the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 all the suffering is nullified — as mentioned above —
 and the sins are also atoned.
 For there — the sins are transformed into merits —
 in the aspect of [Job 14:4]:
 "mi yiten tahor mitame —
 lo echad
 [who can bring forth purity from the impure —
 not one]"
 — that is, the aspect of the ultimate purpose —
 which is the aspect of entirely one — as mentioned above.
 And therefore our Sages taught in truth:
 all who guard the Shabbos, and so on —
 he is forgiven for all his sins.

 And this is what our Sages taught —
 in Bereishis Rabbah, section 10:
 three forms of tzava [host/army] there are —
 tzava for the heavens and the earth —
 as it is stated:
 "vayechulu —
 v'chol haggid —
 v'chol tzeva'am
 [and they were completed —
 and so on —
 and all their host]."
 [Genesis 2:1]

 Tzava for suffering —
 as it is stated [Job 7:1]:
 "halo tzava l'enosh aley aretz
 [is there not a host [of suffering] for a person upon the earth],"
 and so on. [וכו']

 Tzava for students —
 as it is stated [Job 14:14]:
 "kol yemay tzeva'i — ayachel —
 ad bo chalifati —
 ad yakum chalifati
 [all the days of my host — I shall wait —
 until my relief comes —
 until my replacement arises],"
 and so on —
 see Rashi and Mateneh Kehunah there.
 And there it states:
 "zacah — tzava lo
 [if one merited —
 the host is his]"
 (Rashi explains:
 the hosts of heaven and earth were created for his sake)
 — and if not:
 "tzava alav
 [the host is upon him]"
 (that is — suffering and death come upon him —
 heaven have mercy).
 That is — for tzava means the language of
 an end and a time [ketz v'zman] —
 as in [Job 7:1]:
 "halo tzava l'enosh aley aretz —
 v'chimey sachir yamav
 [is there not a host for a person upon the earth —
 and like the days of a hired worker are his days]"
 — that is, that there is an ultimate purpose and an end to every thing —
 at which point it will pass away and cease and be nullified —
 and time itself also has no substance —
 for it flies and floats from moment to moment —
 as the philosopher stated:
 "ha'avar ayin —
 v'ha'atid adayin —
 v'hahoveh k'heref ayin
 [the past is nothing —
 and the future is not yet —
 and the present is the blink of an eye]."
 And therefore one who merits
 to true knowledge and true intellect —
 closes his eyes from the sight of this world —
 and the vanities of time — entirely —
 and looks only toward the ultimate purpose.
 And then one merits to attain the ultimate purpose
 through all the creatures in the world —
 which are the aspects of the heavens and the earth and all their host.
 And this is the aspect of Shabbos —
 which is the ultimate purpose of the work of heaven and earth —
 and as explained in
 Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 39 —
 in the teaching Leku Chazu.
 And then:
 "tzava lo
 [the host is his]"
 — for all the hosts of the heavens and the earth
 were created for his sake —
 since he merits to attain the ultimate purpose through them —
 for the sake of which everything was created — as mentioned above.
 And if not:
 "tzava alav
 [the host is upon him]"
 — that is, suffering comes upon him —
 and he wishes to flee
 and save himself from them —
 and he is compelled to flee from them —
 and to cling himself to the ultimate purpose —
 for from this the nature is embedded in a person:
 to close his eyes forcefully at the time of suffering —
 and as explained within —
 and sometimes actual death comes upon him —
 heaven have mercy —
 and everything is only to bring him to the ultimate purpose.
 And also —
 for all the punishments and the suffering
 are the aspects of death —
 and as explained in
 Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 66.
 But after one returns and comes back
 from the nullification toward the ultimate purpose —
 then the nature of suffering is to intensify even more —
 and then the suffering is cooled —
 and the thirst of the soul is quenched —
 through the Torah novellae
 one merits through the nullification — as mentioned above.

 And this is the aspect of tzava
 stated regarding students —
 as Rashi explained there:
 "kol tzivyoni v'sochalti —
 l'Torah u'l'talmidim
 [all my desire and my hope —
 is for Torah and for students]."
 For when one merits Torah novellae —
 in particular when one merits
 to illuminate one's Torah novellae within one's students —
 then not only is the suffering cooled —
 but even more so:
 one merits to nullify oneself
 each time toward the ultimate purpose —
 not through suffering, heaven have mercy —
 but through the attainment of the Torah novellae
 one merits to attain each time —
 which is completely above the boundary —
 in the aspect of [Psalms 119:96]:
 "l'chol tichla ra'isi ketz —
 rachavah mitzvoscha me'od
 [to every end I have seen a limit —
 but Your commandment is exceedingly broad]."
 For this is the aspect of the ultimate purpose —
 which is completely above all boundary — as mentioned above.
 And therefore the Torah is called
 an inheritance without limits —
 the aspect of the heritage of Yaakov — as mentioned above.
 And this takes place for each person individually.
 But the essential matter of this in its generality
 comes about through the aforementioned master of the field —
 who engages in all of this in its perfection —
 to bring all the souls of Israel to the ultimate purpose —
 which is the aspect of engaging
 in the rectifications of the field — as mentioned above.
 And the master of the field —
 together with the sacred field —
 are the essential aspects of heaven and earth —
 which are the aspects of the Matron
 and the husband of the Matron —
 as is well-known.
 And as it is written [Isaiah 55:10]:
 "ki ka'asher yered hageshem v'hasheleig min hashamayim —
 v'chol haggid —
 ki im hirvah es ha'aretz v'holidah —
 v'chol haggid
 [for as the rain and the snow fall from the heavens —
 and so on —
 but it saturates the earth and makes it give birth —
 and so on],"
 and so on —
 and as is also commonly [cited] in the words of the Sages.
 And through them
 Israel merits to close their eyes
 from the sight of this world entirely —
 and to look only toward the ultimate purpose —
 for this is the aspect of the tzava
 stated regarding heaven and earth — as mentioned above.
 But because it is a very great labor —
 and much suffering and harsh things
 come upon the master of the field —
 before he merits to complete
 all the rectifications of the field.
 And there are great Tzadikim
 who cannot complete this matter
 except through their departure and their literal death —
 heaven have mercy.
 And this is the aspect of the tzava
 stated regarding suffering.
 But through the Torah novellae
 one merits to attain through the nullification —
 through this the suffering is cooled —
 and then — one who has a very great
 and wondrous and awesome power —
 can sometimes complete the rectification
 even while still alive.
 And even if one is compelled to depart for the sake of this,
 heaven forbid —
 he completes the rectification afterward
 through his students.
 And this is the aspect of the tzava
 stated regarding students.

 And this is the aspect of what
 Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him,
 was compelled to depart —
 and afterward Yehoshua brought Israel
 into the Land of Israel —
 and all through the Torah novellae
 that Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, illuminated in him.
 And this is the aspect of what G-d, blessed be He,
 said to Yehoshua [Joshua 1:2, 7]:
 "Moshe avdi mes —
 v'atah kum avor es haYarden hazeh —
 v'chol haggid —
 rak chazak v'ematz me'od —
 lishmor la'asos k'chol haTorah asher tzivecha Moshe avdi
 [Moshe My servant has died —
 and now arise — cross this Jordan —
 and so on —
 only be very strong and courageous —
 to guard and to do according to all the Torah
 that Moshe My servant commanded you],"
 and so on —
 as mentioned above.
 And this [Song of Songs 6:2–3]:
 "dodi yarad l'gano —
 l'aravas habosem —
 lir'os baganim —
 v'lilkot shoshanim
 [my beloved went down to his garden —
 to the bed of spices —
 to graze in the gardens —
 and to gather roses]"
 — and our Sages expounded
 in Midrash Shir haShirim:
 "v'lilkot shoshanim —
 l'salek es haTzadikim sheb'Yisrael
 [and to gather roses —
 to remove the Tzadikim from Israel],"
 and so on —
 that is, for sometimes it is impossible
 to complete the rectification of the garden and the field —
 which is the aspect of:
 "lir'os baganim
 [to graze in the gardens]"
 — except through the departure of the Tzadikim —
 which is the aspect of:
 "v'lilkot shoshanim
 [and to gather roses]."
 And this [Song of Songs 6:3]:
 "ani l'dodi v'dodi li —
 haro'eh bashoshanim
 [I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine —
 who grazes among the roses]."
 For then specifically —
 G-d, blessed be He, completes
 the matter of the rectification of the souls —
 so that they should merit
 to nullify themselves toward the ultimate purpose —
 and to cling to G-d, blessed be He,
 in an extraordinary and wondrous clinging —
 in the aspect of:
 "ani l'dodi v'dodi li"
 — through the Torah novellae
 that the Tzadikim illuminated within their students —
 which is the aspect of:
 "haro'eh bashoshanim
 [who grazes among the roses]"
 — which are the students —
 as our Sages expounded
 [Tractate Shabbos 30b]
 on the verse [Song of Songs 5:13]:
 "sifososav shoshanim —
 al tikri shoshanim ela sheshonim
 [his lips are roses —
 do not read 'roses' [shoshanim]
 but rather 'those who repeat' [sheshonim]],"
 and so on —
 see there.

segments.he: סימן קט-יש הבל
segments.en: And the essential matter is that the person himself should arouse and draw upon himself the awe — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — in the aspect of: "Tzadik moshel yiras Elokim" — as mentioned above — for this is the aspect of: "hi mesurah b'yadchem — v'lo atem mesurim b'yadah" — as mentioned above. And this likewise [Exodus 31:16]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" — and so on — "la'asos [to do]" — specifically — to make for oneself the awe — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of: "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" — that is, the two kinds of awe — specifically. For even the first awe requires guarding — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of: "es Shabsosai tishmoru" — two Shabbosim — as mentioned above. And therefore the essential perfection of prayer and the drawing down of the abundant bounty to Israel and the revelation of His kingship, blessed be He, and the subjugation of the husks beneath holiness — all of this flows in its fullness through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: they give him all the desires of his heart — that is, one merits the perfection of prayer — and one can arouse the bounty in the world through one's prayer. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — as it is stated: "v'atah al bamosemo tidroch" — that is, the husks are subdued beneath the feet of holiness. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of awe — the aspect of: "b'yir'ascha b'zechus Yaakov [in your awe — through the merit of Yaakov]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for Shabbos is the aspect of the revelation of sacred speech — as mentioned above. And from there awe is revealed — in the aspect of [Isaiah 66:2]: "u'midbaryecha pachad libbi [and from Your speech my heart trembles]" — and it is written [Jeremiah 10:7]: "hayirei devar Hashem [those who fear the word of Hashem]." And also — through awe — speech is completed — so that one will be able to draw bounty — in the aspect of: "kol mi she'yesh bo yiras Shamayim — devarav nishma'in [all who have awe of Heaven — their words are heeded]" — as explained within. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for through awe — one's words are in the aspect of the word of Hashem — and draw bounty — in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 15:6]: "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem."

segments.he: מבואר לעיל מענין ההבלים דקדושה שיוצאים בשבת קדש וכבר ידוע גם כן מענין הנפש יתרה ונשמה חדשה שזוכה כל אחד מישראל לקבל בכל שבת כפי בחינתו של כל אחד ואחד. וכפי המבואר בפנים מובן ממילא שנכון להרהר בתשובה מאד בכל ערב שבת ולהתאנח מעומקא דלבא על כל מעשיו וענינים שאינם הגונים שעברו בכל ששת ימי המעשה ועל ידי זה בנקל לו יותר להפסיק עצמו מחבל הטומאה שנקשר בו על ידי ההבלים דסטרא אחרא הבל המה מעשה תעתועים שעברו עליו ח"ו בששת ימי המעשה ונקשר ונדבק מעכשיו אל החבל דקדושה שהן ההבלים דקדושה של שבת ואזי נעשה בריה חדשה ממש בגוף ונפש כמובן בפנים. וכן מובן מזה איך שצריכין ליזהר בשבת להיות בשמחה ולשכוח לגמרי בכל עמלו ויגונו ובכל חסרונותיו הגשמיים. כי אם יזכור בזה ויתאנח על צרכיו הגשמיים בשבת קדש יוכל לפגום על ידי זה בקדושת שבת. כי נפסק על ידי זה קצת מרוחניות קדושת שבת ונקשר בגשמיות ח"ו ועל כן אמרו רז"ל שיהיה בשבת כאלו כל מלאכתו עשויה וגם אמרו שאסור לבקש על צרכיו בשבת היינו כנ"ל. וזה בחינת שבת על שם כל אנחתה השבתי (ישעיה כא) כי נשבתין ונתבטלין כל מיני אנחות ודאגות גשמיות כי דביקין אז רק ברוחניות ובשמחה גדולה. כי צריכין לקבל קדושת שבת בשמחה ולב טוב כמבואר במקום אחר שגם היראה של שבת צריכה להיות בשמחה גדולה וכנ"ל כמה פעמים:
segments.en: Shabbos is the aspect of the nullification of the three completely impure husks — which are the aspect of arlah [the foreskin] — the aspect of cherpah [disgrace] — and [Leviticus 26:19]: "v'hishbati ge'on azim [and I shall cause the pride of the arrogant to cease]." And likewise: "v'yishbas din v'kalon [and judgment and shame shall cease]" — and as mentioned above many times.

segments.he: סימן קטו-ויעמוד העם
segments.en: And also — through the holiness of Shabbos — Da'as is completed — for this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — and through this compassion [rachmanus] is awakened — for this is the aspect of: "yecholah hi shetaracheim [she can show compassion]" — stated regarding the holy Shabbos — (and as brought below within in Siman 119). And likewise [Psalms 119:156]: "rachamecha rabbim" — and so on. And through this one also merits to draw the aspect of great compassion through the prayer of G-d, blessed be He, Himself — as it were. And then one merits complete salvation — as explained within. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: had Israel guarded two Shabbosim — they would have been immediately redeemed — as it is stated [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — v'chol haggid — v'havi'osim el har kodshi — v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi" — as mentioned above. For Shabbos is the aspect of compassion — the aspect of: "yecholah hi shetaracheim" — as mentioned above.

segments.he: עיין זוהר אמור דף צט. מבואר ענין התעורות הדין של ראש השנה וסנטירא אתי למתבע דינא בגין כי אני ה' אוהב משפט וכו' אך מחמת שאהבת ישראל גוברת על אהבת המשפט על כן צוה השם יתברך לתקוע בשופר בכדי לעורר רחמים וכו' ובפנים מבואר שזה ענין מה שכשהאדם רוצה לקרב עצמו אל השם יתברך מזמינין לו מניעות זה מחמת הקטרוג של מדת הדין כי אני ה' אוהב משפט וכנ"ל. אך מחמת שאהבת ישראל גוברת על אהבת המשפט. על כן מסתיר השם יתברך את עצמו כביכול בתוך המניעות עד שעל ידי זה בעצמו יכולין להתקרב כי על ידי הדעת יכולין למצוא אותו יתברך שהוא נסתר בתוך המניעות בעצמן ואפשר שזה היה ענין התקיעות שהיו תוקעין בכל ערב שבת כמו שאמרו רז"ל (שבת ל"ה:) וגם עכשיו צריכין להכריז וכו' וזהו במקום התקיעות כמבואר בשולחן ערוך אורח חיים סימן רנ"ו. כי מחמת שקדושת שבת הוא דבר גדול ונורא ורוחני מאד ושקולה שבת ככל התורה כולה ובכל ימות החול הולך האדם על פי רוב בגשמיות וטרוד בעשיית חפציו ועכשיו כשצריכין ליכנס לרוחניות קדושת שבת אורב על זה הבעל דבר מאד להזמין לו מניעות וטרדות רבות לבלבל אותו מרוחניות קדושת שבת או להביא אותו ח"ו לידי חילול שבת ממש. על כן תקנו רז"ל לתקוע בשופר לעורר רחמים ולהמתיק כל הקטרוגים ברוחניות וגם בגשמיות מזכירין את כל אחד לסלק מעליו כל הטרדות והמניעות ולקבל קדושת שבת. ואפשר שזה גם כן סוד השלהובא דאשא שיורד בערב שבת להכניע הקליפות שלא יעלו כי גם הם רוצים לעלות אז כמבואר בכתבים והם רוצים לעלות ולינק מהקדושה רק בכדי לבלבל קדושת שבת. כי כל כוונתם רק לרע ומזה נמשכין כל המניעות וטרדות וקפידות השכיחין בערב שבת רק מחמת שהשם יתברך אוהב ישראל לכן יורד שלהובא דאשא ומכניע אותם.
segments.en: For Shabbos is the aspect of bris [the covenant] — and it is stated regarding Yosef: "asaf Elokim es cherpasi [G-d has removed my disgrace]" [Genesis 30:23]. And then the good that is in Nogah is encompassed in holiness — and the evil within it — together with the three completely impure husks — are repelled and fall downward through the shalhava d'asha [the flame of fire] that descends on Erev Shabbos — as explained within. And this is likewise the aspect of the commandment of circumcision.

segments.he: וזה שימני כחותם על לבך וכו' כי עזה כמות אהבה קשה כשאול קנאה. כי הקנאה והקטרוגים גוברים מאד ומזה באים מניעות רבות. רשפיה רשפי אש שלהבת יה. היינו על ידי בחינת שלהבוא דאשא הנ"ל שנתעורר על ידי המוחין של קדושת שבת שהוא בחינת שלהבת יה כמבואר בכתבים על ידי זה מים רבים לא יוכלו לכבות את האהבה וכו' אני חומה (לשבר כל המניעות) אז הייתי בעיניו כמוצאת שלום.
segments.en: And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught — specifically: a circumcised person guards the Shabbos — and not a gentile who is uncircumcised. And in the holy Zohar it is explained regarding the matter of [Genesis 17:12]: "u'ven shmonas yamim yimol [and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised]" — in order that Shabbos should pass over him. For both depend upon each other. And therefore one must be very careful on Shabbos to be at peace with all people — and not to arouse any dispute — or disgraces and humiliations — heaven forfend. And even if someone disgraces him — let him be silent toward him — and think in his heart: this is precisely the matter of the holiness of Shabbos — to nullify and repel the impure husks — which are the aspect of arlah — the aspect of cherpah. And this rectification is also made through the fact that one hears one's disgrace and is silent — as explained within.

segments.he: כי באמת השם יתברך חפץ מאד באהבת ישראל ובהתקרבותם אליו ואפילו המניעות בעצמן הם גם כן רק בשביל התקרבות רק אף על פי כן הרבה נמנעין ונתרחקין ממש על ידי זה ואז יש לו יתברך צער מזה כביכול. אבל כשזוכה לשבר המניעות אז גורם להשם יתברך תענוג גדול ואז השם יתברך מקרב אותו ומחבבו באהבה נפלאה ובהתקרבות אמתי. ועל ידי ששיבר את המניעות שנזדמנו לו רק מחמת הקטרוגים שהיו עליו ממעשיו הראשונים שאינם הגונים. ועל כן על ידי זה בעצמו נתתקנין גם כל הקלקולים הנ"ל ונתבטלין כל הקליפות והסטרין אחורנין שנתהוו על ידם רחמנא ליצלן כידוע וזה בחינת אך את שבתותי תשמרו. ידוע כי אכין ורקין מיעוטין זה בחינת מניעות שרוצין למנוע את האדם ולמעטו מקדושת שבת והאדם צריך להתעורר על ידי זה דייקא לשבר המניעות ולקבל קדושת שבת בשלימות. ועל כן דרשו רז"ל מזה באמת (יומא פ"ה) שפיקוח נפש דוחה שבת שנאמר את שבתותי תשמרו יכול לכל תלמוד לומר אך חלק. נמצא שיש לפעמים מה שהוא מניעה באמת מקדושת שבת כגון פיקוח נפש שדוחה שבת. אבל באמת מזה בעצמו אנו רואין שאין שום מניעה באה בשביל התרחקות ח"ו רק מחמת אהבת משפט מוכרח שיזדמן לו איזה מניעה. אבל באמת אהבת ישראל גוברת על אהבת משפט עד שהשם יתברך בעצמו כביכול מסתיר את עצמו בתוך המניעה בכדי שיוכל לשברה כנ"ל.
segments.en: And this is the aspect of [Exodus 20:8]: "zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — and they said: "mei'chad b'Shabbis l'Shabbasa." For since the holiness of Shabbos is very spiritual — therefore one must prepare oneself for this throughout all the days of the week — and remember the holiness of Shabbos each day — which is the aspect of the sight — that one watches and focuses and anticipates and prepares oneself for the holiness of Shabbos. And this is the aspect of the or yashar from the side of the holy Israel — that is, they focus throughout all the days of the week with great concentration on the holiness of Shabbos. And through this their sight reaches the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos in the aspect of a strike — and the sight returns to them in the aspect of or chozer — and they merit to receive the holiness of Shabbos in its fullness. And this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 5:12]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" — and likewise: "shamor es yom haShabbas" — and so on — from the language of waiting and anticipation — for one must wait and anticipate the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of sight. And through this one draws upon himself the holiness of Shabbos in its fullness.

segments.he: וזה אנו רואין בענין זה בצעמו מה שפיקוח נפש דוחה שבת הרי מזה נראה שאף על פי שקדושת שבת שקולה ככל התורה והיא יקרה ואהובה מאד אצל השם יתברך אף על פי כן אהבת ישראל גוברת כל כך עד שפיקוח נפש של אחד מישראל דוחה את השבת וזה אפילו על הפחות שבישראל. ומזה מובן שכל המניעות שאינן פיקוח נפש שנזדמנין לו להאדם למנוע אותו מקדושת שבת או משאר דברים שבקדושה אינם בשביל התרחקות בכדי להרחיק את האדם מהדבר שבקדושה כי איך יתכן זאת שיחפוץ השם יתברך בהתרחקות של האדם אפילו של הפחות שבפחותים מאחר שאנו רואים שגם הוא אהוב ונחמד מאד אצלו יתברך עד שחייבין לחלל שבת אפילו הגדול שבגדולי ישראל בשביל להציל נפש אחת מהפחותים שבישראל. על כרחך לומר שהמניעה באה רק בשביל התקרבות אמתי כנ"ל. וזהו שדרשו שם עוד כי קדש הוא לכם. היא מסורה בידכם ולא אתם מסורים בידה היינו שפיקוח נפש דוחה שבת.
segments.en: Shabbos is the aspect of giving in secret [matan b'seter] — corresponding to what our Sages of blessed memory taught: "matanah tovah yesh li b'veys genzai — v'Shabbas shemah" — and so on — and they stated: all the commandments were given publicly — and Shabbos was given to Israel in privacy. It follows that Shabbos is the aspect of giving in secret. And this "yichpeh af [suppresses anger]" — for on Shabbos all judgments are suppressed and do not stir at all — as explained in the holy Zohar. And this is what is written [Ezekiel 20:21]: "v'es Shabsosai chilelu — va'omar lishpoch chamasi aleihem l'chalos api bam" — and so on — for through the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend — the aspect of burning wrath [charon af] is aroused, heaven forfend. For all who desecrate the Shabbos publicly — it is as if he worshipped idolatry. And likewise — when there is idolatry in the world — burning wrath is in the world, heaven forfend. And also — for through the holiness of Shabbos — all the husks are subdued — in particular that husk — as explained within — may its name be blotted out — as explained in the holy Zohar. And then it has no power to draw sustenance from the six sides of the Aleph-Beis [the letters]. But through the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend — one gives it power to draw sustenance from the aforementioned sides — and from the Feh [the letter Peh] — anger is also made — and the aspect of consuming fire is drawn, heaven forfend — as explained within. And this is what is written [Jeremiah 17:27]: "v'im lo tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — v'ladesh es yom haShabbas — v'hitzasi eish b'sh'areha va'achlah" — and so on — and this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: fire is found only in a place where Shabbos is desecrated.

segments.he: ומזה בעצמו מובן שקדושת שבת מסורה בידינו. היינו שאפילו אם מזדמנין מניעות על זה אם אינם מפיקוח נפש ידע שבוודאי יש לו כח לשברם ולקבל קדושת שבת בשלימות כי היא מסורה בידינו. וזהו שדרשו שם עוד ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת לעשות את השבת וכו' אמרה תורה חלל עליו שבת אחת כדי שישמור שבתות הרבה היינו כי מדרשה זאת מבואר ביותר ענין הנ"ל שהשם יתברך בעצמו מתלבש ומסתיר עצמו תוך המניעה. כי הרי ראינו שאפילו פיקוח נפש שהוא מניעה באמת לקדושת שבת כי הרי הוא דוחה את השבת אף על פי כן בזה בעצמו גם כן מלובש קדושת שבת עד שחילול שבת זה נחשב באמת לשמירת שבת שזה בחינת ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת וכו' אמרה תורה חלל עליו שבת אחת כדי שישמור שבתות הרבה.
segments.en: And this is the aspect of: "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem b'yom haShabbas." And therefore then is the essential time for the sacred union — for then the aforementioned husk is subdued — and then the union is in holiness — in the aspect of: "zachu — Shechinah shruya beineihem [if they merited — the Shechinah dwells between them]." And also our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. It follows that through this — the burning wrath that comes through idolatry — as mentioned above — is also suppressed and nullified. And also — Shabbos is the aspect of the rectification of the bris — the aspect of: "bris olam [everlasting covenant]" [Exodus 31:16] — as explained elsewhere. And then — all the holy sparks that fell to wherever they fell — ascend — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of: "ki pi Hashem diber" — stated regarding the guarding of Shabbos — for then the sides [pa'in] of the letters of speech are rectified. And also — the delight and honor of Shabbos is the aspect of charity to the poor — as mentioned above many times.

segments.he: נמצא שבחילול שבת הזה מלובש בו קדושת שמירת שבת. כי הוא רק כדי שישמור שבתות הרבה ובשביל זה נחשב החילול עצמו גם כן לשמירת שבת שזה בחינת ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת לעשות את השבת היינו כנ"ל. וזהו שדרשו שם עוד וחי בהם ולא שימות בהם ומסיק שם שלימוד זה עדיף מכלהו דמוכח מניה שאפילו ספק פיקוח נפש דוחה את כל המצוות. ומזה רואין אהבת השם יתברך לנפשות ישראל ומובן מזה ממילא שכל המניעות הם רק בשביל הקרבות כנ"ל:
segments.en: Shabbos is "menuchas ahavah v'nedavah [a rest of love and freewill]" — the aspect of the side of the right [sitra d'yemina].

segments.he: וזה בחינת מ'זמור ש'יר ל'יום ה'שבת ראשי תיבות למש"ה שהוא הדעת כי בשבת מאיר הדעת של בחינת משה רבינו עליו השלום בלב כל אחד מישראל ואז רואין שכל המניעות אינם כלום והשם יתברך בעצמו מלובש ומוסתר בהם וזה טוב להודות לה' וכו' להגיד בבוקר חסדך ואמונתך בלילות היינו אפילו בלילה וחשך של התגברות המניעות שהן בחינת חשק כמבואר בפנים אף על פי כן צריכין להתחזק את עצמו באמונה שלימה ולהאמין שהכל רק בשביל התקרבות כנ"ל. וזה מה גדלו מעשיך ה' שהן בבחינת מעשה ידיו אמת ומשפט שמחמת זה מזדמנין להאדם המניעות כי השם יתברך אוהב משפט מאד עמקו מחשבותך כי אף על פי כן אהבת ישראל שעלו במחשבה תחלה גדולה ויתרה ביותר כי מאד עמקו מחשבותיו יתברך והוא מלביש ומסתיר עצמו בתוך המניעה בכדי שיוכל לשברה ואז המניעות הם לו לטובה גדולה כי על ידי זה נתתקנין כל הפגמים שלו שפגם מקודם ונתבטלין כל הסטרא אחרא שנתהוו על ידם כנ"ל. וזה איש בער לא ידע וכו' בפרוח רשעים וכו' היינו הצלחת הרשעים והמונעים הוא רק להשמדם עדי עד. כי כשזוכין לשבר המניעות אז הם כלים ואובדים מאליהם בבחינת כי הנה אויבך ה' היינו כי אויבי ישראל הרוצים למנוע אותם מקדושת ישראל הם אויבי ה' ממש כמו שאמרו רז"ל ועל כן כי הנה אויבך יאבדו וכו' ותרם כראם קרני וכו' וזה גם כן נשאו נהרות ה' וכו' היינו התגברות המניעות שעל ידי המונעים מקולות מים רבים אדירים וכו' אדיר במרום ה' כי ידו יתברך על העליונה תמיד ובוודאי יתבטלו כל המניעות כולם ויזכו כל ישראל לתכליתם הטוב:
segments.en: And from the side of the right — "mocha chavara k'kaspa [the brain is white like silver]." And therefore on Shabbos one merits the aspect of clarity and purity of the mental faculties and thought.

segments.he: וזה אם תשיב משבת וכו' אז תתענג על ה' בחינת אהבה בתענוגים כי תתגלה אליו אהבתו יתברך לישראל עד שהוא עצמו יתברך מלובש ומוסתר בתוך כל המניעות ואז יתענג גם הוא על ה' אהבה גדולה בתענוגים. וכל זה על ידי הארת הדעת של בחינת קדושת שבת שמשם עיקר הענג כנ"ל כמה פעמים והרכבתיך על במותי ארץ ודרשו רז"ל שניצול משיעבוד מלכיות שמהם כל המניעות כמו שאמרו רז"ל רצוני לעשות רצונך אלא שׂאור שבעיסה ושיעבוד מלכיות מעכב. והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב אביך ודרשו רז"ל שזוכה לנחלה בלי מצרים בחינת מלא כל הארץ כבודו כי רואה שאלקותו וכבודו יתברך מלובש בכל מקום בבחינת אל הערפל אשר שם האלקים כמבואר בפנים:
segments.en: And therefore then it is especially propitious to enter the hidden good — and to attain the secrets of the Torah — as brought. And also — Shabbos itself is the aspect of good [tov] — for this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:2]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov" — and as explained in the holy Zohar. And also — for Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah.

segments.he: סימן קטז-הנותן צדקה
segments.en: It follows that within this desecration of Shabbos — the holiness of Shabbos guarding is clothed. For it is only so that he may guard many Shabbosim — and for this sake the desecration itself is also counted as a guarding of Shabbos. For this is the aspect of: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" — as mentioned above. And this is what they further expounded there: "v'chai bahem — v'lo sheyamus bahem" — and it concludes there that this teaching is superior to all of them — for it is proven from it that even a doubtful case of the preservation of life overrides all the commandments. And from this we see the love of G-d, blessed be He, for the souls of Israel — and it is understood from this by itself: that all obstacles are only for the sake of drawing close — as mentioned above.

segments.he: מבואר לעיל כמה פעמים מגודל הרחמים והארת הדעת שמאיר בשבת ועל ידי זה ניצולין מעבירות. כי אין אדם עובר עבירה אלא אם כן נכנס בו רוח שטות ועל כן אמרו רז"ל כל המשמר את השבת הוא מרוחק מן העבירה שנאמר שומר שבת מחללו ושומר ידו מעשות כל רע היינו כנ"ל:
segments.en: And the Torah is called tov [good] — as it is written [Proverbs 4:2]: "ki lekach tov [for a good teaching]." And through the holiness of Shabbos one merits clarity of thought — through which all Israel are called "tovim [good]" — as it is written [Psalms 125:4]: "hatibah Hashem l'tovim v'lisharim b'levosam [do good Hashem to the good and to the upright in heart]." And therefore all agree that on Shabbos the Torah was given — for this is the aspect of: "yavo tov — yekabel tov — mi'tov l'tovim [let the good come — receive good — from the Good One to the good ones]" — as our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Menachos 53b]. And then is fulfilled in its fullness what is explained within in the name of the holy Zohar: "man d'ihu tov — v'chol haggid — hahu tov ganiz — yeyma lei — pitchu lei b'hai tar'a d'iskari ahavah [one who is good — and so on — that hidden good — it is said to him — open for him in this gate called love]" — as mentioned above. Or through "b'hahu tar'a d'ihu teshuvah [that gate which is repentance]" — for Shabbos is the aspect of teshuvah me'ahavah — as mentioned above many times — and as explained within in Siman 58. And therefore one must conduct oneself regarding the honor of Shabbos with the trait of generosity — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "kol hamosif mosifin lo [all who add — they add to him]." For through generosity — which is the trait of our Patriarch Avraham — the man of lovingkindness — through this one merits clarity and purity of thought and mental faculties — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — the world of thought. And one merits through this to attain the hidden good — which is the essential aspect of longevity — as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer: one who sanctifies over wine [Kiddush] on Shabbos nights — his days and years are lengthened — and so on. And likewise our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Megillah 27b] regarding Rabbi Zakkai — that he lived long because he never in his days neglected the Kiddush of the Day [Kiddush haYom]. For the essential beginning of the revelation of the holiness of Shabbos is through the Kiddush. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: "Kiddush haYom kodem l'chevod yom v'chevod lailah [the Kiddush of the Day takes precedence over the honor of the day and the honor of the night]" [Tractate Pesachim 105b]. And therefore through it one merits longevity — as mentioned above.

segments.he: סימן קכט-ארץ אוכלת
segments.en: And this [Isaiah 58:13–14]: "im tashiv miShabbos" — and so on — "az tis'anag al Hashem" — the aspect of love in delights — for the love of G-d, blessed be He, for Israel will be revealed to him — so greatly — that He Himself, blessed be He, is dressed and hidden within all the obstacles. And then he too will delight in Hashem — great love in delights. And all of this through the illumination of the Da'as of the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — from which is the essential delight — as mentioned above many times. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — from whom come all the obstacles — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "retzioni la'asos retzoncha — ela she'or she'ba'isah — v'shibbud malchiyos me'akev [My desire is to do Your desire — but the leaven in the dough — and the subjugation of the kingdoms — prevents me]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — in the aspect of: "melo chol ha'aretz kevodo [the whole earth is full of His honor]" — for one sees that G-d's divinity and honor, blessed be He, is dressed in every place — in the aspect of [Exodus 20:21]: "el ha'arafel asher sham ha'Elokim" — as explained within.

segments.he: שבת הוא בחינת אמונה כנ"ל כמה פעמים. גם הוא בחינת מוחין ודעת ועל כן כשזוכין לקשר עצמו אל קדושת שבת באמת ובאמונה שלימה אזי נתהפכין אל מהות קדושתה ממש. ועל כן המשמר שבת וכו' אפילו עבד עבודה זרה וכו' מוחלין לו. וכן המענג את השבת מוחלין לו על כל עוונותיו כי נתהפך למהות קדושתה ממש. ועל כן מבואר בזוהר הקדוש האי יומא יומא דנשמתין הוא ולא יומא דגופא וכו' כי אז גם הגוף נתהפך למהות הנשמה הקדושה שהוא המוח והדעת וזה בחינת מצוות ענג שבת. כי אז גם תענוגי הגוף יקרים וקדושים מאד. וזה שכן ארץ ורעה אמונה שזה בחינת קדושת שבת קדש שהוא בחינת ארץ ישראל ושלימות האמונה כנ"ל על ידי זה והתענג על ה' וכו' כי אז גם כל תענוגים שלו כולם קדש ועל כן אמרו רז"ל גם כן המשמר את השבת וכו' הוא מרוחק מן העבירה כי נתהפך למהות קדושתה וזה אשרי אנוש יעשה זאת (פירש רש"י שומר שבת וכו') ובן אדם יחזיק בה יחזיק בה דייקא היינו שיחזיק ויקשר עצמו היטב לקדושת שבת באמונה שלימה (אז) שומר שבת מחללו (על ידי זה) ושומר ידו מעשות כל רע היינו שמרוחק מן העבירה כמו שדרשו רז"ל וזה ואל יאמר בן הנכר וכו' הבדל יבדילני ה' מעל עצמו היינו מאחר שלא נולדתי בקדושת ישראל על כן אי אפשר לי להתהפך למהות הקדושה ממש כי איננו בבחינת המזון הטוב שנתהפך לניזון וכמבואר בפנים. וכן ואל יאמר הסריס הן אני עץ יבש כי אמונה הוא בחינת כח הגודל וכח הצומח בבחינת אמונה זה סדר זרעים וכמבואר במקום אחר ועל כן מאחר שאני עץ יבש ואיני עושה פרי בוודאי רחוק אני משלימות האמונה ואי אפשר לי להתהפך למהות קדושתה. כי כה אמר ה' לסריסים אשר ישמרו את שבתותי ונתתי להם וכו' שם טוב מבנים ומבנות.
segments.en: Likewise — regarding Shabbos — one merits through this to receive the holiness of Shabbos in fullness — and then the redemption will come. And in this one can also explain the matter of: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — that is, to prepare one's thought for the holiness of Shabbos throughout all the days of the week — and likewise also in deed — in the aspect of: "mei'chad b'Shabbis l'Shabbasa." For perhaps one does not hold in the fullness of trust — through which one makes a vessel for the bounty — that it should come in its time — and then perhaps the bounty of Shabbos can come to him after Shabbos — or it may not come to him until after a long time. Therefore one must hasten to prepare for Shabbos immediately on the first day of the week. And this was the trait of Shammai — who was from the aspect of judgment — from where comes the grip of mochin d'katnus — the aspect of "achar hadevarim." But Hillel — who was from the attribute of lovingkindness — the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — from which comes the aspect of complete trust — and therefore he would say: "baruch Hashem yom yom [blessed be Hashem day by day]" [Psalms 68:20] — and his trust was firm that the bounty of Shabbos would come in its time. But nonetheless — Hillel also agrees that it is better to do as Shammai taught — as explained in the words of the commentators and the later authorities, of blessed memory, in Siman 242 — for not every person and not in every time does one merit to such clear mental faculties and such strong trust. And this is what they stated there regarding Hillel: there was another trait in him — that all his actions were for the sake of Heaven — that is, the inner dimension of the holiness of his thought was always connected in all his actions — for the sake of Heaven — without any labor and effort whatsoever — for he merited to clear mental faculties. And therefore his trust was also very firm — and he would say: "baruch Hashem yom yom" — and so on — as mentioned above.

segments.he: וכן ובני הנכר וכו' כל שומר שבת מחללו ומחזיקים בבריתי היינו שרוצים וחפצים מאד בהתקשרות אל הקדושה והביאותים אל הר קדשי וכו'. וזה אם תשיב משבת רגלך וכו' וחושב שם כל הענינים שצריכין ליזהר בענין קדושת שבת במעשה ובדיבור ובהילוך וכו' ואז הוא מקושר באמת לקדושת שבת. אז תתענג על ה' היינו שזוכה לבחינת והתענג על ה' הנ"ל. ועל כן הוא גוזר והקב"ה מקיים וממלאין לו כל משאלות לבו. כי נעשה אחדות אחד עם קדושתו יתברך ביכול.
segments.en: The essential perfection of the voice and speech — which are the aspect of Vav-Heh [ו"ה] — is on Shabbos — for this is the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — stated regarding Shabbos — and as mentioned above many times. And likewise — the essential perfection of love and awe — which are the aspect of Yud-Heh [י"ה] — is also on Shabbos — as mentioned above many times.

segments.he: והרכבתיך על במותי ארץ שניצול משיעבוד מלכיות.
segments.en: And this is the aspect of the Name Yud-Heh of Shabbos — as explained in the writings. And therefore then is the essential perfection of Torah and prayer — as mentioned above many times. And through this the kingship of G-d, blessed be He, is revealed — which is the aspect of Shabbas Malketa. And this is the aspect of [Zechariah 14:9]: "v'hayah Hashem l'Melech al kol ha'aretz — b'yom hahu yihyeh Hashem echad — u'shemo echad [and Hashem will be King over all the earth — on that day Hashem will be One — and His Name will be One]" — and this is understood in the holy Zohar in the passage "k'gavna" stated at the entry of Shabbos — that this aspect is drawn through the holiness of Shabbos.

segments.he: כי מאחר שהגוף והגשמיות שלו נתהפך למהות הנשמה הקדושה שזה בחינת לאכול את בשרי המבואר בפנים על יד זה ממילא צרי ואויבי לי המה כשלו ונפלו כמבואר לעיל בפנים בסימן ק"א. והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב אביך היינו שזוכה בשלימות לקדושת ארץ ישראל שיש לה זה הכח להפך היושב בה לקדושתה ממש כמבואר בפנים. ורז"ל דרשו שזוכה לנחלה בלי מצרים. כי מאחר שיוצא מגופניות וגשמיות עד שהגוף גם כן נתהפך למהות הנשמה הקדושה אז הוא כולו רוחני ורוחניות הוא בחינת נחלה בלי מצרים ובלי שום גבול כלל:
segments.en: It is explained within that during the weekdays the outer forces dominate — and their essential dominion is over the aspect of the legs — that is, they do not allow the person to walk in the ways of Hashem, blessed be He. And when the holy Shabbos is sanctified — then: "yispardu kol po'aley aven [all the workers of iniquity are scattered]" [Psalms 92:10] — and then they have no dominion at all — and the legs regain the power of walking — which is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha." But nonetheless — one still needs support to strengthen them. And this support is the aspect of truth [emes]. And Shabbos itself is the aspect of truth — as explained within — (and this is what is brought in the writings: א'ם ת'שיב מ'שבת — initial letters of אמ"ת [emes] — as mentioned above. And this: "raglecha" — for then the legs ascend — as mentioned above — and truth is the support to strengthen them — as mentioned above). But they still need force to be given to them so they can walk properly. And this is through the charity of Shabbos — that is, one gives to the poor for Shabbos — or one hosts a poor person at one's table on Shabbos. And the charity of Shabbos is the aspect of the sun of the future that is destined to be renewed in the time to come — to be like the light of the seven days. And through this it gives force to the aspect of the legs — so that they can walk properly in the ways of Hashem, blessed be He — as explained within.

segments.he: סימן קלה-כי אקח מועד
segments.en: For since his body and physicality were transformed into the substance of the holy soul — for this is the aspect of: "leichol es besari [to eat my flesh]" — as explained within — through this: his enemies and adversaries stumble and fall — as explained above within in Siman 101. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — that is, one merits in fullness the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — which has this power to transform whoever dwells in it into its very holiness — as explained within. And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits. For since one leaves bodily existence and physicality — until the body is also transformed into the substance of the holy soul — then one is entirely spiritual — and spirituality is the aspect of an inheritance without limits — without any boundary at all.

segments.he: שבת הוא תחלה למקראי קדש והוא בחינת משה רבינו עליו השלום כנ"ל כמה פעמים ואז נפתחין כל השערי בינה כמבואר בזוהר הקדוש ואז זוכין לענוה אמתיית שזה בחינת שבו איש תחתיו כנ"ל בסימן ע"ט.
segments.en:
Shabbos = supernal field / world of souls / Chakla Tupichin / Moshe = ba'al hasadeh / Mishkan = sacred field / all souls gathered in / Zohar Chadash / Ari z"l Erev Shabbos descent / Marah / thirty-nine categories of labor / Psalm 92: Shabbos = supernal field (sadeh ha'elyonah) = where all souls of Israel grow = "Shabbas vayinafash" = world of souls = root of all souls of Israel (Zohar; Sefer haBahir). Secret of Chakla Tupichin Kadishin stated regarding Shabbos (Ari z"l) = going out to the field to receive Shabbos. Shabbos also = aspect of the ba'al hasadeh = who strives with all the rectifications of the field = rectifying and bringing in the souls. "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Bnay Yisrael." Moshe = "ba'alah d'Matroniyta" = the field. Commanded on Mishkan = building the stature of the Shechinah (Siman 2 cross-ref.) = itself the sacred field. Commanded also on Shabbos = through Shabbos holiness all souls of Israel assembled and brought into the field = even those driven out = "afilu aved avodah zarah mochalin lo" = also the aspect of the extra soul on Shabbos. Zohar Chadash: rectification of souls of the wicked, heaven forfend = all through Shabbos holiness. Ari z"l: on every Erev Shabbos Moshe descends with great Tzadikim to elevate souls of living and dead from depths of husks. Ba'al hasadeh endures great suffering and bitterness → Sages: "Shabbas b'Marah nitztavu" = bitterness and suffering of the ba'al hasadeh = aspect of Shabbos. Tanna therefore began the 39 categories with "hacharesh v'hazore'a v'hakotzer" = labors of the field (material/weekday pursuits) + work of Mishkan = sacred field; on Shabbos all forbidden = all rectifications of field drawn in wondrous perfection through Shabbos holiness. When souls rectified = beautiful to pray = prayer in its rectification. Psalm 92:2: "tov lehodos." Souls producing fruit → eyes of ba'al hasadeh illuminate = Shabbos = "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" (Tikunim). When eyes illuminate → can look at each person to bring to the ultimate purpose → speech in one aspect = in each word all words encompassed = at the end still standing at the first word = aspect of entirely good / entirely one = "bayom hahu yihyeh Hashem echad u'shemo echad" (Zechariah 14:9). Shabbos = tachlis = ultimate purpose = tachlis of work of heaven and earth = foretaste of World to Come = "yihyeh Hashem echad u'shemo echad." Zohar cited at entry of Shabbos (full Aramaic): "k'govana d'inun mis'yachalin l'eila b'echad… da Atika… raza d'Shabbas ihi Shabbas d'is'achat b'raza d'echad… tzalutha d'ma'alay Shabbata d'ha is'achat kurs'aya yekira kadisha b'raza d'echad." Sages on Psalms 139:16: "yamim yotzaru v'lo echad bahem" = "v'lo" read as "v'lo" [to Him] = "zeh Shabbas" = entirely one = all six weekdays encompassed in it. "Ein tov ela Shabbas" (Zohar) = entirely good / entirely one = tachlis.
