segments.he: ואז עיקר זמן ההתקרבות לצדיקים. כי על ידי קדושת שבת זוכין להרגיש ביותר אור הצדיק. וכן על ידי אור הצדיק זוכין לקבל קדושת שבת ביותר. ועל כן מצוה להקביל פני רבו בשבת כמבואר בזוהר הקדוש ובכתבים כי אז זוכה הצדיק לקבל מוחין דגדלות במעלה מופלגת מאד וטבע הקטנות להתבטל לפני הגדלות ועל כן הוא מתבטל מאד לגבי קדושת הצדיק וקדושת שבת קדש עד שיוכל להתהפך למהות קדושתם באמת. וזה ושמרתם את השבת כי קדש הוא לכם. וכן ביום השביעי יהיה לכם קדש לכם דייקא היינו שקדושתו נמשכת עליכם ממש. וזה בחינת לדעת כי אני ה' מקדשכם. והעיקר לקשר עצמו היטב באמת לקדושת שבת ולקדושת הצדיק. ועיקר התקשרות הוא אהבה בבחינת ונפש יהונתן נקשרה בנפש דוד. ועל כן על ידי ההתקשרות שמקשר נפשו לקדושת שבת שהוא שורש כל הנפשות כנ"ל כמה פעמים. על ידי זה בעצמו זוכה לקבל נפש יתרה של שבת. וזה בחינת מה יפית ומה נעמת אהבה בתענוגים כי ענג שבת צריך להיות באהבה גדולה לקדושת שבת והאהבה תהיה גדולה אצלו מאהבת נשים שזה בחינת לסריסים אשר ישמרו את שבתותי שממתינים בזווגם על קדושת שבת קדש כמבואר בזוהר הקדוש. גם על ידי קדושת שבת עולה המלוכת דקדושה מגלות של הד' מלכיות שזה בחינת מה שאמרו רז"ל שניצול משיעבוד מלכיות. ואז עיקר הכנעת מלכות עמלק כמו שאמרו רז"ל ביום השביעי יצאו מן העם ללקוט מיד ויבא עמלק. כי שבת הוא בחינת תשובה ובחינת יראה כנ"ל כמה פעמים וזה בחינת תקון ועליית המלכות. ועל כן כל קדושת השלש רגלים שבהם עוסקין בתיקון המלכות כמבואר בפנים הכל נמשך מקדושת שבת כמו שאמרו רז"ל שאמר להם הקב"ה אם אתם משמרים את השבת אני נותן לכם מועדים וכו':
segments.en: The essential perfection of awe is on Shabbos — in the aspect of: "yirey shmi — ilu shomrey Shabbas [those who fear My Name — these are the guardians of Shabbos]." And because awe is the aspect of Tzedek — from which comes the awakening of judgments, heaven forfend — this causes the fact that sometimes at the beginning of the entry of Shabbos — a great awe comes upon the person — which is called in Yiddish "frum" — but it is without joy. For it is difficult for him to be joyful — because during the weekday the outer forces sometimes have a grip on this awe — which is the aspect of the fear of punishment [yiras ha'onesh] — the aspect of Tzedek — the aspect of legs — for this is the aspect of [Proverbs 5:5]: "ragleha yordos maves" — heaven have mercy. And therefore — although on Shabbos the legs ascend — in the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and as mentioned above many times — nonetheless — because it is close to where the awe has just ascended from there — it is still difficult for it to be an awe with joy. For on Shabbos one must rejoice greatly — and receive Shabbos with joy and a good heart. And through this specifically — the essential perfection of awe — as explained in Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 17. And therefore the essential perfection of the ascent of the legs — which ascend on Shabbos — is through the light of truth that shines on Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And: "Tzedek — kad is'chabar bah — emes — iskariyas — emunah [Tzedek — when it connects with it — truth — is called — faith]" — and emunah is the aspect of the awe of His majesty [yiras haromemut] — for which there is no grip of judgment at all. On the contrary — through it all external fears are nullified — and all judgments are sweetened — and then the awe is in its perfection — that is, with love and joy. And therefore Shabbos is called: "nachalas Yaakov" — the aspect of: "titen emes l'Yaakov." And this [Isaiah 58:13]: א'ם ת'שיב מ'שבת — initial letters of אמ"ת [emes] — as brought. And this: "raglecha" — for through this is the essential perfection of the legs — as mentioned above. And therefore Shabbos is called: "menuchas ahavah v'nedavah — menuchas emes v'emunah [a rest of love and freewill — a rest of truth and faith]."

segments.he: סימן קמג-ענין קבלת פני תלמיד חכם
segments.en:
Core axis — koach u'po'el (potential and actuality) / two Shabbosim / lechem mishneh / Tzadik as Noach / Tosefta / extra soul / Zohar Terumah 136 / Shabbos Minchah / Atika gali retzonei / rishimah / mesiyas nefesh / three Tzidkascha / Ari z"l / Psalm 92 doubled / Rabbi Yitzchak: The bounty of Shabbos = pi shnatayim = lechem mishneh; Shabbos = aspect of the Tzadik = Noach (Tikunim); Tzadik has ruach d'il'a'ah and ruach d'lata'ah = two Shabbosim = upper Shabbos and lower Shabbos. Extra soul = then the spirit from above descends and connects with the spirit from below; Shabbos = World to Come; Zohar Terumah 136: "u'vema'alay Shabbata gilgula d'nishmatin — ilin azlin v'ilin asyan — ilin salik v'ilin nachtin." Shabbos Minchah = "Atika Kadisha gali retzonei" = because close to departure of Shabbos holiness → great illumination descends → lower Shabbos holiness also departs with it upward = essential time for revelation of Torah secrets of Tzadikim (Sages; many previous simanim); extra attainment of Tzadikim close to their departure. "Keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" = specifically close to departure: upper Shabbos most revealed → then departs; but from the rishimah remaining → receive second Shabbos at even greater level = "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos davka." To receive pi shnatayim from teacher at time of teacher's departure = must be deeply connected to teacher; "v'al menuchasam yekadshu es Shimcha" + accept mesiyas nefesh; three Tzidkascha = Yosef-Moshe-David departed on Shabbos Minchah; obligated to receive face of teacher on Shabbos (Ari z"l) = students receive pi shnatayim. Easier to pray with concentration on Shabbos = because of illumination of pi shnatayim. "Tov lehodos / elyon davka" = illumination of ruach d'il'a'ah = upper Shabbos; Sages on this verse — Rabbi Yitzchak: all matters of Shabbos are doubled — omer doubled — sacrifice doubled — psalm doubled = "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas" = illumination of pi shnatayim → all sacred service completed in pi shnatayim.
 Sof ma'aseh b'machshavah techilah / Aleph = two Yuds and Vav / two Shabbosim / Likutay Torah Ari z"l Parashas Kedoshim / Tikkun 48 / "b'yom haShabbas yipasach" / livelihood from Shabbos / anger and smoke on Shabbos / "lo seva'aru eish" / Tikunim / Nachum 2:14 / Likutay Torah Parashas Kedoshim / death of kings: Shabbos = "sof ma'aseh b'machshavah techilah" = bringing all creation from potential (koach) to actuality (po'el) in perfection = "vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i melachto" (Genesis 2:2; Sages; Zohar) = "tachlis ma'aseh shamayim va'aretz." Six days of deed = the Vav within the Aleph = Vav between two Yuds = koach and po'el. "Es Shabsosai tishmoru" = two Shabbosim = upper Shabbos before creation + Shabbos after creation (after six days of Bereishis; Likutay Torah Ari z"l Parashas Kedoshim). Two Yuds of the Aleph = koach and po'el = beginning of thought and end of deed; Vav between them = six days of deed = Vav within the Aleph. "B'yom haShabbas yipasach" (Ezekiel 46:1) = "poseiach es yadecha" (Psalms 145:16) = completion of rectification of the petach = Vav between the two Yuds; all livelihood flows from Shabbos (Zohar). Severity of anger on Shabbos = "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem b'yom haShabbas" (Tikunim) = don't arouse the smoke and charon af that damages livelihood; "lo seva'aru eish" = literal: fire → smoke = Nachum 2:14 with Targum cited; Shabbos = aspect of eyes = "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein"; Shabbos = nullification of charon af and smoke (Zohar; "kol dinnim atkafyan"). Likutay Torah Parashas Kedoshim: upper Shabbos in first three — not yet rectified — death of kings — sheviyas hakelim — until King Hadar = Yesod = Shabbos before creation → rectified → creation → Shabbos on seventh day; King Hadar = ru'ach avir (writings). Shabbos = teshuvah and charatah (elsewhere) = bringing from koach to po'el in holiness → when Shabbos arrives: great remorse comes = "keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" (elsewhere) → "petach charatah" → mochlin lo; "kol hashomer Shabbas mochalin lo." Three aspects of all poetic action: tziyur, makom, zman → stated regarding Shabbos: Leviticus 23:3 (zman and tziyur); "Shabbas hu laHashem b'chol moshevoseichem" (makom); also Vayakhel; "al yetzei ish mimekomo." "Zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho / zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" = sof ma'aseh b'machshavah techilah = all six days work + bringing material to completion = must connect all to Shabbos = then poetic completion in spiritual sense = then specifically: all labors forbidden. Three instances of "melachto" in Vayechulu = tziyur/makom/zman. "Asher bara Elokim la'asos" (Genesis 2:3; Sages: everything lacks completion — completed through the human being). Creation for the human being → human being is the vehicle of bringing from koach to po'el in all matters; but may not say "kochi v'otzem yadi asah li es hachayil hazeh" (Deuteronomy 8:17) = falls of hitpashetus hayadayim = separates koach from po'el; essential perfection = actuality remains connected to potential = receives sacred vitality from ruach d'il'a'ah = Likutay Halachos. "Sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah / know that labor is done of itself / only through power of Hashem; u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh" = ruach d'il'a'ah shines → labors forbidden → then specifically: completion of bringing from koach to po'el through Israel resting. "Kol hamitpallel b'Erev Shabbas v'omer Vayechulu k'ilu na'asah shutaf laKBH b'ma'aseh bereishis" = essential ultimate purpose of creation in perfection = even after material actuality emerged → connect all creations to supernal potential = "v'yeda kol pa'ul ki atah pe'alto" (Isaiah 60:21) = through guarding Shabbos and testifying to His unity; angels: "v'sar avonecha v'chata'ascha techupar" (Isaiah 6:7) = all sins come from fall of hitpashetus hayadayim; Vayechulu on Shabbos = encompassed in hitpashetus hayadayim of holiness; "al tikri vayechulu ela vayichlu" = also has share in completion of creation → mochlin lo; immediately after: Sages cite Psalms 33:6 "b'dvar Hashem shamayim na'asu" = essential perfection of koach to po'el is through perfection of speech. Speech perfected through Shabbos holiness = "v'daber davar"; Shabbos = World to Come = truth will be revealed = holy face = downfall of wicked = "v'az ehpoch el kol ha'amim safah verurah" (Zephaniah 3:9) = perfection of speech; "v'gercha asher bish'arecha" (Exodus 20:10); Isaiah 56:6 "u'vnay haneychar / kol shomer Shabbas" = drawing close of converts through Shabbos.
 Downfall of wicked / "im tashiv meshabbas" = emes / "penay Shabbas nekablah" / Yaakov = emes / "aseh Shabboscha chol" / Shabbas Malketa / nekudos / cheshek and kisufin through obstacles / "v'lechem setarim yin'am" / Beitzah 16a / two aspects of concealment / "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha" / Maharashal Maharsha Maharam Schiff: Downfall of wicked through Shabbos = "l'hashbis oyev u'misnakeim" (Psalms 8:3) + drawing close of converts. Light of truth shines on Shabbos: "im tashiv miShabbos" = roshei teivos = emes; even am ha'aretz fears to lie on Shabbos (Sages); "penay Shabbas nekablah"; emes = holy face = "v'anpehah nahirin v'chol haggid" stated regarding Shabbos. Yaakov = first described as guarding Shabbos = emes = "titen emes l'Yaakov" (Micah 7:20); "mevakshe fanecha Yaakov selah" (Psalms 24:6). Essential truth = when not dependent on creatures; "aseh Shabboscha chol v'al titztarech livrios" = being dependent changes one's face (= changes one's truth); essential truth is only one; also blemishes Shabbos = "raza d'Shabbas d'is'achat b'raza d'echad." Shabbas Malketa = Shabbos completes letters of speech = Malchus peh; but still needs nekudos and to bring speech from "meytzar hagaron"; accomplished through cheshek and kisufin = through obstacles = "v'lechem setarim yin'am" (Proverbs 9:17) = desired thing shown → immediately snatched away → desire intensifies. Greatness of the hanachshak (desired object) of Shabbos = no need to elaborate = equivalent to all Torah and commandments; "kol hashomer Shabbas / afilu aved avodah zarah mochalin lo"; all greatness declared in Talmud/Midrashim/Zohar/Ari z"l; "chemdas hayamim"; "vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i" = G-d Himself desires Shabbos holiness. According to greatness of hanachshak = greatness of desire; therefore: Shabbos requires preparation (Sages); "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas / mei'chad b'Shabbas l'Shabbasa." Essential spiritual preparation = will and desire and kisufin = yearn throughout all days of week after Shabbos holiness. Also within category of "keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" = each Jew feels extra illumination on Shabbos = extra soul; at Motza'ay Shabbos it is taken → intensifies in extra kisufin → "vav avdah nefesh" → on second Shabbos: merits inner dimension with additional illumination = also "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos."  נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 67 — סימן סז
 Vayiven Hashem es haTzela — Shabbos = root of souls = honor — prayer — Moshe restores the crowns

Shabbos is the world of souls — in the aspect of: "Shabbas vayinafash" — and as mentioned above many times. And this is the aspect of the extra soul one merits to receive on Shabbos. And the root of the souls is honor [kavod] — and this is the secret of the honor of Shabbos. And therefore one must be very careful with the honor of Shabbos — for since it is the root of souls — therefore one who blemishes it and desecrates the Shabbos, heaven forfend — it is said of him: "v'nichresah haNefesh hahi [and that soul shall be cut off]" — for through this his soul departs and is separated from its root, heaven forfend. And all the more one is careful with the honor of Shabbos — the more one merits to receive the illumination of the extra soul. And this is the aspect of [Jeremiah 17:21–22, 24–25]: "hishamu b'nafshotichem — v'al tis'u masa b'yom haShabbas — (b'nafshotichem davka) — v'hayah im shamo'a tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — u'va'u b'sha'arey ha'ir hazos — melachim v'sarim yosh'vim al kisey David [take heed for yourselves — and do not carry a burden on the day of Shabbos — (in your souls — specifically) — and it shall be if you hearken to Me — and so on — and kings and princes shall enter through the gates of this city — sitting on the throne of David]" — the aspect of the rectification of Malchus — the aspect of honor. "V'im lo tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — v'hitzasi eish b'sh'areha [and if you do not hearken to Me — and so on — and I shall kindle fire in its gates]" — for honor is the aspect of fire — in the aspect of [Exodus 24:17]: "u'chevod Hashem k'eish ocheles [and the honor of Hashem is like a consuming fire]" — and as explained within. And therefore when one blemishes the honor of Shabbos — fire comes, heaven forfend — and as our Sages taught: "ein hadeleika metzuyah — v'chol haggid [fire is found only — and so on]" — and as mentioned above many times. And this is the aspect of: "lo seva'aru eish — b'chol moshevoseichem — b'yom haShabbas [you shall not kindle fire in all your dwellings on the day of Shabbos]."

And this is likewise the aspect of the commandment of the meals of Shabbos — for then the table [shulchan] — which is the aspect of honor — the aspect of the table of kings — is in the aspect of the crown of kingship [Keser Malchus] — for on Shabbos the illumination of Keser shines — as is well-known. And then the honor — the aspect of Malchus — has a face — the aspect of: "v'anpehah nahirin [and her face shines]," and so on — the aspect of: "berchu b'me'or panav shel adam — v'chol haggid — berchu b'mat'amim [He blessed it with the light of a person's face — and so on — He blessed it with delicacies]," and so on. And then the table is in the aspect of [Ezekiel 41:22]: "zeh hashulchan asher lifney Hashem [this is the table that is before Hashem]" — the aspect of the lechem hapanim [bread of the Presence] — which is the secret of the twelve loaves of Shabbos corresponding to the twelve loaves of the lechem hapanim — whose arrangement was on Shabbos. For Shabbos is the aspect of the breaking of the lust for eating — the aspect of satiety — as explained in Siman 276. And then the eating is only for the sake of the commandment — for the honor of Shabbos and its holiness — in the aspect of: "tilta hayom kasiv [three times today it is written]" — that the eating is only for the sake of the holiness of the day — in the aspect of [Exodus 16:25]: "ichluhu hayom ki Shabbas hayom laHashem [eat it today — for today is Shabbos to Hashem]" — and as explained elsewhere. And therefore then it is the lifting of the countenance — in the aspect of [Numbers 6:26]: "yissa Hashem panav eilecha — v'yasem lecha shalom [may Hashem lift His countenance toward you — and grant you peace]" — the aspect of Shabbas Shalom — as is well-known.

And therefore through the delight of Shabbos — the kingdoms of the Sitra Achra fall and are nullified — for their kingship is only through arrogance — in the aspect of: "v'hishbati ge'on azim [and I shall cause the pride of the arrogant to cease]" [Leviticus 26:19] — and as mentioned above many times. And this is what our Sages taught: one who delights the Shabbos is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of the shalhava d'asha [flame of fire] that descends on every Erev Shabbos to subdue the impure husks — as mentioned above many times. And then the perfection of the ascent of the sacred Malchus — which ascends from the aspect of: "ragleha yordos maves [her feet descend to death]" [Proverbs 5:5] — as explained in the writings of the holy Ari z"l — and from Tzedek [righteousness] Tzedakah [charity] is made. And this is the aspect of: "shemesh b'Shabbas — Tzedakah la'aniyim [sun on Shabbos — charity for the poor]" — for the honor and delight of Shabbos is itself the aspect of charity — as mentioned above many times. And this is likewise the great excellence of the commandment of charity given to the poor for Shabbos — for through this the Malchus is elevated even more. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:8]: "v'halach lefanecha tzidkecha — (shemarumez al alivat haKavod v'haMalchus el or haPanim k'mevuar b'fanim) — kevod Hashem ya'asfecha [and your righteousness shall go before you — (which alludes to the ascent of the honor and the Malchus to the light of the face — as explained within) — the honor of Hashem shall gather you]," and so on — and juxtaposed to it: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — which alludes to the fact that through the holiness of Shabbos the legs ascend from the aspect of: "ragleha yordos maves" — as explained in the writings of the holy Ari z"l.

And through the holiness of Shabbos the honor returns to those who possess understanding [mevine mada] — for the holiness of Shabbos encompasses both aspects — for it is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of honor — the aspect of the King of Honor — and also the aspect of Binah — as explained in the holy Zohar and the Tikunim — and as mentioned above many times.

And when the honor returns to those who possess understanding — then at the beginning of their dominion dispute arises — and so on — and when their enemies join together — then they draw much sustenance and draw quickly all the waste products and fall — and so on. And perhaps this is the secret of the birth pangs of the Messiah [chavley Mashiach] and the war of Gog and Magog — for then in the days of the Messiah the honor will be returned in its perfection to those who possess understanding — and therefore even before the coming of the Messiah a great dispute will be aroused against Torah scholars — in the aspect of: "dor sheben David ba — kategoria b'Talmidey Chachamim [the generation when the son of David comes — there is an accusation against Torah scholars]" [Tractate Kesubos 112b] — and Rashi explained: many accusers and prosecuting advocates will stand against them — and this is the essential birth pangs of the Messiah — as explained in Rashi, [Tractate Shabbos 118]. And likewise the war of Gog and Magog — when then all the nations will gather to wage war against Israel — and in truth this will be for the good of Israel — for the nations will fall with a complete fall with no one to support them. And because on every Shabbos this aspect is likewise enacted — that Malchus ascends up to Binah — in the aspect of: "u'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi [and you shall guard the Shabbos for it is holy]" — and then the three completely impure husks also wish to ascend with it and draw sustenance from it — and then the shalhava d'asha descends and scorches their heads and they fall — as explained in the writings — and the downfall of the enemies and the husks and the Sitra Achra occurs spontaneously through the holiness of Shabbos. And therefore our Sages taught: one who delights the Shabbos is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah and from the war of Gog and Magog — as mentioned above. And this itself is likewise the aspect of the judgment of Gehinnom — stated concerning it: "al resha'im yachol [it shall befall the wicked]" [Tractate Chagigah 13] — the aspect of the aforementioned shalhava d'asha that descends upon the heads of the husks and scorches them — as mentioned above. And because the sustenance of the enemies comes from the hair [se'aros] — as explained within — therefore if his head-hair has grown long — it is a commandment to cut it — and specifically on Erev Shabbos — as explained in Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 260. And also — Shabbos is the aspect of awe and love [yirah v'ahavah] — and as mentioned above many times — and through this one gives birth to the soul and nurtures it. And this is what our Sages taught [Tractate Shabbos 129b–130a]: "u'meyaldin es ha'ishah b'Shabbas — v'chol haggid — v'koshrin es hatabbur — v'sham (daf kuf lamed): mikan she'meyaldin es havalad b'Shabbas (zeh bechinah haholadah) — v'chotchin es hatabbur — v'rochtzin es havalad — u'malchin es havalad — u'melafipin es havalad b'Shabbas [and one assists women in childbirth on Shabbos — and so on — and ties the umbilical cord — and there (folio 130): from here one may deliver the child on Shabbos (this is the aspect of the birth) — and one cuts the umbilical cord — and bathes the child — and salts the child — and swaddles the child on Shabbos]" — this is the aspect of the growth and strengthening of the child. And therefore one must be very careful on Shabbos to pray with heartfelt concentration [kavannas halev] — for through praying without heartfelt concentration — the soul becomes distanced from the honor — and then there is weariness [ayefus] to the soul — as explained within.

And this [Psalms 92:2]: Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas: "tov lehodos laHashem — v'lezamre lishimcha elyon [good it is to give thanks to Hashem — and to sing praises to Your Name — Most High]" — "elyon [Most High]" — specifically — that is, to direct one's heart properly to Him, blessed be He — Who is exalted above all blessing and praise — in the aspect of: "yisborach v'yishtabach — v'chol haggid — brich Hu l'eila mikol birchata [may He be blessed and praised — and so on — blessed is He above all blessing]," and so on. And this is what is written in the writings: to have in mind מ'זמור ש'יר ל'יום ה'שבת — initial letters: למש"ה [l'Moshe] — and so on. For Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, restores on Shabbos to Israel the crowns that were taken from them and given to him — and so on — for the aforementioned crowns and ornaments were crowned upon Israel when they said "na'aseh v'nishmah [we shall do and we shall hear]" [Exodus 24:7] — and they were as ornaments and as honor for them. And afterward when they sinned with the [golden] calf — they were taken from them — and then the tablets were broken — and forgetting descended to the world — and they became in the aspect of: "zaken she'shachach talmudo l'oneso [an elder who forgot his learning through no fault of his own]" — for they were not so very guilty — but only through the Erev Rav [the mixed multitude]. And then even the thousand lights of Moshe were taken from him. And on Shabbos the thousand lights are returned to Moshe — and he returns to Israel the crowns — for this is the aspect of the rectification of: "hizaharu b'zaken she'shachach talmudo l'oneso l'chavdo [be careful regarding an elder who forgot his learning through no fault of his own — to honor him]." And then the cloud — which is the aspect of forgetting — is split open — and Da'as is revealed — which is the aspect of cool water for a weary soul — for the sin of the calf was also in this aspect — as mentioned above — that is, it was revealed that even when they said "na'aseh v'nishmah" — their heart was not completely with them in fullness — and as understood in the words of the Sages in what they expounded [Tractate Shabbos 88b] on the verse [Song of Songs 4:9]: "libibatini b'achas mei'einayich [you have captured my heart with one of your eyes]," and so on — and see in Midrash Shir haShirim on the verse "libibatini" — it is even more clearly understood — and in Midrash Ki Sisa, section 42 — it is stated explicitly: Rabbi Meir says: not even one day — but they were standing at Sinai and said with their mouths "na'aseh v'nishmah" — and their heart was directed toward idol worship — as it is stated [Psalms 78:36–37]: "vayefasuhu b'fihem — v'chol haggid — v'libbam lo nachon imo [and they deceived Him with their mouths — and so on — and their heart was not steadfast with Him]," and so on — as explained above. And through this the tablets were broken — and forgetting descended to the world — for this is the aspect of [Isaiah 29:13–14]: "ya'an ki nigash — v'chol haggid — b'sefasav kibduni — v'libbam richak mimeni — lachen — v'chol haggid — v'avdah chochmas chachamav [because this people has drawn near — and so on — with their lips they honor Me — but their heart is far from Me — therefore — and so on — and the wisdom of its wise men shall perish]" — that is, the forgetting of the Torah — as our Sages expounded from this [Tractate Shabbos 138b]. And concerning the guarding of Shabbos our Sages taught: even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. Therefore the sin of the calf is rectified through this — for this is the aspect of "Vayakhel Moshe" — and so on — that immediately after Yom Kippur — when they were forgiven for the sin of the calf — Moshe commanded regarding the guarding of Shabbos and regarding the work of the Mishkan — where the revelation of His honor, blessed be He, takes place — in the aspect of [Exodus 29:43]: "v'nikdash b'chevodi [and it shall be sanctified through My honor]" — stated regarding the Mishkan.

And therefore on Shabbos the thousand lights are returned to Moshe — and to Israel the crowns — for this is the aspect of the honor given to the elder who forgot his learning — through which his wisdom returns and is revealed — and cool waters flow to rectify the weariness of the soul that came through the blemish of prayer — as mentioned above. And therefore then is the essential time for the perfection of prayer with concentration — as mentioned above. And therefore one says then in Nishmas Kol Chai: "v'chol haggid — al kein evarim she'filagas banu — v'chol haggid — k'davar she'kasuv: kol atzmosei tomarnah [and so on — therefore the limbs that You distributed within us — and so on — as the matter that is written: all my bones shall declare]," and so on — for through this the bones are also rectified — and one merits to pray in the aspect of: "kol atzmosei tomarnah [all my bones shall declare]" — and so on — as explained within.

And also — our Sages taught: had Israel guarded the first Shabbos — no nation or tongue would have had dominion over them — as it is stated [Exodus 16:27]: "vayehi vayom hashevi'i yatze'u min ha'am lilkot — miyad vayavo Amalek [and it was on the seventh day — some of the people went out to gather — immediately Amalek came]." And therefore it is stated regarding the war of Amalek [Deuteronomy 25:18]: "v'atah ayef [and you were weary]," and so on — the aspect of the weariness of the soul that comes through the distancing of the soul from honor — which comes through blemishing the honor of Shabbos, heaven forfend. And likewise our Sages taught: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they desecrated the Shabbos in it. And therefore in the days of the destruction and the exile it is stated [Lamentations 1:7]: "ra'uhah tzarim — sachu al mishbatehah [enemies saw her — they mocked at her cessations]" — and our Sages expounded: upon her Shabbosim. And it is stated [Lamentations 2:6]: "shachach Hashem b'Tziyon — mo'ed v'Shabbas [Hashem caused to be forgotten in Zion — the appointed time and the Shabbos]." And then the honor of the elders was also blemished — in the aspect of [Lamentations 2:10]: "yeshvu la'aretz yidamu — ziknay vas Tziyon [they sit on the ground in silence — the elders of the daughter of Zion]." And it is stated [Lamentations 5:14]: "zekanim mishsha'ar shavasu — shavasu davka [the elders have ceased from the gate — ceased — specifically]." For this flows from the fact that they blemished the honor of Shabbos — which is the root of the aspect of sacred old-age — the aspect of the thirteen rectifications of the beard [tilissar tikkuney dikna] that ascend there on the holy Shabbos — as is well-known. And therefore when they blemished the honor of Shabbos — in the aspect of [Ezekiel 22:26]: "u'miShabbosai he'elimu eineihem [and from My Shabbosim they averted their eyes]" — through this the clouds that cover the eyes — which are Roma Rabbata and Roma Ze'ira — as explained in the holy Zohar — intensified — and Jerusalem was destroyed — and Israel went into exile — and the inner dimension of the holiness of Shabbos was concealed, as it were — and forgetting fell upon it — in the aspect of: "shachach Hashem b'Tziyon mo'ed v'Shabbas" — as mentioned above. And therefore our Sages taught: had Israel guarded two Shabbosim — they would be immediately redeemed. And the commentators of blessed memory explained: two Shabbosim specifically — one Shabbos to repair the blemish and iniquity of the desecration of the first Shabbos that caused the destruction and the exile — and then the merit of the guarding of the second Shabbos would bring the redemption. That is — for the guarding of the first of the two Shabbosim would be in the aspect of the honor given to the elder who forgot his learning — through which his wisdom returns and is revealed — as mentioned above. Likewise — through the guarding of the first Shabbos — the inner dimension of the illumination of Da'as and the mental faculties of the holy Shabbos that had been concealed until now in the aspect of forgetting would return and be revealed — and the blemish of the desecration of the first Shabbos would be rectified — as mentioned above. And then afterward — through the guarding of the second Shabbos with complete mental faculties and great Da'as — through this they would be redeemed. And the Sages derived this matter properly from what is stated [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — v'chol haggid — v'havi'osim el har kodshi — v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi [who guard My Shabbosim — and so on — and I shall bring them to My holy mountain — and I shall gladden them in My house of prayer]" — for through this one merits to pray with heartfelt concentration — in the aspect of [Psalms 25:1]: "eilecha Hashem nafshi esa — libbi achavin [to You Hashem I lift my soul — my heart I shall direct]" — and through this joy comes — in the aspect of [Psalms 86:4]: "samach nefesh avdecha — ki eilecha Hashem nafshi esa [gladden the soul of Your servant — for to You Hashem I lift my soul]" — and as explained in Sefer haMidos, Simchah, item 12: through heartfelt concentration comes joy.

And also — on Shabbos there is drawn upon each person of Israel the aspect of the sacred old-age [ziknah d'kedushah] — which is the aspect of pure and clear mental faculties — the aspect of: "b'saba mocha shakit v'shchich [in the aged brain that is quiet and still]" — as explained within. And therefore each person of Israel — according to his level — merits then the aspect of rest and repose — also in his mind and his thought — the aspect of: "shevisah mimachsheves avodah [rest from thoughts of work]." And also — through the Da'as itself that is drawn upon each person of Israel on Shabbos — in the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki ani Hashem mekadshechem [to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you]" — and as mentioned above many times — through this each person is in the aspect of: "zaken — zeh kanah chochmah [an elder — who has acquired wisdom]." And when the holiness of Shabbos departs — then the mental faculties and Da'as of Shabbos also depart — and they are concealed in the aspect of forgetting — for this is the aspect of: "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh — avdah milashon shchichah [since it rested — woe — the soul was lost — lost as the language of forgetting]" — as in [Deuteronomy 22:3]: "maher le'abed" — and as explained elsewhere. For the soul is from the aspect of wisdom and remembrance — the opposite of the aspect of forgetting — as explained in the teaching Darshuni, Siman 37. And then the clouds that cover the eyes intensify — and then each person is in the aspect of: "zaken she'shachach talmudo me'chamas oneso [an elder who forgot his learning through no fault of his own]" — for he is not so very guilty — but only because the holiness of Shabbos has departed.

And in truth — if each person had merited on Shabbos to pray at least with complete heartfelt concentration — and to receive the illumination of the holy Shabbos in its fullness — with all his heart and soul — for then the soul would be fully close to its mother [imah] — that is, to the honor of Shabbos in its fullness — then certainly the forgetting would not have been able to intensify so greatly even during the weekdays. And therefore the true Torah scholars are called the aspect of Shabbos even during the weekdays — and as explained in the holy Zohar. But simple people — because even on Shabbos they do not merit to connect themselves so deeply from the inmost part of their soul and thought with the holiness of Shabbos in truth — therefore when the holiness of Shabbos departs — forgetting and concealment fall — and they are in the aspect of: "zaken she'shachach talmudo l'oneso" — and not only that — but they also cause some blemish and concealment even of the aspect of the elders and Torah scholars — in the aspect of [Isaiah 29:14]: "v'avdah chochmas chachamav" — and so on — and as understood within. And through fulfilling [Exodus 20:8]: "zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho" — and our Sages expounded: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — and they stated there: "mei'chad b'Shabbas l'Shabbasa [from the first day for Shabbos]." And behold — the language "zachrehu [remember it]" falls more specifically upon the past Shabbos — that one must remember its holiness and not forget — as mentioned above. And the matter of "mei'chad b'Shabbas l'Shabbasa" is to remember and to prepare oneself for the holiness of the coming Shabbos. But in truth everything is one — for it is impossible to prepare oneself in fullness for the holiness of the coming Shabbos except through connecting one's thought properly to remember the holiness of the past Shabbos upon which forgetting has already fallen — and one is still yearning and longing after its holiness — and one reminds oneself each time with the sweetness of the holiness of the past Shabbos — and one greatly regrets not having merited to receive its holiness in even greater fullness — as mentioned above. This is the aspect of giving honor to the elder who forgot his learning — through which the clouds are split — and the waters of Da'as flow out — and are distributed to each one as is fitting for him — as explained within — that is: through this one merits to prepare oneself in fullness to receive the mental faculties and Da'as of the holiness of the coming Shabbos — in a manner that he will not forget its holiness ever. And this is the essential fullness of Shabbos observance — in the aspect of [Exodus 20:8]: "zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho." And therefore it is common for the guarding of Shabbos to be stated in the form: "Shabsosai" — which are two Shabbosim — that is, the aspect of the two aforementioned Shabbosim — through which the observance of Shabbos is completed as required — and then immediately they are redeemed — as mentioned above.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — which alludes to the ascent of the legs to holiness through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. "Me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — not to engage in labor and the pursuit of one's affairs on Shabbos — for through this one blemishes the holiness of the honor of Shabbos, heaven forfend. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" — that is, the aspect of the meals of Shabbos — for then the table and the eating are in their perfection — in the aspect of: "Tzadik ochel l'sova nafsho [the righteous person eats to satiate his soul]" [Proverbs 13:25] — the aspect of the extra soul one merits on Shabbos. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 55:2]: "shim'u shamo'a eilai va'ichlu tov — v'sisanag b'deshen nafshechem [hearken — hearken to Me and eat what is good — and let your soul delight in abundance]." And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — the aspect of the aforementioned honor.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto" — and our Sages expounded: one should change one's garments [yishaneh milvushav]. For the soul is clothed in honor — therefore one must wear garments of honor for the honor of Shabbos — and for the honor of the extra soul of Shabbos. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos derachecha" — that one's walking on Shabbos should not be like one's walking on a weekday — that one should not take large strides on Shabbos — for through this one gives power to the aspect of the Malchus d'Sitra Achra which has dominion only through arrogance. And also — for large strides confuse the thought from contemplating — for this blemishes, as it were, the holiness of Shabbos — which is the world of thought — the aspect of sacred old-age — the aspect of: "b'saba mocha shakit v'shchich" — the aspect of measured-ness and settled-mindedness [metinus v'yishuv hada'as] — which is the aspect of the way elders walk — slowly and with measured-ness — for they have no waste-surplus of mental faculties [mosar mocha] — and their mind is pure and clear — and they conduct themselves in everything with measured-ness — in the aspect of: "pos'im bo pesi'ah ketanah [they take in it small steps]."

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — that one's speech on Shabbos should not be like one's speech on a weekday — so as not to blemish through this the aspect of honor and the soul of Shabbos. For speech comes from the soul — in the aspect of [Genesis 2:7; Targum Onkelos]: "l'nefesh chayah — l'ru'ach mamallah [to a living soul — to a speaking spirit]" — and as explained elsewhere.

And likewise — the essential honor is in speech — and as explained below within in Siman 194. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha [then you will delight in Hashem — this is the Holy Ancient One]" — that one merits to ascend to the aspect of the holy beard — as it were — where is the essential perfection of the illumination of the supernal holy mental faculties — and there is the essential supernal honor — in the aspect of [Isaiah 24:23]: "v'neged zekeinav kavod [and before His elders — honor]" — the aspect of: "kevod chachamim yinchalu [honor the wise shall inherit]" [Proverbs 3:35].

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — that is, the ascent of Malchus in the aspects of Neh"y — Chag"t — Chab"d. For at first one elevates the aspects of the legs — in the aspect of [Isaiah 41:2]: "Tzedek yikra'ehu l'raglo [righteousness calls him to his feet]" — as explained within. And afterward one must draw the aspect of the rectification of the hands — which are the great hand and the strong hand — for the birth of the soul and its growth — for all of this is likewise the aspect of the rectification of Malchus and honor — as understood within. In particular — as explained in the writings — that on Shabbos Malchus unites to bring forth new souls — that is, the aspect of the birth of souls mentioned above. And the essential perfection of this is when it returns to those who possess understanding — for this is the aspect of Chab"d — the aspect of [Exodus 31:14]: "ki Kodesh hi [for it is holy]" — as is well-known. And in the Gemara our Sages expounded on this: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, the subjugation of the Malchus d'Sitra Achra — which has dominion only through arrogance — as mentioned above. And also: "az tis'anag al Hashem" alludes to the ascent of Malchus to the light of the face — as expounded from the aspect of Atik — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 3:5]: "zaken v'nisa fanim [an elder and one of elevated countenance]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — this is the aspect of the subjugation of the Malchus d'Sitra Achra — so that they have no grip and no sustenance from the Malchus and honor of holiness — but on the contrary — they are lowered and subdued beneath her feet — in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 33:29]: "v'atah al bamosemo tidroch" — and as our Sages expounded.

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of charity — which is the aspect of Yaakov — as explained elsewhere — through which one elevates Malchus and honor — as explained within. And also — Yaakov is the aspect of sacred honor — which is the root of all souls — in the aspect of [Genesis 46:26]: "kol hanefesh haba'ah l'veys Yaakov [all the souls who came to the house of Yaakov]" — and as explained below within in Siman 181. And therefore he is the first of whom it is stated that he guarded the Shabbos — which is likewise from this aspect — as mentioned above. And this is what our Sages expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — that is, the honor of G-d, blessed be He, spreads and is revealed throughout the entire world — in the aspect of [Psalms 72:19]: "v'yimaleh chevodo es kol ha'aretz [and His honor fills all the earth]" — the aspect of [I Chronicles 29:12]: "v'atah moshel bakol [and You rule over all]" — as explained within — which is when one gives charity so as to elevate the honor and the dominion. And charity is from the aspect of Yaakov — the aspect of Ze'ir Anpin — as is well-known. (And see in the Pardes, in the entries of the appellations.) And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — that is, for on Shabbos speech is rectified — which is from the aspect of the soul and honor — so greatly — that the words of speech are in the aspect of the word of G-d — in the aspect of [Isaiah 59:21]: "v'asim devarai b'ficha [and I shall place My words in your mouth]." For when one merits to pray with truly heartfelt concentration — in the aspect of: "kol atzmosei tomarnah [all my bones shall declare]" — then the words of prayer are in the aspect of the word of Hashem — as understood within in the teaching Al asher me'altem, Siman 48. And also — for when one speaks with heartfelt concentration — and the speech comes from the soul whose root is in honor and Binah to come — therefore this itself is likewise the aspect of the honor returning to those who possess understanding — for the aspect of Malchus ascends to Binah — which is the aspect of: "al Hashem" — as explained elsewhere — and then the words of speech are in the aspect of the word of Hashem — in the aspect of [Proverbs 2:6]: "mipiv da'as u'sevunah [from His mouth — knowledge and understanding]." And also — for the heart of Israel is filled with His divinity, blessed be He — and as explained elsewhere — and therefore when one connects the speech to the heartfelt concentration — then the words of speech are in the aspect of the word of Hashem — in the aspect of [Psalms 27:8]: "l'cha amar libbi [to You my heart has said]," and so on — and as explained elsewhere.

 Simanim 68–69 — סימן סח סט
 Chomer Issur Ka'as v'Gezeilah — Severity of anger and theft — Shabbos, wife, wealth, children

Shabbos is the aspect of the root of souls — in the aspect of: "Shabbas vayinafash" — as mentioned above many times. And also — Shabbos is the root of bounty and wealth — from which all six days of the year are blessed — and our Sages taught: "birchas Hashem hi ta'ashir — zeh Shabbas [the blessing of Hashem — it is what enriches — this is Shabbos]" — and the wealthy among the other lands — because they honor the Shabbos.

And therefore the sin of anger on Shabbos is especially severe — as explained in the Tikunim and in other holy books — for through anger one blemishes one's soul and the aspect of wealth — as explained within.

And also — Shabbos is the aspect of the "bas zugo [life-partner]" of Israel — as our Sages taught: "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha [the congregation of Israel shall be your partner]" — and as explained elsewhere. And therefore from there is the root of the wealth that comes through one's wife [bas zugo]. And this is the aspect of the honor of Shabbos — the aspect of: "okiru l'nasheichu — ki heichi d'tis'atru [honor your wives — in order that you should become wealthy]" — and this is the aspect of [Proverbs 31:11]: "botach bah lev ba'alah — v'shalal lo yechsar [the heart of her husband trusts in her — and spoil he shall not lack]" — and as explained in Zohar Vayikra, folio 52.

And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — for through the Shabbos — wealth ascends — which is the aspect of [Numbers 16:32]: "v'es hayekaum asher b'ragleihem [and the substance that was at their feet]" — to holiness. And therefore on Shabbos one must be especially careful about peace with one's wife — as our Sages taught. And therefore on Shabbos is the essential time for sacred union — and through this one merits children who are Torah scholars — for the children are the fruits that grow upon the branches — which are the aspect of wealth and abundance drawn from the holiness of Shabbos. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 1:3]: "asher piryo yiten b'ito [who gives its fruit in its season]" — and our Sages expounded: regarding the Shabbos union.

And therefore our Sages taught: all who add to the expenses of Shabbos — they add to him — and so on — for since one disperses one's money for the honor of Shabbos — through this one completes its light even more — as it were — as also understood within. And through this one receives bounty and even more wealth. And this is what is explained in Tikkun 21, folio 59: "man d'gara mei'oneg Shabbas — k'ilu gazal lei Shechinah [one who diminishes the delight of Shabbos — it is as if he robbed the Shechinah itself]." For this is the aspect of one who robs his fellow's money — through which one blemishes the light of the life-partner of the one robbed — until sometimes one can through this rob one's fellow's wife too, heaven forfend — as brought within.

And see in the writings of the holy Ari z"l — where it is explained also from the secret of the groom and bride [sod chasan v'kallah] encompassed in the holiness of Shabbos — that the prayer of the evening service — "Atah Kidashta [You sanctified]" — corresponds to the aspect of the betrothal [kiddushin] of the bride. And the prayer "Yismach Moshe b'matan chelko" — corresponds to the aspect of the gifts and presents [savlanit u'matanos] that the groom sends to the bride. And the prayer "Tikanta Shabbas" — and so on — is the secret of the banquet [mishteh] that the groom makes on the day of his wedding. And the prayer "Atah Echad" is the secret of the sacred union [yichud] of the groom and bride — and so on. And because the Shabbos night meal corresponds to the aspect of the bride — the aspect of nefesh [soul] — as explained in the holy Zohar and the Tikunim — from which the bounty of wealth and the blessing of riches flows — as mentioned above — therefore it is explained in Zohar Yisro, folio 88: "u'vin kach — man d'ihu b'daraga d'mehemanutha — ba'i l'sadra paturei b'leila d'Shabbata — b'gin d'yisbarach puturei kol inon shita yomim — d'ha b'hai zimuna izdumin berchata l'isburcha kol shita yomim d'Shabbata [and therefore — one who is at the level of faith — must arrange his table on the night of Shabbos — in order that his table should be blessed all those six days — for at this invitation blessing is set to bless all the six days of the week]," and so on — it is understood that the essential bounty of material blessing of food flows from the holiness of the Shabbos night. And this is the aspect of: "shulchan b'tzafon — u'Menorah b'darom — u'Mitah bein tzafon l'darom [a table in the north — and a Menorah in the south — and a bed between north and south]" — as explained in the Tikunim — in the secret of the Shabbos night. The table in the north — this is the aspect of: "harotzeh l'ha'ashir — yatzfin [one who wishes to become wealthy — should face north]" — the aspect of wealth that flows through the aspect of the bride mentioned above — and as explained in Tikkun Shiv'in, folio 126: "u'vah harotzeh l'ha'ashir yatzfin — u'vin dah amar marei Matnisin: okiru l'nasheichu ki heichi d'tis'atru — b'gin d'Tzafon inon — u'mi'Tzafon zahav yeteh [and through her — one who wishes to become wealthy faces north — and therefore said the masters of the Mishnah: honor your wives — in order that you should become wealthy — because they come from the north — and from the north gold comes]" — and as also understood within. The Menorah in the south — this is the aspect of: "harotzeh l'hachkim — yadrim [one who wishes to become wise — should face south]" — the aspect of: "lev chacham l'ymino [the heart of a wise person is to his right]" [Ecclesiastes 10:2] — the aspect of the Torah — the aspect of: "harotzeh lilmod Torah b'tahara — yisa ishah [one who wishes to study Torah in purity — should take a wife]." And our Sages taught [Tractate Yevamos 62]: one who dwells without a wife dwells without Torah and without a wall (that is, the aspect of wealth — as explained within). And this is the aspect of [Proverbs 3:16]: "orech yamim b'yminah — (bechinah mah she'amru Rz"l: Ishah yefah ashrey ba'alah — mispar yamav keflayim) [length of days in its right — (this is the aspect of what our Sages taught: a beautiful wife — happy is her husband — his number of days is doubled)]."

"Osher v'chavod bismalah [wealth and honor in its left]" — (that is, the aspect of the aforementioned wealth).

And therefore our Sages taught: one who is accustomed to the Shabbos candle [ner Shabbas] — will have children who are Torah scholars — for when one takes a wife only for the sake of Torah — one merits children who are Torah scholars — in the aspect of [Isaiah 54:13]: "v'chol banecha limudey Hashem [and all your children shall be students of Hashem]" — as understood within. And this is the aspect of the bed between north and south — which is for the sake of the complete sacred union — through which one merits fitting children who are the good fruits that grow on the branches — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of: "'ha'ishah nikneis b'sheloshah derachim — b'chesef — u'v'shtar — u'v'vi'ah' — 'b'chesef' — this corresponds to the aspect of wealth that flows through her. 'B'shtar' — this corresponds to Torah which is called a book — in the aspect of a document [shtar]. 'U'v'vi'ah' — this corresponds to the children that flow through the sacred union." And this is the aspect of: "chayey — baney — u'mezonay — b'mazla talya milsa [life — children — and sustenance — depend on the constellation]" — that is, these three aspects mentioned above depend on the supernal constellation [mazal] that shines on Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar — which is the aspect of the good woman of whom our Sages said: "hai nami isremey leih bas mazalei [she too was found through his constellation]."

And because one must be very careful not to touch the money of one's fellow — for it is like touching and blemishing, heaven forfend, the life-partner of one's fellow — and sometimes one loses through this one's own life-partner — as explained within — therefore our Sages taught: "aseh Shabboscha chol — v'al titztarech livrios [make your Shabbos into a weekday — but do not become dependent on creatures]" (see also the Tur, Orach Chayyim, Siman 242 — and what the later authorities elaborated on this — and see in the Shulchan Aruch of the Rav, of blessed memory — what he explained in this matter) — for although it is a great commandment to delight and honor the Shabbos — as mentioned above — nonetheless one must take care not to touch for this purpose the money of one's fellow, heaven forfend — for each person — according to his level — has a share in the holiness of Shabbos — and it is the aspect of his life-partner. And according to his level — the influence flows to him from there. And certainly one must be diligent with all one's capacity and tighten one's livelihood during the weekdays — in order to be able to add something for the honor of Shabbos. But not to honor the Shabbos with the money of one's fellow — for through this one may blemish, heaven forfend, one's fellow's share in the illumination of Shabbos that belongs to him.

And not only that — but one can lose, heaven forfend, even one's own share in the illumination of Shabbos — since one is not satisfied with one's own bounty that flows from the holiness of Shabbos — and one touches another's portion. But one who is already in need of others — they give him all his needs for Shabbos as well.

And this is the aspect of the great excellence of charity given for Shabbos — for because through the holiness of Shabbos Malchus ascends — the aspect of the supernal bride — the aspect of nefesh — and then the husks also wish to ascend with it and draw sustenance from it, heaven forfend — primarily from the aspect of the legs — in the aspect of: "ragleha yordos maves" — heaven forfend. And through charity one saves her from this, as it were — in the aspect of [Proverbs 10:2]: "u'tzedakah tatzil mimaves [and charity saves from death]" — as explained within. And through this one merits to receive even more of the bounty of Shabbos. And also — perhaps one has money from theft that came to him through coveting the money of one's fellow — through which one's share in the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos was blemished — as mentioned above — and through charity one rectifies this — as explained within. And therefore the Tanna began [with]: "yetzi'os haShabbas — v'chol haggid — he'ani omed b'chutz [the transgressions of Shabbos — and so on — the poor person stands outside]," and so on — for they engage then in charity to the poor — through which one merits to receive the holiness and the illumination of Shabbos and its bounty even more. But nonetheless one must take care not to bring about through this itself a desecration of Shabbos — in the aspect of: "pashat he'ani es yado — v'chol haggid — he'ani chayav [the poor person stretched out his hand — and so on — the poor person is liable]." And this is the aspect of: "yetzi'os haShabbas — yetzi'os davka [the transgressions of Shabbos — transgressions — specifically]" — from the language of what our Sages taught: one compares the way-out [yetzi'ah] to the coming-in [havi'ah] [i.e., for the laws of marriage and divorce]. Havi'ah is the betrothal [kiddushin] — and yetzi'ah is the separation [pirud] made between them — heaven forbid. And likewise — the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend, is the aspect of the transgressions of Shabbos — and the receiving of the holiness of Shabbos is the aspect of betrothal — as mentioned above.

And behold — our Sages taught: Shabbosim were given only for words of Torah — and as also explained in Shulchan Aruch — that one must engage in Torah on Shabbos — for this is the aspect of: "lev chacham l'ymino" — as mentioned above. For on Shabbos the illumination of Da'as and the exalted mental faculties is drawn upon each person — according to his level — as mentioned above many times. And therefore one must produce Torah novellae on Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar. And one who is not capable of this — at the very least — must engage in words of Torah. And therefore the entire weekly portion is read on Shabbos morning.

And at Minchah one also reads in the Torah — in order to draw the illumination of the Torah also upon the six days of deed. For although during the six days of deed one engages in labor and occupation — all of it is in order to complete the light of one's wife in its particularity — in the aspect of [Aramaic]: "v'ana aflach v'ashakir v'otzin [and I shall work and I shall provide and I shall support]" — and so on — as brought within.

And because the essential flow of sacred bounty comes from the aspect of the light of the life-partner of Israel spiritually and in its generality — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above — and therefore in truth our Sages taught: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — nonetheless — the essential root of the bounty and the sustenance of the tree — which is the woman who fears Hashem — is from the Torah — which is the aspect of the husband of the woman — the aspect of the central column [amuda d'emtza'isa]. And the Torah goes forth from Chochmah and Binah. And this is the aspect of the holiness of the day of Shabbos — which encompasses the aspect of Shabbas ila'ah [upper Shabbos] and Shabbas d'yoma [Shabbos of the day] — and they are the aspects of the spirit [ru'ach] and higher soul [neshamah] of the holy Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar and the Tikunim.

And behold — one who does not fulfill the delight of Shabbos — because one is miserly with one's money —

then ענ"ג [oneg — delight] is transformed for him into נג"ע [nega — affliction] — as explained in the Tikunim — that is, he falls into foolishness which is the opposite of delight — in the aspect of [Proverbs 19:10]: "lo na'avah l'chesil ta'anug [delight is not fitting for a fool]." And through this the aspect of love that comes from the delight of Shabbos — the aspect of: "ahavah b'ta'anugim [love in delights]" [Song of Songs 7:7] — is ruined — and hatred and dispute come upon him — in the aspect of [Proverbs 17:19]: "kol riv v'chol nega [all strife and all affliction]" — the aspect of: "nega v'kalon yimtza [affliction and shame shall he find]" [Proverbs 6:33] — the aspect of [II Samuel 7:14]: "v'hochachtiv b'shevet anashim — u'v'nig'ey vnay adam [and I shall chastise him with the rod of men — and with the afflictions of the children of man]." And also — through this one falls into poverty — as explained in the Tikunim.

And poverty is likewise the aspect of nega tzara'as [the affliction of leprosy] — as explained in Tikkun 22, folio 66. And as our Sages also taught regarding one who marries a woman for the sake of money: a new month enters and a new month goes out — and their money is lost. And it is explained within that one falls into foolishness — and enemies and hatred arise from this — and so on.

And because it is stated there [Tractate Kiddushin 70]: upon all of them Eliyahu writes — and so on — therefore our Sages taught — brought in the Maharil and in the holy Shelah: that at every Motza'ay Shabbos Eliyahu sits and writes the merits of Israel who merited to delight and honor the Shabbos. And therefore one mentions the praises of Eliyahu at Motza'ay Shabbos. And this is what is explained in Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 290: workers and householders should not prolong greatly in the delight of eating and drinking on Shabbos — and it is sufficient for them to delight somewhat — for they must engage greatly in Torah. But Torah scholars may prolong somewhat more in the delight of eating and drinking — and so on. That is — for also within the delight of Shabbos there are aspects of right and left — that is, the aspect of: "orech yamim b'yminah" — the aspect of the delight of Torah study — which is the aspect of the right — and: "osher v'chavod bismalah" — the aspect of the material delight of eating and drinking — which is also a commandment and the honor of Shabbos. But because simple people tend to fall through this into foolishness — in the aspect of: "lev chesil lishmolo [the heart of a fool is to his left]" [Ecclesiastes 10:2] — and to choose only material pleasures even during the weekdays — therefore the primary focus on Shabbos for them is to engage in Torah — which is the aspect of the mental faculties themselves — in order not to fall into the aspect of the surplus-waste of mental faculties — the aspect of hair on the left. But Torah scholars — for whom even their surplus-waste of mental faculties — the aspect of hair — is in the aspect of hair on the right — the aspect of righteous hair — can add somewhat more on Shabbos in the delight of eating and drinking — for through their material delight — which is also of great holiness — through this they have some connection and closeness to the common people — and through this they can also open for them the gates of wisdom and knowledge — to draw them close to G-d, blessed be He. And therefore it is a very great thing to spend Shabbos with the true Tzadikim — and to eat at their table on the holy Shabbos — and for the most part the secrets of Torah are revealed then — and the awe of Heaven is placed in the hearts of the common people.

And this is what is juxtaposed [Song of Songs 7:5–6]: "roshech alecha k'karmel" — Rashi explained: these are the tefillin on the head — (the aspect of the mental faculties themselves). "v'dalas roshech" — Rashi explained: the plaiting of your hair — the aspect of the surplus-waste of the mental faculties — "k'argaman — Melech asur b'rahatim" — and our Sages expounded: "b'rahitey mocha [in the channels of the mind]" — and Rashi explained: in the ringlets — as it is stated [Ezra 8:28]: "nezer Elokav al rosho [the crown of his G-d is upon his head]," and so on — that is, the aspect of the holiness of the hair. And this [Song of Songs 7:7]: "mah yafis u'mah na'amt — ahavah b'ta'anugim [how beautiful and how pleasant — love in delights]" — the aspect of the two kinds of Shabbos delight mentioned above — for both of them are very holy — for even the material delight of Shabbos is also very holy — and the enemies have no sustenance from it, heaven forfend — but on the contrary — love in delights — for at its root even the delight of the Shabbos meal alludes to great mental faculties — as brought in the writings. And also the money dispersed on this for the honor of Shabbos is in the aspect of the nullification of the covetousness of money — the aspect of: "lev chacham l'ymino" — as mentioned above. And therefore — on the contrary — through the power of the delight of Shabbos — it silences the enemy [lehashbis oyev] — and they are rectified — the aspect of the downfall of the enemies — as explained within in the teaching Sha'alu es Riv"k, Siman 57.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — that is, the aspect of the ascent of the sacred legs through the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the prohibition of walking beyond the Shabbos boundary — as explained in the kavannos. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — not to engage in the pursuit of one's affairs as on a weekday — when one engages in this to complete the light of one's wife. But on Shabbos — which is the root of the life-partner of Israel in its generality — it is forbidden to engage in this — for on the contrary — from it all the influences flow — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg — liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — for on the contrary — one must disperse one's money for the expenses of the delight and honor of Shabbos — and all who add — they add to him. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha" — not to take large strides — for this is the aspect of anger and irritation — and takes away one five-hundredth of the light of one's eyes — in the aspect of [Psalms 6:8]: "v'sachah michka'as eini [and my eye has grown dim from vexation]." And this blemishes the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein." And also one blemishes through this the wealth — as explained within and in the teaching Heichal haKodesh, Siman 59. And also — anger is from the aspect of foolishness — in the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 7:9]: "ka'as b'cheik kesilim yanuach [anger rests in the bosom of fools]." And through this one blemishes the eyes — which are from the aspect of wisdom — as it is written [Ecclesiastes 2:14]: "hechacham einav b'rosho [the wise person — his eyes are in his head]."

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — not to speak weekday speech — for then there is sustenance for the foolishness — in the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 5:2]: "kol chesil b'rov devarim [the voice of a fool is in the multitude of words]." And also — through the blemish of speech poverty comes — as explained within in the teaching Anochi, Siman 4. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — from which is the supreme root of the sustenance of the tree and its branches and its fruits — and there everything is of the right — and there is no aspect of the left there at all — as explained within in the teaching l'Shemesh sam, Siman 49.

And from there is the root of all the spiritual and material influences — the aspect of: "chayey — baney — u'mezonay — b'mazla talyin" — as mentioned above. And therefore our Sages expounded on this: they give him all the desires of his heart — that is: life — children — and sustenance — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus on the Shabbos night — which is the aspect of the bride — the aspect of nefesh — for this is the aspect of the drawing of wealth — which is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of [Proverbs 22:7]: "ashir b'rashim yimshol [the rich shall rule over the poor]" — and in a manner where the wealth shall be in supreme holiness — that is, connected to wisdom — in the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 7:12]: "b'tzel hachochmah — b'tzel hakesef [in the shadow of wisdom — in the shadow of silver]" — for this is the aspect of Malchus ascending to Chab"d — as mentioned above.

And therefore our Sages expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, from the grip of the Sitra Achra and foolishness — which is the aspect of: "melech zaken u'chesil [an old and foolish king]."

And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — the aspect of the central column — the aspect of the Torah — from which comes the sustenance of the holy tree — which is the aspect of the woman who fears Hashem — as mentioned above. And Yaakov merited in its fullness the sacred unions — and wealth — and fitting children. And therefore Rachel and Leah said [Genesis 31:16]: "ki kol ha'osher asher hitzil Elokim mei'avinu — lanu hu u'l'vaneinu [for all the wealth that G-d saved from our father — it is ours and our children's]" — that is — for the wealth is from the light of their soul — and it is the aspect of the branches upon which the fruits — which are the children — grow. And this: "v'atah kol asher yomar eilecha Elokim — aseh [and now — all that G-d says to you — do]" [Genesis 31:16] — that is — for it was not in the aspect of one who marries a woman for the sake of money, heaven forfend. But he married them only for the sake of Heaven — for the sake of the fulfillment of the Torah. And through this itself he merited such fitting children — and there was no blemish in his bed — but only in the aspect of [Isaiah 54:13]: "v'chol banecha limudey Hashem" — as explained within. And this is the aspect of an inheritance without limits — as our Sages expounded — that is, the aspect of the fullness of sacred wealth — that nothing is lacking for him — as explained by the commentators of blessed memory. For through the fact that the wealth is connected to wisdom — in the aspect of: "lev chacham l'ymino" — through this nothing is lacking for him — in the aspect of [Tractate Berachos 55a]: "da'as kanisa — mah chasarta [if you have acquired knowledge — what have you lacked?]." And therefore it is stated regarding him: "v'chi yesh li chol [and indeed I have everything]" [Genesis 33:11] — as mentioned above. This [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — that is, for the holiness of Shabbos is the aspect of the perfection of sacred speech — the aspect of Malchus peh — as mentioned above many times. Which is the aspect of the soul — the aspect of: "l'nefesh chayah — l'ru'ach mamallah" — and from there come all the influences — in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 15:6]: "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem [and He will bless you as He spoke to you]" — as explained within in the teaching Va'atem tihyu li, Siman 34. And this is the aspect of [Proverbs 10:20]: "chesef nivchar l'shon Tzadik [the tongue of the righteous is choice silver]" — and our Sages taught: "leshon chachamim ma'ashir [the tongue of the wise enriches]." And speech is the aspect of the revelation of Da'as and wisdom — in the aspect of [Proverbs 2:6]: "ki Hashem yiten chochmah — mipiv da'as u'sevunah [for Hashem gives wisdom — from His mouth — knowledge and understanding]."

 Siman 70 — סימן ע
 Vayehi b'Yom haShemini — Shabbos = Tzadik Yesod Olam — the drawing force — Song of Songs

Shabbos is the aspect of the Tzadik Yesod Olam [the Tzadik who is the foundation of the world] — as explained in the holy Zohar — and it is the aspect of the Tzadik who is the sole unique one in the world — in the aspect of [Psalms 139:16]: "yamim yotzaru — v'lo echad bahem — zeh Shabbas [days were formed — and for Him — one among them — this is Shabbos]."

And it has the drawing force [ko'ach hamoshech] — to draw everything toward it. And therefore it is called "chemdas hayamim [the most beloved of days]" — for all the days and all the created beings — all yearn and long for the holiness of Shabbos — in the aspect of [Genesis 2:2]: "vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i melachto asher asah — mah hayah ha'olam chaseir — menuchah — ba Shabbas — ba menuchah [and G-d completed on the seventh day His work that He had made — what was the world lacking — rest — Shabbos came — rest came]," and so on — and even the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, as it were, longs for it — as our Sages taught. And it is the aspect of humility and lowliness — the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "shvu ish tachtav [let each person remain in his place]" — stated regarding Shabbos — and as explained elsewhere. And from it all the influences flow to the world. And the expenditure dispersed for the delight and honor of Shabbos is in the aspect of charity to the poor — as explained in the holy Zohar and the Tikunim. And it is in the aspect of sowing — in the aspect of [Hosea 10:12]: "zir'u lachem l'tzedakah [sow for yourselves for righteousness]" — like one who sows in good earth — which sprouts immediately double and many times over. Likewise — regarding the expenditure for Shabbos — all who add — they add to him — and it is in the aspect of [Isaiah 61:11]: "k'ganah ziru'eha tatzmiyach [like a garden whose seeds she causes to sprout]" — as explained in Tikkun Shiv'in, folio 38. And also — through the holiness of Shabbos the resting of the divine Presence of His divinity, blessed be He, upon Israel is drawn — as it were — as explained in Zohar Vayikra, folio 179: "b'gin kach lo zazat Shechinah mi'Yisrael b'chol Shabbasos v'Yamim Tovim [therefore the Shechinah does not depart from Israel on all Shabbosim and festivals]," and so on.

And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:16]: "la'asos es haShabbas l'dorosam" — it is written: "la'asos — dirah na'ah laShchinah [to make — a beautiful dwelling for the Shechinah]," and so on — as our Sages taught. And therefore Shabbos is juxtaposed to the Temple and the Mishkan. For the resting of His Presence, blessed be He, in the Mishkan and the Temple — all is drawn through the holiness of Shabbos. And therefore our Sages taught: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they desecrated the Shabbos. And therefore it is a great thing to spend Shabbos with true Tzadikim — for they are the aspects of the branches of Shabbos. In particular — when one merits to spend Shabbos with the Tzadik Yesod Olam — who is himself the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — and then one can receive through him the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos in great fullness — until one merits also the aspect of the resting of the Shechinah — and all the above.

And this is the aspect of [Exodus 35:1]: "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Yisrael" — for Moshe is the Tzadik Yesod Olam — the aspect of Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And therefore he had the power to assemble all of Israel — and to draw them toward him with his drawing force. And then he commanded them regarding the work of the Mishkan and the guarding of Shabbos. And this [Exodus 35:3]: "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem b'yom haShabbas" — for the nature of fire is to lift itself upward — the opposite of the aspect of earth — which has a drawing force through the aspect of humility and lowliness. And in the Temple and the Mishkan — the drawing force was so great — that fire descended from the heavens there — opposite to its nature. And this is what is written [Jeremiah 17:24–25, 27]: "v'hayah im shamo'a — v'chol haggid — v'ladesh es yom haShabbas — v'chol haggid — u'va'u b'sha'arey ha'ir hazos — melachim v'sarim yosh'vim al kisey David" — that is, the aspect of honor and greatness — drawn through the Tzadik Yesod Olam — the aspect of Shabbos — from which all the heads and officers and kings receive their honor — as explained within. And this is the secret of the honor of Shabbos. And [Jeremiah 17:27]: "v'im lo tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — v'hitzasi eish b'sh'areha" — the aspect of the aforementioned fire — which is the opposite of the aspect of the drawing force — as mentioned above.

And this is the aspect of the extra soul that a person merits on Shabbos — all through the greatness of the drawing force of the holiness of Shabbos — through which the Shechinah — which is the aspect of the canopy of peace — spreads her wings over Israel — and with her descend the souls of the Tzadikim to dwell with Israel — and likewise the supernal angels — as explained in the holy Zohar and the Tikunim. And this is what our Sages taught: "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh" — that is — for when the holiness of Shabbos departs — which is the aspect of the drawing force — then the force of compulsion [ko'ach hamachri'ach] begins to dominate. Then at the very least — one must remind oneself each time with the sweetness of the holiness of the drawing force — which is the aspect of the extra soul of Shabbos — as mentioned above — and yearn for it. And this is likewise the aspect of what our Sages taught: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — as mentioned above. And then — through the intensification of the force of compulsion — and through the person intensifying himself each time to remember the drawing force and to long for it — and to draw himself back after it — through this specifically — all the holy clarifications are clarified — that are made through weekday pursuits. And immediately when the holiness of the second Shabbos arrives — then the drawing force intensifies even more — and then all the aforementioned clarifications ascend to their place and their rest in their fullness. And one merits then to receive the holiness of the extra soul of Shabbos in even greater fullness. And this is what our Sages stated in Zohar Vayikra, folio 179 — mentioned above: "b'gin kach lo zazat Shechinah mi'Yisrael b'chol Shabbasos v'Yamim Tovim — v'afilu b'Shabbasos (nuscha achat: b'yomei) d'chol — ela d'ihi sugeres u'msugeres b'hon [therefore the Shechinah does not depart from Israel on all Shabbosim and festivals — and even on the Shabbosim (another version: on the days) of the weekday — but it is closed and locked within them]." For through fulfilling: "zachor es yom haShabbas — zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — as mentioned above — through this one draws the holiness of Shabbos even upon the six weekdays. Through this one draws the resting of the Shechinah — as it were — even during the weekdays. And this is the aspect of: "Shabbasos d'chol — ela d'ihi sugeres u'msugeres b'hon" — that is, then the drawing force is concealed through the intensification of the force of compulsion — but in truth even within the force of compulsion itself — the vitality of the drawing force is clothed. And therefore — through the longing with which one longs — and yearns — and draws oneself after the drawing force — even during the six weekdays — through this specifically holy clarifications are made — precisely through the combination of the two aforementioned forces — the drawing force and the force of compulsion — and as elaborated on this at great length in Likutay Halachos. And then even the weekday labors and occupations are in the aspect of the work of the Mishkan — upon which the aspect of the resting of the Shechinah shines — as it were — as mentioned above.

And this [Psalms 92]: "M'zmor Sh'ir l'Yom haSh'abas" — initial letters: למש"ה [l'Moshe] — for Moshe is the Tzadik Yesod Olam — the aspect of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this [Psalms 92:2]: "tov lehodos laHashem — v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" — that is, to draw oneself in truth after the drawing force that shines on Shabbos — and to give thanks and sing praises to His Name, blessed be He — Who is the essential drawing force — as it is written [Isaiah 26:8]: "l'shimcha u'l'zichrecha ta'avas nefesh [for Your Name and for Your remembrance — is the desire of the soul]." And this [Psalms 92:3]: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — that is, at the time of the revelation of the light of holiness — one must declare His lovingkindnesses, blessed be He — which are the aspect of the drawing force — in the aspect of [Psalms 36:11]: "meshoch chasdecha liyoda'echa [draw Your lovingkindness to those who know You]." And [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — even at the time of the darkness and the concealment — when the force of compulsion intensifies — which is itself the aspect of "choshech" — from the language of restraint — as in [Genesis 22:16]: "v'lo chasachta [and you did not withhold]," and so on.

And as explained elsewhere — one must then also speak words of faith — and draw oneself toward Him, blessed be He — and believe that within the force of compulsion itself — the vitality of the drawing force is also clothed. And the intensification of the force of compulsion is only temporarily — for a brief moment — for the sake of the power of choice. And immediately when the force of compulsion ceases — the drawing force will intensify with even greater strength. And this [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor v'alay navel — alay higgayon b'chinor" — for the sacred melody also has a great drawing force to draw the heart of a person toward G-d, blessed be He — and as explained elsewhere. And the sweetness of melody is the aspect of the clarification of the spirit — which is the aspect of the holy clarifications made precisely through the combination of the two aforementioned forces.
