And this [Psalms 92:5]: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha — b'ma'asey yadecha aranen" — for the general creation was likewise made through the aspect of these two forces — which is the secret of the contraction of the chalal hapanui — which is the hiding of His light, blessed be He — which is the aspect of the force of compulsion — and the drawing of His light, blessed be He, into the aspect of the vessels — for the sake of the revelation and the formation of the entire creation. And this [Psalms 92:6]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem" — the act of creation is the aspect of the force of compulsion — where the light of His divinity, blessed be He, is very hidden. "Me'od amku machshevosecha" — for even there the vitality of the supernal thought is hidden — which is the aspect of the drawing force — which is the aspect of Shabbos — the world of thought — as is well-known. And this [Psalms 92:7]: "ish ba'ar lo yeda — u'chesil lo yavin es zos — b'feroa'ch resha'im k'mo esev — vayatzitzu kol po'aley aven" — for the essential growth of all plants is through the drawing force that exists in the earth — as understood within. For the drawing force draws everything toward itself — and draws vitality and influence to everything. And therefore the fool — who is far from the true sacred wisdom — which is the aspect of the drawing force — in the aspect of [Job 28:18]: "meshoch chochmah mipeninim [drawing wisdom from pearls]" — and as explained elsewhere — is therefore confounded by the success of the wicked. For behold — they are certainly from the aspect of the force of compulsion — and if so — from where do they receive force to bloom and flourish with such great success? — since they are so distanced from the holiness of the drawing force. But in truth — even within the force of compulsion itself — the vitality of the drawing force is clothed — for this itself is the aspect of: "me'od amku machshevosecha" — "me'od" is the aspect of death — as explained elsewhere. And as our Sages taught — and also there is found the aspect of His vitality, blessed be He — but the vitality drawn to the aspect of this force of compulsion is harmful to it. That is — in order to clarify through this the holy sparks — as is well-known. And then death will be swallowed forever — and the aspect of the evil of the force of compulsion will be completely nullified — and all will be drawn after the drawing force. And this: "b'feroa'ch resha'im k'mo esev" — and so on — for their success and their growth is only like grass — which lasts for a brief moment — in the morning it blossoms and changes — by evening it is cut and withers. And also this is only for the sake of their downfall — to be destroyed forever. And: "v'atah marom l'olam Hashem — l'olam yadcha al ha'elyonah" — for the sacred drawing force is very great and powerful — and its hand is always on top — for all will wither as a garment — and so on — and You — He — and Your years shall never end — and so on. And this: "ki hinneh oyevecha Hashem — ki hinneh oyevecha yovadu — yispardu kol po'aley aven — vatarem kir'em karni" — and so on — as mentioned above. "B'kamim alai mere'im" — (the aspect of the intensification of the force of compulsion) — "tishmanah oznai — Tzadik katamar yifrach — k'erez baLevanon yisgeh" — and our Sages expounded: just as the palm tree and the cedar — their hearts are directed upward — and so on — just as the palm tree and the cedar have desire — so too the Tzadikim have desire. And what is their desire? — G-d, blessed be He — and so on. Just as the palm tree produces fruit — and so on — just as the cedar — its stump replenishes — and so on — that is, the Tzadikim who truly draw themselves after the sacred drawing force — which is the aspect of: "libbam mechuvvan l'ma'alah [their hearts are directed upward]" — and they have desire and great longing toward G-d, blessed be He — through this they receive the force of growth and the force of sprouting — and their growth endures forever — and their stump replenishes — and they produce fruit.

"Shetulin b'veys Hashem" — where there is the essential planting — their root and their planting — in the holiness of the drawing force. "B'chatzros Elokeinu yafrichu" — that is, even their outer dimension — eating and drinking and similar things — is likewise of great holiness. And through this specifically — the good that is in the aspect of the force of compulsion is also encompassed in the holiness of the drawing force — and from this wondrous flowers and fruits are made precisely — from the combination of the two aforementioned forces — which is the aspect of what the Tzadikim merit at the very time of their eating and their feast specifically — a wondrous and exceedingly extraordinary illumination of divine will — and as elaborated on this elsewhere.

And this [Psalms 92:16]: "lehagid ki yashar Hashem — tzuri — v'lo avlasah vo" — for everything is straight and correct and trustworthy and beloved — and so on — for the word of Hashem is upright — and so on.

And this [Psalms 93:1]: "Hashem Malach ge'us lavash" — and so on — this is the aspect of the drawing force — where there is the essential kingship and greatness — as explained within. And this [Psalms 93:1]: "af tikon tevel bal timot" — for through the aspect of this drawing force — the world is sustained — and hangs in the middle as it were of His light, blessed be He — and yearns and is drawn to Him, blessed be He — from all sides — and as elaborated in the Or haChayim on the verse [Genesis 2:1]: "vayechulu hashamayim" — and so on — see there in the beauty of his holy words. Or one can say: "Hashem Malach ge'us lavash" — that He clothed and contracted His greatness and power, blessed be He — and as explained below within in Siman 219 — and this is the aspect of the force of compulsion — as mentioned above — and all of this for the sustenance of the world. For through the drawing force alone — it would not sustain, as it were, the creation of the world — and all would be drawn after Him, blessed be He — until they would be completely nullified from their existence. And this [Psalms 93:1]: "af tikon tevel bal timot." And this [Psalms 93:2]: "nakhon kisa'acha mei'az — mei'olam atah" — for even so — the drawing force precedes everything — and is the last of everything — in the aspect of: "ani rishon v'ani acharon [I am the first and I am the last]" [Isaiah 44:6] — in the aspect of [Lamentations 5:19]: "Atah Hashem l'olam teshev — kise'acha l'dor v'dor [You Hashem sit forever — Your throne from generation to generation]." And therefore — even though [Psalms 93:3]: "nasa'u neharos Hashem" — that is, as Rashi explained: even though the gentile nations raised their voice — and they are only from the aspect of the force of compulsion of the Sitra Achra —

and this [Psalms 93:3]: "yis'u neharos dokeyam" — Rashi explained: their depth — and so on — for the force of compulsion of the Sitra Achra intensifies each time even more — until its depth of evil is revealed more each time — for it wishes to completely uproot the person — and to separate him from Him, blessed be He, completely, heaven forfend. And this [Psalms 93:4]: "mikol mayim rabbim addirim — v'chol haggid — addir bamarom Hashem" — as Rashi explained: His hand is powerful over them. For even so — the drawing force is powerful and mighty — and it will certainly complete what is its own. And this [Psalms 93:5]: "edosecha (u'vachtosecha) ne'emnu me'od — l'vayscha na'avah kodesh Hashem l'orech yamim [Your testimonies (and Your promises) are very trustworthy — holiness befits Your house Hashem — for length of days]." For certainly He will rebuild the Holy Temple — and reveal His holiness that is within it — the drawing force to draw the divine Presence of His divinity, blessed be He — and this will be forever — unlike the force of compulsion — which is only temporary — as mentioned above. And likewise — even though according to the lowly understanding of a person it seems to him that it has already been many very long days since the force of compulsion prevailed — and until when is the end of wonders? — even so: if it delays — wait for it.

And one must know and believe that all the more the end is prolonged — certainly through this specifically — the rectification will be completed at an even more wondrous fullness. For certainly the drawing force will complete what is its own — in the ultimate fullness — and precisely through the intensification of the force of compulsion — as mentioned above. And this is what our Sages taught: "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos — miyad nigalin [had Israel guarded two Shabbosim — they would be immediately redeemed]." For Shabbos is the aspect of the drawing force — and after Shabbos the force of compulsion intensifies — and then one must strengthen oneself even more to be drawn — even then — after the drawing force with all one's strength and capacity. And through this one merits to make clarifications — and to receive the illumination of the holiness of the drawing force on the second Shabbos in even greater fullness. And through this specifically the redemption will come — as mentioned above.

And this — one begins Shir haShirim — which is entirely words of yearning and longing and desire after the drawing force. And this: "Shir haShirim asher liShlomoh" — belonging to the King Whose peace [shalom] is His — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — as is well-known. And this [Song of Songs 1:4]: "mishcheni acharecha narutzah" — and so on — the awakening of the drawing force — and it promises him that certainly they will run after it — with both forces — for even the force of compulsion will be encompassed in the holiness of the drawing force — as mentioned above. And this is what it began with: "mishcheni [draw me]" — in the singular — and concluded: "acharecha narutzah [after you we shall run]" — in the plural. And this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 11:13]: "ul'avdo b'chol levavchem — b'shney yitzreichem [and to serve Him with all your heart — with your two inclinations]." And it elaborates on this matter greatly throughout the entire book — and concludes [Song of Songs 8:1]: "mi yittencha k'ach li" — and so on — and [Song of Songs 8:6]: "simeni kachotam al libbecha" — and so on — "ki azzah k'maves ahavah" — and so on — for all the more the love awakens — which is from the aspect of the drawing force — the more the jealousy of the aspect of the force of compulsion arises against it — only that the drawing force prevails so greatly — that on the contrary — the more the force of compulsion intensifies — the more Israel intensify in extra love and longing — for the obstacle is only for the sake of the desire — and as explained elsewhere.

And this [Song of Songs 8:6]: "reshafehah reshefey eish shalheves Yah" — the aspect of the shalhava d'asha that descends on Erev Shabbos — and scorches the heads of the completely impure husks — which are from the aspect of the force of compulsion of the Sitra Achra — for they come from fire — and fire will consume them — for the force of compulsion is from the aspect of fire — which is the opposite of the aspect of earth — as mentioned above — and then the sacred fire forces its nature downward — and subdues them. And this [Song of Songs 8:7]: "mayim rabbim lo yuchlu l'chabes es ha'ahavah — v'neharos lo yishtefuhah" — the aspect of the aforementioned rivers. And [Song of Songs 8:8]: "achos lanu ketanah — v'shadayim ein lah" — and it is explained in the writings of the holy Ari z"l: that שד"י — initial letters of — ש'מאל ד'וחה י'מין מ'קרבת [smol docheh — yamin mekarevet — the left repels — the right draws close] — that is, the aspect of the two aforementioned forces — for in holiness — both of them are needed. But one must be an expert and a great sage in this — to calibrate the balance — and to walk in the middle path — to use the drawing force in its time and its place — and the force of compulsion in its time and its place. For all the time one has not yet merited to complete Da'as — one must distance oneself from one extreme to the opposite extreme completely — as explained in Halachos De'os — and as understood in his words of blessed memory. And this is the aspect of: "azel yittencha k'ach li bshivil d'da'as lo shlemah — v'shedayim ein lah — that is, she has not yet completed her Da'as — and she is not able to calibrate the balance in the matter of the two forces mentioned above — to use them in the aspect of: the left repels — the right draws close. "Mah na'aseh l'achoteinu — b'yom she'yidubbar bah" — Rashi explained: when the gentile nations whisper against her to destroy her — that is, when the evil of the force of compulsion of the Sitra Achra wishes to intensify against her and destroy her completely, heaven forbid.

"Im chomah hi — nivneh alehah tiras kesef" — if she will be firm as a wall — and will sacrifice herself for every matter — so as not to be caught in the net of the force of compulsion, heaven forbid — then: "nivneh alehah tiras kesef" — that is, the illumination of the drawing force will be drawn upon her even more — until she merits to intense holy longings after G-d, blessed be He — and this is what Rashi explained: the holy city will be built for her — and the Chosen Temple — where there is the essential drawing force — and there the holy longings intensify even more — in the aspect of [Song of Songs 3:10]: "toch ratzuf ahavah — mibanos Yerushalayim [its interior lined with love — from the daughters of Jerusalem]." "V'im deles hi — v'chol haggid — v'omeres Keneses Yisrael: ani chomah" — and so on — "az hayisi b'einav k'motzeis shalom" — that is, she merited in her fullness to cleave to the drawing force — which is the aspect of Shabbas Shalom — as mentioned above.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — for during the weekday — when the force of compulsion rules — then its essential intensification is upon the aspect of the legs — in the aspect of: "ragleha yordos maves" — and it prevents one from walking and running after the sacred drawing force — in the aspect of: "acharecha narutzah" — and this is the aspect of: "paras reshet l'ragli [he spread a net for my feet]" [Lamentations 1:13]. But on Shabbos — the legs ascend to holiness.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — one should refrain from pursuing one's weekday affairs — which have a grip of the force of compulsion — but rather engage in the affairs of Heaven — in the aspect of [Psalms 1:2]: "ki im b'Toras Hashem cheftzo [but rather in the Torah of Hashem is his desire]" — and it is written [Psalms 112:1]: "b'mitzvosav chafetz me'od [in His commandments he greatly delights]" — and it is written [I Chronicles 28:9]: "v'avdah b'lev shalem v'nefesh chefetzah [and serve Him with a whole heart and a desiring soul]."

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg — liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — for on Shabbos — when the drawing force shines — then the physical pleasures are precious and very holy — as mentioned above — and there too is the essential honor — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha" — not to take large strides for a matter of choice — but for a matter of a commandment — it is a commandment to even run on Shabbos — as our Sages taught. For this is the aspect of: "acharecha narutzah" — but not to run and be drawn after a matter of choice — which has a grip of the force of compulsion. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — not to speak weekday speech. For the essential intensification of the sacred drawing force is through habituating oneself to always speak holy words — in the aspect of [Jeremiah 20:9]: "ki midy dabriy bo — zachar azkarennu od — al kein hamu me'ay lo [for whenever I speak of Him — I remember Him even more — therefore my insides yearn for Him]." For speech has great power to arouse the heart of a person to be drawn toward G-d, blessed be He. Therefore one must be careful on Shabbos at the very least not to speak words of the weekday — but only holy words — which are the aspects of the holiness of Shabbos — the aspect of the sacred drawing force. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — where there is the root of the illumination of the supernal will — the aspect of: "v'Atika Kadisha gali retzonei" — which is the aspect of the root of the sacred drawing force. And because from the aspect of the drawing force comes the root of all the good influences — therefore our Sages expounded on this: they give him all the desires of his heart.

And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus. For there is the root of all honor and kingship. And in the Gemara our Sages expounded on this: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — which are only from the aspect of the force of compulsion — in the aspect of [Lamentations 1:5]: "hayu tzareha l'rosh [her enemies have become the head]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — which is the central column [amuda d'emtza'isa] — that unites the two forces together — that is, the drawing force — which is the aspect of lovingkindness and love — in the aspect of [Hosea 11:4]: "b'chavley adam emshechem — b'avosos ahavah [with human cords I drew them — with the bonds of love]." Together with the aspect of the force of compulsion — which is the aspect of judgment. And Yaakov — the aspect of Tiferes — the central column — encompasses both of them — and through them completes all the acts and good traits. And this is the aspect of: "olami — olami — v'chol haggid — mi vera'acha — v'chol haggid — Yaakov vera'acha" — for the creation came about through the combination of the two forces together — as mentioned above. And this is what our Sages expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — for then all the constraints are nullified — since the force of compulsion itself is encompassed in the holiness of the drawing force.

And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for Shabbos is the aspect of the holiness of speech in its fullness — as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:23]: "hu asher diber Hashem — Shabbaton — Shabbas Kodesh laHashem" — and so on — and the word of Hashem certainly has a great and awesome drawing force — in the aspect of [Song of Songs 5:6]: "nafshi yatze'ah b'dabro [my soul departed at His speaking]" — until through it all the grip of the evil of the force of compulsion is nullified — which is the source of the success of the wicked — as mentioned above — for this is the aspect of [Isaiah 40:8]: "yaivesh chatzir — naval tzitz — u'dvar Elokeinu yakum l'olam [the grass withers — the flower fades — but the word of our G-d endures forever]." And it is stated: "v'niglah chevod Hashem — v'ra'u kol basar yachdav — ki pi Hashem diber [and the honor of Hashem shall be revealed — and all flesh shall see together — for the mouth of Hashem has spoken]" [Isaiah 40:5]. And it is stated [Psalms 105:18]: "inu v'chevil raglo — barzel ba'ah nafsho — (bechinah hivtergavrus ko'ach hamachri'ach al Yosef haTzadik Yesod Olam she'hu bechinah ko'ach hamoshech) — ad es bo devaro — imras Hashem tzarfashu — shalach Melech vayatirehu [they afflicted his foot with chains — iron entered his soul — (this is the aspect of the intensification of the force of compulsion upon Yosef the Tzadik Yesod Olam — who is the aspect of the drawing force) — until the time His word came — the word of Hashem refined him — the King sent and released him]," and so on — as mentioned above. And Yosef the Tzadik is likewise the aspect of Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar.

Note: Siman 71 states only: "This matter is explained somewhat above in Siman 63."

 ✦ Translator's Summary — Simanim 67, 68–69, 70
 
 Siman 67 — Honor / souls / prayer / Moshe restores the crowns / two Shabbosim: Shabbos = root of souls = honor; blemish of Shabbos = "v'nichresah haNefesh hahi"; the more one is careful with the honor of Shabbos = the more extra illumination of the soul one receives. Jeremiah 17 mapped through honor lens. Shabbos meals = table = Keser Malchus = "Keser Malchus" = "ananpehah nahirin" = twelve loaves = lechem hapanim = Siman 276 cross-ref.; "tilta hayom kasiv"; "yissa Hashem panav eilecha" = Shabbas Shalom. Through Shabbos delight: kingdoms of Sitra Achra fall (arrogance); saved from subjugation; shalhava d'asha descends; "ragleha yordos maves" ascends → "Tzedek Tzedakah" → "shemesh b'Shabbas Tzedakah la'aniyim"; Isaiah 58:8 "v'halach lefanecha tzidkecha / kevod Hashem ya'asfecha." Honor returns to those who possess understanding = Shabbos encompasses Malchus (honor) and Binah; at beginning of their dominion: dispute arises → enemies gather → fall. Birth pangs of Mashiach = Kesubos 112b (Rashi cited); war of Gog and Magog; on every Shabbos: Malchus ascends to Binah = "u'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi" → three impure husks wish to ascend → shalhava d'asha → their downfall; saved from chavley Mashiach and Gog u'Magog; Chagigah 13: judgment of Gehinnom; enemies' sustenance from hair → haircut on Erev Shabbos specifically = SA OC 260. Shabbos = awe and love → birth and nurturing of soul; Shabbos 129b–130a: assisting childbirth on Shabbos / cutting umbilical cord / bathing / salting / swaddling the child. Must pray with heartfelt concentration on Shabbos; prayer without kavvanah = soul distances from honor = weariness of soul. Psalm 92 = "elyon davka" = direct heart to G-d exalted above all blessing = "yisborach v'yishtabach / brich Hu l'eila mikol birchata"; "Mizmor Shir" = roshei teivos = "l'Moshe"; Moshe restores on Shabbos the thousand lights and the crowns taken at the sin of the calf. "Na'aseh v'nishmah" = ornaments and crowns; sin of calf → tablets broken → forgetting descended; "zaken she'shachach talmudo l'oneso"; thousand lights of Moshe taken. On Shabbos: thousand lights returned to Moshe → returns crowns to Israel → cloud (= forgetting) split → Da'as revealed = cool water for weary soul. Shabbos 88b: "libibatini b'achas mei'einayich" (Song of Songs 4:9); Midrash Shir haShirim; Midrash Ki Sisa section 42 (Rabbi Meir: "b'fihem na'aseh v'nishmah / v'libbam to avodah zarah / vayefasuhu b'fihem / v'libbam lo nachon imo"); Isaiah 29:13–14: "v'avdah chochmas chachamav" = Shabbos 138b. Shabbos atones for sin of calf. "Vayakhel Moshe" = immediately after Yom Kippur. "Nishmas kol chai / kol atzmosei tomarnah" = bones rectified through Shabbos prayer. Had Israel guarded first Shabbos = no nation would have dominated = "miyad vayavo Amalek"; "v'atah ayef" = weariness of soul. "Lo charevah Yerushalayim" = desecration of Shabbos; Lamentations 1:7 "ra'uhah tzarim sachu al mishbatehah" (Sages: her Shabbosim); Lamentations 2:6 "shachach Hashem b'Tziyon mo'ed v'Shabbas"; Lamentations 2:10 and 5:14 cited. Thirteen tikkuney dikna ascend to Shabbos; "u'miShabbosai he'elimu eineihem" (Ezekiel 22:26) → clouds of "Roma Rabbata v'Roma Ze'ira" (Zohar) intensify → Jerusalem destroyed → forgetting. "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos miyad nigalin" = commentators: first Shabbos rectifies blemish of first desecration / second Shabbos brings the redemption = both Shabbosim = giving honor to the elder who forgot → Da'as revealed → tikkun of blemish → second Shabbos with complete Da'as → redemption; Isaiah 56:6–7 "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai / v'havi'osim el har kodshi / v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi"; Psalms 25:1 "eilecha Hashem nafshi esa"; Psalms 86:4; Sefer haMidos Simchah item 12: heartfelt concentration brings joy. Shabbos = aspect of sacred old-age ("b'saba mocha shakit v'shchich"); rest also in mind and thought ("shevisah mimachsheves avodah"); each person on Shabbos = "zaken zeh kanah chochmah"; when Shabbos departs: "vav avdah nefesh — avdah milashon shchichah" (Deuteronomy 22:3); soul = from wisdom and remembrance = opposite of forgetting (teaching "Darshuni" Siman 37); clouds intensify; Torah scholars called "aspect of Shabbos" even on weekdays (Zohar); simple people: when Shabbos departs → forgetting → "zaken she'shachach talmudo l'oneso" → blemish even the wisdom of Torah scholars (Isaiah 29:14). "Zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" = "mei'chad b'Shabbas l'Shabbasa": "zachrehu" falls on past Shabbos; "l'Shabbasa" = prepare for coming Shabbos; but everything is one = connect to holiness of past Shabbos (upon which forgetting already fell) = yearn for it = regret not receiving it fully = this is giving honor to the elder who forgot → clouds split → Da'as flows → prepares for coming Shabbos in fullness. "Shabsosai" = two Shabbosim = usual formula. Isaiah 58 mapped: "raglecha" = ascent of legs to holiness; "me'asos chafatzecha" = don't blemish honor of Shabbos; "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" = Shabbos meals = "Tzadik ochel l'sova nafsho" = extra soul = Isaiah 55:2; "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" = the honor; "v'chibadto" = Sages: change garments = soul is clothed in honor; "me'asos derachecha" = no large strides = gives power to Malchus d'Sitra Achra (arrogance) + confuses thought = "b'saba mocha shakit v'shchich" = measured-ness and settled-mindedness = elders walk slowly with small steps; "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" = speech comes from soul = "l'nefesh chayah l'ru'ach mamallah"; essential honor is in speech = Siman 194 cross-ref.; "az tis'anag al Hashem da Atika Kadisha" = ascend to the holy beard = essential illumination of supernal holy mochin = essential supernal honor = "v'neged zekeinav kavod / kevod chachamim yinchalu"; "hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = Neh"y/Chag"t/Chab"d = first: elevate legs = "Tzedek yikra'ehu l'raglo" (Isaiah 41:2); then: rectification of hands (great hand and strong hand) = birth and growth of soul = tikkun of Malchus and honor; on Shabbos: Malchus unites to bring forth new souls (writings); perfection when returns to "mevine mada" = Chab"d = "ki Kodesh hi"; saved from subjugation = Malchus d'Sitra Achra = arrogance; "az tis'anag" = ascent of Malchus to light of the face = "Atik" = "zaken v'nisa fanim"; "hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" = subjugation of Malchus d'Sitra Achra; "v'atah al bamosemo tidroch." "Heritage of Yaakov" = charity = aspect of Yaakov; also: Yaakov = sacred honor = root of all souls = "kol hanefesh haba'ah l'veys Yaakov" = Siman 181 cross-ref.; nachalah b'li metzarim = honor of G-d spreads throughout the world = "v'yimaleh chevodo es kol ha'aretz / v'atah moshel bakol"; Siman 34 "v'havi'osim" cross-ref.; Pardes cited. "Ki pi Hashem diber" = speech rectified = soul and honor → words of prayer = word of G-d = "v'asim devarai b'ficha"; Siman 48 "Al asher me'altem" cross-ref.; speech from soul whose root is in honor and Binah = Malchus ascends to Binah = "al Hashem"; Proverbs 2:6; heart of Israel filled with His divinity; "l'cha amar libbi" (Psalms 27:8).
 Simanim 68–69 — Shabbos/wife/wealth/children / Tikkun 21 / Tikkun 22 / Zohar Yisro 88 / Tikkun Shiv'in 126 / SA OC 290 / Song of Songs 7 / Maharil / Shelah: Shabbos = root of souls + root of bounty and wealth = "birchas Hashem hi ta'ashir — zeh Shabbas" (Sages); wealthy in other lands = because they honor Shabbos. Anger on Shabbos especially severe (Tikunim and other holy books) = blemishes soul and wealth. Shabbos = "bas zugo" of Israel = "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha"; root of wealth from one's wife/partner; "okiru l'nasheichu ki heichi d'tis'atru"; "botach bah lev ba'alah v'shalal lo yechsar" (Proverbs 31:11; Zohar Vayikra 52). "Im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" = wealth = "v'es hayekaum asher b'ragleihem" (Numbers 16:32) ascends through Shabbos; must be careful about peace with one's wife on Shabbos (Sages); Shabbos = essential time for sacred union → children who are Torah scholars = fruits on branches = wealth; "asher piryo yiten b'ito" (Psalms 1:3; Sages: Shabbos union). "Kol hamosif b'hotza'os Shabbas mosifin lo"; Tikkun 21 folio 59: "man d'gara mei'oneg Shabbas k'ilu gazal lei Shechinah" = robbing one's fellow's money = blemishing his partner's light. Ari z"l: secret of groom and bride in Shabbos = "Atah Kidashta" = kiddushin of bride; "Yismach Moshe" = gifts sent to bride; "Tikanta Shabbas" = wedding banquet; "Atah Echad" = yichud of groom and bride. Zohar Vayikra 52 and Zohar Yisro 88 (full Aramaic cited): "u'vin kach man d'ihu b'daraga d'mehemanutha ba'i l'sadra paturei b'leila d'Shabbata b'gin d'yisbarach puturei kol inon shita yomim" = Shabbos night meal → essential material blessing of food flows from Shabbos night holiness. "Shulchan b'Tzafon / Menorah b'Darom / Mitah bein Tzafon l'Darom" (Tikunim: secret of Shabbos night). Table in north = "harotzeh l'ha'ashir yatzfin"; Tikkun Shiv'in folio 126 (full Aramaic cited): "okiru l'nasheichu ki heichi d'tis'atru b'gin d'Tzafon inon u'mi'Tzafon zahav yeteh." Menorah in south = "harotzeh l'hachkim yadrim"; "lev chacham l'ymino"; "harotzeh lilmod Torah b'tahara yisa ishah"; Yevamos 62: "hasharu b'lo ishah sharu b'lo Torah u'v'lo chomah"; "orech yamim b'yminah" (Proverbs 3:16; + Sages: "ishah yefah ashrey ba'alah mispar yamav keflayim"). "Osher v'chavod bismalah." Ner Shabbas → children who are Torah scholars (Sages); "v'chol banecha limudey Hashem." Bed between north and south = complete sacred union → fitting children = good fruits on branches. "Ha'ishah nikneis b'sheloshah derachim: b'chesef (= wealth) / b'shtar (= Torah) / b'vi'ah (= children)." "Chayey baney u'mezonay b'mazla talya milsa" = three aspects = depend on supernal mazal on Shabbos (Zohar) = the good woman = "hai nami isremey leih bas mazalei." Must not touch fellow's money = like touching his wife's light → "aseh Shabboscha chol v'al titztarech livrios" (Tur OC 242; SA of the Rav cited); each person has his own share in Shabbos holiness = his bas zugo; must tighten livelihood during weekdays to add for Shabbos; but not to honor Shabbos with another's money. One who is already in need: given all his Shabbos needs. Greatness of charity for Shabbos = through Shabbos: Malchus (= supernal bride = nefesh) ascends → husks wish to ascend and draw from her = primarily from the legs ("ragleha yordos maves") → through charity: saved from this = "u'tzedakah tatzil mimaves" (Proverbs 10:2); also: perhaps has stolen money from coveting → through charity rectifies this. Tanna began "yetzi'os haShabbas / he'ani omed b'chutz" = charity to poor → merits to receive holiness of Shabbos more; must take care not to bring about desecration of Shabbos itself = "pashat he'ani es yado / he'ani chayav." "Yetzi'os haShabbas davka" = from language of "mekish havi'ah l'yetzi'ah" = havi'ah = kiddushin; yetzi'ah = separation = desecration of Shabbos = separation; receiving Shabbos holiness = kiddushin. "Lo nitnah Shabbasos ela l'divrey Torah" (SA); must produce Torah novellae (Zohar); at minimum: engage in Torah; read entire parasha on Shabbos morning. At Minchah: also read Torah = draw illumination of Torah upon six weekdays; weekday labor = complete light of wife in its particularity = "v'ana aflach v'ashakir v'otzin." Root of sacred bounty = light of life-partner of Israel spiritually and in generality = Shabbos; "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas"; but essential root of bounty and sustenance of the tree = the woman who fears Hashem = from Torah = husband of the woman = amuda d'emtza'isa = oraissa from Chochmah and Binah; Shabbas ila'ah and Shabbas d'yoma = ru'ach and neshamah of Shabbos (Zohar; Tikunim). Miserliness on Shabbos delight: "oneg → nega" (Tikunim) = falls into foolishness; Proverbs 19:10; "ahavah b'ta'anugim" (Song of Songs 7:7) ruined → hatred and dispute = "kol riv v'chol nega" = "nega v'kalon yimtza / v'hochachtiv b'shevet anashim u'v'nig'ey vnay adam" (II Samuel 7:14); poverty (Tikunim); poverty = nega tzara'as = Tikkun 22 folio 66; marrying for money → "month enters and month goes out / money is lost." Kiddushin 70; Maharil and Shelah haKadosh: Eliyahu writes merits of those who delighted and honored Shabbos on every Motza'ay Shabbos. SA OC 290: workers = don't prolong in eating/drinking + engage greatly in Torah; Torah scholars may prolong somewhat more. Two kinds of Shabbos delight = right and left = "orech yamim b'yminah" (Torah/delight = right) + "osher v'chavod bismalah" (material delight = left); simple people tend toward left = "lev chesil lishmolo" → primary focus for them = Torah = mochin themselves = don't fall into mosar mocha = hair on left; Torah scholars: even their mosar mocha = hair on right = "sa'aros b'yamin" = can add more in material delight = closeness to common people → open for them gates of wisdom → great to spend Shabbos with true Tzadikim. Song of Songs 7:5–6: "roshech alecha k'karmel" (Rashi: tefillin on head = mochin themselves) + "v'dalas roshech k'argaman Melech asur b'rahatim" (Sages: "b'rahitey mocha" = channels of mind; Rashi: ringlets = "nezer Elokav al rosho"); Song of Songs 7:7: "mah yafis u'mah na'amt ahavah b'ta'anugim" = two kinds of Shabbos delight = both very holy = enemies have no sustenance from Shabbos delight = "lahashbis oyev" = Siman 57 "Sha'alu es Riv"k." Isaiah 58 mapped: "raglecha" = ascent of sacred legs = prohibition beyond Shabbos boundary; "me'asos chafatzecha" = not to engage in completing light of one's wife (weekday task); Shabbos = root of wife in generality → from it all influences flow; "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg / liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" = disperse money for Shabbos = "kol hamosif mosifin lo"; "v'chibadto / lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah" = anger + "sachah michka'as eini" (Psalms 6:8) + "tlas guvnin d'eina" + Siman 59 "Heichal haKodesh"; "ka'as b'cheik kesilim yanuach" (Ecclesiastes 7:9); "hechacham einav b'rosho"; "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" = foolishness nourished = "kol chesil b'rov devarim"; speech and poverty = Siman 4 "Anochi"; "az tis'anag al Hashem da Atika Kadisha" = root of sustenance = "chayey baney u'mezonay b'mazla talyin" = Siman 49 "l'Shemesh sam"; Sages: "nositin lo kol mishalos libo" = chayey baney u'mezonay; "hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus on Shabbos night = bride = nefesh = wealth = Malchus = "ashir b'rashim yimshol" = connected to wisdom = "b'tzel hachochmah b'tzel hakesef" = Malchus to Chab"d; saved from subjugation = "melech zaken u'chesil"; "heritage of Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin = amuda d'emtza'isa = Torah" = sustenance of holy tree = woman who fears Hashem; Yaakov's sacred unions + wealth + fitting children; Rachel and Leah's words (Genesis 31:16); Yaakov not marrying for money → "v'chol banecha limudey Hashem"; nachalah b'li metzarim = fullness of sacred wealth = nothing lacking = "da'as kanisa mah chasarta"; "v'chi yesh li chol" (Genesis 33:11); "ki pi Hashem diber" = holiness of speech = Malchus peh = "l'nefesh chayah l'ru'ach mamallah" = "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem" = Siman 34; "chesef nivchar leshon Tzadik / leshon chachamim ma'ashir"; Proverbs 2:6.
 Siman 70 — Ko'ach hamoshech (drawing force) vs. ko'ach hamachri'ach (force of compulsion) / Tzadik Yesod Olam / Zohar Vayikra 179 / Siman 219 / Or haChayim / Likutay Halachos / Song of Songs fully mapped: Shabbos = Tzadik Yesod Olam (Zohar) = sole unique one in the world = "yamim yotzaru v'lo echad bahem zeh Shabbas." Has the drawing force = draws everything toward it = "chemdas hayamim" = all days and all created beings yearn and long for Shabbos = "vayechal Elokim / mah hayah ha'olam chaseir / menuchah / ba Shabbas ba menuchah"; even G-d Himself, as it were, longs for it (Sages). Aspect of humility and lowliness = "shvu ish tachtav." Expenditure for Shabbos = charity to poor (Zohar; Tikunim) = sowing = "zir'u lachem l'tzedakah" (Hosea 10:12) = "k'ganah ziru'eha tatzmiyach" = Tikkun Shiv'in folio 38. Zohar Vayikra 179: "lo zazat Shechinah mi'Yisrael b'chol Shabbasos v'Yamim Tovim." "La'asos es haShabbas l'dorosam" = "la'asos dirah na'ah laShchinah" (Sages); Shabbos juxtaposed to Temple and Mishkan; "lo charevah Yerushalayim" = desecration of Shabbos; great to spend Shabbos with true Tzadikim = aspects of branches of Shabbos; in particular with Tzadik Yesod Olam = aspect of Shabbos itself. "Vayakhel Moshe" = Moshe = Tzadik Yesod Olam = aspect of Shabbos = had ko'ach hamoshech to assemble all Israel. "Lo seva'aru eish" = nature of fire = lifts upward = opposite of earth's drawing force; in Temple and Mishkan: drawing force so great = fire descended from heavens = opposite of its nature. Jeremiah 17 cited; honor and greatness drawn through Tzadik Yesod Olam = Shabbos = all heads/officers/kings receive honor from there; "v'hitzasi eish b'sh'areha" = aspect of fire = opposite of drawing force. Extra soul = through greatness of ko'ach hamoshech of Shabbos = Shechinah (= canopy of peace) spreads wings over Israel = souls of Tzadikim descend to dwell with Israel = supernal angels (Zohar; Tikunim). "Keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" = departure of Shabbos = ko'ach hamoshech departs → ko'ach hamachri'ach begins to dominate → must remind oneself each time with sweetness of ko'ach hamoshech = extra soul; "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas." Through intensification of ko'ach hamachri'ach + person draws himself after ko'ach hamoshech → holy clarifications are made from weekday pursuits → when second Shabbos arrives: ko'ach hamoshech intensifies even more → all clarifications ascend to their place → receives extra soul of Shabbos in even greater fullness. Zohar Vayikra 179 (full Aramaic): "lo zazat Shechinah mi'Yisrael b'chol Shabbasos v'Yamim Tovim v'afilu b'Shabbasos d'chol ela d'ihi sugeres u'msugeres b'hon" = through "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas": draw Shabbos holiness even upon six weekdays → draw resting of Shechinah even on weekdays → "Shabbasos d'chol = ihi sugeres u'msugeres b'hon" = within the ko'ach hamachri'ach itself: vitality of ko'ach hamoshech is clothed → through longing after ko'ach hamoshech also during weekdays → holy clarifications made precisely through combination of both forces → weekday labors and occupations also become in aspect of work of Mishkan. Psalm 92 mapped through ko'ach hamoshech/machri'ach lens: "l'Moshe" = Moshe = Tzadik Yesod Olam; "tov lehodos / v'lezamre" = draw oneself after ko'ach hamoshech = give thanks to His Name = "l'shimcha u'l'zichrecha ta'avas nefesh" (Isaiah 26:8); "lehagid baboker chasdecha" = at time of revelation of holy light → declare His lovingkindnesses = ko'ach hamoshech = "meshoch chasdecha liyoda'echa" (Psalms 36:11); "v'emunascha baleilos" = time of darkness when ko'ach hamachri'ach intensifies = "choshech" from language of withholding = Genesis 22:16 "v'lo chasachta"; must speak words of faith; within ko'ach hamachri'ach itself = vitality of ko'ach hamoshech is clothed; intensification of ko'ach hamachri'ach = only temporarily for the sake of free choice; when it ceases = ko'ach hamoshech intensifies with even greater strength. "Alay asor v'alay navel alay higgayon b'chinor" = sacred melody has great ko'ach hamoshech to draw heart to G-d; sweetness of melody = clarification of the spirit = holy clarifications made through combination of both forces. "Ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" = general creation = through aspect of two forces = secret of tzimtzum of chalal hapanui = hiding of G-d's light (= ko'ach hamachri'ach) + drawing G-d's light into the vessels (= revelation of all creation). "Mah gadlu ma'asecha" = po'el = ko'ach hamachri'ach; "me'od amku machshevosecha" = vitality of supernal thought hidden there = ko'ach hamoshech = Shabbos = world of thought. "Ish ba'ar lo yeda / b'feroa'ch resha'im" = essential growth of all plants = through drawing force in the earth; fool is far from true wisdom = ko'ach hamoshech = "meshoch chochmah mipeninim" (Job 28:18); confounded by success of wicked = wicked are from ko'ach hamachri'ach; but within ko'ach hamachri'ach itself = vitality of ko'ach hamoshech is clothed = "me'od amku machshevosecha / me'od is the aspect of death" (elsewhere; Sages); their success = for clarification of holy sparks; then death swallowed forever = evil of ko'ach hamachri'ach nullified. "B'feroa'ch resha'im k'mo esev" = their success = like grass = temporary. "V'atah marom l'olam Hashem / l'olam yadcha al ha'elyonah" = sacred ko'ach hamoshech = very great and powerful = hand always on top = all will wither as a garment. "Ki hinneh oyevecha / yispardu / vatarem kir'em karni" = as mentioned above. "B'kamim alai mere'im" = intensification of ko'ach hamachri'ach; "tishmanah oznai / Tzadik katamar yifrach k'erez baLevanon" = Sages: "libbam mechuvvan l'ma'alah / yesh lahem ta'avah / mah taavasam haKBH"; "mah tamar oseh peiros / arz giz'o machalif" = those who truly draw after ko'ach hamoshech → receive force of growth → growth endures forever → stump replenishes → produce fruit. "Shetulin b'veys Hashem" = essential planting in holiness of ko'ach hamoshech; "b'chatzros Elokeinu yafrichu" = even their outer dimension (eating/drinking) = in great holiness → good of ko'ach hamachri'ach encompassed in holiness of ko'ach hamoshech → wondrous fruits from combination of both forces → Tzadikim merit at very time of their eating/feast: extraordinary illumination of divine will (elsewhere). "Lehagid ki yashar Hashem tzuri v'lo avlasah vo" = everything is straight and correct and trustworthy. "Hashem Malach ge'us lavash" = ko'ach hamoshech = essential kingship and greatness (within); "af tikon tevel bal timot" = through ko'ach hamoshech = world is sustained = hangs in middle of His light = yearns and drawn to Him from all sides = Or haChayim on "vayechulu hashamayim." Or: "Hashem Malach ge'us lavash" = He clothed and contracted His greatness (Siman 219 cross-ref.) = ko'ach hamachri'ach = for sustenance of the world (without ko'ach hamachri'ach: all would be drawn to complete nullification); "af tikon tevel bal timot"; "nakhon kisa'acha mei'az / mei'olam atah" = ko'ach hamoshech precedes all and is last of all = "ani rishon v'ani acharon" (Isaiah 44:6); "Atah Hashem l'olam teshev" (Lamentations 5:19). "Nasa'u neharos Hashem" = Rashi: nations raised their voices = ko'ach hamachri'ach of Sitra Achra; "yis'u neharos dokeyam" = Rashi: their depth = ko'ach hamachri'ach intensifies → reveals deeper evil = wishes to completely uproot person from G-d; "mikol mayim rabbim addirim / addir bamarom Hashem" = Rashi: His hand powerful over them = ko'ach hamoshech is mighty; "edosecha ne'emnu me'od / l'vayscha na'avah kodesh Hashem l'orech yamim" = certainly will rebuild Holy Temple = reveal holiness = ko'ach hamoshech = forever (unlike ko'ach hamachri'ach = only temporary); even if the end seems prolonged = "im yismameh chakei lo" = the more the end is prolonged = the rectification will be completed at even more wondrous fullness → ko'ach hamoshech will complete what is its own through the intensification of ko'ach hamachri'ach. "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos miyad nigalin" = Shabbos = ko'ach hamoshech; after Shabbos = ko'ach hamachri'ach intensifies → strengthen oneself to be drawn after ko'ach hamoshech even then → holy clarifications → receive illumination of ko'ach hamoshech on second Shabbos in greater fullness → redemption will come. "Shir haShirim" = entirely words of yearning/longing/desire after ko'ach hamoshech; "asher liShlomoh" = King Whose peace is His = Shabbos; "mishcheni acharecha narutzah" = awakening of ko'ach hamoshech = promise: will run after it with both forces = even ko'ach hamachri'ach will be encompassed in ko'ach hamoshech; began in singular "mishcheni" / concluded in plural "narutzah" = "ul'avdo b'chol levavchem b'shney yitzreichem" (Deuteronomy 11:13). Song of Songs elaborates throughout; concludes with "mi yittencha k'ach li / simeni kachotam al libbecha / ki azzah k'maves ahavah" = more love (= ko'ach hamoshech) awakens → more jealousy of ko'ach hamachri'ach arises → but ko'ach hamoshech prevails greatly → more ko'ach hamachri'ach intensifies → Israel intensify in extra love and longing → obstacle is only for the sake of desire (elsewhere). "Reshafehah reshefey eish shalheves Yah" = shalhava d'asha on Erev Shabbos = scorches heads of impure husks = ko'ach hamachri'ach of Sitra Achra = they come from fire → sacred fire forces its nature downward → subdues them. "Mayim rabbim lo yuchlu / neharos lo yishtefuhah." "Achos lanu ketanah v'shadayim ein lah" = Ari z"l: "shady"m = roshei teivos = "shmal docheh — yamin mekarevet" = left repels — right draws close = two forces; in holiness: both needed; but must be expert and great sage = calibrate the balance = walk the middle path; if not yet complete Da'as: distance oneself from one extreme to the other extreme entirely = Halachos De'os = "b'sha'as hagzeizah afilu arakvta d'misa'anei yehareig v'al ya'avor." "Achos lanu ketanah" = not yet complete in Da'as = cannot calibrate the balance in matter of two forces; "mah na'aseh l'achoteinu b'yom she'yidubbar bah" = Rashi: when nations whisper to destroy her = evil of ko'ach hamachri'ach of Sitra Achra wishes to prevail completely. "Im chomah hi nivneh alehah tiras kesef" = if firm as a wall = sacrifice herself for every matter → illumination of ko'ach hamoshech drawn upon her even more → intense holy longings = Rashi: holy city built for her and Chosen Temple = essential ko'ach hamoshech → "tuch ratzuf ahavah mibanos Yerushalayim" (Song of Songs 3:10). "Ani chomah / az hayisi b'einav k'motzeis shalom" = merited fully to cleave to ko'ach hamoshech = Shabbas Shalom. Isaiah 58 mapped through ko'ach hamoshech/machri'ach lens: "raglecha" = during weekday: ko'ach hamachri'ach rules → primarily attacks legs = "ragleha yordos maves" → prevents running after ko'ach hamoshech = "acharecha narutzah" → "paras reshet l'ragli" (Lamentations 1:13); on Shabbos: legs ascend to holiness; "me'asos chafatzecha" = refrain from weekday affairs (= ko'ach hamachri'ach) → engage in affairs of Heaven = "ki im b'Toras Hashem cheftzo / b'mitzvosav chafetz me'od / v'avdah b'lev shalem v'nefesh chefetzah"; "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg / liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" = ko'ach hamoshech shines on Shabbos → physical pleasures precious and holy + essential honor; "v'chibadto / lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah" = no large strides for matters of choice; but for a commandment: mitzvah to even run on Shabbos (Sages) = "acharecha narutzah"; "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" = essential intensification of ko'ach hamoshech = through habituating oneself to always speak holy words = "ki midy dabriy bo zachar azkarennu od al kein hamu me'ay lo" (Jeremiah 20:9); speech has great power to draw heart to G-d; "az tis'anag al Hashem da Atika Kadisha" = root of illumination of supernal will = "v'Atika Kadisha gali retzonei" = root of sacred ko'ach hamoshech; "nositin lo kol mishalos libo." "Hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus; root of all honor and kingship; saved from subjugation of kingdoms = only from ko'ach hamachri'ach = "hayu tzareha l'rosh" (Lamentations 1:5). "Heritage of Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin = amuda d'emtza'isa" = unites two forces = ko'ach hamoshech (lovingkindness and love) = "b'chavley adam emshechem b'avosos ahavah" (Hosea 11:4) + ko'ach hamachri'ach (judgment); Yaakov = Tiferes = amuda d'emtza'isa = encompasses both; "olami olami Yaakov vera'acha" = creation through combination of two forces; nachalah b'li metzarim = all constraints nullified = ko'ach hamachri'ach itself encompassed in holiness of ko'ach hamoshech. "Ki pi Hashem diber" = holiness of speech in fullness = "hu asher diber Hashem Shabbaton Shabbas Kodesh laHashem" (Exodus 16:23); word of Hashem = great and awesome ko'ach hamoshech = "nafshi yatze'ah b'dabro" (Song of Songs 5:6); nullifies grip of evil of ko'ach hamachri'ach = success of wicked = "yaivesh chatzir naval tzitz u'dvar Elokeinu yakum l'olam" (Isaiah 40:8); "v'niglah chevod Hashem v'ra'u kol basar yachdav ki pi Hashem diber" (Isaiah 40:5); Psalms 105:18: "inu v'chevil raglo barzel ba'ah nafsho (= intensification of ko'ach hamachri'ach upon Yosef haTzadik Yesod Olam = ko'ach hamoshech) / ad es bo devaro / imras Hashem tzarfashu / shalach Melech vayatirehu"; Yosef haTzadik = aspect of Shabbos (Zohar). Siman 71: "This matter is explained somewhat above in Siman 63."

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 72 — סימן עב
 Strengthening oneself at every time against the evil inclination — the new, refined yetzer hara at entry of Shabbos — Ein Sof illumination requires being entirely good

To strengthen oneself at every time against the evil inclination.

Sometimes a person prepares himself to receive the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos with great desire — and then at the very moment of the entry of Shabbos — sometimes the evil inclination intensifies against him — and he falls from his longing and loses all his desire. Let him not be alarmed by his thoughts, heaven forfend, that his preparation was for naught. But he should know that on the contrary — through his preparation — the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos was drawn upon him — until the material aspect of his evil inclination that he had previously was nullified and subdued — for through the holiness of Shabbos the evil inclination is subdued each time — as mentioned above. And for the sake of the power of free choice — one must be given a new evil inclination — and this evil inclination is somewhat finer and more spiritual than the evil inclination he had previously — and it is from a higher and finer level. And therefore it has the power to prevail against him even after the preparation he had made — for on the contrary — one who is greater than his fellow — his evil inclination is greater than him.

And then — when he knows this — that through the power of the preparation alone — by which he prepared himself on a weekday to receive the holiness of Shabbos — he merited to nullify the aspect of his evil inclination that he had previously — then all the more so: how much he must now hasten and intensify himself — now that he has already entered into the holiness of Shabbos — and not to look at any confusion or obstacle or faint-heartedness at all — and receive the holiness of Shabbos with great joy. For even all those liable to Gehinnom have rest on it [Shabbos] — and all the more so a person while alive — certainly he can intensify with his good choice to believe so greatly in the holiness of Shabbos — until through this itself he is saved from all kinds of darkness and confusion of mind — and then through this specifically he merits to receive the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos with additional extra measure. And sometimes this very darkness that comes upon him at the beginning of the entry of Shabbos — this itself flows from the aspect of the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos. For during the weekday — foolishness prevailed over him so greatly — that he did not know how to understand and discern between day and night — between light and darkness — and he did not feel the lowliness of his level so greatly.

And now — because of the illumination of Shabbos — when then knowledge [da'as] and mental faculties are drawn upon each person according to his level — through this he now begins to feel the darkness. Like the dangerously ill patient — who does not feel his pains at all — and when he begins to feel his pains — it is the sprouting of the horn of salvation to return to his health fully — and as elaborated on this at length in the books of ethical guidance. And this is the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 1:18]: "ki b'rov chochmah rov ka'as — v'yosif da'as yosif mach'ov [for in much wisdom is much vexation — and one who adds knowledge adds pain]" — literally. For at first he was in the aspect of: a fool does not feel anything — and now that the illumination of knowledge has been added to him — he begins to feel. And if so — is it possible that he should fall in his mind from this — heaven forfend? On the contrary — he must greatly strengthen himself from this — since he sees that the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos is beginning to flash within him. Therefore he must greatly strengthen himself to receive the holiness of Shabbos with joy and delight — and to believe that the holiness of Shabbos atones for everything — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And perhaps this is likewise within the category of what our Sages of blessed memory said: "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh" — that is, with simple people — on the contrary — through the holiness of Shabbos — they begin to feel even more the loss of their soul.

And one who does not have true knowledge can fall from this even more, heaven forfend. And one who has some flash of knowledge — on the contrary — strengthens himself through this even more — to yearn after the holiness of Shabbos — until through this itself he merits to receive the extra soul of Shabbos.

And this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: two ministering angels accompany the person — and so on — a good angel and an evil angel — and it is explained in the holy Zohar that they are the good inclination and the evil inclination. For through the holiness of Shabbos — the coarse evil inclination is nullified — and then the evil inclination is in the aspect of an evil angel — for its root is from severities and judgments. It finds his table set and the candle burning — and so on — the good angel says — and so on — and the evil angel reluctantly says "Amen." For through the delight of Shabbos — all judgments are sweetened at their root — and all kinds of anger and irritation are nullified — in the aspect of [Isaiah 14:3]: "b'yom hani'ach lecha mei'atzevecha u'merogzecha [on the day He gives you rest from your anguish and your agitation]," and so on — and as understood in the teaching Sha'alu es Riv"k, Siman 57. And then the evil angel is also sweetened — and answers "Amen" over the blessings. And this is what the Scripture warned: "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem b'yom haShabbas" — and it is explained in the Tikunim that this means to guard oneself from sadness and anger and quarreling. That is — for then the coarse evil inclination is nullified — and one must guard oneself from the fine and somewhat spiritual evil inclination — which is the aspect of anger and judgments — as mentioned above. For on Shabbos — the illumination of Ein Sof [the Infinite] shines in wondrous renewal — and there everything is entirely good. And therefore — in order to merit to receive the illumination of Shabbos in its fullness — one must be entirely good — without any judgments whatsoever — and as explained within.

 Siman 73 — סימן עג
 Ta'avur baMayim — Perfection of prayer and Torah secrets — the vessel called Ani — two Shabbosim — three Shabbosim (Zohar Yisro 92) — ki pi Hashem diber

The matter of how on Shabbos one merits the perfection of prayer and the revelation of Torah secrets — is explained somewhat above in Siman 15. And also — Shabbos is the aspect of the perfection of sacred speech — in the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — stated regarding Shabbos. And it is also the aspect of the world of thought. And it is also the aspect of the Tzadik. And these three aspects are the aspects of the vessel called "Ani [I]" — as explained within — and all the influences descend through this vessel — in the aspect of [Numbers 6:27]: "va'ani avarchem [and I shall bless them]." And therefore Shabbos is the source of blessing — for then one merits to pray with concentration — to connect the thought to the words of prayer in a strong bond — through which the aforementioned vessel is made — which is the source of blessing. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "v'es Shabsosai tishmoru — Ani Hashem [and My Shabbosim you shall guard — I am Hashem]." And likewise [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "matanah tovah yesh li b'veys genzai — v'Shabbas shemah" — and so on — and it concludes there: "matan scharah lo avida l'galeyyei" — that is, the inner dimension of the holiness of Shabbos is not made to be revealed. But only through receiving the holiness of Shabbos simply — and meriting the holiness of speech and thought — which is the aspect of: "es Shabsosai tishmoru" — two Shabbosim — through this the vessel called Ani is completed — and through this one merits to receive the blessings and the good influences of Shabbos — and through this G-d, blessed be He, receives great pleasure from them. For "chefetz chesed hu [He desires lovingkindness]" — which is the aspect of "ishah rei'ach nichoa'ch laHashem [a fire-offering of pleasing fragrance to Hashem]" — in the aspect of what G-d, blessed be He, said to Shabbos: "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha" — specifically. And through this — the inner dimension of the holiness of Shabbos will be revealed to them — which is the aspect of "Kodesh" — as explained in the aforementioned Siman 15. And this: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — and this is the aspect of: "vayevarech vayekadesh [and He blessed and He sanctified]."

And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — this is the aspect of the inner dimension of the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the Yud within Ani — which is the aspect of thought. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — this is the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — the aspect of the Nun within Ani. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov" — the aspect of the Aleph within Ani — for Yaakov is the aspect of the Aleph within the letters Aleph-Mem-Shin [אמ"ש] — as is well-known. And this itself is the aspect of the three Shabbosim explained in Zohar Yisro, folio 92: "Shabbas ila'ah — Shabbas d'yoma — Shabbas d'leila" — and so on. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for Shabbos is the aspect of the revelation of the inner dimension of the depth of the supernal thought through speech — as explained in Zohar Bereishis, folio 32.

 Siman 74 — סימן עד
 Romah al Shamayim — Shabbos = perfection of the soul = sweetening of judgments = dibur b'da'as = Yaakov = Torah — honor of Shabbos = ascent to Chochmah — Isaiah 58 — Zohar Bereishis 32 cited in Aramaic

Shabbos is the aspect of the perfection of the soul — in the aspect of: "Shabbas vayinafash."

And it is the aspect of the sweetening of the judgments — as explained in the holy Zohar. And it is the aspect of speech with knowledge [dibur b'da'as] — in the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — stated regarding Shabbos. And it is written [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem." And it is the aspect of Yaakov — for he is the first of whom it is stated that he guarded the Shabbos. And it is the aspect of the Torah — for all agree that on Shabbos the Torah was given. And this is the aspect of: Shabbos is the time of cessation from crying out — and healing is close to come — the aspect of the healing of the soul — in the aspect of [Malachi 3:20]: "shemesh tzedakah u'marpe b'chenafehah [a sun of righteousness with healing in its wings]" — as explained within. And therefore this verse is stated regarding the guardians of Shabbos — as it is written [Malachi 3:20]: "v'zarachah lachem yirey shmi — (elu shomrey Shabbas) — shemesh tzedakah u'marpe" — and so on — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "shemesh b'Shabbas — Tzedakah" — and so on.

And this is the aspect of the honor of Shabbos. For when one ascends to wisdom [Chochmah] — which is the aspect of Abba — the aspect of "av b'chochmah" — which is the aspect of [Exodus 31:14]: "ki Kodesh hi" — stated regarding Shabbos — as explained in the writings — through this His honor, blessed be He, is revealed — as it is written [Malachi 1:6]: "v'im av ani — ayeh chevodi [and if I am a Father — where is My honor?]" — as explained within.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha." The soul is the aspect of the legs — (as explained within — in Siman 69 — chomer issur gezeilah) — corresponding to the aspect of spirit [ru'ach] and higher soul [neshamah]. And it is from the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of Sarah. And during the weekday the Sitra Achra has a grip upon it — in the aspect of the judgment of impurity — heaven have mercy — for then it is in the aspect of smallness [katnus].

But on Shabbos — the soul ascends to its supernal root — in the aspect of: "meshivas nefesh [restoring the soul]." And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — not to engage in labor and weekday pursuits — which the person's soul desires — and sometimes the Sitra Achra has a grip upon them — in the aspect of [Ezekiel 20:8]: "u'v'shikutzeihem nafsham chafetzah [and in their abominations their soul delighted]." But on Shabbos — one must engage only in the affairs of Heaven — in the aspect of [Isaiah 56:4]: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti" — in the aspect of [I Chronicles 28:9]: "da es Elokei avicha v'avdehu b'lev shalem u'v'nefesh chefetzah [know the G-d of your father and serve Him with a whole heart and a desiring soul]."

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" — the aspect of the supernal wisdom that shines on Shabbos — where there is the essential delight — in the aspect of: "ein l'ma'alah mei'oneg [nothing above is higher than delight]" — as is well-known. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — the aspect of the honor revealed through wisdom. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha" — not to take large strides — for this is from the aspect of anger and judgment — and damages the light of the eyes — which are the aspect of the eyes of wisdom — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein." And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — not to blemish the speech of Shabbos — which is the aspect of speech with knowledge. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that one merit the supernal delight mentioned above. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — where there is the root of the aspect of the soul. And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, from the dross of judgment — from which is the root of the kingdom of Esau the wicked — the aspect of: "nefesh ki techeta [a soul that sins]" — as explained within.

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of speech with knowledge — that connects the soul — from which the outlet of speech flows — as is well-known — to the supernal wisdom. And this is the aspect of an inheritance without limits — as explained in the kavannos. And also — for through this is drawn the aspect of: "al kol ha'aretz kevodecha [upon all the earth is Your honor]" — as explained within. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for Shabbos is the aspect of sacred speech — as explained in Zohar Bereishis, folio 32: "mah d'kasuv — megaleh amukos mini choshech — v'chol haggid — ta chazey — kol inon amikkin stimin d'nafkin mi'go machshavah — u'kala natil lon — lo is'galeyan — ad d'milah mgaleh lon — man milah — hiynoo dibur — v'hai dibur ikri Shabbas [what it is written — He reveals deep things from darkness — and so on — come and see — all those deep hidden things that go forth from within thought — the voice takes them — they are not revealed — until speech reveals them — what is speech — this is the word [dibur] — and this speech is called Shabbos]" — and so on.

And this speech that comes from the side of darkness — reveals the deep things from within it — and so on — see there further — and you will understand its relevance to our matters.

 Siman 75 — סימן עה
 Yevarchenu Elokim — Shabbos = world of souls not world of bodies — awe — body subdued — perfection of speech — blood clarified — holy sparks — redemption — Shabbas Shalom

Shabbos is the day of souls and not the day of bodies — as explained in the holy Zohar — for Shabbos is the aspect of awe — in the aspect of [Malachi 3:20]: "v'zarachah lachem yirey shmi — ilu shomrey Shabbas [and it shall shine for you who fear My Name — these are the guardians of Shabbos]." And this is the aspect of: "yirey Shabbas [one who fears Shabbos]" — and as explained elsewhere. And therefore the body [guf] is subdued then — in the aspect of: "guf kasheh — pachad shavro [a hard body — fear breaks it]." And then one also merits the perfection of speech — in the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — stated regarding Shabbos. And then the body is nullified relative to the sacred speech — in the aspect of [Genesis 2:24]: "v'hayu l'vasar echad [and they shall be one flesh]" — as explained within. And therefore one merits then to pray in the aspect of: "kol atzmosei tomarnah [all my bones shall declare]," and so on. And through this — all the blood in a person is clarified and purified — and encompassed within the sacred words of Torah and prayer that go forth from the soul. And this is the aspect of Shalem [wholeness/peace] — for all the sparks of the letters of the breaking [shevirah] that were clothed within the blood — and were in the aspect of fragments and strife — are now completed and united together — and peace [shalom] is made between them — through their being encompassed within the sacred words of Torah and prayer — as explained within. And this is the aspect of Shabbas Shalom. And this is the aspect of the perfection of the soul merited on Shabbos — for blood is the soul. And this is the aspect of the ascent of the sacred legs that ascend on Shabbos — in the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha." For the aforementioned holy sparks are the aspect of legs. And likewise — the words of Torah and prayer are also the aspect of legs — as explained within.

And therefore the drawing close of the redemption depends on the guarding of Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught — for through this is drawn the aspect of [Zechariah 14:4]: "v'amad raglav b'yom hahu [and His feet shall stand on that day]," and so on — which depends on the clarification and ascent of the holy sparks in their fullness — in the aspect of: "ad d'mati raglin b'raglin [until the legs reach the legs]" — as explained in the holy Zohar. And therefore Shabbos is the source of blessing — for the Holy One, blessed be He, found no vessel to hold blessing for Israel except peace — which is the aspect of the fullness of the ascent of the sparks of holiness that ascend through Shabbos — for this is the aspect of: "oseh shalom u'vorei es hakol [Who makes peace and creates everything]" — as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who pray on Erev Shabbos and say Vayechulu — it is as if one became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the act of creation. For one merits through this the aspect of: "v'lomar l'Tziyon ami atah — mah ana avdit shamaya v'ar'ah b'miluli — af atem ken [and to say to Zion: you are My people — what I did — heaven and earth with My speech — so too you]" — for the completion of the perfection of the rectification of the creation — that is, to raise all the sparks of the breaking — depends on the holy people Israel — and the essential matter through the perfection of the words of Torah and prayer that one merits through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of the holiness of the delight of Shabbos. For within every food and drink — the sparks of the letters that fell are clothed — and from them is the essential delight. But during the weekday — the sparks do not reach their completion until they are encompassed within the words of Torah and prayer. But on Shabbos — they are encompassed at once within the holiness of Shabbos — since the delight and eating and drinking of Shabbos is itself a commandment — and as elaborated on this elsewhere with more explanation.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — the ascent of the aforementioned legs through the holiness of Shabbos. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — one should refrain from doing one's affairs and weekday pursuits — which are from the aspect of the breaking. And Shabbos is the aspect of the world of rectification [olam haTikkun] — as is well-known. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" — the aspect of the delight of Shabbos — which is from the aspect of the soul and not from the aspect of the body — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 55:2]: "shim'u shamo'a eilai va'ichlu tov — v'sisanag b'deshen nafshechem." And [Isaiah 58:13]: "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — which is the aspect of the full ascent of the legs — in the aspect of [Isaiah 60:13]: "u'mekom raglai achabad [and the place of My feet I shall honor]." And also — the essential honor is in speech — as explained elsewhere. And the words of Torah and prayer are the aspect of honor — in the aspect of [Jeremiah 13:16]: "simu chavod tehilaso [give glory to His praise]." And our Sages of blessed memory taught: honor is nothing other than Torah. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha" — not to take large strides for a matter of choice — so as not to blemish the legs. And [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — not to blemish the aspect of speech.

And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — this is the Holy Ancient One — from there is the root of the rectification of the breaking — and it is the aspect of "shalom rav [great peace]" — as is well-known. And this: "v'his'angu al rov shalom [and they shall delight in abundant peace]" [Psalms 37:11]. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — which is the aspect of speech — the aspect of: "Malchus peh." And this is the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 8:4]: "ka'asher dvar Melech shilton [as the word of a king is power]," and so on. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — as it is stated: "v'atah al bamosemo tidroch" — that is, they have no grip and no sustenance from the holy legs — in the aspect of: "hani birkei d'rabbanan d'shalhi minaihu [those legs of the rabbis from which they drink]." But on the contrary — they are subdued beneath the holy legs. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of [Genesis 33:18]: "vayavo Yaakov shalem [and Yaakov came whole]" — the aspect of the wholeness of the entire creation — in the aspect of: "oseh shalom u'vorei es hakol" — as mentioned above — which is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: "olami olami mi vera'acha — Yaakov vera'acha" — and they stated there further: heaven and earth were not created except for the sake of Yaakov — and so on — all was not created except for the sake of Yaakov — as it is stated [Jeremiah 10:16]: "lo k'eileh chelek Yaakov — ki yotzer hakol hu [not like these is the portion of Yaakov — for He is the Maker of everything]." And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for one merits that one's speech is, as it were, the aspect of the word of Hashem — in the aspect of: "mah ana avdit shamaya v'ar'ah b'miluli — af atem ken" — and as mentioned above.

 Siman 76 — סימן עו
 Vayehi Achar haDevorim — Teshuvah me'ahavah — mochin d'gadlus — Adam haRishon / Psalm 92 — strong sight — or yashar and or chozer — Siman 58 cross-reference — Shammai and Hillel (SA 242)

Shabbos is the aspect of teshuvah me'ahavah [repentance from love] — as explained above within in Siman 58 in the teaching tlas nafkin mechad. And through teshuvah me'ahavah one merits mochin d'gadlus [expanded consciousness]. And this is the aspect of the mental faculties of Shabbos. And therefore then it is very good and beautiful to pray — for one has pure intellect — and one can pray without toil [b'li iyyun] — as explained within. And this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: when Adam haRishon did repentance — he recited: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem." And also — Shabbos is the aspect of the power of strong sight [koach hare'iyah hechazak] — in the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas [see that Hashem has given you the Shabbos]" — for Shabbos is: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" — and as explained elsewhere. And therefore all the livelihood of all the days of the week flows from Shabbos. For through the sight one makes a boundary and time — that the bounty shall descend in its proper time. And this is the aspect of [Leviticus 26:4]: "v'nasati gishmeichem b'itam [and I shall give your rains in their time]" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: on Shabbos nights. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "al kein hu nosen lachem b'yom hashishi lechem yomayim [therefore He gives you on the sixth day bread for two days]." For during all the days of the week — they had to focus with strong trust each day before the manna descended — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. But on the holy Shabbos — from which is the root of all the influences — and also through it is the essential strengthening of sight and trust. For through the holiness of Shabbos — one receives great and new mental faculties — to strengthen oneself constantly in trust in Him, blessed be He. Therefore there is no need then to test Israel whether they will be firm in their trust — and lift their eyes to Him, blessed be He, regarding their livelihood. And all the more so — that they should not then make any effort whatsoever for their livelihood — to go out into the field and gather the manna. Rather — the manna descended to them on Erev Shabbos — also for the need of Shabbos. And on Shabbos — all Israel should look and focus only on the spiritual bounty — which is the aspect of the bounty of the holy mental faculties.

And the power of strong sight drawn on Shabbos upon each person of Israel — according to his level. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — the aspect of the bounty of mental faculties and Da'as — which are the aspect of Kodesh — as is well-known.

And this is the aspect of: blessed with manna that descended on Erev Shabbos — and so on — and sanctified with the manna that did not descend at all on it — in order to know that then the bounty does not descend only for that day alone. Rather — all the bounty of all the days flows from that day. And although on that day itself one also needs material bounty — and on the contrary — then the essential commandment of eating and drinking and delighting the Shabbos applies — for the meals of the weekday are optional meals and those of Shabbos are obligatory commanded meals. But nonetheless — due to the immense holiness of Shabbos — it is not appropriate to engage in any act or doing for this purpose — and even to think merely a bare thought.

For then one must be connected with a complete and strong bond — in deed — speech — and thought — only to the spiritual bounty of the holiness of Shabbos — which is a foretaste of the World to Come — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And because in sight there is or yashar [direct light] and or chozer [returning light] — as explained within.

And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "es Shabsosai tishmoru" — "Shabsosai" — specifically — two Shabbosim — for Shabbos is the aspect of the power of sight — the aspect of: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" — as mentioned above. That is — on Shabbos — as it were — the Holy One, blessed be He, gazes upon the entire creation — (and primarily upon Israel — for whom everything was created) — with love and great will — in the aspect of [Genesis 2:1–2]: "vayechulu hashamayim v'ha'aretz — v'chol haggid — vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i melachto asher asah" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: from the language of love and longing. And this is the aspect of or yashar. And through Israel guarding the Shabbos and connecting themselves to its holiness with all their heart — through this the gaze of Hashem, blessed be He, as it were, connects even more to the creation — in the aspect of a strike and a connection literally. And through this is drawn, as it were, the aspect of or chozer — that the sight returns to His knowledge and awareness, blessed be He, as it were. And then Israel are connected to His Da'as and awareness, blessed be He, in fullness — and He draws upon them complete Providence — and grants them all good in its time and proper moment. And this [Exodus 31:17]: "ki os hi beyni u'veineichem l'dorosechem — lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem."

"Lada'as [to know]" — specifically. For through the holiness of Shabbos — Israel are connected to His Da'as, blessed be He, as it were — as mentioned above. And likewise — the holiness of the illumination of His divinity, blessed be He, that shines on Shabbos — connects properly to the Da'as and awareness of Israel — in the aspect of: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — and likewise [Exodus 6:7]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem Elokeichem."

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "matanah tovah yesh li b'veys genzai — v'Shabbas shemah — v'ani rotzeh litnah l'Yisrael" — this is the aspect of the or yashar of the holiness of Shabbos. And this: "lech v'hodiyam" — so that they should prepare themselves to receive the light of this gift — and then the light will shine upon them in the aspect of a strike and a connection — and through this is also made the aspect of or chozer — which is the aspect of the fullness of the holiness of Shabbos. And this is the aspect of: "matan scharah lo avida l'galeyyei" — for the plainness of the holiness of Shabbos that G-d, blessed be He, gave us the Shabbos — which is the aspect of or yashar — this is made to be revealed. But its reward — that is, what we must connect ourselves to its holiness — and through this the sight returns to His knowledge, blessed be He, as it were — as mentioned above — and through this one merits to receive the illumination of the upper Shabbos at its root in fullness — this is not made to be revealed. And therefore G-d, blessed be He, Himself had to make known to us all of this. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory also taught: Shabbos was given in privacy — for just as when one wishes to look at some thing from afar — one must focus and concentrate the sight — and not look at anything from the side — but only at that thing one wishes to see and gaze upon properly — and all of this so that the direct light of the power of sight should reach it with great force. And then — through the strike that it strikes strongly upon the visible thing — through this the thing will return and be depicted in one's eye — in the aspect of or chozer — and as explained elsewhere. Likewise — G-d, blessed be He, did not wish to publicize the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the power of sight — and to give it publicly — so that it should not scatter somewhat from the side as well — as it were. And therefore He gave it in privacy — and made it known only to Israel alone — and in privacy — so that the matter should be in its fullness — as mentioned above. And this is what they said: "matan scharah lo aodiyinhu" — as mentioned above. For G-d, blessed be He, wishes that only the holy Israel should be connected to His Da'as and awareness in fullness through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above — and no one else.
