"Ai nami neshamah yetairah lo aodiyinhu" — for the illumination of the extra soul is from the aspect of the strike — as it were — that the direct light of the holiness of Shabbos — which flows from above from Him, blessed be He, alone — strikes and hits the holiness of the souls of Israel — and through this each person feels in his soul some flash of the illumination of the supernal holiness — which is the aspect of the extra soul. And this itself is the aspect of the notification — that besides the fact that G-d, blessed be He, has mercy upon us and shines upon us the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos through awakening from above alone — for the holiness of Shabbos is established and enduring — as our Sages of blessed memory taught — He also notifies us (through the extra soul — as mentioned above) that the holiness of Shabbos has already flowed upon us — so that we should see to connect ourselves properly to its holiness — and through this the aspect of or chozer is also completed — as mentioned above.

And this is the aspect of [Exodus 20:8]: "zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — and they said: "mei'chad b'Shabbis l'Shabbasa." For since the holiness of Shabbos is very spiritual — therefore one must prepare oneself for this throughout all the days of the week — and remember the holiness of Shabbos each day — which is the aspect of the sight — that one watches and focuses and anticipates and prepares oneself for the holiness of Shabbos. And this is the aspect of the or yashar from the side of the holy Israel — that is, they focus throughout all the days of the week with great concentration on the holiness of Shabbos. And through this their sight reaches the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos in the aspect of a strike — and the sight returns to them in the aspect of or chozer — and they merit to receive the holiness of Shabbos in its fullness. And this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 5:12]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" — and likewise: "shamor es yom haShabbas" — and so on — from the language of waiting and anticipation — for one must wait and anticipate the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of sight. And through this one draws upon himself the holiness of Shabbos in its fullness.

And behold — "shamor" is the attribute of night — the aspect of Malchus — which is the aspect of or chozer. For in its particularity — as it were — there is by Him, blessed be He, the aspect of or yashar and or chozer in the matter of the holiness of Shabbos — and likewise by Israel — as mentioned above. And in its generality: the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos that G-d, blessed be He, grants from above — this is the aspect of or yashar.

And that Israel receive its holiness — and anticipate it and prepare themselves for it — this is the aspect of or chozer.

And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — the aspect of the light of the holiness of Shabbos at its supernal root — which is the aspect of or yashar. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — which is the aspect of the light of Malchus — which is the aspect of or chozer. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — which encompasses both aspects together. And therefore the image of Yaakov is engraved upon the Throne of Honor — which is the aspect of or chozer — for G-d, blessed be He, gazes upon him in the aspect of or yashar — for the entire creation was only for his sake — as mentioned above. Until the sight returns to Him, blessed be He, in the aspect of or chozer. And he is the first of whom it is written that he guarded the Shabbos — and established the Shabbos boundary — and so on. The Shabbos boundary of two thousand cubits [techum Shabbas alpayim amah] — likewise corresponds to the aspect of the two lights mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — which is the aspect of [Isaiah 55:11]: "ken yihyeh devari asher yetzei mipi — lo yashuv eilai reikam [so shall be My word that goes forth from My mouth — it shall not return to Me empty]," and so on — the aspect of or yashar and or chozer. And one must still elaborate on this — but due to the subtlety of the aforementioned matters it is not possible to expand the speech so much.

And see within — it is understood that complete trust — the aspect of the strong power of sacred sight — is the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — the aspect of lovingkindness and mercy. And there it is explained regarding one whose mind is clear and pure — in the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — that he can pray without toil [b'li iyyun] — for his thought connects at once to the words of prayer without any labor and effort at all. And one who is not in this aspect — must raise up his thought before he speaks — for if not — the speech will be without thought — and so on. And behold — for the most part — a person is aroused to this through the fact that he remembers after the prayer that he prayed without concentration — and he is very grieved in his heart from this — and therefore he is afterward careful to toil himself to concentrate in his prayer. And because his mind is not so clear and swift — therefore he almost must concentrate in his thought before he speaks — as mentioned above.

And in this one can understand what our Sages of blessed memory taught: had Israel guarded two Shabbosim — and so on — for on the first Shabbos not every person merits to receive the inner dimension of its holiness in fullness. Only through the fact that after the Shabbos — his heart aches greatly that the Shabbos passed in such smallness [katnus]. And this is the aspect of: "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh" — for this aspect encompasses everything — even one who is at a very small level — and does not merit on Shabbos itself to delight and take pleasure in the fullness of the holiness of the extra soul of Shabbos — nonetheless after the Shabbos he feels the pain of the departure of his extra soul that he merited to receive on Shabbos — which is the aspect of: "vav — avdah nefesh."

And this is the aspect of "achar hadevarim [after the words]" — that his good thought comes to him after the speech. Likewise — the feeling of the holiness of Shabbos comes to him at least at the lowest level — close to the going out of Shabbos — and as also seen in actual experience. And then — through this — he afterward prepares himself throughout all the days of the week to receive the holiness of the second Shabbos in its fullness. And this is the aspect of: one who thinks before he speaks — and then the speech comes with thought.

Likewise — regarding Shabbos — one merits through this to receive the holiness of Shabbos in fullness — and then the redemption will come. And in this one can also explain the matter of: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas" — that is, to prepare one's thought for the holiness of Shabbos throughout all the days of the week — and likewise also in deed — in the aspect of: "mei'chad b'Shabbis l'Shabbasa." For perhaps one does not hold in the fullness of trust — through which one makes a vessel for the bounty — that it should come in its time — and then perhaps the bounty of Shabbos can come to him after Shabbos — or it may not come to him until after a long time. Therefore one must hasten to prepare for Shabbos immediately on the first day of the week. And this was the trait of Shammai — who was from the aspect of judgment — from where comes the grip of mochin d'katnus — the aspect of "achar hadevarim." But Hillel — who was from the attribute of lovingkindness — the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — from which comes the aspect of complete trust — and therefore he would say: "baruch Hashem yom yom [blessed be Hashem day by day]" [Psalms 68:20] — and his trust was firm that the bounty of Shabbos would come in its time. But nonetheless — Hillel also agrees that it is better to do as Shammai taught — as explained in the words of the commentators and the later authorities, of blessed memory, in Siman 242 — for not every person and not in every time does one merit to such clear mental faculties and such strong trust. And this is what they stated there regarding Hillel: there was another trait in him — that all his actions were for the sake of Heaven — that is, the inner dimension of the holiness of his thought was always connected in all his actions — for the sake of Heaven — without any labor and effort whatsoever — for he merited to clear mental faculties. And therefore his trust was also very firm — and he would say: "baruch Hashem yom yom" — and so on — as mentioned above.

 Siman 77 — סימן עז
 V'hayah Hashem l'Melech — Perfection of voice/speech (Vav-Heh) and love/awe (Yud-Heh) both on Shabbos — Name Yud-Heh of Shabbos — Zechariah 14:9 — Zohar Yisro

The essential perfection of the voice and speech — which are the aspect of Vav-Heh [ו"ה] — is on Shabbos — for this is the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — stated regarding Shabbos — and as mentioned above many times. And likewise — the essential perfection of love and awe — which are the aspect of Yud-Heh [י"ה] — is also on Shabbos — as mentioned above many times.

And this is the aspect of the Name Yud-Heh of Shabbos — as explained in the writings. And therefore then is the essential perfection of Torah and prayer — as mentioned above many times. And through this the kingship of G-d, blessed be He, is revealed — which is the aspect of Shabbas Malketa. And this is the aspect of [Zechariah 14:9]: "v'hayah Hashem l'Melech al kol ha'aretz — b'yom hahu yihyeh Hashem echad — u'shemo echad [and Hashem will be King over all the earth — on that day Hashem will be One — and His Name will be One]" — and this is understood in the holy Zohar in the passage "k'gavna" stated at the entry of Shabbos — that this aspect is drawn through the holiness of Shabbos.

Note: Siman 78 does not appear in the source manuscript.

 Siman 79 — סימן עט
 Betach b'Hashem — Complete teshuvah = Moshe Mashiach — seeing one's lowliness — Moshe descends every Shabbos with other Tzadikim — mesiyas nefesh — Megillas Amukos — Psalm 92 — Shadai — delight of Shabbos

It is explained within that Shabbos is the aspect of complete repentance [teshuvah sheleimah] — until it pushes away and the evil is completely nullified — and one has complete rest from everything — and it is transformed from evil to complete good — and one becomes entirely good. This is the aspect of "Moshe Mashiach" [the Moses of the Messiah]. And through this — one can see one's own lowliness — which is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas — re'u davka [see that Hashem has given you the Shabbos — see — specifically]" — for Shabbos is the aspect of: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein." And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "shvu ish tachtav [let each person remain in his place]" — stated regarding Shabbos — that is, he should regard himself as lower than his level. And also — he knows and recognizes the importance and greatness of Israel — and can sacrifice himself for them. This is the aspect of Moshe our teacher — the Faithful Shepherd — who sacrificed his soul for Israel. And this is the aspect of what is brought in the kavannos: "M'zmor Sh'ir l'Yom haSh'abas" — initial letters — "l'Moshe" — that Moshe our teacher — peace be upon him — together with other Tzadikim who are of his aspect — descend at every entry of Shabbos to elevate the souls of the living and the dead who fell to the depths of the husks — heaven have mercy. And this for them is literally self-sacrifice [mesiyas nefesh mamash] for the souls of Israel — since they must lower themselves from their very high and wondrous level into such low and base levels as the depths of the husks — to raise from there the souls of Israel who fell there. And we find that our Sages of blessed memory taught — even regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself — as it were — as it is stated regarding Him: "v'avarti b'eretz Mitzrayim" — and so on — a parable of a priest who went down into a cemetery — and so on. And this [Psalms 92:2]: "tov lehodos laHashem" — the aspect of repentance through the verbal confession [viduy devarim] — as mentioned above in the name of the Midrash. And this [Psalms 92:2]: "v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" — the aspect of the supernal repentance — complete repentance — that one becomes entirely good — which is above, as it were, the aspect of Metatron — who is from the side of life and from the side of death — which is the aspect of the repentance of the six weekdays — and as explained within. And see in Megillas Amukos, Ofan 110 — there it is explained that the shi'ur komah [supernal measure] — as it were — is 236,000 parasangs — and He gave a vision [ayin] of 1000 parasangs to Metatron — and so on — and 166,000 parasangs — He, blessed be He, is above him — "elyon [Most High]" — the gematria of "elyon" is 166 — and so on — see there — it is explained for our matters. And then when the holiness of Shabbos comes — which is the aspect of complete repentance — then there is also an ascent, as it were, even for the aspect of Metatron — as understood within. And then those incomplete thoughts of repentance that have not yet reached full completion — for they are only in the aspect of the repentance of the six weekdays — are also encompassed in the holiness of Shabbos — and they also ascend to their rest. And through this — the aforementioned souls also ascend — through the power of the thoughts of repentance that they had — and as understood in the holy Zohar. And this is the aspect of what is explained in Zohar Chadash, Parashas Bereishis — that the ascent that even the wicked among Israel have — to have a portion in the World to Come — through some of their good deeds — is only through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And all of this through the power of Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, and other Tzadikim who are of his aspect — through whom — through the holiness of Shabbos — the attribute of humility and lowliness within them is aroused even more — and they also see even more the importance and greatness of Israel. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:17]: "ki os hi beyni u'veineichem l'dorosechem — lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — and likewise [Exodus 31:17]: "beyni u'vein Bnay Yisrael os hi l'olam" — and so on.

And through this they sacrifice their souls for them — and go down to where they go down — to raise from there the souls of Israel of the living and the dead — through the power and the merit of the holy Shabbos. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — even if one worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. For through the holiness of Shabbos — true thoughts of repentance certainly reach him — and his repentance also has a complete ascent — as mentioned above — and therefore he is forgiven. And this is the aspect of the delight of Shabbos — the aspect of [Job 27:10]: "ki az al Shadai yis'anag [for then one will delight in the Almighty]," and so on — for the complete repentance of Shabbos is the aspect of Shadai — as explained within. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 37:3]: "betach b'Hashem v'aseh tov [trust in Hashem and do good]," and so on — as explained within. And this [Psalms 37:4]: "v'his'anag al Hashem" — the aspect of the delight of Shabbos — as mentioned above.

 Siman 80 — סימן פ
 Hashem Oz l'Amo Yiten — Shabbos = shalom = source of blessing — Yosef — speech connected to thought and Chochmah — building of Jerusalem — Moshe/Yosef/David — Isaiah 58 — peh im hakolel = Elokim

Shabbos is the aspect of peace [shalom] — the aspect of Shabbas Shalom — and therefore it is the source of blessing — for the Holy One, blessed be He, found no vessel to hold blessing for Israel except peace. And peace connects two opposites — that is, lovingkindnesses and severities — which is the aspect of Yosef — as explained within. And therefore Shabbos is likewise the aspect of Yosef — as explained in the holy Zohar. And it is stated regarding Yosef that he guarded the Shabbos — as it is written [Genesis 43:16]: "v'tavo'ach teva'ach v'hachen [slaughter and prepare]" — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 66:23]: "v'yanuchu vo kol Yisrael mekadshey Shimcha [and all Israel who sanctify Your Name shall rest through it]." And this is likewise the aspect of [Isaiah 66:23]: "v'al menuchasam yekadshu es Shimcha" — that one must accept upon oneself then self-sacrifice for the sanctification of the Name — as brought — for the sanctification of the Name is likewise from the aspect of lovingkindnesses and severities — as explained within. And therefore Shabbos is among the things Israel sacrificed their souls for — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And behold — the essential matter of all the influences and blessings is so that each person of Israel can speak holy words — that is, that the speech should be connected to the thought and the wisdom — which is the aspect of Kodesh. And this is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the world of thought — and also the aspect of the perfection of speech — as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar.

And this is the aspect of the building of Jerusalem — in the aspect of [Psalms 147:2]: "boneh Yerushalayim Hashem [Hashem builds Jerusalem]" — as explained within. And this is the aspect of [Jeremiah 17:24–25, 27]: "v'hayah im shamo'a tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — v'ladesh es yom haShabbas — v'chol haggid — v'yashevah ha'ir hazos l'olam [and it shall be if you hearken to Me — and so on — and sanctify the day of Shabbos — and so on — and this city shall dwell forever]," and so on — "v'im lo tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — v'hitzasi eish b'sh'areha — v'achla armonos Yerushalayim [and if you do not hearken to Me — and so on — and I shall kindle fire in its gates — and it shall consume the palaces of Jerusalem]," and so on — for Jerusalem is the aspect of Tzedek — the aspect of the speech — which is the aspect of severities — only through the holiness of Shabbos — the aspect of the speech being connected to thought — through this the severities are sweetened in lovingkindnesses. And this is the aspect of the building of Jerusalem. And through the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend — through this the severities intensify even more — and they are the aspect of fire — until through this comes the destruction of Jerusalem — which is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they desecrated the Shabbos — and they taught: fire is found only in a place where Shabbos is desecrated. And this [Psalms 92:2]: Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas: "tov lehodos laHashem" — and so on — for then it is very good and beautiful to pray — for one merits to connect the thought to the speech through the peace of Shabbos. And this is the aspect of Moshe — Yosef — David — who departed on Shabbos at Minchah. Moshe is the aspect of thought — as is well-known. David is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of speech. Yosef is the aspect of the peace — through which one merits to connect the thought to the speech. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — even if one worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven — for this is the aspect of: "boneh Yerushalayim Hashem — nidchey Yisrael yechannes [Hashem builds Jerusalem — He gathers the dispersed of Israel]" [Psalms 147:2]. For through the guarding of Shabbos — which is the aspect of Yosef — the aspect of peace — the aspect of the sanctification of the Name — through this even all the dispersed of Israel are gathered — and not only that — but even converts can draw close through the holiness of Shabbos — for this is the aspect of: "u'vnay haneychar hanilavim al Hashem — kol shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo" — and so on — "v'havi'osim el har kodshi" — and so on — "ne'um Hashem mekabbetz nidchey Yisrael — od akabbetz alav l'nikibotzav [the utterance of Hashem Who gathers the dispersed of Israel — I shall yet gather him to his gathered ones]" — and as Rashi explained there. And therefore it is a great commandment to produce Torah novellae on Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar — for this is the aspect of [Isaiah 12:3]: "u'she'avtem mayim b'sasson mimayney hayeshuah [and you shall draw water with joy from the springs of salvation]" — and its Targum: "v'tikablon ulpan chadis [and you shall receive new teaching]," and so on — as explained within. For through the influences and blessings — which are the aspect of the springs of salvation that are opened on Shabbos — through this one merits to receive new mental faculties — which are the aspect of "ulpan chadis" — the aspect of true Torah novellae. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — this is the aspect of the severities — as explained within — that is, through the holiness of Shabbos the legs are elevated — which are the aspect of severities. And [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — for Shabbos is Kodesh — the aspect of the mental faculties — and it is forbidden to engage with one's hands then in one's pursuits — only to engage in the affairs of Heaven — which are the aspects of the mental faculties and lovingkindnesses — in the aspect of: "ki chefetz chesed hu." And this is the aspect of [Psalms 134:2]: "se'u yedeichem Kodesh [lift your hands to the holy]" — as explained within — to lift and raise the hands to the aspect of the mental faculties — which are Kodesh. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" — the aspect of the mental faculties — as is well-known and as mentioned above many times. And [Isaiah 58:13]: "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — the aspect of Malchus — the King of Honor — that is, the aspect of speech — where there is the essential honor — as explained elsewhere. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha" — not to take large strides — which is the aspect of anger — so as not to blemish the legs — where the judgments have the greatest grip — for they are the aspect of severities — as mentioned above. And [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — so as not to blemish the speech. And therefore it is even forbidden then to request one's needs — for then one even more fully attains that the essential matter of all the influences and blessings and salvations is so that one merits to receive new mental faculties — and to speak sacred words before G-d, blessed be He. Therefore one prays then only for spiritual bounty: "kadsheinu b'mitzvosecha" — and so on — "v'taher libbenu l'ovdecha be'emes" — and so on — "v'yanuchu vo kol Yisrael mekadshey Shimcha." And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — that is, one merits to receive supernal and wondrous mental faculties — which are very great lovingkindnesses — the aspect of: "rav chesed [abundant lovingkindness]" — the aspect of Atik — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: they give him all the desires of his heart — for there — in the aspect of rav chesed — all the salvations and blessings are encompassed — and so on. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — which is the aspect of speech — to the mental faculties — which are the aspect of Kodesh. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — as it is stated: "v'atah al bamosemo tidroch" — that is, all the kingdoms of the Sitra Achra — whose sustenance comes from the unfolding of the severities — are subdued beneath the holy feet.

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — which is the aspect of the Vav — as is well-known. The aspect of [Genesis 37:2]: "eileh toldos Yaakov — Yosef [these are the generations of Yaakov — Yosef]" — for Yaakov and Yosef go as one — which are the aspect of the peace that unites the two opposites.

For Yaakov is the aspect of Tiferes — which mediates between Chesed and Gevurah.

And likewise Yosef is the aspect of Yesod — which mediates between Netzach and Hod. And this is the aspect of an inheritance without limits. For since one can unite two opposites — spontaneously all the constraints are nullified. And this is likewise the aspect of: "nidchey Yisrael yechannes" — mentioned above — for even one who is at the ultimate of lowliness — can also be encompassed and return to the supernal holiness — through the aspect of the sanctification of the Name that is drawn from the aspect of Yosef — the aspect of peace — mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for on Shabbos speech is completed and built in its fullness through the mental faculties — which are the aspect of Havayah — and a unity is made between the Name Elokim and the Name Havayah — which is the aspect of the mental faculties and lovingkindnesses — as explained within. "Peh [mouth]" together with the kollel [inclusion] — the gematria [numerical value] of Elokim — as brought.

 Siman 81 — סימן פא
 Alu Zeh baNegev — Shabbos = sanctity of Eretz Yisrael = holiness of speech — secular speech — Teshuvah haDeshen · Rema · Moshvetzos Zahav · Tur"z — Siman 69 cross-reference

Shabbos is the aspect of the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — as mentioned above many times. And it is the aspect of the holiness of speech — in the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — and as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar. And therefore one must be very careful not to speak idle speech [sicha betelah] on Shabbos. But nonetheless — it is explained in Teshuvos haDeshen, Siman 61 — where he was asked about the practice of those who are meticulous — who nonetheless did not accustom themselves to be so careful in this — and gather on Shabbos — and so on — and discuss news about kings and ministers — and so on — see there what he answered: because they take delight in this — and therefore it is permitted — and so on — but those who do not take delight — it is forbidden. And this is also brought in the annotation of the Rema [SA OC 307:1] — and there it is elaborated even further — that one who does not take delight — it is forbidden to say these things so that his fellow should take delight in them. And see in the Moshvetzos Zahav — which resolved what appears at first glance problematic — for idle speech is forbidden even on a weekday — so how is it different? — but on a weekday — it is permitted for one's fellow to take delight from it — and on Shabbos — even this is forbidden. And see in the Tur"z there, paragraph 1 — it is understood that if the speaker himself also has delight from the fact that his fellow takes pleasure in his stories — it is also permitted. And all of this is understood for our matters — according to what is explained within — see there. For the essential delight of Shabbos is the mental faculties — the source of delight — in the aspect of: "ein l'ma'alah mei'oneg" — as mentioned above many times. And therefore sometimes — even on Shabbos — it is permitted to tell some secular conversation — in order to open one's mind and revive oneself — and to return to the level of one's mental faculties — which is the aspect of: one takes delight in the conversation — that is, one thereby comes to the level of the mental faculties — which are the aspect of delight. However — if he himself does not take delight from this — but only tells it so that his fellow should take delight — that is, so that his fellow should come to the level of his mental faculties — on a weekday this too is permitted. But on Shabbos — one should reconsider this — as mentioned above — unless he himself also takes delight from this — from the fact that his fellow takes pleasure in his stories — that is, such as when he tells to a Torah scholar — and through the Torah scholar taking delight in his stories — and returning to the level of his mental faculties — through this — the Torah scholar afterward also elevates the storyteller and connects him to the sacred knowledge — where there is the source of delight — as mentioned above. Which is the aspect of: the storyteller takes delight from the fact that his fellow takes pleasure in his stories — as mentioned above. But in truth — the Torah scholar himself also takes very great delight from this — from the fact that he connects even the common people to the sacred knowledge — which is the essential delight of Shabbos — as mentioned above. For "zachay man d'achid b'yada d'chayyava [praiseworthy is one who holds the hand of a sinner]," and so on. And therefore it is also permitted. However — all of this was said regarding the Torah scholar — who knows how to do every matter in its proper time and its proper moment and its proper measure. And in truth — the conversation of a Torah scholar is itself Torah — and so on — and as explained elsewhere and as also explained within in this teaching. But simple people — who are not fixed in Torah study during the weekday — it is explained in Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 290 — that they should not prolong themselves greatly on Shabbos also in the delight of eating and drinking — but should engage more in Torah. And the Torah scholars may prolong somewhat more in the delight of eating and drinking — and so on. And this is likewise from this aspect mentioned above. For although the delight of eating and drinking is an outer service for Torah scholars — compared to their Torah and prayer — and as explained elsewhere — and it is the aspect of the secular conversation of Torah scholars — nonetheless it is also very holy — and sometimes through this specifically one connects the common people to the sacred knowledge — which is the aspect of the excellence of one who merits to sit at the Shabbos meal at the table of a true Torah scholar and Tzadik — and as elaborated elsewhere. And as mentioned from this also above in Siman 69.

 Siman 82 — סימן פב
 haNe'elavim — Shabbos = nullification of three completely impure husks = arlah = cherpah — bris — Yosef — nega Nogah — shalhava d'asha — Shabbos and circumcision — must be at peace — one who shames him: be silent

Shabbos is the aspect of the nullification of the three completely impure husks — which are the aspect of arlah [the foreskin] — the aspect of cherpah [disgrace] — and [Leviticus 26:19]: "v'hishbati ge'on azim [and I shall cause the pride of the arrogant to cease]." And likewise: "v'yishbas din v'kalon [and judgment and shame shall cease]" — and as mentioned above many times.

For Shabbos is the aspect of bris [the covenant] — and it is stated regarding Yosef: "asaf Elokim es cherpasi [G-d has removed my disgrace]" [Genesis 30:23]. And then the good that is in Nogah is encompassed in holiness — and the evil within it — together with the three completely impure husks — are repelled and fall downward through the shalhava d'asha [the flame of fire] that descends on Erev Shabbos — as explained within. And this is likewise the aspect of the commandment of circumcision.

And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught — specifically: a circumcised person guards the Shabbos — and not a gentile who is uncircumcised. And in the holy Zohar it is explained regarding the matter of [Genesis 17:12]: "u'ven shmonas yamim yimol [and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised]" — in order that Shabbos should pass over him. For both depend upon each other. And therefore one must be very careful on Shabbos to be at peace with all people — and not to arouse any dispute — or disgraces and humiliations — heaven forfend. And even if someone disgraces him — let him be silent toward him — and think in his heart: this is precisely the matter of the holiness of Shabbos — to nullify and repel the impure husks — which are the aspect of arlah — the aspect of cherpah. And this rectification is also made through the fact that one hears one's disgrace and is silent — as explained within.

 Siman 83 — סימן פג
 Matan beSeter — Shabbos = giving in secret = yichpeh af — all judgments suppressed — desecration = charon af — bris — sparks ascend — ki pi Hashem diber = letters of speech rectified — charity and honor of Shabbos = charity to poor

Shabbos is the aspect of giving in secret [matan b'seter] — corresponding to what our Sages of blessed memory taught: "matanah tovah yesh li b'veys genzai — v'Shabbas shemah" — and so on — and they stated: all the commandments were given publicly — and Shabbos was given to Israel in privacy. It follows that Shabbos is the aspect of giving in secret. And this "yichpeh af [suppresses anger]" — for on Shabbos all judgments are suppressed and do not stir at all — as explained in the holy Zohar. And this is what is written [Ezekiel 20:21]: "v'es Shabsosai chilelu — va'omar lishpoch chamasi aleihem l'chalos api bam" — and so on — for through the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend — the aspect of burning wrath [charon af] is aroused, heaven forfend. For all who desecrate the Shabbos publicly — it is as if he worshipped idolatry. And likewise — when there is idolatry in the world — burning wrath is in the world, heaven forfend. And also — for through the holiness of Shabbos — all the husks are subdued — in particular that husk — as explained within — may its name be blotted out — as explained in the holy Zohar. And then it has no power to draw sustenance from the six sides of the Aleph-Beis [the letters]. But through the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend — one gives it power to draw sustenance from the aforementioned sides — and from the Feh [the letter Peh] — anger is also made — and the aspect of consuming fire is drawn, heaven forfend — as explained within. And this is what is written [Jeremiah 17:27]: "v'im lo tishme'u eilai — v'chol haggid — v'ladesh es yom haShabbas — v'hitzasi eish b'sh'areha va'achlah" — and so on — and this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: fire is found only in a place where Shabbos is desecrated.

And this is the aspect of: "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem b'yom haShabbas." And therefore then is the essential time for the sacred union — for then the aforementioned husk is subdued — and then the union is in holiness — in the aspect of: "zachu — Shechinah shruya beineihem [if they merited — the Shechinah dwells between them]." And also our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. It follows that through this — the burning wrath that comes through idolatry — as mentioned above — is also suppressed and nullified. And also — Shabbos is the aspect of the rectification of the bris — the aspect of: "bris olam [everlasting covenant]" [Exodus 31:16] — as explained elsewhere. And then — all the holy sparks that fell to wherever they fell — ascend — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of: "ki pi Hashem diber" — stated regarding the guarding of Shabbos — for then the sides [pa'in] of the letters of speech are rectified. And also — the delight and honor of Shabbos is the aspect of charity to the poor — as mentioned above many times.

 Siman 84 — סימן פד
 Bamah he'Archata Yamim — Shabbos = menuchas ahavah v'nedavah — aspect of the right — pure and clear mental faculties — the hidden good — Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer — Megillah 27 — Kiddush precedes honor — longevity

Shabbos is "menuchas ahavah v'nedavah [a rest of love and freewill]" — the aspect of the side of the right [sitra d'yemina].

And from the side of the right — "mocha chavara k'kaspa [the brain is white like silver]." And therefore on Shabbos one merits the aspect of clarity and purity of the mental faculties and thought.

And therefore then it is especially propitious to enter the hidden good — and to attain the secrets of the Torah — as brought. And also — Shabbos itself is the aspect of good [tov] — for this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:2]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov" — and as explained in the holy Zohar. And also — for Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah.

And the Torah is called tov [good] — as it is written [Proverbs 4:2]: "ki lekach tov [for a good teaching]." And through the holiness of Shabbos one merits clarity of thought — through which all Israel are called "tovim [good]" — as it is written [Psalms 125:4]: "hatibah Hashem l'tovim v'lisharim b'levosam [do good Hashem to the good and to the upright in heart]." And therefore all agree that on Shabbos the Torah was given — for this is the aspect of: "yavo tov — yekabel tov — mi'tov l'tovim [let the good come — receive good — from the Good One to the good ones]" — as our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Menachos 53b]. And then is fulfilled in its fullness what is explained within in the name of the holy Zohar: "man d'ihu tov — v'chol haggid — hahu tov ganiz — yeyma lei — pitchu lei b'hai tar'a d'iskari ahavah [one who is good — and so on — that hidden good — it is said to him — open for him in this gate called love]" — as mentioned above. Or through "b'hahu tar'a d'ihu teshuvah [that gate which is repentance]" — for Shabbos is the aspect of teshuvah me'ahavah — as mentioned above many times — and as explained within in Siman 58. And therefore one must conduct oneself regarding the honor of Shabbos with the trait of generosity — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "kol hamosif mosifin lo [all who add — they add to him]." For through generosity — which is the trait of our Patriarch Avraham — the man of lovingkindness — through this one merits clarity and purity of thought and mental faculties — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — the world of thought. And one merits through this to attain the hidden good — which is the essential aspect of longevity — as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer: one who sanctifies over wine [Kiddush] on Shabbos nights — his days and years are lengthened — and so on. And likewise our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Megillah 27b] regarding Rabbi Zakkai — that he lived long because he never in his days neglected the Kiddush of the Day [Kiddush haYom]. For the essential beginning of the revelation of the holiness of Shabbos is through the Kiddush. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: "Kiddush haYom kodem l'chevod yom v'chevod lailah [the Kiddush of the Day takes precedence over the honor of the day and the honor of the night]" [Tractate Pesachim 105b]. And therefore through it one merits longevity — as mentioned above.

 Siman 86 — סימן פו
 Pos'im bo — The outer forces rule primarily over the legs on weekdays — when Shabbos is sanctified they scatter — legs regain the power of walking — Shabbos = truth = emes — charity of Shabbos = sun of the future

It is explained within that during the weekdays the outer forces dominate — and their essential dominion is over the aspect of the legs — that is, they do not allow the person to walk in the ways of Hashem, blessed be He. And when the holy Shabbos is sanctified — then: "yispardu kol po'aley aven [all the workers of iniquity are scattered]" [Psalms 92:10] — and then they have no dominion at all — and the legs regain the power of walking — which is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha." But nonetheless — one still needs support to strengthen them. And this support is the aspect of truth [emes]. And Shabbos itself is the aspect of truth — as explained within — (and this is what is brought in the writings: א'ם ת'שיב מ'שבת — initial letters of אמ"ת [emes] — as mentioned above. And this: "raglecha" — for then the legs ascend — as mentioned above — and truth is the support to strengthen them — as mentioned above). But they still need force to be given to them so they can walk properly. And this is through the charity of Shabbos — that is, one gives to the poor for Shabbos — or one hosts a poor person at one's table on Shabbos. And the charity of Shabbos is the aspect of the sun of the future that is destined to be renewed in the time to come — to be like the light of the seven days. And through this it gives force to the aspect of the legs — so that they can walk properly in the ways of Hashem, blessed be He — as explained within.

 Siman 87 — סימן פז
 Titen Emes l'Yaakov — Essential perfection of awe is on Shabbos — yiras ha'onesh / yiras haromemut — Tzedek and emunah — light of truth sweetens all judgments — menuchas ahavah v'nedavah menuchas emes v'emunah

The essential perfection of awe is on Shabbos — in the aspect of: "yirey shmi — ilu shomrey Shabbas [those who fear My Name — these are the guardians of Shabbos]." And because awe is the aspect of Tzedek — from which comes the awakening of judgments, heaven forfend — this causes the fact that sometimes at the beginning of the entry of Shabbos — a great awe comes upon the person — which is called in Yiddish "frum" — but it is without joy. For it is difficult for him to be joyful — because during the weekday the outer forces sometimes have a grip on this awe — which is the aspect of the fear of punishment [yiras ha'onesh] — the aspect of Tzedek — the aspect of legs — for this is the aspect of [Proverbs 5:5]: "ragleha yordos maves" — heaven have mercy. And therefore — although on Shabbos the legs ascend — in the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and as mentioned above many times — nonetheless — because it is close to where the awe has just ascended from there — it is still difficult for it to be an awe with joy. For on Shabbos one must rejoice greatly — and receive Shabbos with joy and a good heart. And through this specifically — the essential perfection of awe — as explained in Likutay Moharan Tinyana, Siman 17. And therefore the essential perfection of the ascent of the legs — which ascend on Shabbos — is through the light of truth that shines on Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And: "Tzedek — kad is'chabar bah — emes — iskariyas — emunah [Tzedek — when it connects with it — truth — is called — faith]" — and emunah is the aspect of the awe of His majesty [yiras haromemut] — for which there is no grip of judgment at all. On the contrary — through it all external fears are nullified — and all judgments are sweetened — and then the awe is in its perfection — that is, with love and joy. And therefore Shabbos is called: "nachalas Yaakov" — the aspect of: "titen emes l'Yaakov." And this [Isaiah 58:13]: א'ם ת'שיב מ'שבת — initial letters of אמ"ת [emes] — as brought. And this: "raglecha" — for through this is the essential perfection of the legs — as mentioned above. And therefore Shabbos is called: "menuchas ahavah v'nedavah — menuchas emes v'emunah [a rest of love and freewill — a rest of truth and faith]."

 ✦ Translator's Summary — Simanim 72–87
 
 Siman 72 — New refined yetzer hara / Ein Sof / Shabbos requires being entirely good: Preparation → old yetzer hara nullified → a new, finer, more spiritual yetzer hara is given for free choice ("all the greater — his yetzer hara is greater"). The very darkness felt at entry of Shabbos = itself from the Shabbos illumination = like the ill patient beginning to feel pain = sign of healing = "ki b'rov chochmah rov ka'as v'yosif da'as yosif mach'ov." Must strengthen and receive Shabbos in joy. "Keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" — simple people: through Shabbos begin to feel even more the loss of their soul. Two angels (Zohar: yetzer tov and yetzer ra) = good angel and evil angel = finds table set and candle burning = evil angel reluctantly says Amen. Delight of Shabbos = all judgments sweetened at their root = "b'yom hani'ach lecha mei'atzevecha" = Isaiah 14:3; Siman 57 ("Sha'alu es Riv"k") cross-ref. "Lo seva'aru eish" = Tikunim: guard from sadness and anger and quarreling = the finer spiritual yetzer hara = aspect of anger and judgments. On Shabbos: illumination of Ein Sof shines in wondrous renewal = everything there is entirely good → must be entirely good without any judgments.
 Siman 73 — The vessel called Ani / two Shabbosim / Zohar Yisro 92: Shabbos = perfection of sacred speech ("v'daber davar") + world of thought + aspect of the Tzadik = three aspects = the vessel called "Ani." All influences descend through this vessel = "va'ani avarchem." Shabbos = source of blessing = prayer with concentration = thought connected to words of prayer = creates the "Ani" vessel. "Es Shabsosai tishmoru Ani Hashem" / "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" + Sages' teaching (Beitzah 16a): "matanah tovah yesh li / Shabbas shemah / matan scharah lo avida l'galeyyei" = inner dimension not revealed; through two Shabbosim = "Ani" vessel completed → blessings and influences; G-d, blessed be He, receives great pleasure = "chefetz chesed hu / ishah rei'ach nichoa'ch / Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha davka"; inner dimension revealed = "Kodesh" (Siman 15 cross-ref.); "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem / vayevarech vayekadesh." Isaiah 58 synthesis: "az tis'anag" = Yud within Ani = thought; "hirkavticha" = Nun within Ani = Malchus; "nachalas Yaakov" = Aleph within Ani = Yaakov = Aleph within Aleph-Mem-Shin; three Shabbosim = Zohar Yisro 92: "Shabbas ila'ah / Shabbas d'yoma / Shabbas d'leila." "Ki pi Hashem diber" = revelation of inner dimension of depth of supernal thought through speech = Zohar Bereishis 32 (cross-ref.).
 Siman 74 — Speech with knowledge / Yaakov / honor of Shabbos = Chochmah / Zohar Bereishis 32 in Aramaic: Shabbos = perfection of soul ("Shabbas vayinafash") = sweetening of judgments (Zohar) = speech with knowledge ("dibur b'da'as") = "v'daber davar" + "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" = Yaakov (first to guard Shabbos) = Torah (all agree: Torah given on Shabbos). Shabbos = time of cessation from crying out = healing = "shemesh tzedakah u'marpe b'chenafehah" (Malachi 3:20; Sages: "shemesh b'Shabbas Tzedakah"). Honor of Shabbos: ascent to Chochmah = "av b'chochmah" = "ki Kodesh hi" (writings) → reveals His honor = "v'im av ani ayeh chevodi" (Malachi 1:6). Isaiah 58: "raglecha" = soul = aspect of legs (cross-ref. Siman 69 "chomer issur gezeilah") vs. ru'ach and neshamah; Malchus = Sarah; weekday: Sitra Achra grips the soul ("dina d'mesa'avusa"); on Shabbos: soul ascends to supernal root = "meshivas nefesh"; "me'asos chafatzecha" = "u'v'shikutzeihem nafsham chafetzah" (Ezekiel 20:8); "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" = supernal Chochmah = "ein l'ma'alah mei'oneg"; "v'chibadto / pis'ayah gasah" = anger + judgment + blemish of eyes of wisdom = "tlas guvnin"; "mimitzo / v'daber davar" = don't blemish speech with knowledge; "az tis'anag" = supernal delight; "hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus = root of soul's aspect; saved from subjugation = from dross of judgment = root of kingdom of Esau = "nefesh ki techeta"; "nachalas Yaakov" = speech with knowledge = connects soul (from which speech flows) to supernal wisdom; nachalah b'li metzarim; "al kol ha'aretz kevodecha"; "ki pi Hashem diber" = Zohar Bereishis 32 (full Aramaic): "mah d'kasuv megaleh amukos mini choshech / ta chazey kol inon amikkin stimin d'nafkin mi'go machshavah / u'kala natil lon lo is'galeyan / ad d'milah mgaleh lon / man milah hiyno dibur / v'hai dibur ikri Shabbas." "V'hai dibur d'ati mi'sitra d'choshech megaleh amukos migavyei" — see there further.
 Siman 75 — World of souls / awe / body subdued / blood clarified / holy sparks / Shabbas Shalom / redemption: Shabbos = day of souls not bodies (Zohar) = awe = "v'zarachah lachem yirey shmi ilu shomrey Shabbas"; "yirey Shabbas." Body subdued = "guf kasheh pachad shavro." Perfection of speech = "v'daber davar"; body nullified = "v'hayu l'vasar echad"; prayer with "kol atzmosei tomarnah." All blood clarified and purified = encompassed within sacred words of Torah and prayer = aspect of Shalem = all sparks of letters of shevirah (clothed in the blood = in the aspect of fragments and strife) → now completed and united together = "shalom" made between them = encompassed in sacred words of Torah and prayer. "Shabbas Shalom." Perfection of soul = blood is the soul. Ascent of sacred legs = "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" = the sparks = legs = words of Torah and prayer also = legs. Redemption depends on Shabbos (Sages) = "v'amad raglav b'yom hahu" (Zechariah 14:4) = depends on clarification and ascent of holy sparks in fullness = "ad d'mati raglin b'raglin" (Zohar). Shabbos = source of blessing = "lo matza haKBH keli machzik berachah ela haShalom" = wholeness of ascent of sparks = "oseh shalom u'vorei es hakol." "Kol hamitpallel b'Erev Shabbas v'omer Vayechulu" = partner in creation = "v'lomar l'Tziyon ami atah mah ana avdit shamaya v'ar'ah b'miluli af atem ken" = completion of tikkun of creation = raise all sparks of shevirah = depends on Israel = through perfection of words of Torah and prayer. Holiness of delight of Shabbos = within every food and drink: sparks of fallen letters; on weekday = lack completion until encompassed in words of Torah and prayer; on Shabbos = encompassed at once in holiness of Shabbos since the eating and drinking is itself a commandment (elaborated elsewhere).
