 Siman 89 — סימן פט
 Vat'chasrehu Me'at — Not to request one's needs on Shabbos — the King comes with great joy — cessation from crying out = assurance of healing

Our Sages of blessed memory taught: a person should not ask for his needs on Shabbos — so that he should not remember that he has a sick person within his house and become distressed. And at first glance this is not understood — for even if he does not pray for his needs — he can still remember the sick person he has within his house and become distressed. On the contrary — at first glance — if he is not permitted to pray for him — through this he becomes even more distressed. However — according to what is explained within — this is somewhat understood. For the essential prayer that one prays on a weekday for one's needs must also be only for the lack of the Shechinah — as it were — and this will be the essential distress — as brought in the holy books. And therefore — even on Shabbos — if one were permitted to pray for one's needs — one would remember that one has a sick person within one's house and become distressed. That is — one would also become distressed essentially only over the lack of the Shechinah. But nonetheless — through this — one would not be able to serve G-d, blessed be He, with completely full joy. And in truth — the will of G-d, blessed be He, is that on Shabbos all of Israel should be in great joy — as it is written [Isaiah 14:3]: "b'yom hani'ach Hashem lecha mei'atzevecha u'merogzecha" — and so on — and as brought in the holy Zohar. And therefore — even if one remembers the distress — only that one should also remember in this that the essential distress is directed to the King — that is, to the Shechinah — as it were — but nonetheless — due to the immense holiness of Shabbos — the King comes with such great joy — and wishes to take pleasure together with His beloved children in love and will and joy — so greatly — that He does not want them to remember His distress at all — so as not to disrupt the joy. And then when one remembers this — through this itself one also comes to great joy — and one is crowned with new mental faculties — which is the essential holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And through this itself the distress is sweetened — and the lack is filled. And this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: Shabbos is the time of cessation from crying out — and healing is close to come.

For specifically — through this itself — that one is not permitted on Shabbos to cry out and shout about the distress — as mentioned above — through this one will be certain that healing is certainly close to come.

 Siman 91 — סימן צא
 Vayehi Yadav Emunah — Shabbos = perfection of faith — faith → intellect → greater faith → ascent through Neh"y/Chag"t/Chab"d — two Shabbosim — Avraham/Har; Yaakov/Beis — tachyas hamaysim — Isaiah 58

Shabbos is the aspect of the perfection of faith — as mentioned above many times.

And through the perfection of faith one comes to intellect [sechel] — and then faith is completed even more — and through this one comes to even higher intellect. And this is the aspect of the sacred ascents of Shabbos — for the beginning of the ascent is in Malchus — which is the aspect of faith [emunah] — and Malchus ascends in the aspects of Neh"y — Chag"t — Chab"d — which is the secret of the Holy Apple Orchard — as is well-known. That is — faith is completed each time even more — until it ascends to intellect — which is Chab"d. And afterward one ascends even more. This is the aspect of [Exodus 31:14]: "u'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi" — see in the writings of the holy Ari z"l and you will understand. And this is the aspect of [Malachi 3:20]: "v'zarachah lachem yirey shmi — (ilu shomrey Shabbas k'moh she'darshu Rz"l) — yirah [and it shall shine for you who fear My Name — (these are the guardians of Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded) — awe]" — awe is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of faith — which is completed through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this [Malachi 3:20]: "shemesh Tzedakah" — for through this one merits to come to the light of the intellect — which is the aspect of the sun — as explained within. And this is the aspect of "shemesh Tzedakah" — for that one merits to come to the intellect — this is only a charity and lovingkindness from Him, blessed be He. For faith depends on the person's choice — to strengthen himself in complete faith. But wisdom and intellect — this is only from Him, blessed be He — in the aspect of [Proverbs 2:6]: "ki Hashem yiten chochmah" — and so on — the aspect of [Daily Prayer]: "Atah chonein l'adam da'as [You graciously grant to a person knowledge]." And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: "shemesh b'Shabbas — Tzedakah la'aniyim" — that is — for there is no poor person except one lacking in da'as [knowledge] — and therefore what G-d, blessed be He, grants to a person wisdom and mental faculties through the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of: "shemesh b'Shabbas" — this is only in the manner of charity to the poor. For there is no poor person except one lacking in da'as — and therefore what G-d, blessed be He, grants to a person wisdom and mental faculties through the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of: "shemesh b'Shabbas" — this is only in the manner of charity and lovingkindness — the aspect of charity to the poor. And this is the aspect of: "matanah tovah yesh li b'veys genzai" — and they stated there: "matan scharah lo avida l'galeyyei" — that is, the inner dimension of the holiness of Shabbos — the aspect of the mental faculties that one merits to receive on Shabbos. And this itself is the aspect of the extra soul — the aspect of [Job 32:8]: "v'nishmas Shadai tevinam [and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding]." And this is the aspect of: "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" — and so on — for the guarding of the first Shabbos is only through faith — and through this one merits to intellect — and then one merits to even greater faith and even greater intellect — which is the aspect of the second Shabbos. And therefore they derived this from what is written [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — v'chol haggid — v'havi'osim el har kodshi — v'simachtim beys tefilasi." "Har [mountain]" is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of faith. And this is the aspect of [Song of Songs 4:8]: "tashuri mero'sh Amanah" — and Rashi explained: from the beginning of the faith — that you believed in Me — and so on. Another explanation: the mountain — and so on — and its name is Amanah. "Beis [house]" — this is the aspect of wisdom and intellect — the aspect of [Proverbs 24:3]: "b'chochmah yibbaneh bayis [with wisdom a house is built]." And therefore Avraham — who was the first of the believers — is called a mountain [Isaiah 41:8]. And Yaakov — who is the aspect of the sun — the aspect of intellect — as explained elsewhere — is called a house [Obadiah 1:18]. And because on Shabbos faith is completed so greatly — that it spreads throughout all the limbs — therefore it is a commandment to also delight the body on that day.

And the delight of Shabbos is entirely holy — as explained elsewhere. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 37:3]: "shechen eretz u're'eh emunah — v'his'anag al Hashem [dwell in the land and tend faithfulness — and delight in Hashem]" — which is the aspect of the delight of Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded. And this is certainly a great level — when a person merits such complete faith — that it spreads upon all the limbs of the body and upon all the physical pleasures — for this is the aspect of: "u're'eh emunah" — that one eats and is nourished from faith [emunah]. And afterward — through this — one comes to intellect. And the intellect is, as it were, a portion of the Divine from above — as understood in the teaching Ashrey Zar'eka, Siman 35. And then one is nourished, as it were, from the intellect itself — in the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 7:12]: "haChochmah tichyeh ba'aleha [wisdom will give life to its possessors]." And this is the aspect of [Exodus 24:11]: "vayechezu es Elokim vayochlu vayishtu [and they beheld G-d and they ate and drank]" — as brought. And also in this — there is level above level — for not all the levels of faith are equal — and likewise in the levels of intellect — as is well-known.

Note — Siman 92 (al yedey mah she'ha'adam na va'nad afilu b'soch beyso — yachol l'shachech es ha'eish — through moving from place to place even within one's house one can cool the fire which is the aspect of judgments — and can revive the dead): The full text of this siman appears embedded within Siman 91 in the source manuscript, marked with a special notation. Its content concerns: moving about [na va'nad] cools the fire in the heart = aspect of the lungs [kanfey re'iyah] that breathe upon the heart; Kayin and na va'nad as tikkun; the unintentional killer and the city of refuge [ir miklat]; the Torah scholar as ir miklat = saves from the angel of death (Makkos 11); Yaakov va'yizrach lo hashemesh / vayavo Yaakov shalem ir Shechem; Shechem = ir miklat; vayachan es pney ha'ir = Sages: guarded the Shabbos and established the Shabbos boundary; Yosef sold → the fire and judgments re-awakened → rectification = Israel commanded regarding Shabbos (Zohar); Yaakov and Yosef first of those described as guarding Shabbos = they are the aspect of re'iyah and liba = secret of guarding Shabbos (Tikunim). Isaiah 58: raglecha = do not walk beyond the Shabbos boundary; me'asos chafatzecha = don't blemish holiness of Shabbos; oneg; v'chibadto = Sages: not to take large strides = aspect of anger = arouses the fire; also: the person walking back and forth = aspect of kanfey re'iyah d'nashvei al liba; therefore must not take large strides even on weekdays so as not to blemish the spirit in the wings of the lungs = a gale-wind = would intensify the fire; Sages: large strides removes one five-hundredth of the light of one's eyes = damages the kanfey re'iyah = "why is it called re'iyah? because it illuminates the eyes" = "the veins of the heart depend upon the eyes"; Yosef to his brothers: al tirgazu b'derech = Sages: do not take large strides; on Shabbos must be especially careful; v'daber davar = Tikkun 13 (full Aramaic): u'v'hahu ru'cha havah b'tish b'chamesh nimayin d'chinor d'inun chamesh kanfey re'iyah u'v'kaneh salik kal l'liba = from the five wings of the lung the voice rises to the heart = "is not My word like fire" — therefore must guard from weekday speech on Shabbos; az tis'anag al Hashem da Atika Kadisha = through perfection of kanfey re'iyah: the intellect burns and shines with great light = merits supernal mochin = aspect of Atik = root of sweetening of all judgments and root of tachyas hamaysim (Zohar; Gemara: Sages taught "they give him all the desires of his heart"); hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin = ascent of Malchus to the mochin; Tikkun 13 cited: urkay d'liba inon k'chayalin basar malkiyhon / hachi misnah'agin urkay d'liba l'gabi ru'cha = the spirit in the heart is connected to the mochin from which is the root of the sweetening; saved from subjugation of kingdoms = Sitra Achra draws from the fires and judgments = from the right side of the heart toward the liver = full of blood = from there the sustenance of the minister of Esau the red-complexioned one = Siman 57 cross-reference; nachalas Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin = the Torah = truth = kanfey re'iyah d'manshvei al liba; ki pi Hashem diber = Shabbos = sacred speech = encompasses both the wings of the lungs and the heart = Tikkun 13; therefore through it = essential sweetening; Torah words = kanfey re'iyah = sweeten judgments = tachyas hamaysim = "ki chayyim heim l'motz'eyhem" = Sages: "l'motziyeim b'feh davka" = through speaking with the mouth; Yosef revealed himself to his brothers: al tirgazu b'derech / v'hinei eineichem ro'os v'eyney achi Binyamin / Rashi: just as I have no hatred in my heart for Binyamin my brother so too I have no hatred for you = ki fi hamedaber aleichem = through the mouth-speech the heart is also sweetened = vayenachem osam vayedaber al libbam.

 Siman 93 — סימן צג
 Kol ha'Oseh — Shabbos equivalent to the entire Torah — Yisrael asher b'cha espa'ar — Yisrael alah b'machashavah — Shabbos = above time — Mishkan work = honest commerce — Isaiah 58

Our Sages of blessed memory taught: Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah and the commandments — as mentioned above many times. And also — it is explained in the holy Zohar that the Holy One, blessed be He, says regarding one who properly guards the Shabbos: "Yisrael asher b'cha espa'ar [Israel through whom I am glorified]" [Isaiah 49:3]. And Israel arose in thought — which itself is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — for it is the world of thought. And thought is the aspect of above time. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 139:16]: "yamim yotzaru — v'lo echad bahem" — for Shabbos is the aspect of one — the aspect of above time. And this: "vayevarcheihu mikol hayamim — vayekadshehu mikol hazemanim [and He blessed it above all the days — and He sanctified it above all the times]." And also — Shabbos is the aspect of mochin d'gadlus and clear intellect — as mentioned above many times. And therefore then it is very good and beautiful to pray with concentration — and as also understood within. And this [Psalms 92:2–3]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem — v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" — that is — for prayer is something that stands at the very height of the world — the aspect of above time. And this is the aspect of: "elyon [Most High]." And this is the aspect of [Exodus 35:2]: "sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah" — that is, the work of the Mishkan — which is the aspect of honest commerce in faith [masa u'matan b'emunah] — as explained within in the teaching Ani Hashem, Siman 11. And through engaging in commerce in faith — the aforementioned rectifications are also drawn — as explained within. But [Exodus 35:2]: "u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh Shabbas Shabbason laHashem" — for then all the aforementioned rectifications flow even more through the holiness of Shabbos itself — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that one merits mochin d'gadlus at the ultimate supernal level — up to the aspect of Atik.

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — which is the aspect of prayer — as is well-known — to the mental faculties — that one merits to pray with clear intellect. And one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — from which comes the aspect of alien thoughts that disrupt the concentration of prayer. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — which is the aspect of the entirety of the Torah and the commandments. And therefore it is explained regarding Yaakov that he engaged in commerce in faith — in the aspect of [Genesis 30:33]: "v'anetah bi tzidkasi b'yom machar" — and as explained in the passage Vayichar l'Yaakov — vayarev b'Lavan. And also — it is explained regarding him that he guarded the Shabbos — as mentioned above. And therefore Yaakov merited an inheritance without limits — the aspect of above place — above time. For the aspects of time and place are connected to each other — as understood elsewhere. And he is the essential one about whom it is said: "Yisrael asher b'cha espa'ar" — the aspect of Tiferes Yisrael. And he is the aspect of: "Yisrael alah b'machashavah [Israel arose in thought]."

 Siman 94 — סימן צד
 Zachar Chasdo — All worlds created for Israel — essential influence through speech — Shabbos = Zayin = faith = wisdom — sparks of the letters ascend — Kiddush = Ayin Teivim — Psalm 92 fully mapped — Isaiah 58

All the worlds were created only for the sake of Israel — in order to grant them abundant good. And the essential influence is through speech [dibur]. And Shabbos is the aspect of speech — in the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — and as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar. Therefore the essential influence is through the holiness of Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar. And also — the essential ascent of the holy sparks — which are the sparks of the letters of speech — in their fullness — is likewise only through the holiness of Shabbos — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of [Numbers 28:10]: "olas Shabbas b'Shabato — al olas haTamid [the Shabbos burnt-offering in its Shabbos — upon the daily burnt-offering]" — and so on — for then is the essential fullness of their ascent to their root and their rest. For the essential ascent of the sparks is through faith and wisdom — as explained within. And Shabbos is the aspect of the perfection of faith and the perfection of wisdom and intellect — as mentioned above many times — for Shabbos is the aspect of Zayin [the letter ז] — in the aspect of [Exodus 20:11]: "ki sheshes yamim asah Hashem" — and so on — "vayanuach b'yom hashevi'i [and He rested on the seventh day]" — for all of them are encompassed within it. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 33:4]: "v'chol ma'asehu b'emunah [and all His work is in faith]" — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos. And therefore it is the aspect of Zayin. And it is likewise the aspect of Yud — the aspect of thought — the aspect of wisdom — for Shabbos is the aspect of the world of thought — the aspect of wisdom — as it is written [Exodus 31:14]: "ki Kodesh hi." And then faith — which is the aspect of Malchus — ascends to wisdom — as explained in the writings. And therefore Shabbos is the aspect of the eye [ayin] — the aspect of: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein." And this is the aspect of the Ayin Teivim [the ten words] that are in the Kiddush. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: "u'mhaddar leih b'Kiddushoh d'vey shimshah [and one recites it beautifully in the Kiddush of the eve of Shabbos]." And through this one elevates the sparks of the letters of speech found in everything — and from them words are made — and through this G-d, blessed be He, grants abundant good to Israel. And this is the aspect of: "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" — that is, the aspect of faith and wisdom. "Miyad nigalin" — for through this: "v'niglah kevod Hashem" — and so on — as explained within. And this is likewise the aspect of: "techum Shabbas alpayim amah" — likewise corresponding to faith and wisdom — as mentioned above many times. And this: all who pray on Erev Shabbos and say Vayechulu — it is as if one became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the act of creation — for it is stated: "vayechulu" — do not read "vayechulu" but rather "vayichlu" [and they completed]. And immediately after this: from where that speech is like deed — as it is stated: "b'dvar Hashem shamayim na'asu" — that is — since the creation came about through speech — and there are sparks of letters that fell — therefore the essential perfection of the creation — the perfection of the act of Bereishis — is through the ascent of the aforementioned sparks. And also — for through this He grants abundant good to Israel — for whose sake the entire creation was. And the ascent of the sparks comes about through the holiness of Shabbos — and begins from the evening prayer of Shabbos — when the worlds ascend. And therefore through the words of faith that Israel recite in the passage of Vayechulu — and also in this passage the thirty-two paths of wisdom are alluded to — as explained in the holy Zohar and in the writings. And this itself is the aspect of [Genesis 2:2]: "vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i" — and so on — that is, the aspect of the faith that shines on Shabbos in its fullness — for this is the aspect of: "v'chol ma'asehu b'emunah." And [Genesis 2:2]: "vayishbos b'yom hashevi'i" — and so on — this is the aspect of thought — for there is the essential resting and peace — the aspect of: "shevisah mimachsheves avodah." And likewise [Genesis 2:3]: "vayevarech" — this is the aspect of faith — the aspect of: "ish emunos rav berachos [a man of faith abounds in blessings]." And [Genesis 2:3]: "vayekadesh" — this is the aspect of thought — wisdom — which is the aspect of Kodesh. And through these two aspects — the essential ascent of the sparks and the perfection of the act of Bereishis — and therefore it is as if one became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the act of creation.

And this [Psalms 92:2–3]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem" — and so on — that is, to speak holy words — through which He grants abundant good and lovingkindness to the house of Israel through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this [Psalms 92:3]: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — the aspect of drawing down the lovingkindnesses mentioned above.

And [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — through faith with wisdom — for this is the aspect of: "lehagid" — the language of "milah d'chochmata [a word of wisdom]" — as is well-known. Through this one draws lovingkindnesses through the ascent of the letters of speech. And this [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor" — this is the aspect of the Yud — which is the aspect of wisdom. And [Psalms 92:4]: "v'alay navel" — initial letters of: thirty-two paths of wisdom [ל"ב נתיבות החכמה] — as explained elsewhere. And [Psalms 92:4]: "alay higgayon b'chinor" — which is likewise the aspect of wisdom — and it is not labor [melachah] — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And this is the aspect of: "zamru maskil [sing with wisdom]" — and as explained elsewhere. And this [Psalms 92:5]: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha — b'ma'asey yadecha aranen" — this is the aspect of the ascent of the sparks of the letters of the act of Bereishis — that ascend through the holiness of Shabbos — with great joy — in the aspect of [Isaiah 55:12]: "ki b'simchah tetze'u [for with joy shall you go forth]" — and as explained elsewhere. And this is the aspect of: "shata'aleinu b'simchah l'artzeinu [that You lift us up with joy to our land]." And this: "v'simcheinu b'yeshuasecha [and gladden us with Your salvation]" — for this is His salvation, blessed be He — as explained within.

And this [Psalms 92:6]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem" — this is the aspect of the light of faith — the aspect of: "v'chol ma'asehu b'emunah." [Psalms 92:6]: "me'od amku machshevosecha" — the aspect of thought and wisdom — through which one can bring out and elevate even the sparks that fell into Sitra d'Mausa [the side of death] — for this is the aspect of "me'od" — as is well-known. And this [Psalms 92:7]: "ish ba'ar lo yeda — u'chesil lo yavin es zos" — that is, one who has neither wisdom nor faith — which is the aspect of "zos" — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:8]: "b'feroa'ch resha'im" — and so on — "l'hishamedam adey ad" — for their ascent is the ultimate degree of their descent and downfall — in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 7:10]: "u'meshalem l'son'av el panav l'ha'avido [and He repays His enemies to their face to destroy them]." For through this — all their vitality — which is the holy sparks that fell in their place — goes out from them — and then they are spent and lost entirely. And this [Psalms 92:9]: "v'atah marom l'olam Hashem" — the aspect of the ascent of the sparks of the letters of speech — which are the aspect of "Atah" — as is well-known and understood within. And this [Psalms 92:10]: "ki hinneh oyevecha Hashem" — and so on — "vatarem kir'em karni" — and so on — and this [Psalms 92:12]: "vatabet eini b'shuray" — through the aforementioned aspect of the eye — through which one elevates the holy sparks — through this one also draws the downfall of the wicked — in the aspect of [Psalms 91:8]: "rak b'einecha tabbis — v'shilumas resha'im tireh [only with your eyes shall you behold — and the retribution of the wicked shall you see]" — the aspect of: "nasan einav bo v'na'aseh gal shel atzamos [he gazed at him with his eyes and he became a heap of bones]." For through the gaze and the looking of his eyes alone — one draws out the holy sparks that fell in his place — which is all his vitality. And through this he becomes completely nothing — as also explained within and as brought in Siman 12 regarding: "v'sham'it malchusa v'katleih." And this [Psalms 92:12]: "b'kamim alai mere'im tishmanahoznai" — "Tzadik katamar yifrach" — for the Tzadikim who are united as one with the holy sparks — therefore through the dispute and the persecution that comes upon them — they bloom and grow even more. And this: "shetulin b'veys Hashem" — the aspect of wisdom — as explained within — "b'chatzros Elokeinu" — the aspect of faith — "yafrichu." And this [Psalms 92:15]: "od yinuvun b'seivah" — for as they grow older their mind settles upon them. And this [Psalms 92:16]: "lehagid ki yashar Hashem tzuri" — and so on — for the word of Hashem is upright — and all His work is in faith — and all of it was done for the sake of the ascent of the holy sparks — which are the aspect of the word of Hashem — as mentioned above.

And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — that is, the aspect of the ascent of the sacred legs together with the holy sparks — that ascend through the holiness of Shabbos. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "me'asos chafatzecha b'yom kadshi" — for even the doing of one's pursuits on a weekday — when done properly in holiness — is likewise the aspect of the ascent of the holy sparks — as explained elsewhere.

But on Shabbos — it is forbidden to do any labor — for then is the essential fullness of the ascent of the holy sparks through the holiness of Shabbos itself — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" — the aspect of wisdom — and [Isaiah 58:13]: "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" — the aspect of faith — and as mentioned above many times. And also — through this is drawn the aspect of: "v'niglah kevod Hashem" — as explained within.

And this is likewise the aspect of the honor of Shabbos. And [Isaiah 58:13]: "v'chibadto mei'asos derachecha" — not to take large strides — which removes one five-hundredth of the light of one's eyes — it follows that through this one blemishes the aspect of the aforementioned eyes — which are the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "mimitzo chafatzecha v'daber davar" — so as not to blemish the aspect of the letters of speech that ascend through the holiness of Shabbos. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — for through this G-d, blessed be He, grants abundant good to Israel — which is the essential delight — as explained within. And therefore also he merits to delight in Hashem. And this [Psalms 37:3]: "shechen eretz u're'eh emunah" — through this — "v'his'anag al Hashem" — and He will give you the desires of your heart — for all the good influences are drawn through this. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: they give him all the desires of his heart — as mentioned above. And this is what the holy Zohar expounded: "da Atika Kadisha" — that is, one merits very supernal mental faculties — the aspect of Atik.

And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus to the mental faculties — that is, the fullness of faith — when the mental faculties of wisdom shine upon it. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, the sparks ascend from the aspect of the exile. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — which is the aspect that connects wisdom with faith — for this is the aspect of the holy Torah — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of the heritage of Yaakov. And therefore the essential rectification of the creation — through Yaakov — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "olami mi vera'acha — Yaakov vera'acha" — and as mentioned above many times — which is the aspect of: "bishvili nivra ha'olam [for my sake the world was created]" — as explained within. And this is the aspect of an inheritance without limits — for one can conquer the entire world and elevate it to the fullness of holiness through the gaze of one's eyes alone. And this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 33:28]: "v'yishkon Yisrael betach badad — eyin Yaakov [and Israel shall dwell in safety — alone — the eye of Yaakov]" — "eyin [the eye]" — specifically. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for all of this is done through the holiness of Shabbos — for then the holy sparks — which are the letters of speech — ascend and are unified with G-d, blessed be He — as it were. For this is the aspect of: "ki pi Hashem diber" — as explained within.

 Siman 95 — סימן צה
 Kesha'Parnasei haDor — Moshe said v'nachnu mah — anger = forgetting Shabbos — mah = humility = purity of thought — ra'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas ra'u davka — Ayin = 130 = shem mah

And this is what Moshe said: "v'nachnu mah — ki taluinu aleinu [and what are we — that you murmur against us?]" [Exodus 16:7] — that is: since we have not removed the aspect of mah [what] — therefore the mouth [peh] remains — and disputes and humiliations come. But since we hold ourselves in the aspect of mah — then why do you murmur against us? And therefore afterward — when it is stated [Exodus 16:20]: "vayiktzof alehem Moshe [and Moshe was angry with them]" — over the fact that they left over from the manna — our Sages of blessed memory taught in Midrash Rabbah Beshalach: through the fact that he came to a state of anger — he forgot to warn them regarding Shabbos. And because of this it was said to him afterward [Exodus 16:28]: "ad anah me'anem" — and he was included together with them. As mentioned above — for Shabbos is the aspect of the world of thought. And it is brought in Sha'arey Tziyon and in the writings: to purify the thought — one must have in mind the Name Mah five times in reverse arrangement — and so on — and this: "machashavah" [thought] — "chashav mah" — see there. And therefore through the anger — which is, as it were, the aspect of the removal of mah — through this he forgot to warn them regarding Shabbos — and the mouth [peh] remained — regarding which it is stated: "ad anah" — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "shvu ish tachtav" — stated afterward regarding Shabbos — which alludes to humility — as explained elsewhere. For this is the aspect of mah — mentioned above. And this [Exodus 16:29]: "re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas — re'u davka" — for "ayin" [the letter Ayin] — the gematria [numerical value] of — 130 — that is, the Name Mah in reverse arrangement — as brought in the writings. And this: "ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas" — which is the aspect of the world of thought. Therefore He gives you bread for two days — so that the thought should not be preoccupied with livelihood — but should be connected to the holiness of Shabbos. And this [Exodus 16:29]: "shvu ish tachtav" — the aspect of humility — the aspect of mah — upon which depends the essential holiness of thought and wisdom — as it is written [Job 28:12]: "v'haChochmah mei'ayin timatzei [and wisdom — from where [ayin] is it found?]" — and as explained elsewhere. And this [Job 28:12]: "chochmah" — the letters of: "ko'ach mah" — as mentioned above. And this [Exodus 16:29]: "al yetzei ish mimekomo" — that through this one does not go out from one's place and level — and does not come to humiliations — heaven forfend — as mentioned above.

 Siman 96 — סימן צו (Zomem Rasha l'Tzadik)
 Shabbos = world of thought — ascent of sparks — alien thoughts — when higher than one's level = breaks the wicked's power — Psalm 92 — Erev Shabbas = shalhava d'asha

Shabbos is the aspect of the world of thought — and then is the essential time of the ascent of the sparks in their fullness — for all of them are clarified through thought [machashavah].

And therefore then it is very good and beautiful to pray without alien thoughts [machshavos zaros] — and even if some alien thought comes to him — it is easier then to elevate it. And this [Psalms 92:2–5]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem" — and so on — and this [Psalms 92:5]: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha — b'ma'asey yadecha aranen" — for there is no joy like the resolution of doubts — (and as understood in the Tur"z, Orach Chayyim, Siman 554) — and therefore even though it is always known to all that [Isaiah 6:3]: "melo chol ha'aretz kevodo [the whole earth is full of His honor]" — and certainly there are holy sparks even within alien thought as well — nonetheless — since it is difficult for him to elevate it — he has distress. However — on Shabbos — it is easier for him to elevate it — and he has joy — since everything is the work of His hands, blessed be He — and every act of Hashem is for His sake. But all of this — when an alien thought comes to him — according to the measure at which he stands — and according to his portion in the holiness of Shabbos. However — sometimes an alien thought comes to him that is from the aspect above his level — and then it is difficult for him to elevate it. But even so — through the power of the will — through which he wants to break it and elevate it — through this he breaks the power of the wicked and the disputants — who dispute against some Tzadik — from whom that alien thought comes to him — as explained within. And this [Psalms 92:6]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem — me'od amku machshevosecha" — for sometimes an alien thought comes even on Shabbos — that is difficult to fix and elevate — for there are many aspects and levels in this — and the alien thought is above his level. And this [Psalms 92:7]: "ish ba'ar lo yeda — u'chesil lo yavin es zos" — for why does this alien thought come to him — since it is not of his level? But through this the downfall of the wicked and the disputants — who dispute against the Tzadikim — is drawn. And this [Psalms 92:8–11]: "b'feroa'ch resha'im" — and so on — "l'hishamedam adey ad" — and so on — "yispardu kol po'aley aven — vatarem kir'em karni" — and so on — and [Psalms 92:12]: "vatabet eini b'shuray — b'kamim alai mere'im tishmanah oznai — Tzadik katamar yifrach" — and so on. Or perhaps there are yet more levels in this. For there are alien thoughts that come from the aspect of Nogah — which is mixed with good and evil — and one must elevate the good within them. But there are thoughts that are from the aspect of the three completely impure husks — which one must nullify entirely and repel with complete repulsion. And this also on weekdays and on Erev Shabbos — when then is the time of the ascent of the worlds and the sparks — and the good within Nogah also ascends — and then the completely impure husks also wish to ascend and draw sustenance from the holiness — and then the shalhava d'asha descends and scorches them and causes them to fall — and so on — as explained in the writings. That is — these thoughts cannot be elevated — but only: to arouse against them the sacred force of fire — through the ardor [hitlahavus] in prayer — and then they spontaneously perish and go — in the aspect of [Psalms 97:3]: "eish lefanav teilech — v'tela'het saviv tzarav" — the aspect of [Psalms 68:3]: "k'himos donag mipney eish yovedu resha'im" — and so on. And this is likewise within the category of: "b'feroa'ch resha'im k'mo esev" — and so on — that they also wish to ascend — but this is for their destruction forever. "Yispardu kol po'aley aven — vatarem kir'em karni" — this is the raising of holiness — all of this explained in the kavannos.

 Siman 96 — סימן צו (Elokim al d'mi Lach)
 Shabbos = humility = awe = Malchus = rectification of alien thoughts — prayer = ruling [moshal] — Midrash Rabbah Beshalach — ten utterances of creation = lovingkindness — Isaiah 58

Shabbos is the aspect of humility and lowliness — and it is likewise the aspect of awe and the aspect of Malchus — and the rectification of alien thoughts — as mentioned above many times. And therefore then prayer has its fullness — and one merits the aspect of: a Tzadik who rules through his prayer — as explained in Midrash Rabbah, Parashas Beshalach: one who guards and delights the Shabbos merits the aspect of [Job 22:28]: "v'tigzor omer v'yakum lach [and you shall decree a word and it shall be established for you]" — and they give him all the desires of his heart. And this is the aspect of [Job 22:26]: "ki az al Shadai tis'anag" — and so on — "ta'atir eilav v'yishma'echa" — and so on — "v'tigzor omer v'yakum lach" — and so on [Job 22:26–28] — for this itself is His delight, blessed be He — when there are Tzadikim who pray in this manner. And for their sake was the entire creation — and because of them G-d, blessed be He, also now renews the act of creation and changes nature and performs wonders through their prayer — as understood within. And all of this flows on Shabbos in its fullness — for Shabbos is the ultimate purpose of the work of heaven and earth — and the end of deed is in the beginning of thought. And then the ten utterances [asarah ma'amaros] through which the entire creation came about — shine even more — as it is written [Genesis 2:2]: "vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i" — and so on — and the ten utterances mentioned above are the aspect of lovingkindness. And this is the aspect of the great lovingkindnesses drawn on Shabbos. And through this — the Dalet [ד] becomes Heh [ה] — and this rectification is completed in its fullness through the holiness of Shabbos — as explained in the Tikunim. And through this the bounty flows — for Shabbos is the root of all the influences — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that is, one merits to enter, as it were, into the aspect of His delight, blessed be He — Who takes delight from the fact that there are Tzadikim who rule through their prayer — as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory expounded from this: he too merits this — and they give him all the desires of his heart — as mentioned above. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — the aspect of the ascent of Malchus — which is prayer. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, one is saved through the holiness of Shabbos from arrogance and alien thoughts — which are the aspect of the subjugation of kingdoms. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of humility and awe — the aspect of [Proverbs 22:4]: "ekev anavah yiras Hashem [the reward of humility is the fear of Hashem]" — (and as explained elsewhere) — through which prayer is completed — until one rules through one's prayer — and can change nature. For this is the aspect of: one merits an inheritance without limits. And for this sake the world was created — as mentioned above. And this [Psalms 8:1]: "olami olami — v'chol haggid — mi vera'acha — v'chol haggid — Yaakov vera'acha." And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for one merits that his speech is the aspect of the word of Hashem — and one can through this draw the renewal of the act of Bereishis — for it is stated about this: "b'dvar Hashem shamayim na'asu" — and great lovingkindnesses are drawn — and abundant bounty flows — in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 15:6]: "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem."

 Siman 98 — סימן צח
 Gal shel Atzamos — Shabbos = Tzadik = eynay Hashem el haTzadikim — one examines one's deeds and does teshuvah — the new soul — shemesh Tzedakah u'marpe

Shabbos is the aspect of the Tzadik — as explained in the holy Zohar — and all of Israel — through the fact that they guard the Shabbos — are called Tzadikim. And therefore Shabbos is the aspect of eyes — the aspect of: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" — for this is the aspect of [Psalms 34:16]: "eynay Hashem el haTzadikim [the eyes of Hashem are toward the righteous]."

And this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem es haShabbas — re'u davka" — and as explained elsewhere. And therefore then the person is especially propitious to examine his deeds and to contemplate his ways — for then his eyes are opened — and he sees what had been hidden from him previously — and he sees how far each blemish and each sin reaches — and he does repentance. And therefore Shabbos is the aspect of repentance [teshuvah] — as explained elsewhere. And perhaps this is also within the category of what our Sages of blessed memory said: "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh" — for then he sees and contemplates the extent of the loss of his soul during the weekday — and he does repentance — and through this he merits the extra soul. And this is of great benefit for him — for since his eyes are opened and he sees the full extent of his faults, heaven forfend — through this itself the holiness of Shabbos would have been disrupted for him, heaven forfend — for one must receive Shabbos with joy and a good heart — and as explained elsewhere. But through the fact that he immediately merits the extra soul and a new higher-soul — in the aspect of [Zohar]: "v'chulhon mis'aterin b'nishmatin chadtin — k'din hu shirusa d'tzlosa l'varacha lah b'chedva b'nehiru d'anpin [and all of them are crowned with new souls — then is the beginning of prayer — to bless it with joy — with the light of the face]" — for through the holiness of Shabbos — the person truly becomes a new creation — and as our Sages of blessed memory taught: even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. And through this he can pray and receive the holiness of Shabbos with joy.

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who pray on Erev Shabbos and say Vayechulu — it is as if one became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the act of creation — for through this the aspect of the holiness of the Tzadikim is drawn upon him — regarding whom it is stated [I Chronicles 4:23]: "heima haYotzrim" — "yosh'vey Neta'im im haMelech b'melachto [they are the craftsmen — dwellers of plantings with the King in His work]" — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded. And then his eyes are in the aspect of: "eynay Hashem el haTzadikim" — and he sees clearly how far each matter reaches — and it could disrupt his Shabbos joy, heaven forfend. And therefore afterward — when the angels accompanying him rest their hands upon his head and say to him: "v'sar avonecha v'chata'ascha techupar" — as mentioned above. And this [Malachi 3:20]: "v'zarachah lachem yirey shmi — (ilu shomrey Shabbas) — shemesh Tzedakah" — that is, that a great light is opened for them — and they see everything as in the light of the sun.

But sometimes this itself is a great punishment — when a person suddenly sees the extent of his faults and sins — and as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory truly taught: the wicked are judged on it [Shabbos]. And this is what it concluded [Malachi 3:20]: "u'marpe b'chenafehah" — the aspect of: the righteous are healed through it. For through the holiness of Shabbos itself — everything is atoned — for this is the aspect of healing — as it is written [Psalms 103:3]: "haSolei'ach l'chol avonechai — haRofeh l'chol tachalu'ai [Who forgives all your iniquities — Who heals all your diseases]" — and as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And as it is written [Psalms 30:3]: "Hashem Elokai shiva'ti eilecha — vatirpa'eni" — and Rashi explained: the forgiveness of iniquities — as it is written [Isaiah 6:10]: "v'shav v'rafa lo" — for the righteous and the worthy — the guardians of Shabbos as required — are not disrupted, heaven forfend, through the greatness of the light that is opened for them through the holiness of Shabbos — until they see everything — as mentioned above. Rather — through this they are awakened to complete repentance. And through the power of the repentance and the merit of the holiness of Shabbos — everything is atoned for them — and they are healed with complete healing — for this is the aspect of: "u'marpe b'chenafehah" — as mentioned above.

 Siman 99 — סימן צט
 Va'eschanan — Force oneself to pray with concentration even on weekdays — weekday prayers are elevated by Shabbos — two Shabbosim — even dispersed and convert prayers are elevated — one must hold fast — Reb Nachman's teaching — Isaiah 58 and Isaiah 56

On Shabbos it is easier to pray with great devekus [attachment/cleaving] — as mentioned above many times. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:2]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem — v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" — that is, with wondrous and very supernal devekus. And therefore even on a weekday — when sometimes it is difficult for him to pray with devekus — nonetheless — one must force oneself with all one's powers to pray at the very least with simple sincere concentration — as is proper. And to believe that through the holiness of Shabbos — these prayers will also be elevated — and as explained in the holy Zohar. And on the contrary — if one does not force oneself on a weekday to pray with concentration — then perhaps even on Shabbos one will not merit to pray with devekus. And through the fact that one forces oneself on a weekday to pray with concentration — through this one merits on Shabbos to pray with devekus — and then all the weekday prayers also ascend.

And this is the aspect of: "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas." And also — on Shabbos itself — if one does not merit to pray with devekus in its fullness — this is presumably because one did not prepare oneself on the weekday to receive the holiness of Shabbos as required — for Shabbos requires preparation — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. Nonetheless — one must force oneself to pray with all one's powers — and to draw the holiness of Shabbos even upon the six weekdays — so that one should pray then with concentration too. And through this one merits at the very least to receive the holiness of the second Shabbos in its fullness — and one merits to pray then with true devekus. And this is the aspect of: "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos miyad nigalin" — as it is stated [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — v'chol haggid — v'havi'osim el har kodshi — v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi" — for through this prayer is completed. And this is what it concluded [Isaiah 56:8]: "ne'um Hashem mekabbetz nidchey Yisrael" — that is, that even the prayers that are dispersed [nidchim], heaven forfend, will also be elevated through the holiness of Shabbos. "Od akabbetz alav l'nikibatzav" — these are the converts — that even the prayers of the converts will also be elevated — in the aspect of [Isaiah 56:7]: "ki veisi beys tefilah yikarei l'chol ha'amim."

And therefore everyone must force himself to pray with concentration and with devekus always — in particular on the holy Shabbos itself — for at the time when prayer is completed with true devekus as required — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — then all the prayers are elevated through this — as mentioned above.

And this one can perhaps also understand in the words of our Sages of blessed memory [Tractate Shabbos 69b]: two verses are written: [Exodus 31:16]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" — and it is written [Exodus 31:13]: "es Shabsosai tishmoru." "V'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" — one guarding for each and every Shabbos. "Es Shabsosai tishmoru" — one guarding for many Shabbosim. For there is one who merits to fulfill in fullness and with great devekus an excellent guarding for each and every Shabbos. And there is one who needs to guard many Shabbosim — until he merits within them collectively to a single guarding of one Shabbos in holiness and true devekus as required. And through this — there is also an elevation and completion of all the guardings of all the Shabbosim that were not with complete devekus as required — as long as he guarded them properly in their plainness at the very least — according to the commandments of the Torah. And this is the aspect of [Isaiah 56:1]: "koh amar Hashem — shimru mishpat va'asu tzedakah — ki kerovah yeshuasi lavo — v'tzidkasi l'higalot [so says Hashem — guard justice and do righteousness — for My salvation is close to coming — and My righteousness is about to be revealed]." That is — even though for now you do not yet see through this any sprouting of the horn of salvation — do not say that the justice and righteousness that you are doing is having no effect — because it is not yet at its full perfection as required. Rather know: "ki kerovah yeshuasi lavo v'tzidkasi l'higalot" — for this is close — and a true salvation that is drawn through your justice and righteousness will appear and be revealed. And this [Isaiah 56:2]: "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos" — and so on — and Rashi explained: one who guards the Shabbos. And [Isaiah 56:2]: "u'ven adam yachazik bah — yachazik davka" — specifically — "yachazik" — like a person who holds fast to something and does not let go of it under any circumstances. Likewise — one must hold fast to the holiness of Shabbos — and likewise to all the things of holiness — and not abandon them under any circumstances — even if it seems to him that they are not yet at their fullness. In the end — everything will be elevated to its fullness — until the complete salvation sprouts through them. And this [Isaiah 56:2]: "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo" — for the essential matter is that one guards the Shabbos for now in its plainness — and does not desecrate it, heaven forfend. And this [Isaiah 56:2]: "v'shomer yado mei'asos kol ra" — that is — and likewise regarding the entire holiness of Israel's service — one must also essentially be careful not to do evil — and not to transgress any commandment, heaven forfend. And this teaching has been cited elsewhere in the name of our teacher of blessed memory — who said: "vi men tit tit — men bria men tit — kein shlechts nit [if only one does — one only acts — no evil at all]" — as mentioned above. And then — when one is strong in this — then in the end one will merit to receive the holiness of Shabbos with true devekus as required — and likewise all the commandments and all the sacred service — one will do with true fullness as required — and then everything will be elevated and come to its fullness.

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a shade and a canopy for those who fulfill commandments alongside those who labor in Torah — for what reason? — for: "ki b'tzel haChochmah — tzel haKesef" [Ecclesiastes 7:12] — and it is written [Isaiah 56:2]: "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos — u'ven adam yachazik bah" — and so on — that is — our Sages of blessed memory made known to us how G-d, blessed be He, is engaged in the rectification and the elevation of the service of each one — both through the service of oneself — when one merits to some fullness — as mentioned above. And not only that — but one person is also elevated to his fullness through the service of his fellow — for this is the aspect of: the fact that those who fulfill commandments and those of charity will have a shade and a canopy alongside those who labor in Torah — and will be elevated through them to their fullness — by virtue of the fact that they sustained them and supported their hands to engage in Torah. And this [Isaiah 56:3]: "v'al yomar ben haneychar" — and so on — "havdel yavdileni Hashem mei'al amo" — for he is far from the holiness of Israel's service — and through whom will his service also be elevated? And likewise [Isaiah 56:3]: "v'al yomar hasaris — hen ani etz yavesh" — for sometimes a person is elevated through his children — in the aspect of: "bara mezakeh abba [a son brings merit to his father]." And who greater than Avraham — of whom it is said [Isaiah 29:22]: "koh amar Hashem el beys Yaakov asher padah es Avraham" — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded on this. And therefore the saris can fall in his mind and say: since he is a dry tree and has no children — through whom will the completion of his rectification and the fullness of his elevation come? For [Isaiah 56:4]: "ki choh amar Hashem la'sarisim — asher yishmeru es Shabsosai" — that is, the aspect of the two Shabbosim mentioned above — the aspect of: a single guarding for many Shabbosim — that is, one should always be strong in the matter of the guarding of Shabbos — however it is and however it is — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 56:4]: "u'vachartu ba'asher chafatzti" — that is, at the very least — one should not abandon and let go of one's good will and choice — and should always choose that which I desire. And this [Isaiah 56:4]: "u'machzikim b'vrisi."

That is — the aspect of: "u'ven adam yachazik bah" — mentioned above — that one should hold fast to it always and not abandon it — as mentioned above. And [Isaiah 56:5]: "v'nasati lahem b'veisi u'v'chomasai — yad v'shem tov mibbanim u'mibbanos" — and so on — that is, they too will merit the ultimate fullness through their own service. And likewise [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "u'vnay haneychar" — and so on — "kol shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo — u'machzikim b'vrisi" — likewise as mentioned above. And [Isaiah 56:7]: "v'havi'osim el har kodshi" — and so on — "od akabbetz alav l'nikibatzav" — that is, they too will merit to gather themselves to holiness — and their service will ascend to its ultimate fullness — through being encompassed within the collective of Israel. And when all the dispersed of Israel are gathered — that is, all the dispersed prayers and service — and they ascend then to their fullness — then all the aspects of their prayers and service are also elevated to their ultimate fullness — as mentioned above.

 ✦ Translator's Summary — Simanim 89–99
 
 Siman 89 — Not to request one's needs on Shabbos / the King comes with great joy: Sages: do not ask for one's needs on Shabbos so one does not remember the sick in one's house. Explained: the essential prayer for one's needs on weekdays must also be only for the lack of the Shechinah — as it were. On Shabbos: even if one remembers the distress — one remembers that the essential distress is directed to the King (= Shechinah) — but the King comes with great joy and wishes to take pleasure with His beloved children in love and will and joy — so greatly He does not want them to remember His distress at all so as not to disrupt the joy. When one remembers this → great joy comes → crowned with new mental faculties → distress is sweetened → lack is filled. "Shabbas hu miliz'ok v'refu'ah kerovah lavo" = specifically through this itself: since one is not permitted to cry out — this gives certainty that healing is certainly close to come.
 Siman 91 — Faith / intellect / the sacred ascents — Avraham = mountain / Yaakov = house: Shabbos = perfection of faith. Faith → intellect → even greater faith → greater intellect. Ascent = beginning in Malchus (= emunah) → Neh"y/Chag"t/Chab"d = Holy Apple Orchard; faith completed until ascends to intellect = Chab"d. "U'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi" (Ari z"l writings). "V'zarachah lachem yirey shmi (ilu shomrey Shabbas) yirah = Malchus = emunah" — through Shabbos. "Shemesh Tzedakah" = merits the light of intellect = only as charity from G-d = "ki Hashem yiten chochmah / Atah chonein l'adam da'as." Sages: "shemesh b'Shabbas Tzedakah la'aniyim" = no poor person except one lacking in da'as → what G-d grants wisdom through Shabbos holiness = only charity and lovingkindness. "Matanah tovah / matan scharah lo avida l'galeyyei" = inner dimension of Shabbos holiness = the mochin one receives = extra soul = "v'nishmas Shadai tevinam" (Job 32:8). "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" = first Shabbos = only through faith → merits intellect; through this: greater faith and greater intellect = second Shabbos. Isaiah 56:6–7: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai / v'havi'osim el har kodshi / v'simachtim beys tefilasi." "Har" = Malchus = emunah. "Tashuri mero'sh Amanah" (Song of Songs 4:8; Rashi: from beginning of faith that you believed in Me); the mountain = "Amanah." "Beis" = wisdom and intellect = "b'chochmah yibbaneh bayis" (Proverbs 24:3). Avraham = first of believers = called a mountain (Isaiah 41:8). Yaakov = aspect of sun = intellect = called a house (Obadiah 1:18). Since on Shabbos faith spreads throughout all limbs → mitzvah to delight the body too. Shabbos delight = entirely holy. "Shechen eretz u're'eh emunah v'his'anag al Hashem" (Psalms 37:3; Sages: Shabbos delight). Eats and is nourished from faith; then comes to intellect; intellect = portion of the Divine from above = teaching "Ashrey Zar'eka" Siman 35; "haChochmah tichyeh ba'aleha" (Ecclesiastes 7:12); "vayechezu es Elokim vayochlu vayishtu" (Exodus 24:11); level above level in both faith and intellect. Siman 92 embedded: moving about = aspect of kanfey re'iyah cooling the fire; Kayin / na va'nad / city of refuge; Tikkun 13 (Aramaic: kanfey re'iyah and the voice rising to the heart and fire); Yosef and his brothers; all fully cited as noted above.
 Siman 93 — Shabbos equivalent to all Torah / Israel arose in thought / above time / Mishkan work = honest commerce: Sages: Shabbos equivalent to entire Torah and commandments. Zohar: G-d says regarding one who properly guards Shabbos: "Yisrael asher b'cha espa'ar" (Isaiah 49:3). "Yisrael alah b'machashavah" = Shabbos = world of thought = above time. "Yamim yotzaru v'lo echad bahem" = Shabbos = one = above time. "Vayevarcheihu mikol hayamim vayekadshehu mikol hazemanim." Shabbos = mochin d'gadlus = clear intellect = very good to pray. Psalm 92: "tov lehodos laHashem v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" = prayer stands at the very height of the world = above time = "elyon." "Sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah" = work of the Mishkan = honest commerce in faith (teaching "Ani Hashem" Siman 11). Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag" = mochin d'gadlus at ultimate level = Atik; "hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus (= prayer) to the mochin = pray with clear intellect; saved from subjugation of kingdoms = alien thoughts that disrupt concentration of prayer; "nachalas Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin" = entirety of Torah and commandments; Yaakov: honest commerce (Genesis 30:33; "Vayichar l'Yaakov vayarev b'Lavan") + guarded Shabbos → merited nachalah b'li metzarim = above place and above time; "Yisrael asher b'cha espa'ar / Tiferes Yisrael / Yisrael alah b'machashavah."
 Siman 94 — All worlds for Israel / sparks of speech / Zayin / Ayin Teivim in Kiddush / Psalm 92 fully mapped / Isaiah 58: All worlds created only for Israel to grant them abundant good. Essential influence through speech. Shabbos = speech = "v'daber davar." Essential influence through holiness of Shabbos (Zohar). Essential ascent of holy sparks (= sparks of letters of speech) = only through Shabbos holiness. "Olas Shabbas b'Shabato al olas haTamid" = essential fullness of their ascent to root and rest. Essential ascent of sparks = through faith and wisdom. Shabbos = aspect of Zayin = "ki sheshes yamim asah Hashem / vayanuach b'yom hashevi'i" = all are encompassed within it. "V'chol ma'asehu b'emunah" = aspect of Shabbos holiness = therefore = Zayin. Also = Yud = thought = wisdom = "ki Kodesh hi." Then: Malchus (= faith) ascends to wisdom (writings). Shabbos = aspect of eye = "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein." Aspect of the Ayin Teivim in the Kiddush. Sages: "u'mhaddar leih b'Kiddushoh d'vey shimshah" = through this elevates sparks of letters of speech in everything → makes words from them → G-d grants abundant good. "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" = faith and wisdom. "Miyad nigalin" = "v'niglah kevod Hashem" (within). Techum Shabbas alpayim amah = faith and wisdom. "Kol hamitpallel b'Erev Shabbas v'omer Vayechulu" = partner in creation = "al tikri vayechulu ela vayichlu." Immediately after: speech is like deed = "b'dvar Hashem shamayim na'asu" = since creation was through speech = sparks of letters fell → essential perfection of creation = ascent of sparks = also: grants abundant good to Israel (for whose sake creation was). Ascent of sparks begins from Erev Shabbas evening prayer (worlds ascend). Through words of faith in Vayechulu = also: 32 paths of wisdom alluded (Zohar; writings). "Vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i" = faith on Shabbos in fullness = "v'chol ma'asehu b'emunah." "Vayishbos b'yom hashevi'i" = thought = essential resting = "shevisah mimachsheves avodah." "Vayevarech" = faith = "ish emunos rav berachos." "Vayekadesh" = thought = wisdom = Kodesh. Through faith and wisdom: essential ascent of sparks and perfection of Bereishis. Full Psalm 92 mapped through sparks/faith/wisdom lens: "tov lehodos" = speak holy words → grants abundant good and lovingkindness; "lehagid baboker chasdecha" = drawing down the lovingkindnesses; "v'emunascha baleilos" = faith with wisdom = "lehagid / milah d'chochmata" → draws lovingkindnesses through ascent of letters of speech; "alay asor" = Yud = wisdom; "v'alay navel" = roshei teivos = "32 paths of wisdom" (elsewhere); "alay higgayon b'chinor" = wisdom = not labor (Sages) = "zamru maskil"; "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" = ascent of sparks of letters of Bereishis through Shabbos = "ki b'simchah tetze'u" (Isaiah 55:12; elsewhere) = "shata'aleinu b'simchah l'artzeinu / v'simcheinu b'yeshuasecha" = His salvation; "mah gadlu ma'asecha" = light of faith = "v'chol ma'asehu b'emunah"; "me'od amku machshevosecha" = thought and wisdom = elevate even sparks in Sitra d'Mausa = "me'od" is aspect of death (well-known); "ish ba'ar lo yeda / u'chesil lo yavin es zos" = neither wisdom nor faith = "zos"; "b'feroa'ch resha'im / l'hishamedam adey ad" = their ascent = ultimate degree of their downfall = "u'meshalem l'son'av el panav l'ha'avido" (Deuteronomy 7:10) = all their vitality (= holy sparks) goes out → they perish entirely; "v'atah marom l'olam Hashem" = ascent of sparks of letters of speech = "Atah" (well-known; within); "ki hinneh oyevecha / vatarem kir'em karni"; "vatabet eini b'shuray" = through the eye aspect: elevate holy sparks → draw downfall of wicked = "rak b'einecha tabbis v'shilumas resha'im tireh" (Psalms 91:8) = "nasan einav bo v'na'aseh gal shel atzamos" = through gaze alone: draws out holy sparks = his vitality gone → Siman 12 "v'sham'it malchusa v'katleih"; "b'kamim alai mere'im / Tzadik katamar yifrach" = Tzadikim united with holy sparks = through dispute and persecution: bloom and grow even more; "shetulin b'veys Hashem" = wisdom (within); "b'chatzros Elokeinu" = faith; "od yinuvun b'seivah" = as they grow older their mind settles; "lehagid ki yashar Hashem" = word of Hashem is upright = "v'chol ma'asehu b'emunah." Isaiah 58 mapped through sparks/faith/wisdom lens: "raglecha" = ascent of sacred legs with holy sparks through Shabbos; "me'asos chafatzecha" = even weekday pursuits when done properly = ascent of holy sparks; but on Shabbos: forbidden = then is essential fullness of ascent of sparks; "v'karas l'Shabbas oneg" = wisdom; "liKdosh Hashem mechubbad" = faith + "v'niglah kevod Hashem"; "v'chibadto / lo yifsa'a pis'ayah gasah" = removes one five-hundredth of light of eyes = blemishes the eye aspect of Shabbos holiness; "mimitzo / v'daber davar" = don't blemish letters of speech that ascend through Shabbos; "az tis'anag" = G-d grants abundant good to Israel = His delight = "shechen eretz u're'eh emunah v'his'anag al Hashem" (Psalms 37:3); "da Atika Kadisha" = very supernal mochin = Atik; "hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus to mochin = fullness of faith when mochin of wisdom shine upon it; saved from subjugation = sparks ascend from exile; "nachalas Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin" = connects wisdom with faith = Torah = heritage of Yaakov = "olami Yaakov vera'acha / bishvili nivra ha'olam"; nachalah b'li metzarim = can conquer entire world through gaze alone; "v'yishkon Yisrael betach badad eyin Yaakov — eyin davka"; "ki pi Hashem diber" = holy sparks = letters of speech = ascend and unify with G-d = "ki pi Hashem diber."
 Siman 95 — Moshe's anger = forgetting Shabbos / mah / Ra'u = Ayin = 130 = shem mah: Moshe: "v'nachnu mah ki taluinu aleinu" = since we hold the aspect of mah = why do you murmur against us? Midrash Rabbah Beshalach: Moshe came to anger over the leftover manna → forgot to warn them regarding Shabbos → "ad anah me'anem" = included together with them. Shabbos = world of thought. Sha'arey Tziyon and writings: to purify thought = have in mind the Name Mah five times in reverse arrangement; "machashavah / chashav mah." Through anger = removal of mah → forgot Shabbos warning → peh remained → "ad anah." "Shvu ish tachtav" = humility = aspect of mah. "Re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas re'u davka" = "ayin" [the letter Ayin] = gematria = 130 = Name Mah in reverse arrangement (writings). "Ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas" = world of thought = therefore gives you bread for two days = so thought should not be preoccupied with livelihood. "Shvu ish tachtav" = humility = mah = upon which depends essential holiness of thought and wisdom = "v'haChochmah mei'ayin timatzei" (Job 28:12; elsewhere); "chochmah" = letters of "ko'ach mah." "Al yetzei ish mimekomo" = through this does not go out from one's place and level = does not come to humiliations.
 Siman 96 (first — Zomem Rasha l'Tzadik) — Shabbos = world of thought / alien thoughts / when above one's level = breaks the wicked: Shabbos = world of thought = essential time of ascent of sparks = "kulhon b'machshavah is'barirun." Very good to pray without alien thoughts; even if alien thought comes = easier to elevate on Shabbos. "Ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" = no joy like resolution of doubts (Tur"z OC 554); even though "melo chol ha'aretz kevodo / certainly holy sparks even in alien thought" → since difficult to elevate = distress; but on Shabbos: easier to elevate = joy = "kol po'el Hashem lama'anehu." When alien thought is from above one's level = difficult; but through the will to break it and elevate it = breaks power of the wicked and the disputants who dispute against a Tzadik (from whom the alien thought comes). "Mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem me'od amku machshevosecha" = sometimes alien thought even on Shabbos = difficult to fix = above one's level. "Ish ba'ar lo yeda / u'chesil lo yavin es zos" = why does this alien thought come from above one's level? But through this = downfall of wicked and disputants who dispute against Tzadikim is drawn. Psalm 92:8–11 cited. Or perhaps: alien thoughts from Nogah (= mixed good and evil) = must elevate the good; thoughts from three completely impure husks = must nullify and repel entirely. Also on weekdays and on Erev Shabbas: ascent of worlds and sparks → good in Nogah ascends → completely impure husks also wish to ascend → shalhava d'asha descends and scorches them → these cannot be elevated = only arouse sacred fire through ardor (hitlahavus) in prayer → they perish spontaneously = "eish lefanav teilech / v'tela'het saviv tzarav" (Psalms 97:3); "k'himos donag mipney eish yovedu resha'im" (Psalms 68:3). Also within "b'feroa'ch resha'im k'mo esev" = they also wish to ascend but it is for their destruction. "Yispardu kol po'aley aven / vatarem kir'em karni" = raising of holiness; all explained in the kavannos.
 Siman 96 (second — Elokim al d'mi Lach) — Humility = Tzadik rules through prayer / ten utterances = lovingkindness / Dalet becomes Heh: Shabbos = humility and lowliness = awe = Malchus = rectification of alien thoughts. Therefore: prayer reaches its fullness = merits aspect of Tzadik ruling through his prayer. Midrash Rabbah Parashas Beshalach: one who guards and delights the Shabbos merits "v'tigzor omer v'yakum lach" (Job 22:28) = all the desires of his heart. "Ki az al Shadai tis'anag / ta'atir eilav v'yishma'echa / v'tigzor omer v'yakum lach" (Job 22:26–28) = this itself is His delight, blessed be He — when there are Tzadikim who pray this way = for their sake was the entire creation = G-d renews act of creation and changes nature through their prayer. All of this flows on Shabbos = Shabbos = ultimate purpose of heaven and earth = sof ma'aseh b'machshavah techilah. Ten utterances shine even more on Shabbos (Genesis 2:2; ten utterances = aspect of lovingkindness) = great lovingkindnesses drawn on Shabbos. Through this: Dalet becomes Heh = rectification completed in fullness through Shabbos holiness (Tikunim) → bounty flows = Shabbos = root of all influences. "Az tis'anag al Hashem" = merits to enter into the aspect of His delight = from which he too receives all desires of his heart. "Hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus (= prayer); saved from subjugation = saved from arrogance and alien thoughts = subjugation of kingdoms; "nachalas Yaakov" = humility and awe = "ekev anavah yiras Hashem" (Proverbs 22:4) → prayer completed → rules through prayer → changes nature → nachalah b'li metzarim → "bishvili nivra ha'olam"; "olami Yaakov vera'acha"; "ki pi Hashem diber" = his speech = word of Hashem = draws renewal of Bereishis = "b'dvar Hashem shamayim na'asu" + great lovingkindnesses and abundant bounty = "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem" (Deuteronomy 15:6).
 Siman 98 — Shabbos = Tzadik = eyes / examines one's deeds / new soul / shemesh Tzedakah u'marpe: Shabbos = Tzadik (Zohar) = all Israel who guard Shabbos are called Tzadikim. Shabbos = eyes = "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" = "eynay Hashem el haTzadikim" (Psalms 34:16). "Re'u ki Hashem nasan lachem haShabbas re'u davka" (elsewhere). Then: propitious to examine one's deeds and contemplate one's ways = eyes opened = sees what was hidden + sees how far each blemish reaches → does teshuvah. Shabbos = teshuvah (elsewhere). Also = "keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" = sees extent of loss of his soul during weekday → does teshuvah → merits extra soul. But: great benefit = but through the fact that eyes are opened and sees the full extent of his faults → this could disrupt Shabbos holiness since one must receive Shabbos with joy (elsewhere). But through the fact that he immediately merits extra soul and new higher-soul = Zohar (Aramaic): "v'chulhon mis'aterin b'nishmatin chadtin k'din hu shirusa d'tzlosa l'varacha lah b'chedva b'nehiru d'anpin." Through Shabbos holiness: becomes truly a new creation. Sages: even if worshipped idolatry / mochalin lo. Through this = can pray and receive Shabbos with joy. "Kol hamitpallel b'Erev Shabbas v'omer Vayechulu" = holiness of Tzadikim drawn upon him = "heima haYotzrim yosh'vey Neta'im im haMelech b'melachto" (I Chronicles 4:23; Sages). His eyes = "eynay Hashem el haTzadikim" = sees clearly how far things reach = could disrupt Shabbos joy. Therefore the angels rest their hands upon his head and say "v'sar avonecha v'chata'ascha techupar." "V'zarachah lachem yirey shmi (ilu shomrey Shabbas) shemesh Tzedakah" = great light opened = sees everything as in the light of the sun. But sometimes: sudden seeing of one's faults = great punishment; therefore Sages: wicked are judged on Shabbos. "U'marpe b'chenafehah" = the righteous are healed through it = Shabbos itself atones for everything = aspect of healing = "haSolei'ach l'chol avonechai haRofeh l'chol tachalu'ai" (Psalms 103:3; Sages); "Hashem Elokai shiva'ti eilecha vatirpa'eni" (Psalms 30:3; Rashi: forgiveness of iniquities = "v'shav v'rafa lo" Isaiah 6:10). Righteous and worthy = not disrupted through the greatness of the light → awakened to complete teshuvah → through power of teshuvah and merit of Shabbos = everything atoned = healed with complete healing = "u'marpe b'chenafehah."
 Siman 99 — Force oneself to pray even on weekdays / Shabbos elevates all prayers / two Shabbosim / hold fast / Reb Nachman's teaching in Yiddish / Isaiah 56: On Shabbos easier to pray with great devekus. Even on weekdays = force oneself with all powers to pray at least with simple sincere concentration = to believe: through Shabbos holiness these weekday prayers will also be elevated (Zohar). If one does not force oneself on weekdays → perhaps will not merit to pray with devekus even on Shabbos. "Zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas." Even on Shabbos itself: if one cannot pray with devekus in fullness = presumably did not prepare oneself properly on weekdays (Sages: Shabbos requires preparation). Nonetheless: force oneself to pray with all powers and draw Shabbos holiness upon the six weekdays → merit at least second Shabbos in fullness → pray with true devekus. "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos miyad nigalin" = Isaiah 56:6–7: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai / v'havi'osim el har kodshi / v'simachtim beys tefilasi" → prayer completed. "Ne'um Hashem mekabbetz nidchey Yisrael" = even dispersed prayers will also be elevated through Shabbos holiness. "Od akabbetz alav l'nikibatzav" = converts = even convert prayers elevated = "ki veisi beys tefilah yikarei l'chol ha'amim." All must force themselves to pray with concentration and devekus always — especially on the holy Shabbos — for when prayer is completed with true devekus = all the prayers are elevated. Shabbos 69b: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" = one guarding for each and every Shabbos; "es Shabsosai tishmoru" = one guarding for many Shabbosim. There is one who merits excellent guarding for each Shabbos; and there is one who needs to guard many Shabbosim until within them collectively merits a single guarding of one Shabbos with holiness and true devekus. Isaiah 56:1: "koh amar Hashem / shimru mishpat va'asu tzedakah / ki kerovah yeshuasi lavo v'tzidkasi l'higalot." Isaiah 56:2: "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos" (Rashi: guards Shabbos). "U'ven adam yachazik bah — yachazik davka" = holds fast and does not let go under any circumstances. "Shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo" = guards the Shabbos in its plainness and does not desecrate it. "V'shomer yado mei'asos kol ra" = must essentially be careful not to do evil and not transgress any commandment. Reb Nachman's teaching: "vi men tit tit — men bria men tit — kein shlechts nit" (Yiddish). Isaiah 56: full mapping of ben haneychar / hasaris / saris / two Shabbosim / "u'ven adam yachazik bah" / "u'vnay haneychar / kol shomer Shabbas / v'havi'osim / od akabbetz alav l'nikibatzav" = they too will merit to gather to holiness = encompassed within collective of Israel = when all dispersed prayers gather and ascend to their fullness = all their aspects of prayer also elevated to ultimate fullness.
