 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 102 — סימן קב
 Atah Tihyeh — Shabbos = awe — awe comes from above automatically — but must also be aroused — two kinds of awe = two Shabbosim — hi mesurah b'yadchem — Isaiah 58

Shabbos is the aspect of awe — the aspect of: "yirey Shabbas" — as is well-known and as mentioned above many times. And then the awe comes to the person automatically from above through the light of the holiness of Shabbos — which is established and enduring. But nonetheless — the person must guard it — so that it should not be lost through inattention and forgetting and averting one's eyes — as is well-known. For the person is a being of free choice. But the essential matter is to arouse upon oneself the supernal awe [yirah ila'ah] on the holy Shabbos — for this is the essential perfection of awe — the aspect of: "Tzadik moshel yiras Elokim [a righteous person rules — the awe of G-d]" — as explained within.

And this [Exodus 31:14]: "u'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi lachem" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded [Tractate Yoma 85b]: "hi mesurah b'yadchem — v'lo atem mesurim b'yadah [it is handed over to your hands — and you are not handed over to its hands]" — that is — for the awe that comes from above automatically — it rules over the person and he is handed over to it — for it reaches him whenever it wishes.

And the essential matter is that the person himself should arouse and draw upon himself the awe — which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — in the aspect of: "Tzadik moshel yiras Elokim" — as mentioned above — for this is the aspect of: "hi mesurah b'yadchem — v'lo atem mesurim b'yadah" — as mentioned above. And this likewise [Exodus 31:16]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" — and so on — "la'asos [to do]" — specifically — to make for oneself the awe — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of: "ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" — that is, the two kinds of awe — specifically. For even the first awe requires guarding — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of: "es Shabsosai tishmoru" — two Shabbosim — as mentioned above. And therefore the essential perfection of prayer and the drawing down of the abundant bounty to Israel and the revelation of His kingship, blessed be He, and the subjugation of the husks beneath holiness — all of this flows in its fullness through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: they give him all the desires of his heart — that is, one merits the perfection of prayer — and one can arouse the bounty in the world through one's prayer. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — as it is stated: "v'atah al bamosemo tidroch" — that is, the husks are subdued beneath the feet of holiness. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of awe — the aspect of: "b'yir'ascha b'zechus Yaakov [in your awe — through the merit of Yaakov]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for Shabbos is the aspect of the revelation of sacred speech — as mentioned above. And from there awe is revealed — in the aspect of [Isaiah 66:2]: "u'midbaryecha pachad libbi [and from Your speech my heart trembles]" — and it is written [Jeremiah 10:7]: "hayirei devar Hashem [those who fear the word of Hashem]." And also — through awe — speech is completed — so that one will be able to draw bounty — in the aspect of: "kol mi she'yesh bo yiras Shamayim — devarav nishma'in [all who have awe of Heaven — their words are heeded]" — as explained within. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for through awe — one's words are in the aspect of the word of Hashem — and draw bounty — in the aspect of [Deuteronomy 15:6]: "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem."

 Siman 103 — סימן קג
 Uzi v'Zimras — Shabbos = teshuvah = Torah = sparks gather — Da'as = compassion = yecholah hi shetaracheim — two Shabbosim = simple compassion arouses great compassion = G-d's own prayer — Isaiah 58

Shabbos is the aspect of repentance — as mentioned above many times — and the essential repentance depends on the Torah — as explained within. And all agree that on Shabbos the Torah was given — and then is the essential time of Torah novellae — as mentioned above many times. And through this — the letters and the sparks that were scattered through him are gathered. And this is the aspect of the full ascent of the sparks — that ascend through the holiness of Shabbos — as is well-known.

And also — through the holiness of Shabbos — Da'as is completed — for this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" — and through this compassion [rachmanus] is awakened — for this is the aspect of: "yecholah hi shetaracheim [she can show compassion]" — stated regarding the holy Shabbos — (and as brought below within in Siman 119). And likewise [Psalms 119:156]: "rachamecha rabbim" — and so on. And through this one also merits to draw the aspect of great compassion through the prayer of G-d, blessed be He, Himself — as it were. And then one merits complete salvation — as explained within. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught: had Israel guarded two Shabbosim — they would have been immediately redeemed — as it is stated [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — v'chol haggid — v'havi'osim el har kodshi — v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi" — as mentioned above. For Shabbos is the aspect of compassion — the aspect of: "yecholah hi shetaracheim" — as mentioned above.

And when one merits to guard two Shabbosim — that is, the aspect of the lower Shabbos and the upper Shabbos — that is, one merits that simple compassion [rachamim peshutim] awakens the great compassion [rachamim gedolim] — for this is the aspect of the prayer of G-d, blessed be He, Himself. Then complete salvation comes — and one merits eternal redemption. And this is the aspect of: "v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi" — for this is the aspect of the prayer of Hashem, blessed be He — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded — and as also brought within.

And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:16]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" — that is, the plain Shabbos — the aspect of simple compassion. And this [Exodus 31:16]: "la'asos es haShabbas" — that is, to arouse through this the upper Shabbos — which is the aspect of great compassion. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Shabbos 12]: one who enters to visit the sick person says: "Shabbas hi miliz'ok — v'refu'ah kerovah lavo" — that is, during the weekday one must cry out in order to at least arouse the simple compassion. And on Shabbos there is no need for this — for through the holiness of Shabbos itself compassion is awakened — and therefore healing is close to come. And Rabbi Meir says: "yecholah hi shetaracheim" — that is, he explains further the matter of the awakening of compassion through the holiness of Shabbos. Rabbi Yehudah says: "haMakom yerachem alecha v'al cholei Yisrael [may the Omnipresent have compassion upon you and upon all the sick of Israel]." Rabbi Yosei says: "haMakom yerachem alecha b'soch cholei Yisrael [may the Omnipresent have compassion upon you among the sick of Israel]" — (Rashi's explanation: so that his prayer should be heeded in their merit). Shevna the Jerusalemite — and so on — says: "Shabbas hi miliz'ok — v'refu'ah kerovah lavo" — as mentioned above. And: "v'rachamav meru'bim — v'Shabbato b'shalom [and His compassions are many — and his Shabbos shall be in peace]" — that is — for even if the healing cannot come through the aspect of simple compassion — there is by Him, blessed be He, the aspect of great compassion — which is likewise awakened through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above — for this is the aspect of: "v'rachamav meru'bim" — and through this healing will certainly come.

And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — that is, one merits to draw the aspect of great compassion — which is the aspect of Atik — as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory expounded from this: they give him all the desires of his heart — for through this aspect of compassion — they can certainly fulfill all his desires. And as elaborated in Likutay Halachos, Halachos Techum Shabbas. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" — the ascent of Malchus to the mental faculties. And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, the sparks and the letters that are in the aspect of Malchus — that were scattered in exile to wherever they were scattered — now they are gathered and ascend through the holiness of Shabbos — until one merits through this to complete Da'as — for this is the aspect of ascending to the mental faculties. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — the aspect of the holy Torah — as is well-known. And likewise — the simple compassion — which is the aspect of the compassion of Ze'ir Anpin — through which the great compassion is also drawn — through the simple compassion praying for and awakening the great compassion. For this is the aspect of the prayer of G-d, blessed be He, Himself — as mentioned above. And this is what it concluded [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — that is, one merits through this to awaken the prayer of G-d, blessed be He, Himself — so that He, blessed be He, Himself, as it were, prays and speaks — to arouse the aspect of great compassion — which is the aspect of the compassion of Atik — as mentioned above.

 Siman 109 — סימן קט
 Yesh Hevel — Sacred havalim [breaths/vapors] go forth on the holy Shabbos — repentance before Shabbos — attach to the sacred chevel — on Shabbos: be joyful and forget all physical lack and sorrow

It is explained above regarding the matter of the sacred havalim [breaths/vapors] that go forth on the holy Shabbos — and it is also already known regarding the matter of the extra soul and the new higher-soul that each person of Israel merits to receive on every Shabbos — according to the level of each and every one. And according to what is explained within — it is understood by itself that it is proper to reflect much in repentance on every Erev Shabbos — and to sigh from the depths of one's heart over all one's deeds and matters that are not fitting — that passed during all the six days of deed. And through this — it is easier for him to separate himself from the chevel [cord/rope] of impurity — to which he was bound through the havalim [vapors] of the Sitra Achra — the empty vanities [Jeremiah 10:15]: "hevel heima ma'aseh ta'tu'im" — that passed upon him, heaven forfend, during the six days of deed. And now he binds and cleaves himself to the sacred chevel — which is the sacred havalim of Shabbos. And then he truly becomes a new creation entirely — in body and soul — as understood within. And likewise — it is understood from this — how one must be careful on Shabbos to be joyful — and to completely forget all one's toil and sorrow and all one's physical lacks. For if he remembers these things and sighs over his physical needs on the holy Shabbos — he can blemish through this the holiness of Shabbos. For through this the connection to the spirituality of the holiness of Shabbos is somewhat broken — and he becomes bound to the physical, heaven forfend. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: one should be on Shabbos as if all his work is done. And also they taught: it is forbidden to request one's needs on Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of Shabbos — named for [Isaiah 21:2]: "kol anachosah hishbati [all its sighing I have caused to cease]" — for all kinds of sighs and physical worries cease and are nullified — for then one is attached only to spirituality and in great joy. For one must receive the holiness of Shabbos with joy and a good heart — as explained elsewhere — for even the awe of Shabbos must be with great joy — and as mentioned above many times.

 Siman 115 — סימן קטו
 Vaya'amod haAm — Obstacles on Erev Shabbos — shalhava d'asha — blowing the shofar — G-d hides Himself within the obstacles — pikuach nefesh — hi mesurah b'yadchem — all obstacles are only for drawing close — Psalm 92 — Isaiah 58

See Zohar Emor, folio 99. There the matter of the arousal of the judgment of Rosh haShana is explained: "santeira atei l'mitva dinah — begin ki Ani Hashem ohev mishpat" — and so on — but because the love of Israel prevails over the love of justice — therefore G-d, blessed be He, commanded to blow the shofar in order to arouse compassion — and so on. And it is explained within: this is the matter of the fact that when a person wants to draw himself close to G-d, blessed be He, — obstacles [meni'os] are arranged for him. This is because of the accusation of the attribute of Justice — for: "Ani Hashem ohev mishpat" — and as mentioned above. But because the love of Israel prevails over the love of justice — therefore G-d, blessed be He, hides Himself — as it were — within the obstacles — until through this itself one is able to draw close. For through Da'as one can find Him, blessed be He, Who is hidden within the obstacles themselves. And perhaps this was the matter of the tekiyos [shofar blasts] that they would blow on every Erev Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Shabbos 35b]. And also today — one must announce — and so on — and this is in place of the tekiyos — as explained in Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 256. For because the holiness of Shabbos is a very great and awesome and very spiritual thing — and Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah — and during all the weekdays the person goes mostly in physicality and is preoccupied with doing his pursuits — and now when one must enter the spirituality of the holiness of Shabbos — the ba'al devar [adversary] lies in wait for him greatly — to arrange for him many obstacles and preoccupations — to confuse him from the spirituality of the holiness of Shabbos — or to bring him, heaven forfend, to an actual desecration of Shabbos. Therefore our Sages of blessed memory instituted to blow the shofar — to arouse compassion and to sweeten all the accusations — spiritually. And also physically — to remind each person to remove from himself all the preoccupations and obstacles — and to receive the holiness of Shabbos. And perhaps this is likewise the secret of the shalhava d'asha that descends on Erev Shabbos — to subdue the husks so that they should not ascend — for also they wish to ascend then — as explained in the writings. And they wish to ascend and draw sustenance from the holiness — only to confuse the holiness of Shabbos. For their entire intention is only for evil — and from this come all the obstacles and preoccupations and irritations that are common on Erev Shabbos — only — because G-d, blessed be He, loves Israel — therefore the shalhava d'asha descends and subdues them.

And this [Song of Songs 8:6]: "simeni kachotam al libbecha" — and so on — "ki azzah k'maves ahavah — kashah kish'ol kinah [for love is as strong as death — jealousy is as hard as the grave]." For the jealousy and the accusations intensify greatly — and from this come many obstacles. "Reshafehah reshefey eish — shalheves Yah" — that is, through the aspect of the shalhava d'asha mentioned above — which is aroused through the mental faculties of the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of: "shalheves Yah" — as explained in the writings. Through this: "mayim rabbim lo yuchlu l'chabes es ha'ahavah" — and so on. "Ani chomah [I am a wall]" — to break through all the obstacles — "az hayisi b'einav k'motzeis shalom [then I was in his eyes as one who finds peace]."

For in truth — G-d, blessed be He, desires greatly the love of Israel and their drawing close to Him. And even the obstacles themselves are likewise only for the sake of drawing close. But nonetheless — many are prevented and truly distanced through this. And then He, blessed be He, has sorrow from this — as it were. But when one merits to break the obstacles — one thereby causes G-d, blessed be He, great delight — and then G-d, blessed be He, draws one close and cherishes one with wondrous love and true closeness. And through the fact that one broke the obstacles that were arranged for him — only because of the accusations that were against him from his earlier deeds that were not fitting — therefore through this itself all the aforementioned faults are rectified — and all the husks and reverse-sides that were formed through them are nullified — heaven have mercy — as is well-known. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "ach es Shabsosai tishmoru." It is known that "ach" and "raq" are diminutive expressions [miy'utim] — this is the aspect of obstacles — that wish to diminish and minimize the person from the holiness of Shabbos — and the person must be awakened specifically through this — to break the obstacles and receive the holiness of Shabbos in its fullness. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory truly expounded from this [Tractate Yoma 85]: that the preservation of life [pikuach nefesh] overrides Shabbos — as it is stated: "es Shabsosai tishmoru" — one might think: for everything. The Torah therefore teaches: "ach" — dividing it. It follows that there is sometimes something that is a true obstacle to the holiness of Shabbos — such as the preservation of life — which overrides Shabbos. But in truth — from this itself we see: no obstacle comes for the sake of distancing, heaven forbid. Only because of the love of justice one is compelled that some obstacle should arise for him. But in truth the love of Israel prevails over the love of justice — so greatly — that G-d, blessed be He, Himself, as it were, hides Himself within the obstacle — so that he can break it — as mentioned above.

And from this itself we see: that the holiness of Shabbos is handed over to our hands [mesurah b'yadeinu]. That is — even if obstacles arise for this — if they are not a matter of the preservation of life — one should know that he certainly has the power to break them and receive the holiness of Shabbos in its fullness — for it is handed over to our hands. And this is what they further expounded there [Exodus 31:16]: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" — and so on — the Torah said: desecrate one Shabbos for him so that he may guard many Shabbosim — that is — for from this teaching it is even more clearly evident: that G-d, blessed be He, Himself dresses Himself and hides Himself within the obstacle. For behold — we see that even the preservation of life — which is a true obstacle to the holiness of Shabbos — for it overrides Shabbos — nonetheless — even within this itself the holiness of Shabbos is clothed — until this desecration of Shabbos is counted as truly a guarding of Shabbos. For this is the aspect of: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" — the Torah said: desecrate one Shabbos for him so that he may guard many Shabbosim.

It follows that within this desecration of Shabbos — the holiness of Shabbos guarding is clothed. For it is only so that he may guard many Shabbosim — and for this sake the desecration itself is also counted as a guarding of Shabbos. For this is the aspect of: "v'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" — as mentioned above. And this is what they further expounded there: "v'chai bahem — v'lo sheyamus bahem" — and it concludes there that this teaching is superior to all of them — for it is proven from it that even a doubtful case of the preservation of life overrides all the commandments. And from this we see the love of G-d, blessed be He, for the souls of Israel — and it is understood from this by itself: that all obstacles are only for the sake of drawing close — as mentioned above.

And this is the aspect of מ'זמור ש'יר ל'יום ה'שבת — initial letters — למש"ה — for the Da'as — for on Shabbos the Da'as of the aspect of Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, shines in the heart of each person of Israel. And then one sees that all the obstacles are as nothing — and G-d, blessed be He, Himself is dressed and hidden within them. And this [Psalms 92:2–3]: "tov lehodos laHashem" — and so on — "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — that is, in times of goodness — when the obstacles do not intensify so greatly — one must certainly give thanks to Hashem and declare His lovingkindnesses, blessed be He. And [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — that is, even in the time of the intensification of the darkness and the troubles and the obstacles — heaven have mercy — one must also be firm in faith in Him, blessed be He — and serve Him, blessed be He, with joy and diligence — in the aspect of [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor v'alay navel" — and so on — "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" — and so on. [Psalms 92:6–8]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem" — which are in the aspect of: "ma'asey yadav emes u'mishpat" — for this reason the obstacles are arranged for the person — for G-d, blessed be He, loves justice greatly. "Me'od amku machshevosecha" — for even so — the love of Israel who arose in the beginning of thought is even greater and more exceedingly so — for His thoughts, blessed be He, are very deep — and He dresses and hides Himself within the obstacle — so that one can break it — and then the obstacles become a great good for him — for through this all his faults are rectified — and all the Sitra Achra that was formed through them is nullified — as mentioned above. And this [Psalms 92:7–8]: "ish ba'ar lo yeda" — and so on — "b'feroa'ch resha'im" — and so on — that is, the success of the wicked and those who obstruct — it is only for their destruction forever. For when one merits to break the obstacles — then they perish and are lost by themselves — in the aspect of [Psalms 92:10]: "ki hinneh oyevecha Hashem" — for the enemies of Israel who wish to prevent them from the holiness of Israel — they are literally the enemies of G-d — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And therefore [Psalms 92:10]: "ki hinneh oyevecha yovadu" — and so on — [Psalms 92:11]: "vatarem kir'em karni" — and so on. And this likewise [Psalms 93:3–4]: "nasa'u neharos Hashem" — and so on — that is, the intensification of the obstacles through those who obstruct. [Psalms 93:4]: "mikol mayim rabbim addirim" — and so on — [Psalms 93:4]: "addir bamarom Hashem" — for His hand, blessed be He, is always on top — and certainly all obstacles will be nullified — and all of Israel will merit their good ultimate purpose.

And this [Isaiah 58:13–14]: "im tashiv miShabbos" — and so on — "az tis'anag al Hashem" — the aspect of love in delights — for the love of G-d, blessed be He, for Israel will be revealed to him — so greatly — that He Himself, blessed be He, is dressed and hidden within all the obstacles. And then he too will delight in Hashem — great love in delights. And all of this through the illumination of the Da'as of the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — from which is the essential delight — as mentioned above many times. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — from whom come all the obstacles — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "retzioni la'asos retzoncha — ela she'or she'ba'isah — v'shibbud malchiyos me'akev [My desire is to do Your desire — but the leaven in the dough — and the subjugation of the kingdoms — prevents me]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — in the aspect of: "melo chol ha'aretz kevodo [the whole earth is full of His honor]" — for one sees that G-d's divinity and honor, blessed be He, is dressed in every place — in the aspect of [Exodus 20:21]: "el ha'arafel asher sham ha'Elokim" — as explained within.

 Siman 116 — סימן קטז
 haNoten Tzedakah — Shabbos = great compassion and illumination of Da'as = saved from sin — for no person sins unless a spirit of foolishness enters him

It is explained above many times regarding the greatness of the compassion and the illumination of Da'as that shines on Shabbos. And through this one is saved from sins. For no person transgresses a sin unless a spirit of foolishness [ru'ach shtus] enters him. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — they are distant from sin — as it is stated [Isaiah 56:2]: "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo — v'shomer yado mei'asos kol ra" — as mentioned above.

 Siman 129 — סימן קכט
 Eretz Ocheles — Shabbos = faith — attachment to Shabbos = transformed into its very holiness — body becomes like the soul — delight of Shabbos = transformation — eretz Yisrael — Isaiah 58 — Yaakov / Yivkeh / nachalah b'li metzarim

Shabbos is the aspect of faith — as mentioned above many times. And it is also the aspect of mental faculties and Da'as. And therefore when one merits to truly connect oneself to the holiness of Shabbos with complete and sincere faith — then one is transformed into the very substance of its holiness. And therefore — all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. And likewise — all who delight the Shabbos are forgiven all their sins — for one is transformed into the very substance of its holiness. And therefore it is explained in the holy Zohar: "hai yoma — yoma d'nishmatin hu — v'lo yoma d'gufa" — and so on — for then the body is also transformed into the substance of the holy soul — which is the mind and the Da'as. And this is the aspect of the commandment of the delight of Shabbos. For then even the physical pleasures are precious and very holy. And this [Psalms 37:3]: "shechen eretz u're'eh emunah" — which is the aspect of the holiness of the holy Shabbos — which is the aspect of Eretz Yisrael — and the fullness of faith — as mentioned above. Through this [Psalms 37:4]: "v'his'anag al Hashem" — and so on — for then even all his pleasures are entirely holy. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory also taught: all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — they are distant from sin. For one is transformed into the very substance of its holiness. And this [Isaiah 56:2]: "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos" — (Rashi explained: one who guards the Shabbos — and so on) — "u'ven adam yachazik bah — yachazik bah davka" — that is, one should hold fast and connect oneself properly to the holiness of Shabbos with complete faith. Then — "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo" — (and through this) — "v'shomer yado mei'asos kol ra" — that is, one is distanced from sin — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded. And this [Isaiah 56:3]: "v'al yomar ben haneychar" — and so on — "havdel yavdileni Hashem mei'al amo" — for he was not born into the holiness of Israel — therefore it is not possible for me to be transformed into the very substance of holiness — for I am not in the aspect of the good food that is transformed into the one who consumes it — and as explained within. And likewise [Isaiah 56:3]: "v'al yomar hasaris — hen ani etz yavesh" — for faith is the aspect of the power of growth and the power of sprouting — in the aspect of: "emunah zeh Seder Zera'im [faith — this is the Order of Seeds]" — and as explained elsewhere. And therefore since I am a dry tree and do not produce fruit — certainly I am far from the fullness of faith — and it is not possible for me to be transformed into the very substance of its holiness. For [Isaiah 56:4]: "ki choh amar Hashem la'sarisim — asher yishmeru es Shabsosai — v'nasati lahem" — and so on — "shem tov mibbanim u'mibbanos."

And likewise [Isaiah 56:6–7]: "u'vnay haneychar" — and so on — "kol shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo — u'machzikim b'vrisi" — that is, they desire and wish greatly for the attachment to holiness. And [Isaiah 56:7]: "v'havi'osim el har kodshi" — and so on. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and so on — and it considers there all the matters one must be careful of regarding the holiness of Shabbos — in deed and in speech and in walking — and so on. And then one is truly connected to the holiness of Shabbos. [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that is, one merits the aspect of: "v'his'anag al Hashem" — mentioned above. And therefore — he decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills — and they give him all the desires of his heart. For he becomes a single unity with His holiness, blessed be He, as it were.

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms.

For since his body and physicality were transformed into the substance of the holy soul — for this is the aspect of: "leichol es besari [to eat my flesh]" — as explained within — through this: his enemies and adversaries stumble and fall — as explained above within in Siman 101. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — that is, one merits in fullness the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — which has this power to transform whoever dwells in it into its very holiness — as explained within. And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits. For since one leaves bodily existence and physicality — until the body is also transformed into the substance of the holy soul — then one is entirely spiritual — and spirituality is the aspect of an inheritance without limits — without any boundary at all.

 Siman 135 — סימן קלה
 Ki Ekach Mo'ed — Shabbos = first of the holy convocations = Moshe = all gates of Binah open — true humility — drawing close to Tzadikim — receiving the face of one's teacher — love = attachment — extra soul — the three Festivals flow from Shabbos

Shabbos is the first of the holy convocations — and it is the aspect of Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him — as mentioned above many times. And then all the gates of Binah are opened — as explained in the holy Zohar. And then one merits to true humility — for this is the aspect of [Exodus 16:29]: "shvu ish tachtav" — as mentioned above in Siman 79.

And then is the essential time of drawing close to the Tzadikim. For through the holiness of Shabbos — one merits to feel even more the light of the Tzadik. And likewise — through the light of the Tzadik — one merits to receive the holiness of Shabbos even more. And therefore it is a commandment to receive the face of one's teacher on Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar and in the writings. For then the Tzadik merits to receive mochin d'gadlus at an exceedingly lofty level — and the nature of smallness is to nullify itself before greatness. And therefore one nullifies oneself greatly before the holiness of the Tzadik and the holiness of the holy Shabbos — until one can be transformed into the very substance of their holiness truly. And this [Exodus 31:14]: "u'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi lachem." And likewise [Exodus 35:2]: "u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh — lachem davka [and on the seventh day it shall be holy for you — for you — specifically]" — that is, its holiness is drawn upon you literally. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 31:13]: "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem." And the essential attachment is love — in the aspect of [I Samuel 18:1]: "v'nefesh Yehonatan nikeshrah b'nefesh David [and the soul of Yehonatan was bound to the soul of David]." And therefore — through the attachment by which one binds one's soul to the holiness of Shabbos — which is the root of all the souls — as mentioned above many times — through this itself one merits to receive the extra soul of Shabbos. And this is the aspect of [Song of Songs 7:7]: "mah yafis u'mah na'amt — ahavah b'ta'anugim" — for the delight of Shabbos must be with great love for the holiness of Shabbos. And this love will be greater than the love of women — for this is the aspect of [Isaiah 56:4]: "la'sarisim asher yishmeru es Shabsosai" — who wait for their union for the holiness of the holy Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar. And also — through the holiness of Shabbos the sacred Kingship ascends from the exile of the four kingdoms — for this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms. And then is the essential subjugation of the kingdom of Amalek — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "b'yom hashevi'i yatze'u min ha'am lilkot — miyad vayavo Amalek" [Exodus 16:27]. For Shabbos is the aspect of repentance and the aspect of awe — as mentioned above many times — and this is the aspect of the rectification and ascent of Malchus. And therefore all the holiness of the three Festivals — in which they engage in the rectification of Malchus — as explained within — all of it flows from the holiness of Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: G-d, blessed be He, said to them: if you guard the Shabbos — I shall give you the Festivals — and so on.

 Siman 143 — סימן קמג
 Inyan Kabbalas Pnei Talmid Chacham — Receiving the face of the Torah scholar — berchu b'me'or panav shel adam — panim b'fanim diber Hashem imachem — nullification of arrogance and covetousness of money

Our Sages of blessed memory taught [Genesis 2:3]: "vayevarech Elokim es yom hashevi'i" — "berchu b'me'or panav shel adam" — and so on. And therefore it is explained in the holy Zohar and in the writings that a person must receive the face of his teacher on Shabbos. For since everyone then has a shining face [anpin nehirin] — through this one can receive a face — that is, to receive upon one's face the very light of the teacher's face — until the teacher's face is visible upon his face. For this is the aspect of [Deuteronomy 5:4]: "panim b'fanim diber Hashem imachem [face to face Hashem spoke with you]" — which was likewise on Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And also — on Shabbos there is drawn the aspect of the nullification of the lust for money [bitul ta'aves mamon]. And also the aspect of the nullification of the arrogance of the Sitra Achra — the aspect of arrogant-facedness [azus panim] — as mentioned above many times. And through this one merits the sacred face — the aspect of the shining face mentioned above.

 Siman 155 — סימן קנה
 Atzvus hi midah ra'ah me'od — Shabbos = nullification of sadness and laziness = long-suffering — thirteen tikkuney dikna — extra soul = breadth of heart — Eretz Yisrael depends on Shabbos — Ezekiel 20 — Psalm 92 — Isaiah 58

Shabbos is the aspect of the nullification of sadness and laziness — in the aspect of [Isaiah 14:3]: "b'yom hani'ach Hashem Elokecha mei'atzevecha u'merogzecha" — the aspect of the nullification of anger and irritation. And one merits then to joy and diligence — and to pray with concentration and sacred vitality and ardor — as mentioned above many times.

For Shabbos is the aspect of faith — the aspect of the nullification of idolatry — and the sweetening of the burning wrath — as mentioned above many times. And then one merits to long-suffering [arichas apayim]. And this is what is brought in the kavannos: in [Psalms 29]: "Mizmor l'David — havu" — and so on — to have in mind the thirteen rectifications of the beard of Arich Anpin [the Long-Suffering One] of Asiyah — and of Yetzirah — and of Beriyah — and so on — see there. And see in the kavannos of the Minchah prayer of Shabbos. And perhaps this itself is the aspect of the extra soul one merits on Shabbos — for this is the aspect of breadth of heart for repose and joy — and so on — and one's soul is not impatient — as Rashi explained [Tractate Beitzah 16] — as mentioned above. For during the weekday — sometimes the person has the aspect of shortness of spirit [kitzur nefesh] — in the aspect of [Numbers 21:4]: "vatiktzar nefesh ha'am" — and so on — that is, one becomes weary and fatigued and confused from the magnitude of the obstacles and the tribulations that each person undergoes according to his level. And on Shabbos one merits the extra soul and a new higher-soul — and breadth of heart — so as not to look at any confusion or preoccupation or obstacle at all — but only to be strong and joyful always in one's faith in Him, blessed be He — and to engage in the service of G-d with diligence and joy — and to have long-suffering toward everything — and nothing should worry him at all. And through this he grows and sprouts and succeeds always in his service of G-d, blessed be He — as explained within. And therefore the essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael — where one merits this attribute of long-suffering — all flows from the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And this is what is written [Ezekiel 20:15]: "v'gam ani nasa'ti es yadi lahem bamidbar — l'vilti havi osam el ha'aretz asher nasati — v'chol haggid — ya'an b'mishpatai mas'u — v'chol haggid — v'es Shabsosai chilelu — ki acharei giluleihem libbam holech" — (for the desecration of Shabbos is like worshipping idolatry — as our Sages of blessed memory taught) — "es Shabsosai chilelu — va'omar lishpoch chamasi aleihem l'chalos api bam bamidbar" [Ezekiel 20:13]. And there [Ezekiel 20:23]: "gam ani nasa'ti es yadi lahem bamidbar l'hafitz osam bagoyim — v'lizros osam ba'aratzos — ya'an mishpatai lo asu — v'chol haggid — v'es Shabsosai chilelu" — and so on — as mentioned above. For the essential continuity of Israel's dwelling in Eretz Yisrael — where one merits to faith — and to nullify the burning wrath, heaven forfend, that is drawn through idolatry — and to merit long-suffering — all depends on the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this is what is written there [Ezekiel 20:20]: "v'es Shabsosai kaddeshu — v'hayu l'os beyni u'veineichem — lada'as ki Ani Hashem Elokeichem" — for this is the aspect of: all who dwell in Eretz Yisrael — it is as if one has a G-d — for this is the aspect of the fullness of faith — as explained within. And therefore on the holy Shabbos — one must be especially careful of anger and irritation — which is the opposite of the aforementioned attribute of long-suffering. And this matter is explained in [Psalms 92]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem" — for then it is very good to pray in fullness — as mentioned above. And this [Psalms 92:2]: "v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" — that is, to strip one's thought from all the matters of obstacles and confusions and preoccupations and sorrows of this world — and to cleave to G-d, blessed be He, Who is exalted above everything — in the aspect of [Psalms 97:9]: "ki atah Hashem elyon al kol ha'aretz" — and so on.

And this [Psalms 92:3]: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — that is, in times of goodness — when the obstacles do not intensify so greatly — one must certainly give thanks to Hashem and declare His lovingkindnesses, blessed be He. And [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — that is, even in the time of the intensification of the darkness and the troubles and the obstacles, heaven have mercy — one must also be firm in faith in Him, blessed be He — and serve Him, blessed be He, with joy and diligence — in the aspect of [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor v'alay navel" — and so on — "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" — and so on. [Psalms 92:6–9]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem — me'od amku machshevosecha — ish ba'ar lo yeda" — and so on — "b'feroa'ch resha'im" — and so on — "l'hishamedam adey ad — v'atah marom l'olam Hashem" — for His hand, blessed be He, is always on top. And one who is firm in his faith in Him, blessed be He — certainly will grow and sprout and succeed in his service of G-d, blessed be He — forever. And then one will see that all the success of the wicked and the intensification of the obstacles — all of it was for good — as mentioned above many times. And this [Psalms 92:10]: "ki hinneh oyevecha Hashem — ki hinneh oyevecha yovadu" — and so on — [Psalms 92:11]: "vatarem kir'em karni" — and so on. [Psalms 92:12–13]: "b'kamim alai mere'im tishmanah oznai — Tzadik katamar yifrach — k'erez baLevanon yisgeh" — and certainly many winds and rains and storms and the like pass over the palm tree and the cedar — until it grows and blooms — and so on. Likewise — the Tzadik is not moved at all by the obstacles and disputes that pass over him — but is firm in faith in Him, blessed be He — and has very great long-suffering. And through this he grows and sprouts and succeeds and produces fruit and his stump replenishes. And this [Psalms 92:14–15]: "shetulin b'veys Hashem — b'chatzros Elokeinu yafrichu — od yinuvun b'seivah" — and so on — for longevity also flows from the attribute of Arich Anpin [long-suffering] — as mentioned above — and as explained in the Tikunim. And this [Psalms 93:1]: "Hashem Malach ge'us lavash" — and so on — likewise revolves around this matter. And this is what it concluded [Psalms 93:5]: "edosecha ne'emnu me'od — l'vayscha na'avah kodesh Hashem l'orech yamim" — that is, even though it has already been many days and we have not yet been saved with complete salvation — nonetheless — certainly G-d, blessed be He, will complete what is His own — through this very thing — at the greatest possible level. Therefore one must strengthen oneself greatly in faith and the aforementioned long-suffering — for this itself is likewise the aspect of: "l'orech yamim" — mentioned above.

And this [Isaiah 58:13–14]: "im tashiv miShabbos rglecha" — and so on — "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that one merit the attribute of long-suffering — whose root is from the aspect of Arich Anpin — for this is the aspect of: "al Hashem" — as is well-known. And this likewise [Psalms 37:3–4]: "shechen eretz u're'eh emunah — v'his'anag al Hashem" — as mentioned above. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — the plain interpretation: the inheritance of the land of Eretz Yisrael — which is exalted above all the lands. For there in Eretz Yisrael one merits these attributes — as mentioned above. And also: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" alludes to the ascent of Malchus — which is the aspect of faith. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — from whom come the essential obstacles and hindrances to the service of G-d. And one is saved from them through the power and merit of one's sacred faith. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of truth — the aspect of: "titen emes l'Yaakov." For the holiness of Shabbos and the holiness of Eretz Yisrael are likewise the aspect of truth — for this is the aspect of: "emes ra'ey" — as explained within. And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — that is, one merits to draw the holiness of Eretz Yisrael to every place — in the aspect of: "Eretz Yisrael is destined to spread throughout the entire world" — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And therefore the holiness of Shabbos is called: "menuchas emes v'emunah" — as mentioned above. And this: "menuchas shalom v'shalvah v'hashket u'vetach [a rest of peace and serenity and quiet and security]." For through these attributes one passes through everything in peace — and merits a rest of peace and serenity — and so on. And this [Genesis 33:18]: "vayavo Yaakov shalem ir Shechem asher b'Eretz Kena'an — vayachan es pney ha'ir" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: he guarded the Shabbos and established the boundaries. For Eretz Yisrael and the holiness of Shabbos are from one aspect — and both are the aspect of truth and faith — which is the secret of the techum Shabbas of two thousand cubits — as mentioned above many times. (And see in the kavannos: "eretz" — gematria of twice Aleph — and so on — which is the aspect of the techum Shabbas two thousand cubits — mentioned above.) And this: juxtaposed immediately: "vayikken es chelkas hasadeh" — and so on — "b'me'ah kesitah" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded [Tractate Sanhedrin 111]: G-d, blessed be He, said to Moshe: I said to Yaakov — and so on — he wanted to plant his tent and could not find a place — until he bought it for one hundred kesitah — and he did not question My attributes. And it is understood from there: this was the aspect of long-suffering in Yaakov — for even though G-d, blessed be He, had promised him that all the land was his — and now he wanted to plant his tent and had to purchase it for a very great sum — nonetheless he extended his patience and strengthened himself in faith in Him, blessed be He — and did not question His attributes. And this itself is the aspect of the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — as mentioned above.

 Siman 156 — סימן קנו
 Lev Tahor — On Shabbos a supernal fire descends into the heart — pure heart — new spirit — the sacred fire = Tikkun 6 — matzdikey harabbim — two Shabbosim = simple fire awakens supernal fire — Isaiah 58

On the holy Shabbos — a supernal fire descends into the heart of each person of Israel. For this is the aspect of what is explained in the sixth of the final Tikunim [Tikkun Shitasi]: "esh d'chol lo tzarich l'is'chazei b'Shabbas Kodesh — esh d'Kodesh" — and so on — "u'bigin da — mani haMavdil bein Kodesh l'chol" [the fire of the weekday should not appear on the holy Shabbos — the fire of holiness — and so on — and therefore one recites: Who distinguishes between the sacred and the mundane]. And from this fire — warmth and sacred ardor flows in the heart of each person — burning toward G-d, blessed be He, with great sacred ardor and warmth — in the aspect of [Song of Songs 8:6]: "reshafehah reshefey eish — shalheves Yah" — stated likewise regarding Shabbos — as explained in the writings. And this fire drives out the spirit of impurity from the heart. For this is the aspect of what scorches the heads of the impure husks — and so on — as explained in the writings. And through this — each person merits to purify his heart — for this is the aspect of [Prayer]: "v'taher libbenu" — and so on — "v'hanchilenu b'ahavah u'v'ratzon Shabbas Kodshecha [and let us inherit in love and will Your holy Shabbos]." And therefore each person then becomes truly a new creation — in the aspect of [Psalms 51:12]: "lev tahor bara li Elokim — v'ru'ach nachon chadesh b'kirbi [a pure heart create for me O G-d — and a steadfast spirit renew within me]." And this is the aspect of the good gift of Shabbos — the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 7:3]: "lev matanah [a heart is a gift]." And this is likewise the aspect of [Ezekiel 36:26]: "v'nasati lachem lev chadash — v'ru'ach chadashah etein b'kirbechem — v'hasirosi es lev ha'even mibsarchem — v'nasati lachem lev basar — v'es ruchi etein b'kirbechem" — and so on. And this is the aspect of the holy spirit [ru'ach haKodesh] that the people of Israel merit to receive on the holy Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar. For when the heart is pure — then everything the heart says are the literal words of G-d, blessed be He. And this is the aspect of holy spirit — as explained within in this teaching. And likewise above within in Siman 138. And also — the holiness of Shabbos is the aspect of: "u'matzdikey harabbim kachochavim [and those who justify the many — are like the stars]" — as explained within. For just as the essential warmth of the foundation of fire — is what it receives from the movement of the stars — likewise one who justifies the many [matzdig es harabbim] — and draws them close to the service of G-d — and draws down warmth and sacred ardor into their hearts — and likewise one who judges every person favorably [dan es kol ha'adam l'chaf zechus] — which is likewise called: justifying the many — also draws down warmth and ardor toward G-d, blessed be He — as explained within. And all of this is encompassed in the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of: justifying the many. For then — true thoughts of repentance reach each person. And even an unlearned person fears to lie on Shabbos. And also our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. And also — then everyone is judged favorably [niddon l'chaf zechus] — for all judgments are suppressed and do not stir at all — as explained in the holy Zohar. It follows that the holiness of Shabbos is the aspect of justifying the many. And through this — the warmth and ardor of holiness descends in the hearts of Israel. And the holy Shabbos itself receives — as it were — the aspect of warmth from what is above it — that is, from the aspect of the upper Shabbos — for this is the aspect of the two Shabbosim that our Sages of blessed memory taught. And also in its plain sense: it is stated [Genesis 2:3]: "vayevarech Elokim es yom hashevi'i — vayekadesh oso" — and so on. And through the warmth and sacred ardor one merits to receive on the holy Shabbos — one burns always and is never extinguished — in the aspect of [Song of Songs 8:7]: "mayim rabbim lo yuchlu l'chabes es ha'ahavah" — and so on. And therefore then is the essential time for those who justify the many — to gather congregations and to expound words of Torah and ethical guidance and the awe of Heaven — as our Sages of blessed memory taught regarding [Exodus 35:1]: "Vayakhel Moshe" — and so on — for then those who justify the many receive power and sacred warmth from the holy fire of Shabbos. And through this they can draw down and bring sacred warmth into the hearts of those who hear — in such a manner that this warmth will endure in their hearts always — and their lamp shall never be extinguished — forever and ever. And this is what in the passage of Vayakhel [Exodus 35:3] it is commanded: "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem b'yom haShabbas" — that is, not to arouse any weekday fire then — since then is the essential time of drawing down and bringing the fire and the warmth of holiness — which is the aspect of the sacred fire — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — that is, that one should connect oneself fully to the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that is, one merits to receive the warmth and sacred ardor toward G-d, blessed be He, — (which is the essential delight — the aspect of love in delights) — from a very high and wondrous level — which is the aspect of the Holy Ancient One [Atika Kadisha] — for this is the aspect of: "al Hashem" — specifically. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, one merits to drive out and burn entirely the spirit of impurity from one's heart — for this is the aspect of the subjugation of kingdoms. And one merits the purity of heart — which is the aspect of the rectification and the ascent of the sacred Malchus — as brought in the kavannos regarding: "v'taher libbenu" — and so on. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — that is, one merits the resting of the Shechinah and the holy spirit — as Rashi explained regarding: "v'nichalnenu" — this is the request of: "v'nafleinu ani v'amcha" — that the Shechinah should not rest upon the gentile nations. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — for his heart is full of His divinity, blessed be He — as explained in the aforementioned Siman 138. And this is certainly an inheritance without limits — in the aspect of: "Ani chelkecha v'nachalasecha [I am your portion and your inheritance]."

And also — for through the holy spirit — one gazes and looks from one end of the world to the other — and nothing is hidden from him — for this is the aspect of an inheritance without limits. And also — for one merits through this to speak new words before G-d, blessed be He, each time — words that are the aspect of holy spirit. And this is likewise the aspect of an inheritance without limits — since one merits each time to the aspect of: "v'ru'ach nachon chadesh b'kirbi" — as explained within. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — for one merits that everything the heart says — are the literal words of G-d, blessed be He — in the aspect of [Psalms 27:8]: "l'cha amar libbi" — and then one's speech is likewise in the aspect of: "ki pi Hashem diber." And also — for one merits through this to draw everyone close to G-d, blessed be He — and to justify the many — and to draw sacred warmth into their hearts — in a manner that it should endure with them forever — as mentioned above. Since one's words are the words of G-d — as it were — regarding which it is stated [Jeremiah 23:29]: "halo chen d'varay ka'eish [is not My word like fire?]" — it follows that one's words are from the aspect of the supernal fire. And therefore one can draw close to others — and bring down for them sacred warmth — in a manner that it should endure with them forever — as mentioned above — since one receives the warmth from what is above — as mentioned above.

Note — Siman 159 (embedded at the end of Siman 156 in the source): Shabbos is the aspect of the Shechinah — the aspect of Malchus d'Atzilus [Malchus of the World of Emanation] — and through it all the sacred Torah studies ascend — and from this flows both spiritual and material bounty. For all influences flow through the holiness of Shabbos. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah — and they derive it from verses of Torah, Prophets, and Writings. And likewise in Zohar Yisro 92: "v'ilin inon kelala v'raza d'chol orayta — Torah Neviim u'Chsuvim" [and these are the comprehensive principle and secret of the entire Torah — Torah, Prophets, and Writings]. And therefore then is the essential fullness of the ascent of the sacred Torah study. And even one who does not merit even then that his study ascends to the Shechinah itself — as it were — his study at the very least becomes Tal Torah [dew of Torah] — and not one of the thirty-nine labors. For all the thirty-nine labors are nullified on Shabbos. And this is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught in the Yerushalmi and in the Pesikta: one said: Shabbosim were given only for delight — and one said: they were given only for words of Torah — and they do not disagree. One who says: only for delight — this refers to Torah scholars who toil in Torah all the weekdays — and on Shabbos they come and take delight. And one who says: only for Torah study — this refers to workers who are engaged in their labor all the weekdays — and on Shabbos they come and engage in Torah. (Brought in the Beis Yosef and in the annotation of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 296) — and this is as mentioned above. For the Torah scholars who always toil in Torah — and from all aspects of their studies there is formed for them Tal Torah — which is the aspect of spiritual bounty — therefore on Shabbos they must take delight — in order to draw material bounty as well — as understood in the holy Zohar. But the workers who are engaged in their labor all the weekdays — it follows that for them there is formed the aspect of the thirty-nine labors. Therefore on Shabbos — when all the thirty-nine labors are nullified — they must cleave themselves at least to Tal Torah. And this [Exodus 35:1–3]: "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Yisrael" — and so on — "sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah — u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh" — and so on — for within this are encompassed all the congregation of Israel — for even those who engage in the thirty-nine labors during the six weekdays — on Shabbos all the thirty-nine labors are nullified — and they must cleave themselves only to Tal Torah. Only — in truth — even on weekdays one must cleave oneself only to Torah — and then the labor is done of itself — in the aspect of: "ta'aseh melachah" — and as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And then certainly even the Shabbos delight — which is in the aspect of: "lachem" — according to what our Sages of blessed memory taught: "chetzyo lachem [half of it for you]" — will also be holy. (And this explanation is also brought.) And this [Exodus 35:3]: "lo seva'aru eish b'chol moshevoseichem" — for it is forbidden to arouse weekday fire there — for we are engaged then only in Tal Torah — which flows from the right aspect of Torah — which is the aspect of spiritual bounty — which flows from the force of fire that is in the Torah — as explained within. And this is what it concludes at the end of Kabbalas Shabbas: "Hashem l'orech yamim" — that is, the aspect of spiritual bounty — which is the aspect of: "orech yamim b'yminah" [length of days in its right]. And therefore one must complete one's Torah portion with the community — twice the text and once the Targum. Twice the text corresponds to the aspect of the study that ascends to the Shechinah — from which flow both spiritual bounty and material bounty — and both are holy — as mentioned above. And once the Targum corresponds to the study that cannot ascend — for this is the aspect of Targum — as the ministering angels do not recognize the language of Targum [Tractate Shabbos 12b]. Nonetheless — even from this study at least Tal Torah will be formed — whose root is from spiritual bounty — the aspect of longevity. And therefore one merits through this to longevity — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: one should not eat the Shabbos morning meal until one completes one's portion twice the text and once the Targum — as mentioned above. For through this even the Shabbos delight is holy — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13–14]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and so on — "az tis'anag al Hashem" — that one's study ascends to the Shechinah — as it were. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: they give him all the desires of his heart — for through this all kinds of spiritual and material influences flow. And in the holy Zohar they expounded: "al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — where everything is of the right — as explained elsewhere. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, from the yoke of the thirty-nine labors — which are the aspect of the yoke of kingship and the yoke of the way of the land — as it is written [Exodus 1:14]: "vayemar'aru es chayeihem b'avodah kashah" — and so on — and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded [Lamentations 1:14]: "nasani Hashem b'yadei lo uchal kum" — this is the yoke of livelihood — and so on. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha" — this is the aspect of Tal Torah — which is the inheritance of Yaakov — as it is written [Deuteronomy 33:4]: "Torah tzivah lanu Moshe — morashah kehilas Yaakov [the Torah that Moshe commanded us — is the inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov]." And also — Yaakov was blessed with this sacred dew — as it is written [Genesis 27:28]: "v'yiten l'cha ha'Elokim mital hashamayim [and G-d give you of the dew of the heavens]" — and so on — and as explained in Zohar Toldos, folio 143b. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one merits an inheritance without limits — in the aspect of: "tal lo miy'atzer [dew is not withheld]" — as our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Taanis 3b].

Note — Siman 175 (embedded in the source immediately following Siman 156): The essential excellence of weeping [bechiyah] — see in the annotation of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 288 — and likewise: one who has delight [oneg] from weeping — so that the sorrow goes out from his heart — it is permitted to weep on Shabbos. And the Tur"z wrote: specifically when weeping from the abundance of devekus in G-d, blessed be He — it is permitted to weep — and so on. And the matter is explained for our subjects — for Shabbos is the aspect of Binah to the heart [Binah l'Lev] — as mentioned above many times. And from there is the awakening of weeping — for bechiyah [weeping] has the gematria [numerical value] of the full spelling of the Name Samech-Gimmel [63] — which is in Binah. And there is likewise the source of joy — in the aspect of [Psalms 4:8]: "nasata simchah b'libbi [You have placed joy in my heart]." And therefore through this — the weeping is sweetened — when it is out of joy. And therefore the Rema's view — that if one has delight from weeping so that the sorrow should go out from one's heart — even if one weeps from one's sorrow alone — only that one knows that this is delight for him — for through this it will be lighter for him to bear his sorrow — and the sorrow will go out from his heart — then this too is permitted. For also through this — the weeping is sweetened through an illumination from the aspect of Binah l'Lev — since his intention is that the sorrow should go out from his heart — and this too is delight for him. And the Tur"z holds: it is permitted only if one weeps from the abundance of devekus in G-d, blessed be He — for this is the aspect of weeping from joy literally. And then the weeping is completely sweetened — until such weeping is permitted even on Shabbos — since the awakening of the weeping is from joy — whose source is in Binah l'Lev — where is the essential delight of Shabbos — as mentioned above many times. And see there further in the Be'er Heytev and in the Moshvetzos Zahav — what they brought in this regard in the name of the Eliyahu Rabbah.

 ✦ Translator's Summary — Simanim 102–156
 
 Siman 102 — Two kinds of awe / two Shabbosim / hi mesurah b'yadchem: Shabbos = awe; awe comes from above automatically = established and enduring; but must also guard it against inattention. Essential = arousing the supernal awe ["Tzadik moshel yiras Elokim"]. "U'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi lachem" — Sages (Yoma 85b): "hi mesurah b'yadchem v'lo atem mesurim b'yadah" = the awe that comes automatically rules over the person; but the essential = the person himself arouses it = "hi mesurah b'yadchem." "V'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas" = "la'asos davka" = make for oneself the awe. "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos" = two kinds of awe — specifically — even the first awe requires guarding. "Es Shabsosai tishmoru" = two Shabbosim. Isaiah 58 mapped: "az tis'anag" = perfection of prayer = draw down bounty through prayer; "hirkavticha" = husks subdued beneath the feet of holiness; "nachalas Yaakov" = aspect of awe = "b'yir'ascha b'zechus Yaakov"; "ki pi Hashem diber" = from speech: awe revealed = "u'midbaryecha pachad libbi" (Isaiah 66:2) + "hayirei devar Hashem" (Jeremiah 10:7); through awe: speech completed = "kol mi she'yesh bo yiras Shamayim devarav nishma'in"; speech = word of Hashem = "vayevarech eschem ka'asher diber lachem."
 Siman 103 — Teshuvah = Torah = sparks gather / compassion / two Shabbosim = simple compassion arouses great compassion = G-d's own prayer: Shabbos = teshuvah; essential teshuvah depends on Torah; Torah was given on Shabbos = essential time for Torah novellae = letters and sparks scattered through him gather = full ascent of sparks. Through Shabbos holiness: Da'as completed = "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem" → compassion awakened = "yecholah hi shetaracheim" (stated regarding Shabbos; cross-ref. Siman 119) + "v'rachamav meru'bim." Through this: merit to draw great compassion through the prayer of G-d Himself, blessed be He, as it were → complete salvation. "Ilmalai shamru Yisrael shtay Shabbasos miyad nigalin" = Isaiah 56:6–7. Shabbos = aspect of compassion = "yecholah hi shetaracheim." Two Shabbosim = lower Shabbos (= simple compassion) awakens upper Shabbos (= great compassion) = G-d's prayer = "v'simachtim b'veys tefilasi" = G-d's prayer (Sages; within). "V'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas" = plain Shabbos = simple compassion; "la'asos es haShabbas" = arouse the upper Shabbos = great compassion. Tractate Shabbos 12: visiting the sick: "Shabbas hi miliz'ok v'refu'ah kerovah lavo" = through Shabbos holiness itself compassion is awakened → healing close to come. Rabbi Meir: "yecholah hi shetaracheim" = further explains the awakening of compassion through Shabbos; Rabbi Yehudah; Rabbi Yosei (Rashi: in their merit); Shevna the Jerusalemite; "v'rachamav meru'bim / v'Shabbato b'shalom" = even if simple compassion insufficient: great compassion → healing will certainly come. Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag = da Atika Kadisha" = aspect of great compassion = Atik; "nositin lo kol mishalos libo"; Likutay Halachos Halachos Techum Shabbas cross-reference; "hirkavticha = Chakla Tupichin" = ascent of Malchus; saved from subjugation = sparks and letters of Malchus scattered in exile → gathered and ascend through Shabbos → complete Da'as; "nachalas Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin" = Torah + simple compassion (= compassion of Ze'ir Anpin) that prays for and awakens the great compassion = G-d's prayer = "ki pi Hashem diber" = through this: G-d Himself speaks to arouse great compassion = aspect of the compassion of Atik.
 Siman 109 — Sacred havalim / Erev Shabbos = repentance / forget all physical sorrow on Shabbos / Shabbos = cessation of all sighing: Sacred havalim go forth on Shabbos; extra soul and new higher-soul. Proper to reflect much in repentance on every Erev Shabbos and sigh from the depths of one's heart over all one's deeds during the six weekdays → easier to separate from the cord of impurity (= havalim of the Sitra Achra = "hevel heima ma'aseh ta'tu'im") → now binds and cleaves to the sacred chevel = sacred havalim of Shabbos → becomes truly a new creation in body and soul. On Shabbos: must be joyful and completely forget all physical toil and sorrow and lacks — for if one sighs over physical needs on Shabbos = connection to spirituality of Shabbos is somewhat broken = becomes bound to the physical, heaven forfend. Sages: "one should be on Shabbos as if all his work is done"; "forbidden to request one's needs on Shabbos." Shabbos named for "kol anachosah hishbati" (Isaiah 21:2) = all kinds of sighs and physical worries cease and are nullified = attached only to spirituality and in great joy. Must receive Shabbos with joy and a good heart; even the awe of Shabbos must be with great joy.
 Siman 115 — Obstacles on Erev Shabbos / shofar / G-d hides within the obstacles / pikuach nefesh / hi mesurah b'yadchem / all obstacles are only for drawing close: Zohar Emor folio 99: arousal of judgment at Rosh haShana = "santeira atei l'mitva dinah / ki Ani Hashem ohev mishpat"; love of Israel prevails over love of justice → blowing the shofar arouses compassion. Applied to obstacles when drawing close to G-d: accusation of the attribute of Justice = "Ani Hashem ohev mishpat"; but G-d hides Himself within the obstacles so that through them specifically one can draw close = through Da'as can find Him within the obstacles themselves. Perhaps this is the matter of the tekiyos blown on every Erev Shabbos (Shabbos 35b); and today = announce (SA OC 256). Holiness of Shabbos = very great and awesome = ba'al devar lies in wait = arranges many obstacles and preoccupations. Sages instituted shofar = arouse compassion + sweeten all accusations spiritually; and physically = remind each person to remove preoccupations. Perhaps also this is the secret of the shalhava d'asha on Erev Shabbos = subdue husks that wish to ascend and disturb Shabbos holiness. Song of Songs 8:6: "ki azzah k'maves ahavah / kashah kish'ol kinah" = jealousy and accusations intensify; "reshafehah reshefey eish shalheves Yah"; "mayim rabbim lo yuchlu"; "ani chomah / az hayisi b'einav k'motzeis shalom." G-d desires greatly the love of Israel and their drawing close; even the obstacles themselves are only for the sake of drawing close; when one breaks the obstacles = great delight to G-d = draws one close with wondrous love = all the faults are rectified = all Sitra Achra formed through them is nullified. "Ach es Shabsosai tishmoru" = "ach" and "raq" are diminutive expressions = obstacles = wish to minimize from holiness of Shabbos; person must be awakened specifically through this to break obstacles. Sages (Yoma 85) expounded: pikuach nefesh overrides Shabbos = "es Shabsosai tishmoru / ach" divides it. But from this itself: no obstacle comes for the sake of distancing; G-d hides Himself within the obstacle. "V'shamru vnay Yisrael es haShabbas la'asos es haShabbas / desecrate one Shabbos for him so that he may guard many Shabbosim" = even within this desecration: holiness of Shabbos is clothed = desecration = guarding. "V'chai bahem v'lo sheyamus bahem" = even doubtful pikuach nefesh overrides all = love of G-d for souls of Israel = all obstacles only for drawing close. "Mizmor Shir = l'Moshe" = Da'as of Moshe shines on Shabbos = sees that all obstacles are as nothing = G-d Himself is hidden within them. Psalm 92 mapped through obstacles/faith lens: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" = in times of goodness: give thanks; "v'emunascha baleilos" = even in time of intensification of obstacles: be firm in faith + serve with joy and diligence; "mah gadlu ma'asecha / me'od amku machshevosecha" = even so: love of Israel in beginning of thought is even greater → G-d hides Himself within the obstacle so that one can break it → obstacles become great good; "ish ba'ar lo yeda / b'feroa'ch resha'im" = success of wicked/those who obstruct = only for their destruction forever; "ki hinneh oyevecha Hashem" = enemies of Israel who prevent them from Israel's holiness = literally enemies of G-d (Sages); "nasa'u neharos Hashem" = intensification of obstacles; "addir bamarom Hashem" = His hand always on top. Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag" = love in delights = love of G-d for Israel revealed; "hirkavticha" = saved from subjugation of kingdoms = from whom come all the obstacles; Sages: "retzioni la'asos retzoncha / ela she'or she'ba'isah v'shibbud malchiyos me'akev"; "nachalas Yaakov" = nachalah b'li metzarim = "melo chol ha'aretz kevodo" = sees G-d's divinity and honor dressed in every place = "el ha'arafel asher sham ha'Elokim" (Exodus 20:21).
 Siman 116 — Compassion and illumination of Da'as = saved from sin / spirit of foolishness: Greatness of compassion and illumination of Da'as that shines on Shabbos → saved from sins; for no person transgresses a sin unless a spirit of foolishness enters him. Sages: all who guard the Shabbos = distant from sin = Isaiah 56:2 "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo v'shomer yado mei'asos kol ra."
 Siman 129 — Attachment to Shabbos = transformed into its very holiness / body becomes like the soul / emunah zeh Seder Zera'im / Eretz Yisrael / Isaiah 58: Shabbos = faith + mochin and Da'as. When truly connected to Shabbos holiness with complete faith = transformed into the very substance of its holiness. Therefore "kol hashomer es haShabbas / afilu aved avodah zarah / mochalin lo." Also: "kol hame'aneg es haShabbas mochalin lo al kol avonasav" = transformed into very substance of its holiness. "Hai yoma yoma d'nishmatin hu v'lo yoma d'gufa" = body also transformed into substance of holy soul = mind and Da'as = aspect of commandment of delight of Shabbos = physical pleasures precious and very holy. "Shechen eretz u're'eh emunah" = Eretz Yisrael = fullness of faith. "V'his'anag al Hashem" = all pleasures entirely holy. Sages: "kol hashomer Shabbas" = distant from sin. Isaiah 56:2 "ashrey enosh ya'aseh zos" (Rashi: guards Shabbos); "u'ven adam yachazik bah davka" = hold fast and connect to holiness of Shabbos with complete faith; "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo / v'shomer yado mei'asos kol ra" = distant from sin. Isaiah 56:3: "ben haneychar" = not born into holiness of Israel → cannot be transformed into very substance of holiness; "hasaris" = faith = aspect of power of growth and sprouting = "emunah zeh Seder Zera'im" (elsewhere); Isaiah 56:4–7 mapped. Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag" = merits "v'his'anag al Hashem"; decrees and G-d fulfills = all desires; "hirkavticha" = saved from subjugation = body and physicality transformed into substance of holy soul = "leichol es besari" (within) = enemies stumble and fall = Siman 101 cross-reference; "nachalas Yaakov" = fullness of Eretz Yisrael holiness = power to transform whoever dwells in it; nachalah b'li metzarim = entirely spiritual = without any boundary at all.
 Siman 135 — Shabbos = first of holy convocations = Moshe / all gates of Binah open / true humility / drawing close to Tzadikim / love = attachment = extra soul / three Festivals flow from Shabbos: Shabbos = first of holy convocations = Moshe (many times); all gates of Binah opened (Zohar). Merits true humility = "shvu ish tachtav" (Siman 79 cross-ref.). Essential time of drawing close to Tzadikim = through Shabbos: feels more the light of the Tzadik; through light of Tzadik: receives Shabbos holiness more. Commandment to receive the face of one's teacher on Shabbos (Zohar; writings) = Tzadik merits mochin d'gadlus at exceedingly lofty level = nature of smallness to nullify itself before greatness → nullifies oneself greatly before the Tzadik's holiness → can be transformed into very substance of their holiness. "U'shmartem es haShabbas ki Kodesh hi lachem"; "u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh — lachem davka" = its holiness drawn upon you literally; "lada'as ki Ani Hashem mekadshechem." Essential attachment = love = "v'nefesh Yehonatan nikeshrah b'nefesh David" (I Samuel 18:1). Through attachment of one's soul to Shabbos holiness (= root of all souls) → merits extra soul of Shabbos. "Mah yafis u'mah na'amt ahavah b'ta'anugim" = Shabbos delight must be with great love for Shabbos holiness — greater than the love of women = Isaiah 56:4 "la'sarisim asher yishmeru es Shabsosai" = who wait for their union for holiness of Shabbos (Zohar). Through Shabbos: sacred Malchus ascends from exile of four kingdoms = saved from subjugation of kingdoms. Essential subjugation of kingdom of Amalek = Sages: "b'yom hashevi'i yatze'u min ha'am lilkot miyad vayavo Amalek" (Exodus 16:27). Shabbos = teshuvah + awe = rectification and ascent of Malchus. All holiness of three Festivals = engaging in rectification of Malchus (within) = all flows from Shabbos = Sages: if you guard Shabbos I shall give you the Festivals.
 Siman 143 — Receiving the face of the Torah scholar / shining face / panim b'fanim diber Hashem: Sages on Genesis 2:3: "vayevarech Elokim es yom hashevi'i" = "berchu b'me'or panav shel adam." Zohar and writings: must receive the face of one's teacher on Shabbos = since everyone has shining face [anpin nehirin] → can receive upon one's face the very light of the teacher's face → teacher's face visible on his face = "panim b'fanim diber Hashem imachem" (Deuteronomy 5:4; Sages: on Shabbos). Also on Shabbos: drawn = nullification of lust for money; nullification of arrogance of Sitra Achra = "azus panim" (many times) → merits sacred face = shining face.
