Shabbos = faith = nullification of idolatry = sweetening of burning wrath (many times) → merits long-suffering [arichas apayim]. Kavannos: "Mizmor l'David havu" = have in mind thirteen tikkuney dikna of Arich Anpin of Asiyah/Yetzirah/Beriyah; see in kavannos of Shabbos Minchah prayer. Extra soul = aspect of breadth of heart for repose and joy = "soul is not impatient" (Rashi, Beitzah 16). During weekdays: sometimes person has shortness of spirit = "vatiktzar nefesh ha'am" (Numbers 21:4) = weary and fatigued. On Shabbos: extra soul + new higher-soul + breadth of heart → not look at any confusion or obstacle at all → strong and joyful always → diligence and joy → long-suffering toward everything → nothing worries him → grows and sprouts and succeeds. Essential holiness of Eretz Yisrael = where one merits this attribute of long-suffering = all flows from holiness of Shabbos (many times). Ezekiel 20:15 + 20:13 + 20:23 cited fully: desecration of Shabbos = like idolatry (Sages) = burning wrath = scattered among the nations. Ezekiel 20:20: "v'es Shabsosai kaddeshu / lada'as ki Ani Hashem Elokeichem." Essential continuity of Israel's dwelling in Eretz Yisrael + faith + nullify burning wrath + long-suffering = all depends on Shabbos holiness. On Shabbos: especially careful of anger and irritation = opposite of long-suffering. Psalm 92 fully mapped through long-suffering/faith/obstacles lens: "tov lehodos" = very good to pray in fullness; "v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" = strip thought from all confusions and preoccupations → cleave to G-d exalted above everything = "ki atah Hashem elyon al kol ha'aretz" (Psalms 97:9); "lehagid baboker chasdecha" = times of goodness: give thanks; "v'emunascha baleilos" = even in times of darkness: firm in faith + serve with joy and diligence; "mah gadlu ma'asecha"; "ish ba'ar lo yeda"; "b'feroa'ch resha'im"; "v'atah marom l'olam Hashem" = one who is firm in faith: will grow and sprout and succeed forever; "ki hinneh oyevecha"; "vatarem kir'em karni"; "b'kamim alai mere'im / Tzadik katamar yifrach k'erez baLevanon" = many winds and rains pass over palm tree and cedar → grows and blooms; likewise Tzadik = firm in faith = long-suffering → grows and succeeds and produces fruit and stump replenishes; "shetulin b'veys Hashem / b'chatzros Elokeinu yafrichu / od yinuvun b'seivah" = longevity flows from attribute of Arich Anpin (Tikunim); "Hashem Malach ge'us lavash"; "edosecha ne'emnu me'od / l'vayscha na'avah kodesh Hashem l'orech yamim" = even though already many days and not yet fully saved → G-d will complete what is His at the greatest possible level → must strengthen oneself greatly in faith and long-suffering. Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag" = merit attribute of long-suffering whose root is from Arich Anpin = "al Hashem"; "shechen eretz u're'eh emunah v'his'anag al Hashem"; "hirkavticha" + "nachalas Yaakov" = plain interpretation: inheritance of Eretz Yisrael = there one merits these attributes; also: "hirkavticha" = ascent of Malchus (= faith); saved from subjugation = from whom come the obstacles; "nachalas Yaakov" = truth = "titen emes l'Yaakov"; Shabbos holiness + Eretz Yisrael = truth = "emes ra'ey" (within); nachalah b'li metzarim = draw holiness of Eretz Yisrael to every place = "Eretz Yisrael is destined to spread throughout the entire world" (Sages); Shabbos = "menuchas emes v'emunah" / "menuchas shalom v'shalvah v'hashket u'vetach"; "vayavo Yaakov shalem ir Shechem asher b'Eretz Kena'an vayachan es pney ha'ir" = Sages: guarded Shabbos and established boundaries; Eretz Yisrael and Shabbos holiness = from one aspect = truth and faith = secret of techum Shabbas two thousand cubits (many times); kavannos: "eretz" = gematria of twice Aleph = techum Shabbas alpayim amah; Sanhedrin 111: Yaakov could not find a place to plant his tent = had to purchase it for great sum = yet extended his patience and strengthened in faith and did not question G-d's attributes = aspect of long-suffering = holiness of Eretz Yisrael.
 Siman 156 — Supernal fire descends into the heart on Shabbos / pure heart / new spirit / Tikkun Shitasi / matzdikey harabbim / two Shabbosim / Isaiah 58; with embedded Siman 159 (Torah study ascends to Shechinah / Tal Torah / 39 labors nullified / twice the text and once the Targum) and Siman 175 (weeping on Shabbos / Rema / Tur"z / Binah l'Lev / bechiyah = gematria of shem Samech-Gimmel 63): On Shabbos: supernal fire descends into heart of each person of Israel. Tikkun Shitasi (sixth of final Tikunim) cited (Aramaic): "esh d'chol lo tzarich l'is'chazei b'Shabbas Kodesh esh d'Kodesh / u'bigin da mani haMavdil bein Kodesh l'chol" = weekday fire should not appear on Shabbos = therefore one recites Havdalah. From this fire: warmth and sacred ardor = "reshafehah reshefey eish shalheves Yah" stated regarding Shabbos (writings). This fire drives out the spirit of impurity from the heart = scorches heads of impure husks (writings). Through this: each person merits to purify his heart = "v'taher libbenu / v'hanchilenu b'ahavah u'v'ratzon Shabbas Kodshecha." Each person becomes truly a new creation = "lev tahor bara li Elokim / v'ru'ach nachon chadesh b'kirbi" (Psalms 51:12). Good gift of Shabbos = "lev matanah" (Ecclesiastes 7:3). Also = Ezekiel 36:26: "v'nasati lachem lev chadash / v'ru'ach chadashah etein b'kirbechem / v'hasirosi es lev ha'even / v'nasati lachem lev basar / v'es ruchi etein b'kirbechem." Aspect of holy spirit [ru'ach haKodesh] that Israel merits to receive on Shabbos (Zohar). When heart is pure = everything the heart says = words of G-d literally = aspect of holy spirit (within; Siman 138 cross-reference). Shabbos = aspect of "u'matzdikey harabbim kachochavim" (within). Just as warmth of fire = received from movement of the stars; likewise: one who justifies the many and draws them close to G-d + one who judges every person favorably = draws down warmth and ardor toward G-d. All encompassed in holiness of Shabbos = justifies the many = repentance thoughts reach each person = even am ha'aretz fears to lie on Shabbos = "kol hashomer Shabbas afilu aved avodah zarah mochalin lo" = all judged favorably = "kol dinin atkafyan v'lo mis'arin." Shabbos itself receives warmth from above = from the upper Shabbos = the two Shabbosim (Sages). Also plain: "vayevarech Elokim es yom hashevi'i vayekadesh oso." Warmth and sacred ardor = burns always and never extinguished = "mayim rabbim lo yuchlu l'chabes es ha'ahavah." Essential time for those who justify the many = gather congregations and expound Torah and ethical guidance and awe of Heaven (Sages: "Vayakhel Moshe") = those who justify the many receive power and sacred warmth from holy fire of Shabbos → can draw down warmth into hearts of listeners → warmth will endure always → lamp never extinguished. "Lo seva'aru eish" in Vayakhel = don't arouse weekday fire = now is time for drawing down the sacred fire. Isaiah 58: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" = connect fully to holiness of Shabbos; "az tis'anag = Atika Kadisha" = warmth and sacred ardor from very high and wondrous level = "al Hashem davka"; "hirkavticha" = saved from subjugation = drives out spirit of impurity from heart = tikkun and ascent of sacred Malchus = "v'taher libbenu" (kavannos); "nachalas Yaakov" = resting of Shechinah and holy spirit (Rashi: "v'nichalnenu" = "v'nafleinu ani v'amcha" = Shechinah should not rest upon the nations); nachalah b'li metzarim = heart full of G-d's divinity (Siman 138); + through holy spirit: gazes from one end of the world to the other; + speaks new words each time = "v'ru'ach nachon chadesh b'kirbi"; "ki pi Hashem diber" = everything the heart says = words of G-d = "l'cha amar libbi"; draws everyone close to G-d and justifies the many = "halo chen d'varay ka'eish" (Jeremiah 23:29) = receives warmth from above → can bring down sacred warmth into others that will endure forever. Siman 159: Shabbos = Shechinah = Malchus d'Atzilus; all Torah studies ascend through it = spiritual and material bounty; Sages: Shabbos equivalent to entire Torah; Zohar Yisro 92 (Aramaic: "v'ilin inon kelala v'raza d'chol orayta"); even one who doesn't fully merit: his study becomes Tal Torah and not 39 labors. Yerushalmi and Pesikta: one says Shabbosim given only for delight / one says only for Torah study = they don't disagree: Torah scholars (= always toil in Torah = their study = Tal Torah = spiritual bounty) → on Shabbos: delight to draw material bounty too; workers (= engaged in 39 labors all week) → on Shabbos (= 39 labors nullified) → must cleave to Tal Torah. SA OC 296 cited. "Vayakhel Moshe / sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah / u'vayom hashevi'i yihyeh lachem Kodesh" = encompasses all Israel = even those who engage in 39 labors: on Shabbos these are nullified → cleave to Tal Torah. On weekdays also: cleave to Torah → labor done of itself; then: Shabbos delight ("lachem") = also holy. "Lo seva'aru eish" = don't arouse weekday fire = engaging only in Tal Torah = from right aspect of Torah = spiritual bounty = from force of fire in Torah (within). "Hashem l'orech yamim" at end of Kabbalas Shabbas = spiritual bounty = "orech yamim b'yminah." Must complete parasha: twice the text and once Targum; twice the text = study that ascends to Shechinah → two influences (spiritual + material bounty) = both holy; once Targum = study that cannot fully ascend (angels don't recognize Targum; Shabbos 12b) = yet: at least Tal Torah = whose root = spiritual bounty = longevity; Sages: one merits longevity; Sages: don't eat Shabbos morning meal until complete shanayim mikra v'echad Targum. Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag" = one's study ascends to Shechinah; "da Atika Kadisha / kula yemina" (elsewhere); "hirkavticha" = saved from subjugation = yoke of 39 labors = "yoke of kingship and yoke of the way of the land" = "vayemar'aru es chayeihem b'avodah kashah / nasani Hashem b'yadei lo uchal kum zeh ol haparnasah"; "nachalas Yaakov" = Tal Torah = inheritance of Yaakov = "Torah tzivah lanu Moshe morashah kehilas Yaakov" (Deuteronomy 33:4); Yaakov blessed with sacred dew = "v'yiten l'cha ha'Elokim mital hashamayim" (Genesis 27:28; Zohar Toldos 143b); nachalah b'li metzarim = "tal lo miy'atzer" (Taanis 3b). Siman 175: weeping [bechiyah] on Shabbos; SA OC 288 annotation (Rema: if has oneg from weeping = permitted); Tur"z: specifically when weeping from abundance of devekus. Shabbos = Binah l'Lev (many times) = source of awakening of weeping; "bechiyah" = gematria of full spelling of Name Samech-Gimmel [63] = in Binah; source of joy = "nasata simchah b'libbi" (Psalms 4:8) → weeping sweetened when out of joy. Rema's view: if weeping so that sorrow should go out from heart → even from sorrow alone if knows it is delight for him = also permitted = weeping sweetened through illumination from Binah l'Lev (since intention: sorrow should go out from heart = delight). Tur"z's view: only permitted if weeping from abundance of devekus in G-d = weeping from joy literally = completely sweetened = permitted even on Shabbos = awakening of weeping from joy whose source in Binah l'Lev = essential delight of Shabbos (many times). Be'er Heytev and Moshvetzos Zahav: brought in name of Eliyahu Rabbah.

 נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן

 Siman 178 — סימן קעח
 Da ki Tzarich Davva — Viduy Devarim — Shabbos = complete stature = all the commandments encompassed — verbal confession on Shabbos — Tikkun 21 — unity of voice and speech — Psalm 92 — Isaiah 58

It is explained in Tikkun 21, folio 57: "leis pikuda d'aseh v'lo ta'aseh d'lo ishtech b'Shabbas — u'begin da Shabbas hi shekulah k'chol orayta" — and so on. And therefore one must rejoice on Shabbos exceedingly — very greatly — for [Psalms 19:9]: "pikudei Hashem yesharim — mesamchei lev" — and since the guarding of the holy Shabbos is the totality of all of them — certainly one must rejoice very greatly — beyond all measure entirely. But because it is the nature of sins to draw anxiety — in the aspect of [Psalms 38:19]: "edaig mecha'tati [I am anxious about my sin]" — therefore when one comes to enter into the holiness of the joy of Shabbos — which is the aspect of complete stature — since it is the totality of everything — as mentioned above.

Therefore — the blemishes of the sins come and wish to confuse his joy. In particular — since Shabbos is the aspect of sacred speech — as explained in Zohar Bereishis, folio 32. And the blemish of sin in the soul — which is the aspect of speech — as explained within. Therefore — even though the holiness of Shabbos prevails and covers over everything — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who delight the Shabbos — they are forgiven all their sins. And our Sages of blessed memory taught: even if he worshipped idolatry — and so on — he is forgiven. Nonetheless — through this one remembers all one's blemishes — and one can through this make a verbal confession [viduy devarim] in fullness. And through this itself the speech is rectified and built — and the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is made [yichud Kud'sha B'rich Hu u'Shechinteih] — which itself is likewise the secret of the holiness of Shabbos — as explained in the Tikunim and the holy Zohar. And this [Psalms 92:2]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos" — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: from the language of verbal confession [viduy devarim] — through which the speech is rectified — the aspect of Malchus — and one merits to hear voices from above — and so on — as explained within. And this [Psalms 92:2]: "v'lezamre lishimcha elyon."

And this [Psalms 92:3]: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — and it is explained in the kavannos that this is the aspect of Ze'ir Anpin d'Atzilus — and [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — the aspect of Malchus d'Atzilus — that is, through this the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is made — the aspect of the unity of voice and speech [yichud kol v'dibur]. And this touches on the secret of hearing the sound of music and musical instruments. And this [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor v'alay navel — alay higgayon b'chinor." And this [Psalms 92:5]: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" — the aspect of the aforementioned joy. And this [Psalms 92:8–10]: "b'feroa'ch resha'im" — and so on — "l'hishamedam adey ad" — and so on — "ki hinneh oyevecha yovadu — vatarem kir'em karni" — and so on. And this is in general. And likewise in particular — the blemishes of the sins come to confuse the joy — as mentioned above. And all of this is the work of the ba'al devar [the adversary]. But in truth — on the contrary — specifically through this is the essential subjugation and nullification of them in fullness. For through this one remembers them and makes a verbal confession over them explicitly — and through this everything is rectified in fullness — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and so on — that is, one should guard the holiness of Shabbos in fullness. [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da Atika Kadisha" — where is the source of the supernal and very wondrous joy — as explained in Zohar Vayikra, folio 133: "sos asis b'Hashem — b'Atik Yomin is'mar — d'ha hu chedvasa d'chola [I will greatly rejoice in Hashem — this is said regarding the Ancient of Days — for He is the joy of all]." And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz" — this is the aspect of the full ascent of Malchus — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — that is, one destroys the buildings of the Sitra Achra — which are the aspect of the kingdoms of the Sitra Achra — which were built through one's blemishes. And one builds the aspect of the sacred speech — which is the aspect of the ascent of the sacred Malchus.

And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da Ze'ir Anpin" — which is the aspect of the voice — "kol kol Yaakov" [the voice — the voice of Yaakov] — that is, the voice is unified with the speech. And this [Isaiah 58:14]: "ki pi Hashem diber" — this is the aspect of the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah — that the speech is unified, as it were, with Hashem — as explained in the teaching Vayiten Oz l'Malko, Siman 78 — and in the teaching Zachar Chasdo, Siman 94.

 Siman 179 — סימן קעט
 Da sheKeneged — Shabbos = peace — charity on Erev Shabbos — fasting on Erev Shabbos — delight of Shabbos itself is more than a thousand fasts — extra soul = will — tachyas hamaysim

Shabbos is the aspect of peace — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And therefore one must give charity for Shabbos — and as explained elsewhere — for increasing charity increases peace. And this is what is explained in Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayyim, Siman 249: the way of people of deed is to fast on every Erev Shabbos — in particular one who has no desire to eat at night if he eats during the day. And every person is in any case forbidden to establish on Erev Shabbos a meal that he is not accustomed to on weekdays — for this too is the aspect of a fast. And through this one merits to receive the peace of Shabbos — for through fasting — strife is nullified and peace is made — as explained within. And in truth — the special virtue of the delight of Shabbos itself is as propitious as a fast — and more than this — and as explained elsewhere. And as our Sages of blessed memory taught [Midrash Tanchuma, Bereishis]: "kevod Shabbas adif me'elef tani'yos [the honor of Shabbos is superior to a thousand fasts]." For the virtue of fasting is to nullify one's will before the will of G-d, blessed be He — as explained within. And Shabbos is even more propitious for this — for this is the aspect of the extra soul of Shabbos — for nefesh [soul] is an expression of will — as explained within. And then each person of Israel merits good and holy wills — and as mentioned above many times.

And this [Prayer]: "v'taher libbenu l'ovdecha be'emes — v'hanchilenu Hashem Elokeinu b'ahavah u'v'ratzon Shabbas Kodshecha." And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught regarding one who guards and delights the Shabbos — and so on — he decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills — and they give him all the desires of his heart. For this is the essential perfection of peace — that nothing is done to him that is against his will. And as explained within. And this is the aspect of the joy of Shabbos — for when there is peace — then joy and gladness. For the holiness of Shabbos is likewise the aspect of the resurrection of the dead — in the aspect of [Shabbos liturgy]: "ta'ameha chayyim zachu [those who taste it merited life]" — for Shabbos is a foretaste of the World to Come — which will be after the resurrection — as it is written [Daniel 12:13]: "v'tanuach v'ta'amod l'goralscha l'keitz hayamin." And also — for the essential vitality of holiness of all the days of the week comes from Shabbos — for this is the aspect of [Exodus 20:8]: "zachor es yom haShabbas l'kadsho" — "zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas." And therefore Shammai used to eat all his days in honor of Shabbos — so that all the power and vitality he received through his eating would be only from the holiness of Shabbos. And therefore through the holiness of Shabbos — the stature of joy is built — and new sacred vitality and joy are drawn upon the entire creation. For this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:5]: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" — and so on — which is said in the psalm for the Shabbos day. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded [Psalms 139:16]: "yamim yotzaru — v'lo echad bahem" — this is the Shabbos day — for it is the vitality of all of them.

 Siman 188 — סימן קפח
 Da sheTzarich — Shabbos = returning of lost objects — the one thousand lights restored to Moshe — Moshe restores the crowns to Israel — v'lo echad bahem — the Tzadik is the shofar of returning

Shabbos is the aspect of the returning of lost objects — as explained in the writings of the Ari z"l: they restore then to Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, the one thousand lights that were taken from him. And Moshe restores to Israel the crowns [ketarim] that were taken from them. And in its plain sense as well — our Sages of blessed memory taught: "keivan she'shavas — vav — avdah nefesh" — it follows that there is then a loss for each person. And on Shabbos — one's lost object is returned to him — and one merits to receive the extra soul. And this is the aspect of [Exodus 20:8]: "zachor es yom haShabbas" — the opposite of forgetting — which is the aspect of loss. And since one does not return a lost object until one inquires whether he is a deceiver and a liar — therefore [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — for this is likewise the aspect of the returning of the lost object — as understood — א'ם ת'שיב מ'שבת — initial letters of אמ"ת [emes] — as brought in the writings. And therefore then is the essential time to come to the Tzadik — to reclaim one's lost object.

And therefore one must receive the face of one's teacher on Shabbos — as explained in the holy Zohar. And this is the aspect of the tekiyos [shofar blasts] they would blow on Erev Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught — in the aspect of [Isaiah 27:13]: "b'yom hahu yitaka b'shofar gadol — u'va'u ha'ovdim" — and so on — in the aspect of the returning of the aforementioned lost objects.

 Siman 225 — סימן רכה
 Da kesha'haRe'iyah biShleimus — Shabbos = the spirit of life in the wings of the lungs — therefore extra soul and sacred mental faculties — trust — charity — speech — Psalm 92

Shabbos is the aspect of the spirit of life [ru'ach chayyim] in the wings of the lungs — as explained above. And through this is the essential sustaining of the intellect — which is the aspect of the higher soul [neshamah]. And therefore on Shabbos one merits the extra soul and sacred mental faculties. And through this one merits trust [bitachon] — for this is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught: "luvu alai va'ani porei'a [borrow on my account and I shall repay]." And through this one gives charity — which is the aspect of the fullness of the charity of Shabbos — and as explained elsewhere. And the delight of Shabbos itself is the aspect of charity — as mentioned above many times. And through this one comes to the level of a person — which is the aspect of speech [dibur] — for this is the aspect of: "v'daber davar" — stated regarding Shabbos — and as mentioned above many times in the name of the holy Zohar. Until one merits to make words from the sound of the chirping [tziptzufim] — and to hear words from the sound of the harp — as explained within. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:2]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem" — and so on. And this is through the aspect of the sacred words that are then opened. And this [Psalms 92:3]: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — "lehagid" — this is the language of a word of wisdom [milah d'chochmata]. This is the aspect of the fullness of the intellect and the mental faculties — which are the aspect of lovingkindnesses — as is well-known.

And [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — this is the aspect of strengthening trust even in the aspect of night and darkness. And this [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor" — and so on — [Psalms 92:4]: "alay higgayon b'chinor" — that is, one merits to make words from the sound of the harp.

 Siman 234 — סימן רלד
 Da sheSippurei Ma'asiyos miTzadikim — Shabbos = world of thought = mochin d'gadlus — songs of the Creator's greatness at entry of Shabbos = purity of thought — Havdalah = distinction between righteous and wicked

Shabbos is the world of thought — the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — as is well-known. And therefore at the beginning of the entry of Shabbos — we recite psalms of the greatness of the Creator, blessed be He — Who is the righteous One of the world. And through this one merits the purity of thought. And this is what we say in the psalm for the Shabbos day: [Psalms 92:6]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem — me'od amku machshevosecha" — and afterward it explains at length the distinction between the stories of the success of the wicked — which is only temporary and for the moment — and for their destruction forever. But the stories of the success of the righteous are true and eternal — forever and ever. And this is what we say at the going out of Shabbos [Havdalah]: "haMavdil bein Kodesh l'chol — bein or l'choshech — bein Yisrael la'amim" — for Israel as a collective are righteous against all the nations — as it is written [Isaiah 60:21]: "v'amech kulam tzadikim [and your people are all righteous]." And this [Havdalah]: "bein yom hashevi'i l'sheshes yemey haMa'aseh" — as mentioned above.

 Siman 250 — סימן רנ
 Da shekol Miney Tza'ar — On Shabbos one merits complete Da'as and complete faith — all suffering nullified — saved from the exile of the kingdoms — Shabbos = foretaste of the World to Come — Shabbos = tlas guvnin d'eina = light of Providence

On Shabbos one merits complete Da'as and complete faith — to believe and know that everything is conducted only through His Providence, blessed be He. And through this all kinds of suffering and afflictions are nullified — in the aspect of [Isaiah 14:3]: "b'yom hani'ach lecha mei'atzevecha u'merogzecha" — and so on. And also one is saved from the subjugation of kingdoms — which is the aspect of the sorrow of exile. For Shabbos is a foretaste of the World to Come — which will be the day that is entirely Shabbos — and then nature will be entirely nullified — and there will be only Providence alone. And therefore — also now — through the holiness of Shabbos one merits to draw the light of His Providence, blessed be He, from the aspect of the final end. And through this Israel are elevated above nature — and an end and a conclusion comes to all those who oppress us. And therefore Jerusalem was destroyed only because they desecrated the Shabbos — and had the children of Israel guarded the first Shabbos — no nation or tongue would have had dominion over them. And had they guarded two Shabbosim — they would have been immediately redeemed. And in Midrash Rabbah, Parashas Beshalach, it is explained that even through the merit of one Shabbos one is redeemed. And all this is because — had all of Israel merited to guard the Shabbos in fullness — the light of Providence would have flowed upon them in fullness as well — from the aspect of the final end. And they would certainly have been redeemed with eternal redemption. And therefore for the most part the guarding of Shabbos is mentioned in the plural — such as [Exodus 31:13]: "es Shabsosai tishmoru" — for through the plain guarding of Shabbos one merits to draw the light of the future Shabbos — which will be the day that is entirely Shabbos — as mentioned above. And perhaps this itself is the aspect of the two Shabbosim mentioned above that our Sages of blessed memory taught. And therefore Shabbos is the aspect of: "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" — which is the aspect of the aforementioned light of Providence.

 Siman 276 — סימן רעו
 Da she'Achilat Shabbas — The essential satiety is on Shabbos — the three Shabbos meals are to draw bounty on all six days — vayikadesh = no manna descended on Shabbos — the great Tzadikim feed on spiritual bounty — supporting Torah scholars — Isaiah 58

It is explained within that the essential satiety is on Shabbos — for then is the essential fullness of the light of the eyes — which is the aspect of: "pos'im bo pesi'ah ketanah" — and so on — and therefore then is the essential satiety. For the essential satiety comes through the sight of the eyes — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And therefore why do we eat three meals on Shabbos? Only: "begin d'yisbrechu minei kol shita yomin" — as explained in the holy Zohar. And perhaps through this one can also resolve the question that the Zohar asks: since the manna did not descend on Shabbos — what blessing is found in it? — and so on. For on the contrary — this is the essential blessing — that there is in it such satiety that they did not need physical eating and drinking at all. For Shabbos is a foretaste of the World to Come — in which there is no eating and drinking. And the commandment of eating and the meals of Shabbos is only in order to draw bounty upon all the weekdays. And therefore the manna did not descend on Shabbos — but on the sixth day they were given bread for two days — so that there would also be something for the meals of Shabbos — for the weekday prepares for Shabbos — but Shabbos does not prepare for the weekday — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And this is as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of [Genesis 2:2–3]: "vayevarech vayekadesh" — blessed it with the manna that descended on the sixth day — bread for two days — so that there would also be something for the meals of Shabbos — which are only to draw blessing upon all the weekdays. For "miShabbas nafkin birchan l'chulhu" — and so on — and sanctified it with the manna that did not descend on it at all — that is, to indicate the immensity of the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the World to Come — in which one has no need at all for eating and drinking for its own sake — but only to draw blessing upon all the six days. And in this one can also understand something of the matter of the great Tzadikim — through whom the entire world is sustained — and they themselves lack sustenance. And this is likewise from the aforementioned reason — for they — according to the immensity of their holiness — almost have no need at all for material influence and sustenance — for their food and sustenance is only from spiritual bounty. And as explained in the holy Zohar, Beshalach, folio 61: "mezonah ila'ah yatir mikola hu mezonah d'chavrayya — inon d'mishtadlin b'orayta — d'achlei mezonah d'rucha v'nishmata — v'lo achlei mezonah d'gufa klal — v'hiynoo me'atar ila'ah yakira al kola — v'itkari chochmah" — and so on — "v'achlei mezonah d'rucha v'nishmata me'atar rachika ila'ah yakira mikola" — and so on — "zakai chulkah d'gufa d'yachil l'is'zanah b'mezonah d'nafsha" — and so on. And that nonetheless they also need to eat and drink like all people — this is only for the benefit of the world — so as to draw bounty and blessing to the entire world. And from this one understands by itself how one must strongly support Torah scholars — and provide for all their needs amply and honorably. Since from their own side — they would not need any of this at all — but only for the benefit of the world. And if so — how could it be that they too are preoccupied with their livelihood, heaven forfend? Is it not so that Shabbos does not prepare for the weekday — but rather the weekday must prepare for Shabbos — as mentioned above? And whatever one increases in supporting Torah scholars — by itself one's own livelihood also flows more abundantly and generously — as our Sages of blessed memory taught regarding Shabbos: "kol hamosif mosifin lo" — as mentioned above.

And from this one also understands by itself the matter of the prohibition of labor and doing one's pursuits on Shabbos. For since Shabbos itself has no need for this at all — as mentioned above — it follows that if one performs labor, heaven forfend, on Shabbos — for the sake of the livelihood of the weekdays — one thereby greatly blemishes and desecrates the honor of Shabbos, heaven forfend.

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded [Isaiah 56:2]: "u'ven adam yachazik bah" — regarding those who support Torah scholars — and juxtaposed: "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo" — for they are in one aspect — as mentioned above. And this [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and so on — that is, one should refrain from all weekday pursuits on Shabbos — and fulfill also the delight and honor of Shabbos. [Isaiah 58:14]: "az tis'anag al Hashem — da se'udasa d'Atika Kadisha" [the meal of the Holy Ancient One]. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'hirkavticha al bamosey aretz — da se'udasa d'Chakla Tupichin Kadishin" [the meal of the Holy Apple Orchard]. And [Isaiah 58:14]: "v'ha'achalticha nachalas Yaakov avicha — da se'udasa d'Ze'ir Anpin" [the meal of Ze'ir Anpin] — and so on. Behold and look from afar — the greatness of the awesomeness and the wondrous spirituality of the holiness of the Shabbos meals — how such spiritual matters are clothed in the secret of the commandment of the Shabbos meals plainly — to eat and drink and take delight in them. And all of this for the benefit of the world — "begin d'yisbrechu minei kol shita yomin" — as mentioned above.

 Siman 277 — סימן רעז
 Tzadik kaTamar Yifrach — Shabbos = peace and nullification of all enemies and strife — shalhava d'asha — Eretz Yisrael = healed — Zohar Vayikra 12 — the small steps of Shabbos = tikkun for desecration of Shabbos — the small child who begins to walk

Shabbos is the aspect of peace and the nullification of all enemies and strife — in the aspect of [Psalms 92:10]: "oyevai yashuvun yevoshu raga" — as explained within.

And this is the aspect of Shabbos — whose virtue is to silence the enemy and the avenger — as explained within in Siman 57. And see in Karnayim, the teaching Zayin — the secret of the month of Iyar — is from the secret of Shabbos — and there it brings: "dan yadinenu — a'yovai yashuvun yevoshu raga" — initial letters of — איי"ר — and as also explained within in this teaching. And from there — from the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos — peace — the earth receives the power for all the influences and for all the healings. And then it is in the aspect of [Psalms 67:7]: "eretz nasna yevulah [the earth has given its produce]." And the essential matter is Eretz Yisrael — and as explained within. And this is what is explained in Zohar Vayikra, folio 12: "eimasai is'rabias ar'ah kadisha v'is'atras b'atrah — havi omer b'yom haShabbas — k'din is'chavras kalah b'malka — l'afaka deshayin u'virchan l'alma" [when is the holy land enlarged and crowned with its crown? — say: on the day of Shabbos — then the bride is joined to the King — to bring forth abundant grasses and blessings to the world]. And this is the aspect of: "Shabbas hi miliz'ok — v'refu'ah kerovah lavo." And also then all judgments are sweetened — and they have no grip at all in the dispute that is in holiness. For then one merits complete Da'as — to know that the dispute of Tzadikim is only for good — for this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:12–13]: "b'kamim alai mere'im" — and so on — "Tzadik katamar yifrach" — as explained within. And therefore this matter is explained in the psalm for the Shabbos day. And also — it is explained within regarding the matter of Shabbos eating — that it is very precious — for it is entirely divinity — entirely holy. And therefore it is a great commandment to eat abundantly at the Shabbos meals — and it is a tikkun for the desecration of Shabbos. For it is easy to stumble into the desecration of Shabbos, heaven forfend.

And the tikkun is through the eating of Shabbos. For the desecration of Shabbos is the aspect of "chalal" — the aspect of departure, heaven forfend. And one whose first wife died — his steps become shorter. And Shabbos is the aspect of the first wife — in the aspect of: "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha [Congregation of Israel shall be your partner]." It follows that the desecration of Shabbos is the aspect of shorter steps — in the aspect of: his steps become shorter. And behold — we find that on the contrary — the honor of Shabbos is to take small steps — and large strides are forbidden on Shabbos. But the matter is: since during the weekday there is some drawing of sustenance by the Sitra Achra from the legs of the commandments — in the aspect of [Proverbs 5:5]: "ragleha yordos maves" — and on Shabbos the legs ascend from the husks — in the aspect of [Isaiah 58:13]: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" — and as brought in the writings of the Ari z"l. And then the commandment begins to walk before G-d, blessed be He. And behold — at the beginning of the walking — it is certainly in the aspect of small steps and a fine and narrow path. But it is like the parable of the infant when beginning to walk — that at first he cannot walk well. But the father — from his love and the great delight he takes in his child — makes from the child's small footsteps a well-trodden path — in the manner of a father who makes from every deed of his small child a great thing. Likewise — G-d, blessed be He — when the commandment begins to walk before G-d, blessed be He — or when a person makes some new path toward G-d, blessed be He — even though at first it is a fine and narrow path — nonetheless — because of the immensity of His delight, blessed be He, in this — He makes from its small footsteps a well-trodden path. And all of this is done through the eating of Shabbos. For through eating — the legs receive strength. And then — from the small steps — a well-trodden path is made — as mentioned above. And therefore through the eating of Shabbos — the desecration of Shabbos — which is the aspect of shortened steps — is rectified.

For through the eating of Shabbos — from short steps — broad steps are made — and from them a well-trodden path is made — as mentioned above. All of this is explained within.

 Siman 282 — סימן רפב
 Azamrah l'Elokai b'Odi — On Shabbos everyone is judged favorably — the good point in every person of Israel — Zohar Chadash Bereishis — joy of Shabbos = goodness in every soul — Psalm 92 fully expounded — Vayakhel Moshe — Moshe = the public cantor who encompasses all good points — children of the house of the teacher — 25 children = 25 letters — Shema Yisrael — Tikun haMishkan

On Shabbos — everyone is judged favorably — for then all judgments are suppressed and do not stir at all. And then the good point that exists in every person of Israel shines — even in one who is completely wicked, heaven forfend. As it is explained in Zohar Chadash, Parashas Bereishis: there is no wicked person of Israel who does not have good deeds — that will bring him to the World to Come. And when do they bring him? On the day of Shabbos — to crown everyone with the crown of Shabbos. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught in the Midrash of Shir haShirim: "shechorah ani b'yemay hachol — v'na'avah ani b'Shabbas [I am black on the weekdays — and I am beautiful on Shabbos]." And through the fact that the person is judged favorably on Shabbos — as mentioned above — through this he truly rises to the scale of merit — and merits repentance. And therefore Shabbos is the aspect of repentance — as mentioned above many times. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: all who guard the Shabbos — and so on — he is forgiven all his sins — that is, through the fact that he truly rises from the scale of guilt to the scale of merit. And this is the aspect of the great joy of Shabbos. And it is explained in Zohar Shemos, folio 256: in one chamber there are those appointed to gladden the world. These — when the soul is added on Erev Shabbos — when it goes out — these go out with it — and they pass over Israel — removing from them all sadness and all weariness and all bitterness of soul and all the irritations of the world. And these are the ones who gladden the world. For then all sadness and all kinds of melancholy are repelled — and all of this through the immensity of the illumination of the holy Shabbos — through which all the good points that are in each person of Israel begin to flash and shine. And from these are made melodies and tunes [zemiros v'nigunnim]. And then one can pray and sing and praise Hashem — as explained within. And this is the aspect of [Psalms 92:2]: "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas — tov lehodos laHashem — v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" — "elyon" — specifically — for Hashem is supremely awesome — and so on — in the aspect of: "ant hu ila'ah al kol ila'in" — and so on — "v'leis machshavah tefisah bei k'lal" — how He, blessed be He, constricts His simple will — as it were — to receive delight and pleasures from the service of Israel — even from the greatest of the great. But nonetheless: "u'vemakom she'atah motzeh gedultaso — sham atah motzeh anavtanuso [where you find His greatness — there you find His humility]." And He wishes specifically for the service of the lowly person — in the aspect of [Isaiah 57:15]: "v'avit tehilah megoshah afar" — and so on. And according to this — it is possible also that He receives pleasures likewise from some small good point that is found — even in the most lowly of the lowly among Israel. On the contrary — this lowest one must rejoice even more — from the fact that he too merited to be within the category of Israel — and to cause — through the small good point that is in him — some delight and pleasure and nachas to the Most High G-d — the Creator of heaven and earth — exalted above all exalted ones — and so on — the cause of all causes — and so on — blessed be His Name. And he should believe: a small amount of light repels a large amount of darkness. And through the power of his good point — and the greatness of His compassion, blessed be He — and the power and merit of the guarding of the holy Shabbos — he too can return with complete repentance — and truly rise from the scale of guilt to the scale of merit — until he is transformed into complete good. And this is likewise within the category of: for Hashem is supremely exalted — and as explained elsewhere — for the greatness of G-d, blessed be He, is without limit — and there are lovingkindnesses of such a nature by Him, blessed be He, that through complete repentance — everything can be transformed into good — until from sins they become merits — and as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And this [Psalms 92:3]: "lehagid baboker chasdecha" — that is, when one merits to feel some illumination and flash of holiness — which is the aspect of morning — one must certainly thank and declare His lovingkindnesses, blessed be He. And [Psalms 92:3]: "v'emunascha baleilos" — that is, even in the time of the intensification of the darkness — and many and many kinds of darkness — which is the aspect of "baleilos" [in the plural nights] — nonetheless — one must also then be firm and strong in his faith in Him, blessed be He — and increase words of faith — both for oneself and for one's fellow — and to believe: specifically where you find His greatness, blessed be He, there you find His humility — until He, blessed be He, receives great delight from the good points that are in each person of Israel — even from the smallest of the small — as mentioned above.

And this [Psalms 92:4]: "alay asor v'alay navel — alay higgayon b'chinor" — this is the aspect of the melodies and tunes that are made through this. And this [Psalms 92:5]: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha — b'ma'asey yadecha aranen." For when a person contemplates his deeds — and it seems to him that his sins are more numerous than his merits — until his merits are not considered at all — in particular since even they are full of deficiencies and ulterior motives and the like. And then he will think in his heart: for what purpose did You create all human beings? Is it not so that every act of Hashem is for His sake? And to His glory I was created — and so on. And would that he not blemish against His honor, blessed be He, at the very least, heaven forfend. And already they concluded: it would have been better for a person not to have been created. And if so — it is truly difficult for him: for what purpose was he created? But when Shabbos arrives — and the sacred vitality of the light of the good point in each person of Israel begins to shine and flash — then he understands and sees from afar that everything is worthwhile — for the sake of one single good point — to give nachas to his Father in Heaven. And: "leis re'useh tav d'is'avid" — and in the end G-d, blessed be He, will complete what is His own with each person of Israel — until all of them will truly rise to the scale of merit — and will merit the fullness of their ultimate purpose — until the honor of Heaven is magnified through them. And therefore one should rejoice greatly in His acts, blessed be He — in the aspect of: "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" — and so on — as mentioned above. And this is what the Sages concluded there: "v'achshav shenevra — yefashpesh b'ma'asav" — that is, he should examine and separate his deeds — so that good and evil should not be mixed together — until the excellence of the good is not recognizable because of the abundance of the evil. Rather — he should separate and distinguish the evil alone — and the good points that are found in him should also be alone. And he should revive himself and rejoice in them greatly. And then — the small good within him will outweigh all the evil — until he merits complete repentance. And the evil within him will fall and be nullified entirely — and the good within him will grow and bloom like a palm tree and a cedar — "od yinuvun b'seivah — deshanim v'ra'ananim yihyu." And there is another version: "v'amri lei — yemashmesh b'ma'asav" — that is, before he does something — he should feel it carefully to see whether it is good or evil — and he should assess in his mind the greatness of the Creator, blessed be He, and the great harm of a transgression, heaven have mercy. And likewise the opposite — the great excellence of the commandment — until every single good point is very precious — beyond all measure. And then he will certainly always walk in the good path. And this [Psalms 92:6]: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem — me'od amku machshevosecha" — that is, likewise in the aforementioned matter — there is such great depth — that it is impossible to explain at all the depth of the matter within this. And as understood somewhat also in Likutay Halachos. And around this revolves and goes the entire subsequent matter of the psalm — and it explains how the success of the wicked is only for the moment — a brief instant — and in the end they are spent and lost. And the success of the righteous is eternal — and they produce fruit and their stump replenishes — like the palm tree and the cedar — and so on. And this is in general. And from this one can understand also in particular: that the essential matter is to strengthen oneself in complete faith — in His abundant lovingkindness and goodness and the greatness of His compassion, blessed be He — and to feel deeply sorry for having rebelled against His honor, blessed be He — even for some blemish however small — for who can assess the harm of even a minor transgression, heaven have mercy. And likewise the opposite — to strengthen oneself and greatly rejoice one's soul in every single good point. And then one will certainly merit complete repentance — and the evil within him will fall and be nullified entirely — and the good within him will grow and bloom like a palm tree and a cedar — "od yinuvun b'seivah — deshanim v'ra'ananim yihyu."

And this is what is explained in the writings regarding [Psalms 92]: "M'zmor Sh'ir l'Yom haSh'abas" — initial letters — למש"ה — and so on — for then Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, together with other Tzadikim with him — are engaged in elevating the souls of the living and the dead — who fell to the depths of the husks, heaven have mercy — as mentioned above. For this was the service of Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, in his lifetime — and also now — to search out and find the good within each person of Israel — and to judge each person favorably. And the essential fullness of this matter is done through the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And this [Exodus 35:1]: "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Yisrael" — and it is explained in Zohar Vayakhel, folio 195: "begin d'havu Erev Rav beinaihu — itzterich Moshe l'achnasha lon — v'leyachda lon mibeinhaihu" — see there at length. And this is likewise in the aspect of the aforementioned. For at first they were mixed with the Erev Rav — (which is the aspect of the good being mixed together with much evil — and this caused them the sin of the golden calf). And therefore afterward — Moshe separated them from the Erev Rav — and gathered them together — that is, he gathered and collected together all the good points of the holiness of Israel within them. And then they were commanded regarding the work of the Mishkan — for from these good points the Mishkan was built — as also understood within in this teaching — and as likewise explained in Likutay Halachos. And they were also commanded regarding the warning of Shabbos — for the work of the Mishkan does not override Shabbos — for on the contrary — all the essential power to gather and clarify the good points that are in Israel — and to build the Mishkan through this — all of it flows from the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And see in Likutay Halachos, Halachos Techum Shabbas — where this matter of the holiness of Shabbos is explained according to this teaching in wondrous things.

And see within: it is explained regarding the matter of: in every generation there is a shepherd — and he is the aspect of Moshe — who is the faithful shepherd. And this shepherd builds a Mishkan. And know: the children of the house of the teacher receive the breath of their mouth — in which there is no sin — from this Mishkan — and so on — see there. And this is the aspect of the passage [Numbers 7:1]: "vayehi b'yom kalos Moshe l'hakim es haMishkan" — and so on — concluding: "u'v'vo Moshe el Ohel Mo'ed l'daber ito — vayishma es haKol midaber eilav — mibein shney haKeruvim — vayedaber eilav" — and so on. And it is known and brought in the Introduction of the Zohar, folio 1: for the Keruvim are the root of the aspect of the children of the house of the teacher — for this is the aspect of "keruvim k'ravya [cherubs — like children]" — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. For Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, is the aspect of: entirely good — as it is written [Exodus 2:2]: "ki tov hu" — and he had a quality like this — that all the good points in Israel yearned to be encompassed within him. For this is the aspect of: "Vayakhel Moshe es kol adas Bnay Yisrael" — as mentioned above. And therefore he was able to clarify every good point that is in each person of Israel — and to elevate him through this to the scale of merit — until each person — according to his good point — contributed to the Mishkan. And from this were made all the matters of the Mishkan. And [Numbers 7:1]: "vayavi'u es haMishkan el Moshe" — and [Exodus 40:18]: "vayakem Moshe es haMishkan" — for only he was able to erect it — for he was the true public prayer leader [shali'ach tzibbur] — who was encompassed within him all the good points of all the congregation — as mentioned above. And from the aspect of this Mishkan — which is entirely good — from there the children receive the breath of their mouth that has no sin — that is, it is likewise entirely good — with no mixture of evil at all — since they have no sin yet. Which is the aspect of what our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Shabbos 119]: the breath of the mouth that has no sin is not comparable to the breath of the mouth that has sin.

And behold — it is known what Rashi of blessed memory explained — and our Sages of blessed memory likewise taught — regarding what Lot said: "pen tidbakeni hara'ah" — when I was among the people of Sodom — I appeared righteous — and when I come next to a righteous person — I appear as wicked. And likewise the woman of Tzarfas said to Eliyahu — and so on. It follows that accordingly — on the contrary — when the Tzadik is entirely good — the good points that are in one's fellow — and are mixed together with much evil — might be even more nullified relative to the goodness of the Tzadik — (who is entirely pure and clear) — until they are not seen or recognizable at all — as mentioned above. But in truth — it is only Lot and the woman of Tzarfas who were concerned about this — perhaps it will be so. And perhaps there is sometimes some aspect in this manner as well. Therefore — the essential tikkun is through a Tzadik of this kind — who is the aspect of Moshe our teacher — who was exceedingly humble above all people — and so on. And who was able to conceal and hide the good within him so greatly — until no accusation at all was aroused through him, heaven forfend, against the good of his fellow — which does not yet have complete fullness. But on the contrary — the light of the good point within each person of Israel shines and illuminates even more — even if it does not yet have fullness. And because of this itself — all the good points yearn and anticipate to be encompassed within him — as mentioned above. And something like this is brought in the holy books — and is also understood from his teachings of blessed memory in many places. And perhaps this is the aspect of the small Aleph of Vayikra. And something like this is explained in Zohar Vayechi, folio 234b: "tu — Aleph ze'ira — me'atar ze'ira havah — ze'ira d'ihu rav b'ischabrutei l'eila" — and so on. And this is something like what we explained above — that specifically through the recognition of some part of the immensity of His greatness, blessed be He, — until one knows that all the great service of the greatest of the great is absolutely nothing and literally null before the immensity of His greatness, blessed be He — but because of the greatness of His compassion and lovingkindness — He wishes to receive nachas and pleasures from lowly human beings specifically. And then one knows likewise that on the contrary — His compassion, blessed be He, is so abundant — that every good point of the most lowly among Israel — its excellence is great and awesome beyond all measure — as mentioned above.

And behold — all the clarifications that are made through the weekday pursuits of the six days of deed — are in the aspect of the work of the Mishkan. And all is done through the power of the holiness of Shabbos — as mentioned above. And from there — from the aspect of this Mishkan — the children receive [their portion] — for this is the aspect of the fact that one begins with the child by learning from [Leviticus 1:1]: "Vayikra el Moshe" — as explained within. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: one teacher should not teach more than twenty-five children — twenty-five — specifically — corresponding to the twenty-five letters that are in the verse Vayikra — (from the word vayedaber to the end of the verse — that is, the word leimor) — and it is explained in the holy Zohar that these twenty-five letters correspond to the twenty-five letters in the verse Shema Yisrael. And therefore it is explained in the Zohar that the twenty-five children mentioned above are likewise corresponding to the twenty-five letters in Shema Yisrael. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught [Tractate Nedarim 37 — and brought in Shulchan Aruch, Yoreh De'ah, Siman 245, paragraph 14]: one does not teach children on Shabbos something new that they have not yet learned — because of the burden of Shabbos [tirchah d'Shabbas]. But what they have already read once — they review for them on Shabbos. And this is as mentioned above. For Shabbos is the aspect of the ultimate purpose of heaven and earth — as it is written [Genesis 2:2]: "vayechal Elokim b'yom hashevi'i" — and so on — which is likewise the aspect of the completion of the work of the Mishkan — in the aspect of [Exodus 35:2]: "sheshes yamim ta'aseh melachah — u'vayom hashevi'i" — and so on — for the image of the Mishkan is like the image of the act of Bereishis [creation]. And our Sages of blessed memory taught: on the day the Mishkan was erected — the entire world was erected with it — and so on. And then immediately — the children come and receive from the aspect of the erecting of the aforementioned Mishkan. For this is the aspect of what they read in the Torah on Shabbos — for then all of them are in the aspect of children of the house of the teacher — for the breath of their mouth that has no sin — for each one receives an extra soul — a new higher-soul — and is like a small child who was born — and he is forgiven all his sins through the guarding of Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. And then all of them receive the sacred havalim of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the breath of the mouth that has no sin — as mentioned above many times. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory taught: Shabbosim were given only for Torah study — for then is the essential fullness of the study — since the breath is the breath of the mouth that has no sin. But nonetheless — since the essential breath of the mouth that has no sin that they receive from the aspect of the Mishkan — is with actual children — whose breath of the mouth has literally no sin at all in its plain sense — since they have no sin yet — therefore one should not teach new things with them on Shabbos because of the burden of Shabbos.

And it would thereby blemish, heaven forfend, the holiness of Shabbos — from which is all the power and the root of the matter of the erecting of the Mishkan — as mentioned above. Only — what they have already read once — one reviews for them on Shabbos. For what they have already read in the weekday — this was from the aspect of the erecting of the Mishkan of the previous Shabbos. Therefore — this will not blemish, heaven forfend, the holiness of this Shabbos. And therefore likewise — the matter of the prayer leader [chazan] who sees where the children are reading — as explained within — is stated likewise regarding Shabbos. For from there is the root of the learning of the children — as mentioned above. And this is what they concluded: but he should not read — for the entire matter of what he is a chazan and a shali'ach tzibbur — and all the good points of Israel are encompassed within him — and he comes and prays with them — and so on — all of this is because — from the immensity of his humility — it never occurs to him at all — the immensity of the excellence of the holiness of the good within him — but on the contrary — he is exceedingly humble above all people — and so on — as mentioned above. For if he were to begin to make use of the great power of the good within him — then perhaps on the contrary — the good points in the rest of Israel would become even more hidden and nullified — in the manner of: "bast eilai l'hazkir es avoni" — as mentioned above. But because he is exceedingly humble — because of the immensity of his attainment — until it seems to him that the good within his fellow is even more praiseworthy — since his mind is not yet complete — and nonetheless there is such good within him — and therefore he is the shali'ach tzibbur and prays only through the connection to the congregation — and arouses and illuminates the merit of their good point even more each time — until the aspect of a Mishkan is built from this — and from there the children receive — as mentioned above. And this is likewise only because of the aforementioned — for had he made use of the power of the good within him — then the learning of the children would not have had such importance. For even though it has no sin — but nonetheless their mind is not yet complete — since they are still small — and what will all the good within them amount to compared to the service and the learning of the aspect of Moshe himself — who certainly has no sin — and has completely and wondrously complete Da'as at the utmost level? But since — on the contrary — the more one attains the fullness of Da'as — the more one comes through this very thing to even greater humility — until the good within him is not considered at all in his own eyes — and he seeks only a free gift — and gathers and arouses the good within all of Israel — and clarifies it from within the evil and the dross literally, heaven have mercy — and builds from this the Mishkan. And from there specifically the children receive — for then certainly there is great importance to their learning — since they have no sin. And even though their mind is not yet complete — on the contrary — through this he considers the good within them even more praiseworthy — since they are still small — and their mind is not yet complete — and nonetheless there is such good within them. And therefore — the essential completion of the erecting of the Mishkan — which was on the eighth day of the consecration — was on the first day of the week — which is Shabbos — as our Sages of blessed memory taught. For all of it was through the power of the previous holy Shabbos. And since every true Tzadik in the generation is the aspect of a shepherd — and builds the aspect of a Mishkan — and from there the children receive — and so on — and it has already been explained that the essential matter is done through the holiness of Shabbos. And on Shabbos — all of Israel are in the aspect of children of the house of the teacher — as mentioned above. And therefore it is especially propitious to be with true Tzadikim on the holy Shabbos. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory expounded [Exodus 35:1]: "Vayakhel Moshe" — that it is a commandment to gather congregations on every Shabbos — and to expound words of Torah to them — and this is as mentioned above.

Note — end of Siman 282: (From the words "And see within: it is explained regarding the matter" — and so on — this was written only as general discussion [pilpula b'alma] — for I have no business with such fine and spiritual matters.) — Tushlab"a [thus far Part One of Yikara DiShabsa].

 ✦ Translator's Summary — Simanim 178–282
 
 Siman 178 — Verbal confession / joy of Shabbos / Tikkun 21 / unity of voice and speech: Tikkun 21 (folio 57) cited (Aramaic): "leis pikuda d'aseh v'lo ta'aseh d'lo ishtech b'Shabbas" = therefore Shabbos equivalent to entire Torah. Must rejoice very greatly. Nature of sins = draws anxiety = "edaig mecha'tati." When entering joy of Shabbos = Shabbos = complete stature = totality of all commandments → blemishes of sins come to confuse joy. In particular: Shabbos = sacred speech (Zohar Bereishis 32); blemish of sin in the soul = aspect of speech (within). Even though Shabbos holiness covers over everything ("kol hame'aneg es haShabbas mochalin lo / afilu aved avodah zarah mochalin lo") → through this: one remembers all one's blemishes → can make verbal confession in fullness → speech rectified and built → yichud Kud'sha B'rich Hu u'Shechinteih = secret of holiness of Shabbos (Tikunim and Zohar). Psalm 92: "tov lehodos" = Sages: from language of viduy devarim = through which speech rectified = Malchus = merit to hear voices from above; "v'lezamre lishimcha elyon"; "lehagid baboker chasdecha" = Ze'ir Anpin d'Atzilus (kavannos); "v'emunascha baleilos" = Malchus d'Atzilus → yichud Kud'sha B'rich Hu u'Shechinteih = unity of voice and speech (kol v'dibur); touches on the secret of hearing the sound of musical instruments; "alay asor v'alay navel alay higgayon b'chinor"; "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" = aspect of joy; "b'feroa'ch resha'im / ki hinneh oyevecha yovadu / vatarem kir'em karni" = in general; and also in particular: blemishes of sins come to confuse joy = all work of the adversary; but on the contrary: specifically through this is the essential subjugation and nullification of them = through this one remembers them and makes verbal confession over them explicitly → everything rectified in fullness. Isaiah 58: "az tis'anag = da Atika Kadisha" = source of supernal and very wondrous joy = Zohar Vayikra 133 cited (Aramaic): "sos asis b'Hashem b'Atik Yomin is'mar d'ha hu chedvasa d'chola"; "hirkavticha" = full ascent of Malchus = destroys buildings of Sitra Achra (built through one's blemishes) and builds sacred speech = ascent of sacred Malchus; "nachalas Yaakov = Ze'ir Anpin" = voice = "kol kol Yaakov" = voice unified with speech; "ki pi Hashem diber" = yichud Kud'sha B'rich Hu u'Shechinteih = speech unified with G-d = cross-references to Siman 78 and Siman 94.
 Siman 179 — Shabbos = peace / charity on Erev Shabbos / fasting on Erev Shabbos / delight of Shabbos superior to a thousand fasts / extra soul = will / tachyas hamaysim: Shabbos = peace (Sages) → must give charity for Shabbos = "marbeh tzedakah marbeh shalom." SA OC 249: way of people of deed = fast on every Erev Shabbos; also: everyone must not establish a new meal on Erev Shabbos = aspect of a fast → through fasting: strife nullified and peace made. In truth: delight of Shabbos itself more propitious than a fast and more than this (elsewhere). Midrash Tanchuma Bereishis: "kevod Shabbas adif me'elef tani'yos." Virtue of fasting = nullify one's will before G-d's will (within). Shabbos even more propitious = extra soul of Shabbos = "nefesh" is an expression of will (within) = then each person of Israel merits good and holy wills (many times). "V'taher libbenu l'ovdecha be'emes / v'hanchilenu b'ahavah u'v'ratzon Shabbas Kodshecha." Sages: guardian and delighter of Shabbos = decrees and G-d fulfills = all desires of his heart = essential perfection of peace = nothing done to him against his will. Joy of Shabbos = when there is peace → joy and gladness. Shabbos = aspect of tachyas hamaysim = "ta'ameha chayyim zachu." Shabbos = foretaste of World to Come = after the resurrection = Daniel 12:13. Essential vitality of holiness of all weekdays comes from Shabbos = "zachor es yom haShabbas / zachrehu mei'echad b'Shabbas." Shammai ate all his days in honor of Shabbos = so all the vitality he received through eating would be only from Shabbos. Through Shabbos: stature of joy is built = new sacred vitality and joy drawn upon entire creation = "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha" (Psalm 92). Sages on Psalms 139:16: "yamim yotzaru v'lo echad bahem" = this is the Shabbos day = vitality of all of them.
 Siman 188 — Shabbos = returning of lost objects / the one thousand lights / Moshe restores the crowns / the Tzadik as shofar: Shabbos = returning of lost objects (Ari z"l writings): they restore to Moshe our teacher the one thousand lights that were taken from him; Moshe restores the crowns taken from Israel. Also plain: "keivan she'shavas vav avdah nefesh" = there is a loss for each person; on Shabbos: one's lost object returned = extra soul. "Zachor es yom haShabbas" = opposite of forgetting = opposite of loss. Since one does not return a lost object until one inquires whether he is a deceiver and a liar: "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" = also aspect of returning the lost object = "im tashiv miShabbas" roshei teivos emes (writings). Therefore essential time to come to the Tzadik = reclaim one's lost object. Must receive the face of one's teacher on Shabbos (Zohar). Aspect of the tekiyos blown on Erev Shabbos = "b'yom hahu yitaka b'shofar gadol u'va'u ha'ovdim" (Isaiah 27:13) = returning of the lost objects.
 Siman 225 — Shabbos = ru'ach chayyim in kanfey re'iyah / extra soul and sacred mochin / trust / charity / speech / Psalm 92: Shabbos = ru'ach chayyim in wings of the lungs (explained above) = essential sustaining of the intellect = neshamah. Therefore on Shabbos: extra soul and sacred mochin. Through this: trust = "luvu alai va'ani porei'a." Through this: charity = fullness of charity of Shabbos; delight of Shabbos itself = aspect of charity (many times). Through this: comes to the level of a person = aspect of speech = "v'daber davar" stated regarding Shabbos (Zohar many times). Until: merits to make words from sound of chirping and hear words from sound of the harp (within). "Mizmor Shir l'Yom haShabbas tov lehodos laHashem" = through sacred words opened then; "lehagid baboker chasdecha" = "lehagid" = milah d'chochmata = fullness of intellect and mochin = lovingkindnesses; "v'emunascha baleilos" = strengthening trust even in darkness; "alay asor / alay higgayon b'chinor" = merits to make words from sound of the harp.
 Siman 234 — Shabbos = world of thought = mochin d'gadlus / songs of Creator's greatness at entry of Shabbos / Havdalah = righteous vs. wicked: Shabbos = world of thought = mochin d'gadlus. At entry of Shabbos: recite psalms of the Creator's greatness (= righteous One of the world) → purity of thought. Psalm 92: "mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem me'od amku machshevosecha" = then elaborates at length: stories of success of wicked = only temporary = for their destruction forever; stories of success of righteous = true and eternal — forever. Havdalah: "haMavdil bein Kodesh l'chol / bein or l'choshech / bein Yisrael la'amim" = Israel as a collective are righteous against all the nations = "v'amech kulam tzadikim" (Isaiah 60:21). "Bein yom hashevi'i l'sheshes yemey haMa'aseh" = as mentioned above.
 Siman 250 — Complete Da'as and complete faith on Shabbos / all suffering nullified / Shabbos = foretaste of World to Come = light of Providence / tlas guvnin d'eina: On Shabbos: complete Da'as and complete faith = everything conducted only through Providence of G-d → all kinds of suffering and afflictions nullified = "b'yom hani'ach lecha mei'atzevecha u'merogzecha." Also: saved from subjugation of kingdoms = sorrow of exile. Shabbos = foretaste of World to Come = day that is entirely Shabbos = then nature entirely nullified = only Providence alone. Also now: through Shabbos holiness one merits to draw light of Providence from the aspect of the final end → Israel elevated above nature → end and conclusion comes to all those who oppress us. "Lo charevah Yerushalayim ela al she'chilellu bah es haShabbas / ilmalai shamru Yisrael Shabbas rishonah lo hayah shum umah v'lashon sholetin bahem / ilmalai shamru shtay Shabbasos miyad nigalin." Midrash Rabbah Beshalach: even through merit of one Shabbos one is redeemed. If all Israel had merited to guard Shabbos in fullness → light of Providence would have flowed in fullness → certain eternal redemption. "Es Shabsosai tishmoru" mostly in plural = through plain guarding of Shabbos one merits to draw light of future Shabbos (= day that is entirely Shabbos). Perhaps this itself = the two Shabbosim. Shabbos = "tlas guvnin d'eina u'vat ein" = light of Providence.
 Siman 276 — The essential satiety is on Shabbos / three Shabbos meals are to draw bounty on all six days / great Tzadikim feed on spiritual bounty / support Torah scholars / Isaiah 58: Essential satiety on Shabbos = fullness of light of the eyes = "pos'im bo pesi'ah ketanah." Essential satiety = through sight of the eyes (Sages). Three Shabbos meals: "begin d'yisbrechu minei kol shita yomin" (Zohar). Resolution of Zohar's question re no manna on Shabbos: on the contrary = this is the essential blessing = such satiety that no need at all for physical eating and drinking. Shabbos = foretaste of World to Come = no eating and drinking. Commandment of eating Shabbos meals = only to draw bounty on weekdays. Manna did not descend on Shabbos; on sixth day = bread for two days for the Shabbos meals. "Chol mekhin l'Shabbas v'ein Shabbas mekhin l'chol." "Vayevarech vayekadesh": blessed = manna on sixth day; sanctified = no manna = to indicate immensity of holiness of Shabbos = aspect of World to Come (no eating for its own sake = only to draw blessing on six days). Great Tzadikim: through whom the entire world is sustained yet they themselves lack sustenance = from the aforementioned reason: their food and sustenance is only from spiritual bounty. Zohar Beshalach 61 (Aramaic) cited: "mezonah ila'ah yatir mikola hu mezonah d'chavrayya — inon d'mishtadlin b'orayta — d'achlei mezonah d'rucha v'nishmata — v'lo achlei mezonah d'gufa klal — v'hiynoo me'atar ila'ah yakira al kola v'itkari chochmah / v'achlei mezonah d'rucha v'nishmata me'atar rachika ila'ah yakira mikola / zakai chulkah d'gufa d'yachil l'is'zanah b'mezonah d'nafsha." They eat only for benefit of the world = to draw bounty and blessing to the entire world → must strongly support Torah scholars and provide for all their needs amply and honorably. "Ain Shabbas mekhin l'chol ela chol tzarich sheychin l'Shabbas." "Kol hamosif mosifin lo." Prohibition of labor on Shabbos: since Shabbos itself has no need for this = laboring on Shabbos for the sake of weekday livelihood = greatly blemishes and desecrates the honor of Shabbos. Sages on Isaiah 56:2: "u'ven adam yachazik bah" = regarding supporters of Torah scholars; juxtaposed: "shomer Shabbas mecha'lelo" = they are in one aspect. Isaiah 58 mapped: "az tis'anag = da se'udasa d'Atika Kadisha"; "hirkavticha = da se'udasa d'Chakla Tupichin Kadishin"; "nachalas Yaakov = da se'udasa d'Ze'ir Anpin." See and look from afar: greatness of awesomeness and wondrous spirituality of holiness of Shabbos meals — how such spiritual matters are clothed in the secret of the plain commandment of eating and drinking — all for benefit of the world = "begin d'yisbrechu minei kol shita yomin."
 Siman 277 — Peace and nullification of all enemies / Eretz Yisrael healed / Zohar Vayikra 12 / small steps of Shabbos = tikkun for desecration / the infant who begins to walk: Shabbos = peace = nullification of all enemies and strife = "oyevai yashuvun yevoshu raga" (Psalms 92:10; within). Shabbos = virtue to silence the enemy and the avenger (Siman 57 cross-ref.). Karnayim, teaching Zayin: secret of month of Iyar from secret of Shabbos; "dan yadinenu / a'yovai yashuvun yevoshu raga" = roshei teivos = Iyar. Through Shabbos: earth receives power for all influences and all healings = "eretz nasna yevulah" (Psalms 67:7). Zohar Vayikra 12 (Aramaic): "eimasai is'rabias ar'ah kadisha v'is'atras b'atrah — havi omer b'yom haShabbas — k'din is'chavras kalah b'malka — l'afaka deshayin u'virchan l'alma." "Shabbas hi miliz'ok v'refu'ah kerovah lavo." All judgments sweetened on Shabbos = no grip in sacred dispute = complete Da'as = dispute of Tzadikim only for good = "b'kamim alai mere'im / Tzadik katamar yifrach" (within). Shabbos eating = precious = entirely divinity = entirely holy = great commandment to eat abundantly at Shabbos meals = tikkun for desecration of Shabbos. Desecration of Shabbos = "chalal" = departure; one whose first wife died = steps become shorter; Shabbos = first wife = "Keneses Yisrael yihyeh ben zugcha" → desecration of Shabbos = shorter steps. Honor of Shabbos = small steps; large strides forbidden on Shabbos. Explanation: during weekdays: Sitra Achra draws from legs of commandments = "ragleha yordos maves"; on Shabbos: legs ascend from husks = "im tashiv miShabbos raglecha" (Ari z"l writings) → commandment begins to walk before G-d. At first = small steps and fine narrow path. Like the parable of the infant beginning to walk = father makes from child's small footsteps a well-trodden path = father makes from every deed of his small child a great thing. Likewise G-d, blessed be He, when commandment begins to walk before Him or when person makes some new path toward G-d = even though at first a fine narrow path = because of immensity of His delight → makes from its small footsteps a well-trodden path. All done through eating of Shabbos = through eating: legs receive strength → from small steps: well-trodden path is made → tikkun for desecration of Shabbos (= shortened steps) → from short steps broad steps are made → from them a well-trodden path is made (all explained within).
 Siman 282 — On Shabbos judged favorably / the good point in every person of Israel / joy of Shabbos = zemiros v'nigunnim / Psalm 92 fully expounded / Vayakhel = gathering of good points = Mishkan / Moshe = shali'ach tzibbur = encompasses all good points / children of the house of the teacher = 25 children = 25 letters = Shema Yisrael / end of Part One: On Shabbos: everyone judged favorably = all judgments suppressed (Zohar); good point in every person of Israel shines = even in one completely wicked, heaven forfend. Zohar Chadash Bereishis: no wicked person of Israel without good deeds that bring him to World to Come; when? On day of Shabbos. Midrash Shir haShirim: "shechorah ani b'yemay hachol v'na'avah ani b'Shabbas." Through being judged favorably → truly rises to scale of merit → merits repentance. Shabbos = teshuvah (many times). Sages: "kol hashomer Shabbas v'chol haggid mochalin lo al kol avonasav" = truly rises from scale of guilt to scale of merit. Zohar Shemos 256 (Aramaic): "in one chamber there are those appointed to gladden the world... when the soul is added on Erev Shabbos... they pass over Israel removing from them all sadness and all weariness and all bitterness of soul and all the irritations of the world." Then: all sadness and melancholy repelled → from all the good points flashing and shining: made melodies and tunes (zemiros v'nigunnim) → can pray and sing and praise G-d. Psalm 92 fully expounded through "good points" / "judged favorably" lens: "tov lehodos laHashem v'lezamre lishimcha elyon" = "elyon davka" = G-d is supremely exalted ("ant hu ila'ah al kol ila'in / v'leis machshavah tefisah bei klal") = how G-d constricts His simple will to receive delight from service of Israel even from the greatest; but: "u'vemakom she'atah motzeh gedultaso sham atah motzeh anavtanuso" = wishes specifically for service of the lowly person = "v'avit tehilah megoshah afar" (Isaiah 57:15); even the most lowly must rejoice greatly = caused delight to the Most High G-d through even a small good point; "a small amount of light repels a large amount of darkness"; through one's good point + G-d's compassion + merit of guarding Shabbos = can return with complete repentance; sins can become merits (Sages). "Lehagid baboker chasdecha" = when one merits to feel some illumination and flash = must thank and declare G-d's lovingkindnesses; "v'emunascha baleilos" = even in time of intensification of darkness (plural nights): firm and strong in faith + increase words of faith for oneself and for one's fellow. "Alay asor v'alay navel alay higgayon b'chinor" = melodies and tunes made through this; "ki simachtani Hashem b'fa'alecha b'ma'asey yadecha aranen" = when person contemplates his deeds and it seems his sins outweigh his merits = thinks: for what purpose was I created? But when Shabbos arrives = sacred vitality of light of good point begins to shine → understands: everything worthwhile for the sake of one single good point to give nachas to Father in Heaven = "leis re'useh tav d'is'avid"; in the end G-d will complete what is His own with each person of Israel. Sages: "v'achshav shenevra yefashpesh b'ma'asav" = examine and separate deeds so good and evil not mixed together; let good points alone = revive oneself and rejoice greatly in them; then small good will outweigh all evil → complete repentance; evil falls and nullified; good grows and blooms "k'tamar v'erez / od yinuvun b'seivah deshanim v'ra'ananim." Also: "v'amri lei yemashmesh b'ma'asav" = before doing something: carefully feel whether good or evil; assess immensity of Creator's greatness and the harm of transgression and the excellence of commandment → every single good point precious beyond all measure → will always walk in the good path. "Mah gadlu ma'asecha Hashem me'od amku machshevosecha" = great depth in this matter; impossible to explain fully. Entire subsequent Psalm 92 revolves around this: success of wicked = only for a moment; success of righteous = eternal; in general and in particular = essential = strengthen in complete faith in G-d's abundant lovingkindness and compassion + feel deeply sorry for any blemish + strengthen and greatly rejoice in every single good point → complete repentance → evil nullified → good grows like palm tree and cedar → "od yinuvun b'seivah deshanim v'ra'ananim yihyu." "Mizmor Shir = l'Moshe" = Moshe together with other Tzadikim engaged in elevating the souls of the living and the dead.
